title: Lamar Jackson out of Wednesday's Week 5 practice
summary: The Ravens have brought in a new center, but they don't currently have a healthy quarterback.
full_text: ' The Ravens have brought in a new center, but they don't currently have a healthy quarterback. According to multiple reporters on the scene, Lamar Jackson is not practicing on Wednesday. Jackson is dealing with a sprained ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was unsure of Jackson's availability for Sunday's game against Atlanta. Additionally, receiver Zay Flowers, safety Kyle Hamilton, edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, cornerback Marlon Humphrey, receiver Rashod Bateman, and guard Andrew Vorhees also were not spotted during the portion of practice open to media on Wednesday. Baltimore's full injury report with practice participation levels will be released later on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Rhamondre Stevenson, Mack Hollins set to miss practice for Patriots
summary: The Patriots are set to open the practice week without a couple of key offensive players.
full_text: The Patriots are set to open the practice week without a couple of key offensive players. Head coach Mike Vrabel said at his Wednesday press conference that running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver Mack Hollins are expected to sit out the team's first on-field work of Week 5. Stevenson was injured late in last Sunday's win over the Bills. Vrabel did not specify the nature of what appeared to be a lower body injury, but word will come on the injury report. The Patriots worked out Jamaal Williams on Tuesday in a move that was likely related to the uncertainty about Stevenson's availability. Hollins injured his calf in Buffalo. Vrabel also said that cornerback Christian Gonzalez will remain out of practice. He missed all of last week with a shoulder injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles trade Cam Jurgens to Ravens
summary: Baltimore has acquired the two-time Pro Bowler to help solve its injury issues along the offensive line.
full_text: Earlier this week, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters that he was pleased with the play of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens. But now, Jurgens is headed elsewhere. Jurgens has been traded to the Ravens, the team announced on Wednesday. Baltimore will receive Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. "We are excited to acquire a two-time Pro Bowl center, Cam Jurgens, from the Eagles in a trade,” Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta said in a statement. "Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process. He's a young foundational piece along our offensive line - a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore. We are confident that Cam will significantly impact our team and community." Baltimore has had several injury issues on the interior of the offensive line, which Jurgens should be able to help solve. But Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol. The Ravens will play the Falcons on Sunday night this week.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson successfully appeals his beer celebration fine
summary: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk wasn't the only player to win his appeal of a fine for pretending to drink a beer as part of an in-game celebration in Week 2.
full_text: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk wasn't the only player to win his appeal of a fine for pretending to drink a beer as part of an in-game celebration in Week 2. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that tight end Jake Ferguson also prevailed in his appeal. Ferguson had been fined $13,611 for miming chugging a beer after a touchdown in the Cowboys' win over the Commanders. Ferguson's appealed because he said he was mimicking taking a drink from a Gatorade bottle and shared documentation that showed he has done the same celebration on a number of other occasions. The NFL also fined Colts guard Matt Goncalves for a similar celebration and there's been no word about the result of his appeal.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kevin Byard: Mike Vrabel used Allen Iverson video to get Patriots "stepping over people"
summary: One week after the Patriots were bullied by the Jaguars, New England roared into Buffalo's next stadium and gave the Bills their first loss there.
full_text: One week after the Patriots were bullied by the Jaguars, New England roared into Buffalo's next stadium and gave the Bills their first loss there. Appearing Tuesday on NBC Sports Boston, Patriots safety Kevin Byard explained coach Mike Vrabel's strategy for giving the team a spark. "He showed a video of the famous Allen Iverson, NBA Finals, making the three-point shot, stepping over Tyronn Lue ," Byard said. "So, at first, you don't really know where he's going with it. . . . I think the overall messaging was, 'It's time to start stepping over people.' You know what I mean? It's time to get back to where we're stepping over people and making sure that we're not about to be the team that's gonna let people bully them. . . . "So yeah, I think that was kind of the overarching message to, hey, we are physical. We are a tough team. Let's, let's start stepping over people kind of like how A.I. did in that video." It worked. The Pats were far more physical than they had been in Jacksonville, and in turn far more effective. The Patriots avoided a 1-3 start and a three-game hole in the AFC East. Instead, they're only one game behind Buffalo — and they'll have a chance to complete the sweep when the two teams meet again in Week 13.
author: Mike Florio

title: 1989 book claimed that "no fewer than 70" NFL games had been fixed
summary: The cesspool that is social media often kicks out some bubbling crude.
full_text: ' The cesspool that is social media often kicks out some bubbling crude. (Oil, that is.) A clip from a 1989 episode of The Pat Sajak Show (yes, Wheel of Fortune was once so popular that the host got a late-night show, for 15 months) has been making the rounds on Twitter. In it, Dan Moldea discusses his book, Interference: How Organized Crime Influences Professional Football . During the nearly eight-minute interview, Moldea makes some startling claims. He says that "no fewer than 26" past and present team owners have documented ties to the gambling community and/or organized crime. Moldea also contends that, as of 1989, "no fewer than 70 NFL games have been fixed." Moldea's claim was bolstered by bookmaker Don Dawson admitting to participating in the fixing of no fewer than 32 games. Dawson told Moldea that he rigged the final scores by working with the quarterback. Moldea says that his book names players who were involved in fixing games, and that it identifies eight specific 1979 games that were fixed by two referees who were later investigated by the FBI and the IRS. So how did none of this ever come to light at the time it was happening? "No fewer than 50 legitimate investigations of corruption within the NFL have been either suppressed or just flat-out killed as a result of a sweetheart relationship between NFL Security, which is the internal police force within the league, and a variety of federal and state and local law-enforcement agencies," Moldea contends. Sajak somewhat jokingly asks Moldea if he fears for his safety, given that the book delves into issues of organized crime. "No one's tried to kill me in almost six years," Moldea says. Thirty-seven years later, Moldea's book resonates. Especially with legalized gambling in most states and prediction market-style gambling in all states. I've found and ordered a copy of the book. And Moldea apparently has yet to be whacked; we may have to track him down for more details.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders designate CB Trey Amos, DE Deatrich Wise, RB Jeremy McNichols for return
summary: The Commanders have started the process of bringing a few players back from their injury lists.
full_text: The Commanders have started the process of bringing a few players back from their injury lists. They announced that they have designated cornerback Trey Amos, defensive end Deatrich Wise, and running back Jeremy McNichols for return. Amos and McNichols are on injured reserve while Wise is on the physically unable to perform list. All three players will be able to return to practice Wednesday and they will have 21 days to work with the team before they have to be activated or shut down for the year. They can be activated at any point within that window, so some or all of the trio could be back to help the Commanders against the Giants in Week 5.
author: Josh Alper

title: Buccaneers K Chase McLaughlin set to play Thursday after landing on injury report
summary: Buccaneers kicker Chase McLaughlin was added to the injury report on Tuesday, but the team won't be adding a different kicker to handle the role against the Cowboys on Thursday night.
full_text: '' Buccaneers kicker Chase McLaughlin was added to the injury report on Tuesday, but the team won't be adding a different kicker to handle the role against the Cowboys on Thursday night. Head coach Todd Bowles said on Wednesday that McLaughlin will play in Dallas. McLaughlin was added to the report as a non-participant due to right hip and groin injuries. McLaughlin is 9-of-9 on field goals and 7-of-7 on extra points so far this season. Bowles also said that rookie linebacker Rueben Bain is expected to return after missing two games with groin and shoulder injuries. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), safety Antoine Winfield (rib), cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad), and linebacker SirVocea Dennis (ankle, foot) have all been ruled out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Reichard named NFC special teams player of the week
summary: The Vikings may not have reached the end zone in Sunday’s 15-10 victory over the Dolphins, but they did have an accurate kicker.
full_text: '' The Vikings may not have reached the end zone in Sunday’s 15-10 victory over the Dolphins, but they did have an accurate kicker. That’s why Will Reichard has been named NFC special teams player of the week. Reichard hit on all five of his field goal attempts from 47, 50, 33, 41, and 29 yards to score all 15 of Minnesota’s points. This is Reichard’s first career player of the week award. He’s the third Vikings player to earn the honor this season following Isaiah Rodgers in Week 2 and Myles Price in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Chiefs P Matt Araiza named the AFC special teams player of the week
summary: Chiefs punter Matt Araiza used his feet to help the team in multiple ways in Week 4.
full_text: ' Chiefs punter Matt Araiza used his feet to help the team in multiple ways in Week 4. Araiza had five punts against the Raiders and all of them landed inside of the Las Vegas 20-yard-line with one pinning the Raiders inside the 5-yard-line. Araiza also converted a fake punt with a 12-yard run in the first quarter of the 30-27 win. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Araiza has been named the AFC special teams player of the week. It's the first time that Araiza has earned that honor. Araiza averaged 47.6 yards per punt last Sunday and is averaging 52.3 yards per kick for the entire season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deonte Banks named NFC defensive player of the week
summary: Giants cornerback Deonte Banks put an exclamation point on the Giants’ victory over the Cardinals with a 98-yard pick-six as time expired.
full_text: ' Giants cornerback Deonte Banks put an exclamation point on the Giants’ victory over the Cardinals with a 98-yard pick-six as time expired. He’s now been named NFC defensive player of the week. Banks had four total tackles with four passes defended and his interception returned for a touchdown. Banks is the first Giants cornerback to be named defensive player of the week since 2019. The Giants will be on the road to face the Commanders in Week 5.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jaguars LB Foye Oluokun is the AFC defensive player of the week
summary: The Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season against the Bengals last Sunday and linebacker Foye Oluokun was integral to their success.
full_text: The Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season against the Bengals last Sunday and linebacker Foye Oluokun was integral to their success. Oluokun had seven tackles, an interception, a forced fumble and a quarterback hit to help the Jags to a 22-17 win. The interception came at Jacksonville's 10-yard-line early in the fourth quarter and kept the Jaguars up 16-10 heading into the final minutes of the contest. On Wednesday, the NFL announced that Oluokun has been named the AFC defensive player of the week. It is the fourth time Oluokun has been awarded conference player of the week honors. The first two came while he was with the Falcons and the last two have come since he moved on to the Jaguars.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tetairoa McMillan wins first NFC offensive player of the week award
summary: Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was dominant in Sunday's victory over the Lions and now the league has recognized him for his performance.
full_text: Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was dominant in Sunday's victory over the Lions and now the league has recognized him for his performance. McMillan has been named NFC offensive player of the week. McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards with two touchdowns in the 32-26 victory, setting career highs in both catches and yards. McMillan is the first receiver in Panthers franchise history to win NFC offensive player of the week. He tied the Panthers franchise record for receptions in a single game on Sunday. McMillan will get a chance to rest after so many catches, as he and the Panthers have a Week 5 bye.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Drake Maye named the AFC offensive player of the week
summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's first three games raised a lot of red flags around New England, but they are harder to find after last Sunday's win over the Bills.
full_text: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's first three games raised a lot of red flags around New England, but they are harder to find after last Sunday's win over the Bills. Maye went 22-of-37 for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including one that wide receiver Efton Chism used one hand to secure for the winning points in a 29-26 victory. Maye also ran eight times for 54 yards. The NFL announced on Wednesday that the performance landed Maye recognition as the AFC offensive player of the week. It is the second time that Maye has won the award. Maye did have a pair of turnovers in the game after having seven in the first three games, so there's still some work to do to get back to his 2025 level of play. The overall effort provided reason to believe that can happen and that was the best development of the week for the Patriots.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles to sign RB Dameon Pierce to 53-man roster
summary: The Eagles are making a move to bolster their ailing running back group.
full_text: The Eagles are making a move to bolster their ailing running back group. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that they will sign Dameon Pierce to the active roster from the practice squad. Pierce signed with the Eagles in March and returned to the practice squad after being released at the end of the summer. He had four carries for 10 yards in one game for the Chiefs and 10 carries for 26 yards in four games for the Texans last year. He also spent the previous three seasons with the Texans and had 415 carries for 1,674 yards and eight touchdowns over his entire run in Houston. Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby both left last Sunday's loss to the Rams with injuries. Barkley hurt his hamstring and is questionable for the near future while Bigsby suffered a core muscle injury that requires surgery.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants signing QB Jake Haener to 53-man roster
summary: The Giants will have three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.
full_text: ' The Giants will have three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, New York is signing Jake Haener back to the active roster from the team's practice squad. Haener had previously been promoted to the 53-man roster after Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury. But Haener was waived and re-signed to the practice squad after the club traded for J.J. McCarthy. With three QBs on the active roster, the Giants will be able to designate either McCarthy or Haener as the emergency third quarterback. At 3-1, the Giants will be on the road to face the Commanders in Week 5.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Odell Beckham Jr. joins Vikings practice squad
summary: Beckham is reuniting with HC Kevin O'Connell, who was his OC with the Rams in 2021.
full_text: '' Odell Beckham Jr. is headed for another reunion. Beckham is signing with the Vikings practice squad, Minnesota announced on Wednesday. Minnesota head coach Kevin O'Connell was the Rams' offensive coordinator when Beckham won Super Bowl LVI with Los Angeles to cap the 2021 season. Beckham caught 27 passes for 305 yards with five touchdowns in eight regular-season games for the Rams that year. He then had 21 receptions for 288 yards with two TDs in the postseason before tearing his ACL in the Super Bowl. While Beckham appeared in three games for the Giants this season, he did not catch a pass. The Vikings have also signed receiver Jeshaun Jones to their practice squad. Center Michael Jurgens and tight end Ben Yurosek have also returned to practice from injured reserve.
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFL rescinds Kyle Juszczyk's beer chugging celebration fine
summary: Juszczyk appealed the fine and said his celebration was tied to his "Juice" nickname.
full_text: ' 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk was one of the players fined by the NFL for mimicking drinking a beer during celebrations earlier this season, but he won't have to pay it. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Juszczyk's fine has been rescinded after an appeal. Juszczyk argued that he has done the celebration throughout his career without receiving any discipline for the act and that it references his nickname "Juice" rather than the alcoholic beverage. It appears that point was central to the decision to overturn the fine as the league said they came to the decision “because his celebration was simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer." Schefter also notes that Juszczyk pointed out the "hypocritical" nature of the league fining a player for drinking a beer while also receiving sponsorships from beer companies. Colts guard Matt Goncalves was fined for the same reason, but there's been no word of any change to his punishment.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL Referees Association objects to "severity" of suspensions of Adrian Hill, Jeff Seeman
summary: NFLRA contends the punishments exceed past disciplinary practices.
full_text: ' The NFL Referees Association believes the league is being over-officious when it comes to the discipline imposed on a pair of officials. Referee Adrian Hill (pictured) was suspended one game for his interaction with Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson. Line judge Jeff Seeman was suspended two games for the comments he made to Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the union representing the NFL's game officials said this: "The NFL Referees Association believes the suspensions imposed by the NFL on two officials following incidents this past weekend were excessive and inconsistent with past precedent. Given these concerns, the NFLRA will challenge the severity of those suspensions and meet with the NFL Officiating Department to discuss the League's disciplinary standards. The association also plans to meet with NFL Players Association leadership to address on-field conduct and the growing levels of confrontation between players and officials." The statement also included a quote from NFLRA executive director Scott Green. “NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," Green said. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent. “Officials are routinely subjected to highly charged interactions and, at times, verbal abuse from players and coaches. While that never excuses misconduct by an official, it shouldn't be dismissed as simply part of the game. The League expects the highest level of professionalism from its officials, and it should demand the same from everyone on the field. “We will defend the principle that discipline must be fair, consistent and proportionate. Holding officials accountable while ignoring or minimizing the conduct directed at them is neither fair nor an effective way to address this issue. We look forward to working with the League and NFLPA toward that shared goal.” Ultimately, it's a labor-management issue. The league has created a workplace precedent over the years when it comes to discipline. The NFLRA will argue that the punishment exceeds the established pattern and practice. And the arbitration procedures in the collective bargaining agreement between the NFL and the NFLRA will drive the final analysis.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers sign CB Terrell Smith off of Commanders practice squad
summary: The Steelers made an addition to their 53-man roster on Tuesday.
full_text: The Steelers made an addition to their 53-man roster on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed cornerback Terrell Smith off of the Commanders' practice squad. They had an open roster spot after making other moves on Monday, so there was no need to make a corresponding drop from the active roster. Smith was a Bears fifth-round pick in 2023 and he played in 26 games over his first two seasons. He tore his patellar tendon last year and was signed by Washington after being cut in Chicago this summer. Smith has 68 tackles, an interception, 10 passes defensed, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery while with the Bears. The Steelers also announced that they have signed defensive lineman K.J. Henry to the practice squad. Linebacker Bradyn Swinson was released to open a spot for him.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles DC Vic Fangio: Number of snaps impacted defense against Rams, but have to finish
summary: The Eagles had a 20-10 lead over the Rams deep into the fourth quarter of last Sunday's game against the Rams, but they wound up losing when the Rams scored back-to-back touchdowns in the final four minutes of the game.
full_text: The Eagles had a 20-10 lead over the Rams deep into the fourth quarter of last Sunday's game against the Rams, but they wound up losing when the Rams scored back-to-back touchdowns in the final four minutes of the game. The first Rams scoring drive started at their own 2-yard-line and the second covered 79 yards. Los Angeles only faced two third downs on the 21 snaps that made up those possessions, which led to a question for Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio about whether the cumulative effect of being on the field for 82 snaps — including penalties, but excluding one kneeldown at the end of the game — wore the unit down. "Well, I'm not going to insult your or anybody's intelligence that yeah, it has an effect, but we got to find a way to finish," Fangio said, via a transcript from the team. The Eagles couldn't finish on either side of the ball against the Rams. If the offense continues to fail to do so in the future, the job Fangio and the defense will have to do for the team to win games will only get more difficult.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders worked out QB Jack Plummer
summary: The Commanders are keeping an eye on the quarterback market.
full_text: The Commanders are keeping an eye on the quarterback market. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Washington worked out free-agent quarterback Jack Plummer on Wednesday morning. Garafolo reports Plummer threw well, but the Commanders do not plan to sign him at this time. He could be a consideration down the road, as the team currently doesn't plan to place Marcus Mariota on injured reserve. Plummer, 26, was most recently with the UFL’s Orlando Storm, where he earned the league’s MVP award. Plummer previously spent time with the Panthers. He has worked out for the Jets, 49ers, and Dolphins since the end of the most recent UFL season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steelers-Browns racks up 16.59 million viewers on Prime Video
summary: More than a few people saw Thursday night's F-bomb interaction between Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy.
full_text: More than a few people saw Thursday night's F-bomb interaction between Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy. The Week 4 Thursday night game on Prime Video averaged 16.59 million viewers. It's a 19-percent increase over last year's Week 4 Thursday night meeting between the Seahawks and Cardinals. That game averaged 13.94 million viewers. The number, per Amazon, made it the most-watched Week 4 Thursday night game since Prime Video assumed the package in 2022. An unresolved question lingers as to whether Amazon is goosing the numbers by autoplaying the game for anyone who visits their Prime page while the game is being televised. The higher numbers are obviously good for Amazon, and in turn good for the NFL. Either way, Thursday Night Football is here to stay. The only question is whether and when it will be joined by a Tuesday night and/or Wednesday night effort on a weekly basis.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Campbell: We won't accept mediocrity on either side of the ball
summary: The Saints knocked the Lions out of the top spot for points allowed on Monday night, but being anywhere near the top of that list is not where teams want to be four weeks into the season.
full_text: ' The Saints knocked the Lions out of the top spot for points allowed on Monday night, but being anywhere near the top of that list is not where teams want to be four weeks into the season. Detroit has allowed at least 24 points and 355 yards in each of their four games, which led to head coach Dan Campbell's vote of confidence for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard after Sunday night's loss to the Panthers. During an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Campbell pointed to a lack of discipline and a lack of trust among players on the unit as reasons why the defense has been so easily torn apart. He added that others will get opportunities as the team looks for the right mix to improve their results. "We’re going to give some other guys an opportunity , and go, man. But we’re not going to accept mediocrity. That’s not what we’re doing here," Campbell said. "We've got too many guys playing at a high level, and we’re going to raise the floor on this team." The Lions offense ranks fifth in the league in points scored, but some have wondered if the defense's inability to get stops has an adverse effect on the offense. Campbell was asked about that, but said he thinks the team has been "average" across the board and that the offense has room to improve alongside the defense. "Man, if you want to be great, they should want to score 35 points a game, at a minimum," Campbell said. "That’s what greatness is. That’s what they’re charged with. We've got plenty of weapons on offense and if we’re gonna accept mediocrity, then yeah, we can make all the excuses in the world. If we want to spit and sputter and be average, that’s one thing. We’re not going to be average. We’re going to raise the floor on these guys, man. We’re going to push ‘em. We've got too much offensively right now. Our quarterback’s too good, our playmakers are too good, and we've got a young, hungry offensive line that’s got a ton of room to grow." Campbell was adamant this summer that the Lions' Super Bowl window is not closed , but the first four weeks haven't done much to support the feeling that big things are in store for the team this season. That will need to change quickly if they want to avoid calls for more sweeping changes to how business is getting done in Detroit.
author: Josh Alper

title: North Carolina hires search firm to help find new G.M. to work with Bill Belichick
summary: North Carolina's ongoing support, fulsome or not, of coach Bill Belichick comes with expectations.
full_text: North Carolina's ongoing support, fulsome or not, of coach Bill Belichick comes with expectations . One of these expectations will be that he won't hire aa crony or a family member to be the next G.M. of the program. In the aftermath of G.M. Mike Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick resigning amid an investigation regarding various still-unspecified irregularities within the program, UNC is looking for a new General Manager. And the program isn't letting Belichick simply bring in someone with whom he is already comfortable. Via Brian Murphy of WRAL, North Carolina has hired Sean Magee of Turnkey ZRG to assist with the search for Lombardi's replacement. Magee previously was the G.M. at Michigan, and he has a degree from Navy. Which could make Belichick inclined to cooperate with Magee, given Belichick's affinity for the Naval Academy. (His dad was a longtime scout there, and it was a moth-eaten Navy sweatshirt that Belichick was wearing in the 2025 CBS softball interview that was treated by Belichick and his handler as chin music.) “I am really looking forward to working with Sean, given his many years of high-level executive leadership experience in both professional and collegiate football,” Belichick said in a statement. In light of Belichick's tenuous status in Chapel Hill, the job may not be a desirable one. Unless the program hires someone who regards it as an opportunity to help shape the direction of the program without Belichick in 2027. Either way, the clock is ticking. Recruiting never ends, and the Tar Heels have gone more than two months without a G.M. on the job, due to Lombardi being placed on paid leave before he abruptly decided to walk away from the job. Even if Belichick isn't fired, he could decide after the dust settles on the 2026 season that he, too, has had enough. The investigation, which at one point seemed to be looking for anything it could find to justify firing the head coach without pay, may have prompted Belichick to react to the probe that took out both his consigliere and his son by treating the current season as his last ride with the Tar Heels.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles RT Lane Johnson announces retirement
summary: He played 171 games in 14 seasons with the Eagles, who made him a first-round pick in 2013.
full_text: Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson was unexpectedly scratched from the lineup on Sunday, with the team citing "personal reasons." On Tuesday, he announced his retirement. "I have given it my all for 14 years, season after season pushing my body to the max and tirelessly working my craft to not only live up to the legacy of the guys that came before me, but to set a new standard of success for the best franchise in all of sports," Johnson wrote, in part, in a statement on social media. "I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year, to take the field with my brothers for one last season. But after a lot of reflection, I've realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed. Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game. And right now, my heart is telling me that it's time to say goodbye to football. "At this time, I have made the incredibly difficult decision to retire from the National Football League." Johnson missed time at the start of training camp and said his mother had been dealing with some health issues when he returned to the team. The Eagles lost on Sunday, dropping their record to 18-30 without Johnson and 122-63-1 with him since drafting him in the first round in 2013. Johnson, 36, is a six-time Pro Bowler and was first-team All-Pro twice. He started 171 career regular-season games and 15 in the postseason, and Johnson won two Super Bowl rings. He missed seven games last season with a Lisfranc foot injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts sign DE Carl Lawson to their practice squad
summary: The Colts have added a veteran defensive end ahead of Week 5.
full_text: The Colts have added a veteran defensive end ahead of Week 5. The team announced that they have signed Carl Lawson to their practice squad. Tight end Kenny Fletcher was released in a corresponding move. Lawson played in one game for the Ravens last season and he's played in 90 games since the Bengals made him a fourth-round pick in 2017. He spent four seasons in Cincinnati and played for current Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo in his last two years with the team. Lawson moved on to the Jets and spent three seasons with them — he missed all of the 2021 season with a torn Achilles — and played for the Cowboys in 2024. He has 135 tackles, 32 sacks, four forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over his entire career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills DC Jim Leonhard: We have to make home crowd an advantage for us
summary: Home field advantage is something that is talked about often in the NFL, but Bills cornerback Dee Alford didn't feel much of one during last Sunday's loss to the Patriots.
full_text: Home field advantage is something that is talked about often in the NFL, but Bills cornerback Dee Alford didn't feel much of one during last Sunday's loss to the Patriots. Alford said, via Nick Suss of ESPN.com, that the crowd at Highmark Stadium can get " super loud to the point where we're not able to get the play as fast as we need it" and that leaves the defense scrambling because of communication breakdowns. During a press conference this week, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was asked about Alford's comments. Leonhard acknowledged the difficulties that can arise in a loud environment, but said that the opposing team faces more of them and that the Bills have to view the home crowd into a plus rather than an obstacle. "It's always harder to communicate at home than it is on the road. If we complain about that, we are a———s," Leonhard said. "We have to turn that into the biggest advantage we have. As hard as it is for us, it's significantly harder for an offense. We have to find a way to make that an advantage for us. If we ever use that as a cop out — I have to be smart in how we game plan. There’s certain things you can do on the road that are a little bit easier than they are at home from a communication standpoint." The Bills won two of their first three games in their new stadium and they won't be back there until November 1, so it will be a while before they get to test out any new strategies for dealing with the volume from the stands.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles trade Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens for two draft selections
summary: Baltimore is reportedly sending Philadelphia a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder for Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens lost their top three options at center due to injury this season, so they were forced to peruse the trade market to find a new starter. The Ravens found a trade partner in the Philadelphia Eagles , who sent two-time Pro Bowler Cam Jurgens plus a 2027 seventh-round pick to Baltimore in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
Jurgens has made the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons. The Eagles drafted him with the No. 51 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Nebraska, and he replaced Jason Kelce once the longtime center retired following the 2023 season. However, Jurgens has played at multiple spots on the interior of the offensive line over his five NFL seasons. He spent the majority of his time in 2023 at right guard, played a combined 1,867 snaps at center from 2024-25, then shifted to left guard this season while Drew Kendall took over at center. Jurgens has struggled at guard this year, but should return to his natural position of center in Baltimore.
The Ravens had Danny Pinter suffer a torn patellar tendon in training camp, which ended his season before it began, then saw Jovaughn Gwyn suffer an ankle injury and Ethan Pocic a knee injury in the Week 3 victory against the Dallas Cowboys . That forced first-round pick Vega Ioane to move from right guard to center, while Andrew Vorhees came off the bench to start at right guard in Week 4. Now, the Ravens have not only found an answer at center for this year, but likely for years to come. Jurgens signed a four-year, $68 million extension just last offseason.
For the Eagles, this trade marks the second solidified starter that Philly has lost in the last 24 hours. Six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson announced his immediate retirement from the NFL on Tuesday afternoon, saying that it is "critical" that he focuses on his mental health at this moment. The Eagles now prepare to travel across the pond to face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday with a very different-looking offensive line.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade packages: What Cardinals could get for former No. 4 overall pick
summary: These deals could move Harrison out of Arizona and help revitalize his career
full_text:
An elusive breakout season still has not materialized for Marvin Harrison Jr. , and as the disappointing start to his career continues, the chances of the Arizona Cardinals moving on from him are at an all-time high. Teams have begun due diligence on a potential trade and reached out to the Cardinals to gauge his ability, a ccording to ESPN .  While Arizona is reportedly "not all that enthralled with trading him," the wide receiver position is a seller's market with so many teams desperate for help, and the Cardinals could hear an offer they cannot decline.
What might that trade package look like? ESPN reports that Harrison's value slipped over the last three years from that of an early first-round pick to a "quality Day 3 pick." That is the assessment of at least one team placed on the former No. 4 overall selection.
The Cardinals hold all the leverage and could decline any offers that do not exceed that valuation. Harrison is a young asset under contract through 2027, and the Cardinals hold a club option for 2028. Plus, injuries across the league could spark a modest bidding war for a starting-caliber wide receiver.
Harrison appears in need of a change of scenery. The Ohio State product opened his career with an immensely promising 885-yard, eight-touchdown rookie season, but regressed over the last season and change. He has only five catches through the first four games of 2026 and is on pace for a career low in yardage. Harrison's effort has come into question, too, as he occasionally looks out of place in first-year coach Mike LaFleur's offense.
A fresh start in a new system might be in Harrison's best interest. His potential is still as high as nearly any young wide receiver in the NFL . As he slips behind tight end Trey McBride and fellow receiver Michael Wilson in the pecking order for targets in Arizona, though, his present situation is far from conducive to turning him into the star evaluators expected him to become when the Cardinals invested valuable Day 1 draft capital in him in 2024.
As teams kick the tires on a trade for Harrison, here are three potential deals that would make sense for all parties involved.
This is the home-run scenario for the Cardinals. Given the Day 3 evaluation on Harrison, finding a team that would be willing to give up a Day 2 pick one-for-one is about as much as Arizona could ask for. The Houston Texans' desperation to improve an offense that continues to underwhelm and to climb out of an 0-4 hole to start the year makes them a prime candidate to spend up for a wide receiver.
Houston is a perfect landing spot for Harrison, and the Texans ought to feel as though they have as strong a chance to unlock his potential as anyone. They possess the quarterback in C.J. Stroud , who turned Harrison into an All-American at Ohio State. In 2022, Stroud connected with Harrison 77 times for 1,263 yards and an FBS-best 14 touchdowns. As Stroud and Harrison both face career crossroads, pairing them back up could help both salvage the less-than-stellar opening stages of their professional careers.
What's more, the Texans have a need at wide receiver now and into next season. They lack a bona fide No. 2 option behind Nico Collins and instead spread targets out evenly across multiple role players. Houston just opened Tank Dell's practice window, but as someone who has not played since 2024, it is reasonable to wonder how much he has to offer upon his return from a devastating knee injury. He, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte will all hit unrestricted free agency at the end of the season, whereas Harrison remains under club control for at least one more year, if not two.
At 3-1 on the year, the Las Vegas Raiders are surprise AFC West contenders who might be buyers at the trade deadline -- with the caveat that they likely still want to remain fairly young and build around a budding core. Harrison fits this plan. He aligns with the roster's trajectory as a 24-year-old with upside and an already established base as a No. 1 receiver. Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins could help him settle into Klint Kubiak's offense this year before he eventually settles in as a long-term pairing with this year's top overall pick, Fernando Mendoza .
The Raiders lack that go-to weapon on the outside that Mendoza will need in order to flourish once he takes over the offense. Brock Bowers is the top pass-catcher on the offense, but is a tight end. There is no wide receiver on the roster that projects as an obvious primary target; Las Vegas presently relies on Trey Trucker and Jalen Nailor while the duo of Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton resides on injured reserve.
What makes buying at the deadline tricky for the Raiders is that they do not possess a sixth- or seventh-round pick in the 2027 draft. As a team that is still in the midst of a rebuild despite its early-season success, it may be opposed to coming out of this deal with only four remaining picks. Plus, the Raiders undoubtedly want to continue to stack young talent, so in order to part with Day 2 draft capital, they may seek a late-round throw-in alongside Harrison to get the deal over the finish line.
ESPN may have dropped a hint that the Indianapolis Colts are among the teams that have called about a Harrison trade. When asked if the Colts were interested, he responded, "Wouldn't that make a lot of sense?" It certainly would have addressed their needs at wide receiver and Harrison's familial ties to the franchise.
Marvin Harrison Sr. spent the entirety of his Hall of Fame career with the Colts. If the younger Harrison were to join the team with which his father starred, the pressure to live up to his father's legacy could go one of two ways. It might either suffocate him or deliver the motivational spark he needs to get his career back on track.
Alec Pierce is on injured reserve with a heel injury and may never be at full strength this year following his offseason surgery, and depth is a major concern behind him -- to the point where the Colts signed Keenan Allen ahead of the campaign and still need help. Indianapolis does not have a first-round pick in 2027 and thus would seem likely to protect its remaining early-round capital. Plus, general manager Chris Ballard is already under scrutiny for overpaying on Sauce Gardner in last year's trade deadline blockbuster. With those factors in mind, the Colts may be less likely to spend up for Harrison and instead pay only the reported market rate for a fourth- or fifth-round pick.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Former NFL rushing TD leader eyes comeback, works out for Patriots
summary: The 2022 NFL rushing touchdowns leader hasn't played in over a year after spending two seasons in New Orleans following his breakout campaign in Detroit
full_text:
A former NFL running back is attempting a comeback, as Jamaal Williams worked out for the New England Patriots this week. Williams has been out of the NFL for over a year now, and last played for the New Orleans Saints --rushing for 470 yards and two touchdowns over two seasons.
Williams led the NFL in rushing touchdowns back in 2022 with the Detroit Lions , a season in which he rushed for 1,066 yards and a whopping 17 touchdowns. He served as Jared Goff's lead back as Detroit registered its first winning season in five years, while Williams established himself as a formidable power back who dominated in short-yardage situations. His performance landed Williams a new three-year contract from the Saints in free agency, while the Lions replaced his production with Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery .
The Patriots' running back room currently consists of Rhamondre Stevenson , TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner . Stevenson and Henderson have supported what is currently a top 10 rushing offense, having combined for 304 rushing yards and two touchdowns through the first four games of the season. But there may be a reason why Mike Vrabel is looking to add another running back to his roster.
On New England's final drive of its eventual 29-26 upset victory over the rival Buffalo Bills on Sunday, Rhamondre Stevenson appeared to suffer some kind of lower-body injury during his last touch of the game. Stevenson was folded awkwardly while being hit by three defenders, and limped off the field while speaking with trainers. He did not take another snap.
Stevenson wasn't seen sporting a boot or on crutches after the game, but it was notable that he did not re-enter the contest as the Patriots looked to chew clock late in the fourth quarter. We will gain more insight into Stevenson's injury -- if he has one -- when the Patriots' mid-week injury report is released Wednesday afternoon.
Stevenson is the Patriots' leading rusher this season with 163 yards and one touchdown on 44 carries. The fact that the Patriots are working out Williams does not guarantee that Stevenson suffered some kind of injury that will force him to miss time. New England could simply be looking to add to its room and bring in a veteran on the practice squad. With that said, let's take a look at Williams' NFL career.
The BYU product was selected by the Green Bay Packers in the fourth round of the 2017 NFL Draft . He was actually the first of THREE running backs the Packers selected that year, followed by Aaron Jones in the fifth round and Devante Mays in the seventh. Ty Montgomery was the Packers' leading rusher the previous year with 457 yards, so Green Bay clearly wanted to address the room.
Williams came in and led the Packers in rushing as a rookie, recording 556 yards and four touchdowns the season Aaron Rodgers missed nine games with a broken collarbone. That was the only year Williams led the Packers in rushing, as Jones eventually took over as the starting back in 2018. However, Williams was the solidified No. 2 who recorded 1,985 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns over 60 career games with the Packers.
Following the 2020 season, Williams signed a two-year deal with the Lions to run the ball for a brand new head coach by the name of Dan Campbell. In his first season with Detroit, Williams rushed for what was then a career-high 601 yards and three touchdowns. D'Andre Swift led the team with 617 rushing yards and five touchdowns as the Lions went 3-13-1.
The following year was when the Lions as an organization made their jump. They went from 3-13-1 to 9-8 and from the 22nd-best offense in the NFL to the fourth-best. Williams was their lead back and registered his first 1,000-yard rushing season with 1,066 yards and a league-leading 17 touchdowns. Those 17 rushing touchdowns were four more than Derrick Henry , Austin Ekeler and Jalen Hurts scored that year.
Williams' 2022 campaign landed him a three-year, $12 million deal with the Saints to come in and run the ball with Alvin Kamara . However, he registered what was then a career-low 306 yards rushing and one touchdown while missing four games with a hamstring injury. Williams' lone touchdown that year came on the Saints' final play of a 48-17 blowout of the Atlanta Falcons in the final game of the season. Quarterback Jameis Winston revealed afterward that the team went rogue after Saints head coach Dennis Allen called for a kneel-down. Winston instead handed the ball off to Williams to get him into the end zone one time that season.
"It was a team decision," Winston said, via Pro Football Talk . "We know how much Jamaal means to this team. And I understood from D.A.'s perspective, D.A. didn't condone that at all, but we decided as a team to do it."
Falcons head coach Arthur Smith was very upset with Allen for running up the score. It ended up being Smith's final game as the lead man in Atlanta.
Arthur Smith was HOT after Dennis Allen scored a late touchdown. Cussing up a dang storm! pic.twitter.com/mgPX318fyq
The following season, Williams rushed for 164 yards and one touchdown, making it eight straight seasons in which he found the end zone. Last March, the Saints released him.
Williams reportedly worked out for the Chicago Bears ahead of the 2025 season, but ultimately went unsigned last year. He isn't ready to close the book on his playing career just yet, though. During a recent interview with Jordan Schultz , Williams encouraged all players who were still looking for an opportunity to keep the faith.
"If you know you can still play, please, keep playing," Williams said. "Play until you know that you can't play anymore. Because that love for football is just a different breed, man. If you can play, please play, and play with the gratefulness of your body allows you to play that game for, because this game is not forever. Play with respect, love the game, love yourself and just don't give up on yourself if you know you can make it..."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Vikings sign Odell Beckham Jr. following release from Giants
summary: Beckham Jr. is officially joining Minnesota's practice squad
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are adding some depth to their wide receiver corps by signing Odell Beckham Jr. , the team announced . Specifically, the veteran pass catcher will join Minnesota's practice squad.
Beckham wasn't on the open market long following his Sept. 29 release from the New York Giants . That concluded a brief second stint with New York after initially signing with the club on June 1 and making the opening 53-man roster. Despite making the team, Beckham wasn't utilized at all in the Giants' passing game, logging zero catches and zero targets over three games played.
Judging by his social media activity following his release, Beckham was less than thrilled about his return to the Giants being cut short. Head coach John Harbaugh said following Beckham's release that it just "wasn't working for us."
Now, Beckham gets a fresh start in Minnesota, where he does have some familiarity with the coaching staff, specifically head coach Kevin O'Connell. O'Connell was the offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams when Beckham was acquired by the franchise during the 2021 season.
In eight regular-season games played that year under O'Connell, Beckham caught 27 balls for 305 yards and five touchdowns. During the club's run to a Super Bowl LVI title, Beckham took it to another level, catching 21 passes for 288 yards and two touchdowns. He seems primed to win Super Bowl MVP honors as he made an early impact in that title win over the Cincinnati Bengals , but tore his ACL in the midst of the contest.
While Beckham, 33, isn't the same player he was back then, he does give Minnesota some much-needed depth at receiver. Top wideout Justin Jefferson has been dealing with an ankle injury, which forced him to miss the Week 5 win over Miami. After Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings headline the wide receiver depth chart on the active roster.
Beckham entered the NFL as the No. 12 overall pick of the Giants during the 2014 NFL Draft out of LSU. Over the course of his career, he's made two second-team All-Pro teams (2015 and 2016) and has 575 career regular-season catches to go along with 7,987 receiving yards and 59 touchdown receptions.

title: NFL reverses Kyle Juszczyk fine over 49ers touchdown celebration
summary: Juszczyk was fined $14,926 for an "offensive demonstration" after scoring against the Dolphins, but the NFL has now reversed its decision
full_text:
The NFL rescinded its $14,926 fine of San Francisco 49ers tight end Kyle Juszczyk for "engaging in offensive demonstration" after scoring a touchdown during the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins .
The league initially thought that Juszczyk imitated a beer chug during his touchdown celebration, which is apparently a no-no. Juszczyk said after the game that his celebration was an ode to his nickname, Juice.
"Yeah I've seen Juice do his celebration for like five years," 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy said at the time . "So, I'm a little confused with the punishment he's dealing with."
The fine occurred after Juszczyk caught a touchdown pass that extended San Francisco's lead to 28-6 late in the third quarter.
Kyle Juszczyk extends the @49ers ' lead MIAvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dpt6NfGpWy
Brock Purdy's TD pass to Kyle Juszczyk looked familiar 👀 @49ers @insidetheNFL Week 2 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/CN1xjLK5lw
The NFL has also shaved about $4,000 off of Juszczyk's previous fine for "impermissible use of the helmet" that occurred during the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams.
#49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk was fined $20,033 for use of the helmet on this lead block. pic.twitter.com/lY2Yh5x4Tx
While rare, the NFL has rescinded fines before. In January of 2025, then-Texans running back Joe Mixon had his fine rescinded after he was initially docked $25,000 for comments he made following Houston's playoff loss to the Chiefs . The league, upon further review, determined that Mixon's comments did not warrant a fine.
Juszczyk, 35, is in the middle of his 14th season with the 49ers, who took him in the fourth round of the 2013 NFL Draft . A 10-time Pro Bowler and two-time All-Pro, Juszczyk has been a key cog in helping the 49ers get off to a 4-0 start.

title: Predicting the full 14-team NFL playoff bracket heading into Week 5: Jaguars, Vikings both make surprise runs
summary: All 208 remaining regular-season games and 13 playoff games were simulated to determine the postseason field and crown a Super Bowl LXI champion
full_text:
Since the start of the season, we've been projecting the full NFL playoff field every week, and after four weeks of action, things are suddenly starting to get a little clearer around the NFL. For instance, we can probably all agree that the Chargers won't be in the playoffs.
With the NFL season nearly 25% complete, we're starting to get a sense of who the contenders are and who the pretenders are. To figure out who the true playoff contenders might be, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season.
There are 208 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated ALL of them. Not only did he project the 14 teams that will end up making the playoffs, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
Before the season started, Pete Prisco predicted that the Jaguars would win the Super Bowl and I'm not sure if he somehow hacked our projection, but right now, the Jags are looking like they're going to finish near the top of the AFC.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field: 1. Chiefs (4-0) -- AFC West champion 2. Jaguars (3-1) -- AFC South champion 3. Bills (3-1) -- AFC East champion 4. Ravens (3-1) -- AFC North champion 5. Colts (2-2) 6. Broncos (2-2) 7. Patriots (2-2)
The computer has the top six teams comfortably getting into the playoffs, but there was a big battle for the final wild-card spot in the AFC. In our projection, the Patriots ended up edging out the Bengals on a tiebreaker to earn the last spot. If that actually happens, Zac Taylor's job security will become a hot topic going into the offseason.
Now, let's talk about a few of the teams that didn't make the postseason in our projection. There are two surprise teams in the AFC: the Raiders (3-1) and Browns (3-1). Although they've both played well over three weeks, the computer doesn't project either team making the postseason. The biggest problem for the Raiders is that they have an absolutely brutal schedule coming up with four of their next five games coming against the Patriots, Bills, Rams and 49ers . As for the Browns, our projection has them getting to eight wins, which would be good for Cleveland, but not good enough to make the playoffs.
The Atlanta Falcons have officially arrived on the scene. After watching the Falcons win two straight games in blowout fashion, our computer has been so impressed that Atlanta is now projected to win the NFC South.
Here's the projected NFC playoff field: 1. Seahawks (3-1) -- NFC West champion 2. Vikings (4-0) -- NFC North champion 3. Eagles (2-2) -- NFC East champion 4. Falcons (2-2) -- NFC South champion 5. 49ers (4-0) 6. Rams (2-2) 7. Bears (3-1)
The Seahawks and Eagles are both projected to win their divisions, even though neither is currently in first place. The computer doesn't see the Giants being a factor in the NFC East, which will end up being a battle between the Cowboys and Eagles. In the NFC West, the Seahawks and 49ers are actually playing THIS WEEK and that game will likely have a major impact when it comes to who wins the division. The computer loves the NFC West and currently has three teams from that division making the playoffs.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Jaguars and Vikings), the team that won the Super Bowl last year (Seahawks), and the team that has won two of the past four Super Bowls (Chiefs).
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at what the projected Super Bowl has been each week.
Right now, the Seahawks are on top, but that could certainly change this week, especially with Seattle getting ready for a Week 5 showdown against the undefeated 49ers.

title: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon explains why she roams sidelines on game day, defends position
summary: The Colts owner explains why she roams the sideline with pen and paper during games as she holds Shane Steichen and Chris Ballard accountable in a pivotal season
full_text:
When Carlie Irsay-Gordon became the principal owner and CEO of the Indianapolis Colts in 2025, following the death of her father, Jim Irsay, she became quite visible. Irsay-Gordon famously roams the Colts' sidelines during games, pen and paper in hand, locked in on the action more than any fan.
She's been doing this for over a year now, but the attention around her game-day activities has not subsided. There was an instance during the Colts' Week 4 victory over the Washington Commanders in London where TV cameras captured Irsay-Gordon approaching a coach and asking questions about her notes -- clearly confused about or questioning some element of the game plan.
Irsay-Gordon explained she's simply trying to educate herself about the organization's football operations, revealed during a recent interview with Front Office Sports in London. Because that's what a good leader would do.
"I like to say on a good day I have like a fifth-grade reading level understanding of the game and just the basic concepts of what we're trying to do, depending on the week and depending on our opponent and depending on the situation," Irsay-Gordon said. "But I think, then, it just helps to understand and to ask questions because I think one of the things, in my opinion, like being a good leader is about listening, really to understand. And I think that's what the best teams do."
It's clear that Irsay-Gordon wants to be involved as much as possible. Colts safety Cam Bynum said last year that the team owner is in the building every single day, being a "normal person" -- humble enough to have "casual conversations" with people.
Her sideline presence is still a strange sight, given that most NFL owners are enjoying Sundays in their private suites. It's also fair to speculate that Irsay-Gordon's hyperfocus brings a different kind of pressure to the coaching staff. She's interested in Shane Steichen's process as much as she is the play-calls, and if something starts to go awry, she will notice.
"I need to learn more about this," Irsay-Gordon said about her game day process last year. "I need to be able to say, 'Is this person full of BS? Do they even know what they're talking about?' ... It's such a complex organism, a football team, and how it operates on game day."
The Colts are 2-2 entering Week 5, and Irsay-Gordon put Steichen as well as general manager Chris Ballard on notice in the offseason. She expects to win games and get to the playoffs, and she will be right there, pen in hand, whether Indianapolis succeeds or fails.
"We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher," Irsay-Gordon said following the 2025 season. "Chris and Shane are both capable of facing this challenge head-on and finding a way to achieve the results that our fans deserve, which is winning games, getting to the postseason and ultimately winning championships."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL MVP rankings: Kenneth Walker III overtakes Josh Allen for No. 1 after Week 4
summary: The Chiefs running back unseats Josh Allen atop this week's MVP rankings after another dominant performance, while Brock Purdy and Bijan Robinson continue to climb
full_text:
The NFL MVP race looks vastly different from the way it did a week ago. Aa new face is atop the leaderboard. The former front-runner took a major dip in the standings this week after his team suffered its first loss of the season. We also saw the inclusion of two new quarterbacks.
Prescott edged out Jared Goff for the final spot. While Goff and the Lions came up short in Carolina, Prescott led the Cowboys to a road win over the Texans . In the 34-30 win, Prescott threw for a season-high 335 yards and completed 71.1% of his passes.
Through four games, Prescott is completing 70% of his passes with eight touchdowns and just one interception.
While he doesn't have gaudy numbers, Lawrence has nonetheless helped lead the Jaguars to a 3-1 start. If the Jaguars keep winning, Lawrence's MVP buzz will gain more steam.
A week after throwing three touchdowns in a blowout win over the Patriots , Lawrence outplayed Joe Burrow (who fell out of the MVP standings) while leading Jacksonville to a road win in Cincinnati. In the win, Lawrence threw for 227 yards and a score and completed an impressive 78.3% of his passes.
Like any non-quarterback, Smith-Njigba has little margin for error if he wants to be the first receiver to win league MVP. That's the main reason why he fell five spots in this week's standings.
After producing like Jerry Rice in the season's first three games, Smith-Njigba somewhat came back down to earth in Week 4. He still put up a solid stat line against the Chargers with 76 yards on five catches.
Smith-Njigba fell from first to third in the NFL in receiving yards this week, but he is still leading the league in touchdown catches and remains on pace to break Calvin Johnson's single-season record.
Cousins fell a few spots after being on the short end of Sunday's loss to Kansas City. Cousins played well, but he ultimately missed an opportunity to gain major MVP momentum. The Raiders also came up just short of what would have been their biggest win in years.
The veteran quarterback lost some ground, but he is still very much in the MVP conversation. He's tied for the league lead in touchdown passes and has been a driving force behind the Raiders' surprising 3-1 start.
Lamb's Week 4 performance put him right into the thick of the MVP race. He caught a whopping 17 passes (on 21 targets!) for 189 yards and a score in Dallas' win over Houston. Lamb set a Cowboys single-game receptions record for a wide receiver -- tight end Jason Witten holds the all-time record with 18 catches -- while passing Hall of Famer Drew Pearson on the team's career receiving yardage list.
CEEDEE LAMB IS A CHEAT CODE FROM OUTERSPACE 17 CATCHES 189 REC YARDS TD pic.twitter.com/Enll9u0zjz
Lamb's historic performance made him the NFL's leader in receptions and receiving yards through four games. He's on pace to catch 153 passes for 2,117 yards, which would both be NFL records.
If Mahomes ends up winning his third MVP, his 55-yard completion to Tyquan Thornton in Sunday's win over the Raiders will be one of the reasons why. It was a clutch play in a clutch moment from a clutch player who is already one of the most decorated in league history.
Mahomes' success moving forward will at least partly depend on how the Chiefs deal with their rash of injuries at receiver. Thornton will be out at least three months after dislocating his ankle, and Rashee Rice is dealing with a tweaked hamstring. The Chiefs are looking into the possibility of re-signing Tyreek Hill , who enjoyed a prolific partnership with Mahomes from 2018-21.
Allen fell back after Sunday. After scoring nine touchdowns in Buffalo's first two games, Allen scored "just" four touchdowns in the Bills ' last two outings. He's tied for the league lead in touchdown runs (seven), but his six touchdown passes are tied for 13th in the league.
Stats aside, Buffalo's loss to New England is the biggest reason for Allen's slide. Allen had a solid game, but he essentially sealed the 29-26 loss when he threw a head-scratching interception with 1:14 left.
Fortunately for Allen, he and the Bills have another opportunity to win a marquee game this Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams .
Robinson's last two games have reinforced his status as one of the NFL's elite players. A week after running roughshod for 194 yards and two scores against the Packers , Robinson ran circles around the Saints ' defense to the tune of 145 yards and two more touchdowns. His 59-yard scoring jaunt less than two minutes into the game set the tone for Atlanta's 45-24 win.
Was a great night last night if your name was @Bijan5Robinson 😌 @insidethenfl Week 4 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/50xcj1pciF
Robinson and the Falcons will get another opportunity to shine this Sunday night against the Baltimore Ravens .
While he is often overshadowed by other quarterbacks, Purdy's play during the season's first four weeks has put himself in an early position to possibly become the fourth 49ers quarterback to win league MVP and the first to do so since 1994.
Purdy has played with surgeon-like precision. He's tied for the league lead in touchdown passes, has thrown just one interception, is completing nearly 70% of his throws and has the NFL's highest passer rating (126.2). Purdy's play has keyed San Francisco's 4-0 start.
BROCK PURDY TO MIKE EVANS EXTENDS THE LEAD @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ScREsrmsVw
Like Allen and Robinson, Purdy also has a big Week 5 matchup that will shape the MVP race. The 49ers will travel to Seattle to take on the defending NFC champions in a rematch of last year's NFC divisional round showdown.
Walker's performance against the Raiders earned him the No. 1 spot entering Week 5. His 177-yard day included two touchdowns in a span of 19 seconds. His 22-yard rumble proved to be the game-winning score.
KENNETH WALKER JUST SCORED A TOUCHDOWN ON BACK-TO-BACK SCRIMMAGE PLAYS! TWO TDs IN 22 SECONDS 🤯🤯🤯 (via @Chiefs ) pic.twitter.com/peoM1k0xxo
The reigning Super Bowl MVP, Walker, has infused life into the Chiefs. Walker leads the NFL in scrimmage yards, rushing yards and yards-per-carry average (6.2). He's on pace to smash Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record, which has stood for 42 years.
If he stays healthy, Walker has a good chance at becoming the fitst non-quarterback to win league MVP since Adrian Peterson did so back in 2012.

title: NFL Week 5 picks, odds: Jaguars bludgeon Eagles in London, Colts get exposed
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 5 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
The first month of the regular season gave us a last-minute elbow to the ribs right before we closed the book on it.
The Week 4 slate was a tough one, particularly when it came to betting against the spread. I managed just a 5-10-1 ATS record for the weekend. Gross. That said, we managed it pretty well everywhere else. I went 10-6 straight up and 2-2-1 ATS with my five locks of the week. Within those locks, we were part of the unlucky bunch who were spurned by one of the worst beats of the young season.
If you missed it, we had the Vikings covering an 11.5-point spread against the Dolphins . With two minutes to play in regulation and Minnesota at the Miami 11-yard line with a 15-10 lead, Kyler Murray hit tight end T.J. Hockenson for what should've been a wide-open touchdown. That would've cleared the spread, and everyone with a Vikings ticket would go home happy. Instead of scoring, however, Hockenson slid down at the one, knowing that he had enough for the first down and Minnesota could simply kill the clock and lock in the victory.
Savvy play by TJ Hockenson to stop short of the end zone MIAvsMIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/z81tAE4wNy
Well, we'll shake that rough ATS loss off and now turn our attention to Week 5, which, as always, begins with my five locks of the week.
Note : Kansas City and Carolina are on the bye in Week 5.
I think someone on the Colts may have upset the schedule makers or something, because they are getting a raw deal in this Week 5 matchup against Pittsburgh. Last week, Indianapolis played in London and will now have to go on the road the following week for an international game and face a Steelers team that is on extended rest after playing last Thursday night. That's as significant a rest advantage as you may find outside of bye weeks, and I think Pittsburgh takes advantage.
Don't be fooled by the 30-13 win in London last week; the Colts -- outside of Jonathan Taylor -- looked terrible. Daniel Jones has yet to recapture the spark he had in the first half of last season before tearing his Achilles. So far this season, Jones is averaging just 5.7 yards per attempt, has four total touchdowns and seven total turnovers. He's also completed just one pass (on nine attempts) of 20-plus air yards.
The Steelers, meanwhile, have been far better at home this season than on the road, owning a 2-0 record and averaging 25 points per game. Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh offense have shown sparks through the first month, and I'd expect to see more of that on Sunday against an Indy defense that is allowing the second-most yards per game in the NFL this season. The Steelers are also 5-0 SU and ATS in their last five games following an ATS loss.
Projected score : Steelers 27, Colts 20 The pick : Steelers -2.5
Sure, they couldn't fend off the Chiefs last week and stay undefeated, but I think the Raiders still validated their strong start to the year in that game. They are still a developing team, but they hung right with Kansas City, who looks like one of the elite teams in the conference. The offense has played extremely well and is averaging 28.8 points per game, while Kirk Cousins -- who is 7-1 SU and ATS over his last eight starts --  is tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns (11).
I think they have enough firepower to hang around with New England on the road to stay within the number, especially with the spread sitting at a field goal and a hook. That said, I think the Patriots carry the momentum of a massive win in Buffalo last Sunday into Week 5.
Drake Maye looked much more confident in the pocket last week, specifically when it came to dealing with pressure. Against the blitz, Maye was 9-of-14 for 118 passing yards and three touchdowns, which was good for a 130.4 passer rating. That's close to the MVP runner-up we saw last year. He also used his legs more effectively. Maye could pop again against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed more points, yards, and rushing yards in each game this season.
Projected score : Patriots 24, Raiders 21 The pick : Raiders +3.5
The vibes around the Eagles are either at or near an all-time low. They just blew a double-digit fourth-quarter lead to the Rams in Week 4, are remarkably banged up, and just saw Lane Johnson announce his retirement. It's unclear if Saquon Barkley (hamstring) or DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will play this week as Philly heads to London to face Jacksonville this weekend. If neither is able to go, that'd be an offense reeling after failing to convert a single one of its 12 third-down opportunities last week. Going back to Week 3, Philly enters this game on a 0-17 streak on third down.
Meanwhile, they square off against a Jaguars team that I believe is the best in the AFC at the moment. They're 3-1 and have an offense that is essentially the polar opposite of Philly's. The Jags have the third-best third-down conversion rate (51.1 %) in the NFL entering Week 5, the second-best red zone touchdown rate (81.8%), and Trevor Lawrence is sneakily playing like an MVP candidate. Of the 24 quarterbacks who've thrown at least 100 passes this season, Lawrence is second in passer rating at 111.2.
The Jags are too hot to fade at the moment, and face an Eagles team that feels like they are about to roll over.
Projected score : Jaguars 30, Eagles 17 The pick : Jaguars -6.5
I told you this after Week 3, and it's only become more true as the season has gone on -- the Chargers are a dumpster fire . They're 0-4 on the season and have largely looked lifeless in the process. And don't let the 30-23 final score against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks fool you; Los Angeles piled up most of those points when the game was out of reach (trailed 27-6). Justin Herbert has thrown more interceptions (6) than touchdowns (4) this season and is currently last in the NFL with a 70.6 passer rating (min. 100 pass attempts).
The Broncos haven't been much better than the Chargers, if we're being honest, as their 2-2 start to the season has been disappointing when you look under the hood. Specifically, they are starting out games extremely flat on offense, totaling just 13 points in the first half, which is last in the NFL. They've been able to rebound with frantic second halves, scoring the fifth-most second-half points in the league (61). That at least shows there is a spark that can be tapped when backed into a corner.
However, this game will be won in the trenches. Specifically, the Broncos should take advantage of a banged-up Chargers offensive line. Even when they have been healthy, L.A. is giving up the second-highest pressure rate per dropback in the NFL (46.9%). They now have to try to improve on that figure without left tackle Rashawn Slate, who is expected to miss this game with a high ankle sprain. Projected score : Broncos 26, Chargers 20 The pick : Broncos -3.5
As I noted last week in my Cover 32 column , the Packers just don't have it, and I don't see them as a true playoff threat in the NFC, let alone as a division winner. They're 28th in the NFL in points per game (18.8) and are last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (58.0) as well as on third down (26%).
