title: NFL overreactions or reality? Sorting fact from fiction after the first quarter of the 2026 season
summary: We sort through what's real and what's an overreaction, from the Chiefs' resurgence to Bryce Young's breakout
full_text:
There is no longer an official one-quarter mark of the NFL season now that the league operates with a 17-game schedule, but with four games in the books, the campaign is about 25% complete. That is a large enough sample size to begin to draw conclusions about teams, players and coaches, even if some of those takeaways will age poorly over the remaining three-fourths of the year.
In some cases, it is not too early to write the book on a team's season. For instance, the five winless teams can effectively wave goodbye to their postseason hopes because it will be nearly impossible to climb out of the deep trenches they dug themselves into over the season's first month. Even the Houston Texans , who entered the year as Super Bowl hopefuls, look like an afterthought in the race to the playoffs.
The rest of the campaign will prove that some four-game starts are nothing more than hot streaks and cold stretches. But for now, all we can run with is what we have seen in a month's worth of action.
Let's separate overreactions from reality as the NFL's regular season reaches its quarter-way mark.
The Kenneth Walker III signing might have been the most impactful free agency move of the offseason. The Kansas City Chiefs are a completely different beast in 2026 than they were a year ago, and it all stems from the reintroduction of a prolific rushing attack. The $14.35 million the Chiefs are paying the reigning Super Bowl MVP suddenly looks like a steal, because Walker leads the NFL in rushing through four games with his 537 yards. That is 116 more than the second-most-prolific ballcarrier and last year's rushing title winner, James Cook.
Because the Chiefs boast the No. 3 rushing attack in the league, Patrick Mahomes does not have to shoulder an immense load with his arm as he did in years past. This not only helps him ease back into action following his ACL tear, but it should also aid in his career longevity. The passing offense is so much more impactful than it was one year ago, it was the only thing that worked. Just look at Travis Kelce's resurgence this season as a top-tier receiving tight end.
Kansas City needs help at wide receiver, but even with the depth concerns there, it is one of three undefeated teams and has the look of the same unstoppable force that won three Super Bowls in five years and went to two others since 2019.
There was no more disappointing individual player in the first three weeks of the season than Drake Maye . Last year's MVP runner-up was the second-worst quarterback in the NFL by passer rating through three games. That is an unfathomable fall from grace. Even after a bounce-back performance on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills , Maye leads the league in interceptions with seven and fumbles with five. His mistakes cost the New England Patriots mightily in their two early-season losses.
Week 4 was a reminder not to fall victim to the moment, though, and to recognize that this is the same player who orchestrated a 10-win turnaround and a trip to the Super Bowl a season ago. Maye showed tremendous growth in the Patriots' 29-26 upset of the Bills, especially under duress. According to ESPN Insights , Maye completed 50% of his passes for 76 yards and a touchdown across a career-high 21 pressures against Buffalo. That is in contrast to the 42% completion rate, zero touchdowns and three interceptions under pressure in Weeks 1-3.
Drake Maye's huge day led the Patriots to a win in Buffalo 🙌 @FedEx pic.twitter.com/BZe1LtAkVP
A lot of Maye's struggles to open the year may have come from between the ears. His disastrous Super Bowl performance seemed to linger as he walked into the same kinds of trouble in the first three games of 2026. Losing his top target, A.J. Brown , to a high ankle sprain did not help. Sunday's win was the kind of confidence-building moment that could pull Maye out of his slump for good, and Brown should be back before long. A return to MVP-caliber play in the weeks to come is not out of the question.
The Chicago Bears are 3-1, and each of their victories came with a different starting quarterback. Caleb Williams won the season opener, Case Keenum delivered a surprising win over the Eagles after Williams went down with a hamstring strain in Week 2 and Tyson Bagent stepped in on Sunday to deliver a triumph over the New York Jets . This says something about the strength of the Bears' quarterback room, but it says even more about coach Ben Johnson and his offensive prowess.
Johnson was already renowned as a rising offensive mastermind heading into the year. His work as the Detroit Lions ' offensive coordinator was evidence enough, and a prolific debut season with the Bears backed it up. This is his most dazzling effort yet, though. The ability to put second- and third-string quarterbacks in positions to not just win games but also excel in the process says everything about Johnson's stardom.
Before the season, Johnson said that he wanted to field the highest-scoring offense in NFL history. That looked like a legitimate possibility after Week 1. It will not happen now, but when Williams returns to the lineup, there is a real chance Chicago will dominate the league as the most unstoppable unit in football.
Trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie , signing Jaylen Watson and pulling Aaron Donald out of retirement made the Los Angeles Rams the winners of the offseason. No team generated more positive buzz this spring and summer, and for good reason. The additions to the defense included two future Hall of Famers and two impact cornerbacks, and that pairs with an offense that features the reigning MVP in Matthew Stafford , a superstar wide receiver in Puka Nacua , another potential Hall of Famer in Davante Adams and other high-impact standouts.
But then the season arrived, and the Rams laid an egg in Australia with a 27-7 divisional loss to the San Francisco 49ers . They blew a 16-0 lead to the Denver Broncos two weeks later, dropping to 1-2. And it took a miraculous late-fourth-quarter comeback to get past the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. Those are not the kinds of results expected of a super team.
It is still too early for major concern, though. Garrett has not played since Week 1 and was not at full strength in his lone outing. Donald is nursing a back issue. The offense has not had time to gel because of Nacua's early absence. Once these superstars get onto the field together at the same time, the Rams should hit their stride. Los Angeles' schedule is incredibly manageable outside of NFC West play, so the wins should pile up even if it takes longer than anticipated for the full system to fire on all cylinders.
It is extremely difficult to go an entire season without winning a single game, especially now that the campaign is 17 games long. No team has gone winless since the NFL expanded its schedule in 2021, and before that, the Cleveland Browns were the last 0-16 squad all the way back in 2017. There will eventually be a team that drops all 17 games, however, and this year's Miami Dolphins are the strongest candidate to date.
The Dolphins already held the worst roster in the league, and that was before they lost De'Von Achane for the season. The star running back tore his ACL in Week 3, which stripped Miami of its best player and the only Pro Bowler in town. Without Achane, the franchise is incredibly young and inexperienced and rid of high-upside talent.
Miami showed some fight defensively in Week 4 when it held the Minnesota Vikings out of the end zone, but if the Dolphins cannot win a game in which they hold the opposing team to five field goals, then who will they beat? The also-winless Los Angeles Chargers and reeling Green Bay Packers present the two best opportunities, and there are two matchups with the Jets up ahead. But the Dolphins could be underdogs in each of those games, and the rest of the schedule is grueling.
For the first two years (and even into the third season) of Bryce Young's career, the former No.…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Russell Wilson says Chiefs should call Tyreek Hill amid WR injuries: 'Why would you not do it?'
summary: On this week's episode of 'Set Hut,' the former Super Bowl-winning quarterback explains why a Hill reunion is best for business in Kansas City
full_text:
Should the Kansas City Chiefs call Tyreek Hill ? Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson and former Chief Kyle Long think so.
In this week's installment of CBS Sports' "Set Hut," the two former players discussed how K.C. looks right now and why they should pick up the phone to call Hill in for a workout.
"I'm going after Tyreek Hill right now if I'm the Chiefs. ... Think about the yards," Wilson said. "If he's healthy, why would you not do it? ... Chiefs Kingdom would go crazy for it."
Wilson noted how the offense would open up, and because the Chiefs didn't have the run game they do now years ago, they'll be that much more elevated.
"They've got explosive plays in the pass game, they've got explosive plays in the running game. I don't know how you're going to beat these guys," Wilson said, in a world where the Chiefs have Hill.
Long was a 2021 Chiefs teammate of Hill. That season, Hill posted 111 receptions for 1,239 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 games, 16 of which were starts. Having a front-row seat to the connection between Hill and Mahomes, Long says the "unspoken communication" and chemistry they share "can be huge and so priceless for the Chiefs."
Some are hesitant about the 32-year-old because he is returning from such a gruesome leg injury. Even if he can't do all the things he used to be able to on the field, Long still thinks the WR can make an impact.
"If you're worried about the ins and outs cuts that Tyreek Hill can do with his newly reconstructed leg, how about you say, just go run straight down the field and force that safety to cover you, and it opens up so much of the middle of the field," Long said.
The Chiefs are coming off a win over the Las Vegas Raiders , who were 3-0 going into the divisional contest. This week, they are on a bye, and in Week 6, Kansas City will face the Los Angeles Chargers .
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Best NFL futures bets to make after the first month of the 2026 season: Buy Dallas Cowboys, Bijan Robinson
summary: Don't sleep on Kyle Shanahan to win Coach of the Year either
full_text:
Four weeks of NFL action are now in the rearview mirror. The rust has been shaken off, and clubs are now getting into a groove as we continue to barrel down the road that'll eventually lead us to Super Bowl LXI. Of course, before we get to that matchup, there's plenty that still needs to be determined, so how about we roll up our sleeves and call some shots?
Below, we're going to roll through a handful of futures bets to make now that we've seen these teams up close for four games. In this very story a year ago , we clued you in on a number of winners, including the Jaguars winning their division, New England going over their then-8.5 over/under win total, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba leading the league in receiving yards. Each of those paid out at plus money, with Smith-Njigba being our biggest winner at +600.
With 14 weeks left in the 2026 regular season, let's jump on some early value on the futures market while we still can.
NFL odds as of Oct. 6 and courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
This is just as much of a play against the rest of the division as it is buying Dallas. While the Giants were my preseason dark horse to burst onto the scene in the NFC East, the Jaxson Dart season-ending knee injury imploded that prediction. Meanwhile, the Commanders have QB injuries of their own, with Jayden Daniels again dealing with a left elbow injury. He's slated to return at some point, but they've dug themselves into a 1-3 hole through the first month and are already 0-2 in the division, including a head-to-head loss to the Cowboys .
Then there's the Eagles . Despite sitting at 2-2, they look lost offensively. Even before dealing with an onslaught of injuries to the likes of DeVonta Smith , Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert , it just hasn't looked right. Through the first month, their yards-per-play average is tied for the third-lowest in the NFL, with teams like the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers moving the ball at a more efficient clip. While the injury luck could eventually flip in the Eagles' favor, this just doesn't feel like Philadelphia's year.
That brings us to Dallas. Sure, their defense hasn't looked much improved from last year despite a slew of new faces being injected into that side of the ball. But they still feel like the most complete team in the division. They also just traded for corner Joey Porter Jr. , and his arrival could help bring the defense to a more serviceable level.
Even if they get there, the strength of this team will remain its offense, and it's that unit that gives us confidence in this future. The Cowboys are tied for the second-highest scoring offense in the NFL (30.5 points per game), fourth-best on third down (51.02%) and the third-best in the league in the red zone (81.25%). They also protect the football well with just two turnovers through the first four games.
Their upcoming schedule is pretty soft, which will be an opportunity to pile up some wins. Over the next seven games, they'll face the likes of the Buccaneers , Packers , Cardinals , Colts , and Titans, which could all be looked at as penciled-in wins.
If you want to play this more conservatively and look at the Cowboys to simply make the playoffs, that sits at -114.
Let's take advantage of the uncertainty surrounding Caleb Williams ' return from his hamstring injury and jump on this value with Chicago to win the NFC North.
Minnesota currently is the betting favorite to win this division at +125, but I think its 4-0 record is a bit hollow. It beat up on bad competition in the Packers, Bucs, and Dolphins . While the Vikings claimed a head-to-head win over the Bears , that was when Williams went down. They might be able to win games solely based on their lethal defense, but I think rubber will eventually meet the road, and they'll need their offense to muster something. So far, I don't know if Kyler Murray is the best fit for Kevin O'Connell's system, which has me questioning their ability to hang onto their division lead.
Beyond the Vikings , this division doesn't feel as fearsome as it did heading into the year. The Lions ' defense leaves them vulnerable, and the Packers haven't instilled any faith , so I think this is Chicago's division to lose. Williams will be back sooner rather than later, and, when he does, I'd expect this number to shrink. That'll be especially true if their defense continues to play at a high level after allowing less than 13 points in each of its last three games.
I think Jacksonville is hiding in plain sight as the best team in the AFC. Sure, Kansas City's revival with its 4-0 start has the NFL buzzing, but the Jaguars feel like a sleeping giant. Dating back to 2025, the club is 11-1 over its past 12 regular season games. There's a lane for them to possess the top seed and first-round bye when the dust settles on the regular season.
The Jaguars, who are 3-1 and currently atop the AFC South, have the easiest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL. They'll be in London over the next two weeks and face a depleted Eagles team in Week 5 before their first divisional matchup of the year against the current 0-4 Texans in Week 6. They'll be favored in both of those games, meaning they could be 5-1 as they enter the Week 7 bye week.
After that, their toughest remaining games are arguably at the Ravens in Week 9, at the Bears in Week 13, and at the Cowboys in Week 16. It wouldn't surprise me if they go into any of those environments and pull out the victory. But let's say they lose all three of those games and take care of business elsewhere; that'd put them at 13-4 for the second-straight year, which would certainly put them in prime position to claim the No. 1 seed.
Robinson is looking up to both Jahmyr Gibbs (+400) and Kenneth Walker III (+380) in the race currently, but I think this is a fantastic price for the Falcons star back. He's currently second in the NFL in rushing and total yards from scrimmage, trailing Walker by just 43 rushing yards and 7 scrimmage yards. Robinson has caught up in the standings after going nuclear over the last two games, once Michael Penix Jr . returned at quarterback.
While it's hard to imagine Robinson keeping up his current pace with Penix under center, let's just have some fun and project out what these numbers would look like over a full 17-game season. That'd come out to about 2,881 rushing yards and 34 rushing touchdowns. LOL!
That's just an extreme projection to illustrate that Robinson has the ability to light it up now that the Falcons are getting stable quarterback play with Penix. He's just as — if not slightly more — talented than both Gibbs and Walker, and if the Falcons go on to win the NFC South (currently tied with the Panthers after the first month), I believe he'll be given the large chunk of the credit in the form of OPOY votes.
Let me lay out some of the current odds surrounding the 49ers . After Week 4, they are the betting favorite to have the most regular-season wins at +350, meaning that they are also the favorites to be the No. 1 seed in the NFC (+190) as well as win the NFC West (+100). If all that comes to fruition and they are the top dogs in the conference with a big win total (currently 4-0), why wouldn't Kyle Shanahan be the favorite to win Coach of the Year?
Shanahan would have once again navigated his team through another pile of injuries and firmly have them in the Super Bowl conversation. This is almost exactly what he did a year ago, only the Niners fell to the Seahawks in Week 18, which spurned them the opportunity to be the No. 1 seed. Had they won that game, I think Shanahan would've won COY then. Now, he has a similar opportunity and, given the +1200 price point, it's maybe the best value on the entire futures board.
The only candidate that truly makes me nervous in this race is Todd Monken (+700). He has the Browns at 3-1 on the year, and Cleveland is tied for the third-easiest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL. Given how low the bar has been with that…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFC team grades: 49ers top of class through four games, Rams, Eagles slip to middling marks
summary: Plus, the reigning Super Bowl champs still look the part
full_text:
The first month of the NFL season can play tricks on us. Last year through four games, Baker Mayfield was looking like an MVP candidate, and the Buccaneers were 3-1. The Colts were also 3-1, and Daniel Jones was not only putting up even better numbers than Mayfield, but putting up some of the best numbers in the league — one of the most out-of-nowhere quarterback surprises in recent memory.
On the other side, the Panthers were 1-3 and coming off a 26-10 shellacking courtesy of the Jaguars . The Texans were also 1-3. Both of those teams made the postseason.
Of course, there are plenty of early signs that turn out to be true, too. The Bills and Eagles were the only undefeated teams through four weeks last year, and both were playoff teams. The Saints , Titans and Jets — all 0-4 at this point last year — ended up continuing their poor play and landing top-10 picks.
What we can say for sure is that it's early. The standings of today will look very different one month from now, let alone three months from now when the regular season wraps up. Still, with four games down, we've seen enough to hand out first-quarter grades to every team, taking into account not just their record, but how they've looked getting there and how that projects moving forward.
After hitting the AFC yesterday , we move to the NFC.
If Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns were healthy and the Giants were 3-1, this would be an "A" or "A-" easily. Instead, both suffered season-ending knee injuries. Dart is the one that really, really hurts. Based on the tiny sample size we saw, he looked excellent. Yes, the Giants lead the NFC East, but their last two wins were 12-7 over the Titans and a win over the Cardinals that came down to a goal-line stand in the final seconds. Any team wondering whether to start Jameis Winston or J.J. McCarthy can't really get a grade much higher than this, especially given the short- and long-term implications of Dart's injury.
The defense deserves a "B-" or a "C+." The offense deserves a "D" ... or maybe worse. Hence, the "C-" mark. The Eagles are 29th in offensive success rate and 31st in EPA per play, only ahead of the Buccaneers. Yikes. Jalen Hurts looks completely lost, and Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are both dealing with injuries. The offensive line, due to injuries and significant skill decline, is a shell of its former self. The defense has been much better, but still disappointing given its lofty expectations. The Eagles' wins are narrow ones over the Commanders and Titans. They got blown out by the Case Keenum-led Bears and blew a 10-point lead with under five minutes left against the Rams , who made so many mistakes they were practically begging the Eagles to win the game. Nick Sirianni, Sean Mannion, Hurts and many others are drawing the ire of Philadelphia faithful.
The Cowboys currently have the fifth-highest-scoring offense on a per-drive basis of the 21st century. Dak Prescott has been outstanding, and CeeDee Lamb and/or George Pickens can dominate any defense, as seen against the Texans in Week 4 . Plus, the Cowboys are about to get their best offensive lineman, Tyler Smith , back. For as good as the offense is, though, the defense is just as bad. Dallas' defense is 20th in EPA per play, 31st in success rate and 31st in explosive play rate. They're allowing a league-worst 6.4 yards per play. The Joey Porter Jr . addition should help, but he's just one of the 11 players on the field.
In Week 1, the Commanders' defense looked good, but the offense looked bad. In Week 2, the offense started to come around, but then Jayden Daniels got hurt again, and Washington got blown out. Week 3 remains one of the most surprising results in the NFL this season, a 33-31 win over the Seahawks . But any chance at building hope and momentum dissipated in Week 4, where Marcus Mariota got hurt, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis . Other than first-round rookie Sonny Styles looking very good, it's hard to find good news for a team that very much looks like last year's 5-12 outfit. Washington is 30th in offensive success rate and 23rd in defensive success rate.
How does a 4-0 team receive a "B" mark? Well, how about this: Over the last three weeks, the Vikings have scored one offensive touchdown. Every other team in the NFL has at least three. The Vikings beat the Bears 9-3 in a downpour in Week 2, a game Caleb Williams left early. They beat the winless Buccaneers 23-16 in Week 3, a game Baker Mayfield left early. They nudged past the winless Dolphins 15-10 in Week 4. That does not inspire much confidence. The defense is the best in the league in both EPA per play and success rate. Brian Flores is simply superb. That's an "A+" unit. The offense is a "D" at best, ranking dead last in yards per play. Kyler Murray and co. have to figure something out. The 4-0 record bumps the grade up a hair, but this style of winning doesn't seem sustainable.
The Bears have won three games using three different quarterbacks, a remarkable feat in and of itself. The offense looked magnificent in Week 1 with Williams at the helm, and then it looked bad in a rainstorm in Week 2, even before Williams left early. The Bears' domination of the Eagles despite playing third-string quarterback Case Keenum is one of the more impressive performances of the season. There are still major questions about the defense, but it has at least somewhat started heading in the right direction, albeit against weak competition. Williams' hamstring injury knocks this grade down a bit, mostly because of the long-term implications. Yes, he's expected back sooner rather than later, but how healthy will he truly be? His mobility, escapability and scrambling are crucial parts of his game and the Bears' offense as a whole.
The Lions ' defense ranks dead last in EPA per play and explosive play rate. It's hard to be much worse than that, right? Everyone is frustrated, Dan Campbell is fielding questions about defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard , and the talent in the secondary simply isn't up to par. The eventual return of Brian Branch will help, but he can't fix everything — and he shouldn't be expected to — especially coming off an Achilles tear. The offense is generally very good: second in EPA per play and third in success rate and points per drive. But there's so much pressure for Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs and co. to score a touchdown every time they touch the ball. Week 4's loss to the Panthers was a prime example: Detroit scored on six of its 10 drives and lost.
The Packers ' two wins this year are a three-point overtime win against the Jets (in a game they very easily could have and perhaps should have lost) and a three-point win over the Buccaneers, quarterbacked by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels . That doesn't exactly inspire confidence. Neither do huge losses to the Vikings (a Carson Wentz-led comeback) and the Falcons . There are gigantic issues running the ball (31st in success rate) and stopping the run (28th in success rate). The Packers are scrambling at the offensive line. Jordan Love already has three interceptions; he threw six all of last year. The defense just lost Edgerrin Cooper to a torn Achilles. Micah Parsons ' looming return will help, but there are just so many issues here.
Here's a sentence you probably didn't expect to read four weeks into the season: Bryce Young leads the NFL in passing yards. It's not just the counting stats, either. He's sixth in EPA per dropback and seventh in yards per attempt. He has taken a gigantic leap forward in every aspect , though it hasn't been against the world's best competition. Regardless, Carolina should be thrilled. The defense has been less thrilling. If we take out a Week 2 game against the Cooper Rush-led Falcons, Carolina has a -0.15 defensive EPA per play, which would rank 29th. Without starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson , it could get worse before it gets better, too.

title: Prisco's Week 5 NFL picks: Cowboys rout Buccaneers on Thursday, Packers upset Bears
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 5 picks, including the Texans getting their first win and the Jets over the Browns
full_text:
So much for starting October the right way.
My picks stunk last week. I was OK straight up, going 9-7, but the late-game shenanigans cost me a chance at a decent week against the spread. I went 4-11-1 ATS last week as many back-door covers got me.
My straight-up record for the season is 38-26-0 and my ATS record is a dismal 25-37-2. How can I be that bad?
No time for sulking. It's time to turn it around and this week I think I have a chance to move closer to .500 for the season. Then we can build on things from there.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Bucs are 0-4 and playing a rookie at quarterback in Jalon Daniels . He will be making his first road start. On a Thursday night? That's tough. The Cowboys are coming off a big win at Houston and the offense was dynamic. Dak Prescott keeps it going in this one.
The Eagles are so banged up and coming off a tough loss to the Rams . Then, right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday. They have so many key players out, which has to help the Jaguars . The Jaguars are second in scoring defense and have stopped the run all year long. They will limit the Eagles' offense in this one. The Jaguars go to 4-1.
Pick: Jaguars 28, Eagles 16
These two don't like each other. The Bears have been great running the ball, but this could be the game where playing without Caleb Williams shows up. Look for Jordan Love to have a big day throwing it on the other side — finally. The Packers win it in an upset.
Pick: Packers 27, Bears 24
Both of these teams are 0-4, which is surprising when it comes to the Texans . The Titans have played a lot of close games, which they will again here. But C.J. Stroud will make the plays late to win this one.
Pick: Texans 23, Titans 17
The Bengals are hurting at receiver with both Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase suffering injuries last week against the Jaguars. But there is a chance they can play. Even if they don't, the Bengals will move the football. Miami plays hard, but they are undermanned.
Pick: Bengals 23, Dolphins 13
This is a long trip for the Raiders , coming off a tough division loss. The Patriots seemed to right things against the Bills , which meant Drake Maye came alive. Look for that to continue here as the Patriots get to 3-2.
Pick: Patriots 28, Raiders 24
The Saints looked awful in their loss to the Falcons on Monday night and now face an undefeated Vikings team. That Minnesota defense is special. The Saints are really banged up on defense. Maybe Kyler Murray can get it going against them. I think he does.
Pick: Vikings 24, Saints 17
The Browns are 3-1 and have won three straight, while the Jets have lost three straight. But they are back home after two on the road. That matters. Look for a better showing here from their offense as they upset the Browns.
The Colts have won two straight as they head to face the Steelers on the road after beating the Commanders in London last week. That's a tough turnaround, while the Steelers have extra days of rest. That matters. The Steelers will get back on track with a victory led by Aaron Rodgers .
Pick: Steelers 33, Colts 23
There is a chance Jayden Daniels will play for the Commanders. That's the good news. But he will be wearing a brace on his elbow. How much will it restrict him? The Giants are 3-1, but this is a big road test. I think they will be up to it. Give me Jameis Winston playing well as the Giants get to 4-1.
Pick: Giants 26, Commanders 24
The Broncos are playing consecutive road games after losing at San Francisco last week. The Chargers haven't won. They will here. Desperation will be in play for the Chargers. The Broncos have offensive issues right now that will show up. Look for Los Angeles to quiet the critics for a week.
Pick: Chargers 23, Broncos 17
The Lions are playing on the road off a Sunday night loss. They can't stop anybody on defense. But the Cardinals have some defensive issues as well. Look for the Lions to outscore Arizona in a shootout as Jared Goff puts up big numbers.
Pick: Lions 40, Cardinals 31
This is an enormous division game that will be a physical war, as they always are between these two. The 49ers are undefeated, but this is a tough road test. The Seahawks are the healthier team, but the 49ers have played better. The 49ers have played well in Seattle, but I think the Seattle defense will come up big late to win it.
Pick: Seahawks 28, 49ers 21
This could be a Ravens team without Lamar Jackson after he suffered an injured ankle last week. If he can't go, Tyler Huntley will start. That means this will be a Derrick Henry game. The Falcons impressed Monday night, beating up the Saints, but this is a short week and a better opponent. The Ravens will rally if Jackson doesn't play and be thrilled if he does.
Pick: Ravens 24, Falcons 17
This is one of the best games of the week. The Bills are coming off a tough loss to the Patriots, while the Rams rallied to beat the Eagles. Look for a lot of points in this one as Josh Allen and Matt Stafford have big games. In the end, the Rams will make the plays late to win it.
author: Pete Prisco

title: Eagles' Lane Johnson retires from NFL due to personal reasons after Week 4 absence
summary: Johnson's surprise exit from football ends a legendary career in Philadelphia
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles six-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Lane Johnson announced his immediate retirement from the NFL on Tuesday.
Johnson was a surprise scratch from the Eagles' Week 4 lineup. The team listed him as inactive due to personal reasons and did not disclose specific details. His retirement comes just two days after he missed the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams .
In his announcement, Johnson said it is "critical" that he focuses on his mental health at this moment.
Over the final years of his career, Johnson opened up about his mental health struggles and revealed that he battled anxiety dating back to his freshman year of college in 2008. Earlier this year, he missed multiple training camp practices for personal reasons and said he felt the pull of off-field responsibilities weighing on him. In turn, Johnson said in August that 2026 would likely be his final year in the NFL.
Thank you. 🦅 pic.twitter.com/up2kH1K40p
Prior to his offseason announcement that he was trending toward retirement, a season-ending injury 10 games into the 2025 campaign raised questions about Johnson's long-term future in the league. He signed a contract extension in May 2025 that was set to keep him with the Eagles through 2027.
Johnson stands among the greatest offensive linemen of the 21st century. He is a two-time Super Bowl champion and five-time All-Pro, and the former No. 4 overall pick out of Oklahoma ends his career as an Eagles legend. He spent his entire career in Philadelphia and was a stalwart in the trenches for the franchise from 2013 through the third game of the 2026 campaign.
The impact Johnson made on Philadelphia's offense was undeniable. Entering this season, the Eagles averaged 0.04 EPA per play with Johnson on the field (good for the third-best mark in the NFL) and -0.05 EPA per play without him (which made the offense the sixth-worst).
Exemplifying why Johnson is widely considered to be one of the greatest right tackles in NFL history was the streak from Week 11 of the 2020 season to Week 9 in 2023, where he set a record for consecutive snaps without allowing a sack. Johnson kept his quarterbacks upright across a stretch of 1,405 straight pass-blocking snaps. During that timeframe, he set a separate record with 961 snaps without a knockdown.
Johnson is a strong candidate for enshrinement in the Pro Football Hall of Fame and will be eligible in five years.
