It is extremely rare to come across a player like @LaneJohnson65 . Extremely rare In the spring of 2013, I found myself on a field in East Texas working out a young Lane Johnson. I believe he was 22 years old All these years later, to say I am proud of the career you built and… pic.twitter.com/Fqd5owQhr5
Lane Johnson's longtime teammate and friend Jordan Mailata reacts to Lane's retirement announcement. "I'm just thinking about how much I'm going to miss him." ❤️ pic.twitter.com/IgH0gBVyJI
Legendary career! Enjoy retirement
A true legend! Congrats on an amazing career my guy!! https://t.co/EvmicGg44G
One of the greatest to ever do it. Enjoy the well-earned rest Legend.
author: Carter Bahns

title: How can Nick Sirianni save his job? Eagles' path becomes more difficult without Lane Johnson
summary: Sirianni has his work cut out for him after his star right tackle called it a career
full_text:
A 2-2 start to the season and the offensive woes that caused it increased the scrutiny on Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. Less than two years removed from a Super Bowl victory, Sirianni entered the 2026 campaign with little concern about his job security, but his seat warmed over the first four weeks and could reach scalding temperatures if he cannot reverse the Eagles' fortunes.
The chances of Sirianni righting the ship took a significant blow on Tuesday when star offensive tackle Lane Johnson announced his sudden retirement from the NFL . Over the course of Johnson's career, Philadelphia ranked in the top three in offensive efficiency with him on the field and in the bottom six without him. His now permanent absence does not bode well for a unit that has looked bleak thus far in 2026.
Regardless of Johnson's availability, Philadelphia owns a bottom-tier defense through four games. The Eagles rank 26th in scoring at 18.8 points per game and an even worse 29th in total offense at 269.8 yards per game. Despite boasting an elite running back in Saquon Barkley , the squad is a middle-of-the-pack rushing offense. And only two teams hold a lower EPA per pass.
Last week, the Eagles made franchise history with their worst third-down execution in a single game. They went 0-for-12 on third down in the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams , which contributed largely to a late collapse in which they squandered a 10-point lead with less than four minutes to play.
The issues are not limited to just one facet of the offense. This was an issue last year, too, and now that it has become a trend, eyes are on Sirianni as the man responsible for fixing it.
In Sirianni's defense, most coaching staffs would have found it difficult to move the ball against the star-studded Rams with the personnel available to him. Preventing Los Angeles' fourth-quarter comeback would have been a challenge considering the state of the defense, too. The following notable players were either inactive for Week 4 or suffered in-game injuries that prevented them from finishing the contest.
That does not even include the likes of Hollywood Brown, Tank Bigsby , Fred Johnson and other key non-starters who are on the shelf.
Only two of Sirianni's three offensive coordinator hires have been fruitful. And since Kellen Moore left at the end of the 2024 season, the team has not been able to acquire a similarly high-caliber play-caller. There was hope that Sean Mannion would bring a fresh perspective this season in his first year as a coordinator, but the results thus far are underwhelming at best, and Sirianni has to own that.
Jalen Hurts ' own limitations at quarterback and the loss of A.J. Brown following his trade to the New England Patriots have been obvious. The Eagles need a coordinator who can mask those deficiencies like Moore and Shane Steichen did in their combined three seasons at the helm. The jury is still out on Mannion, but early returns are not nearly as promising as the team would have hoped.
If Sirianni has to fire a second offensive coordinator in as many years, the focus will be trained even more closely on himself moving forward. And at the rate things are declining, it is uncertain whether he would even have time to make another change to his staff before his time is up.
Philadelphia's next three-game stretch is a grind. Each of its next three games comes against potential playoff teams in the Jacksonville Jaguars , Carolina Panthers and Dallas Cowboys . Considering the Eagles just dropped back-to-back games against that caliber of opponent, they will need to perform at a higher level in order to prevent an extended losing streak. Emerging from this stretch at 2-1 and thus holding a winning record through Week 7 would go a long way in keeping Sirianni's sixth year afloat.
It will take a lot of behind-the-scenes work to achieve those results. Sirianni first has to figure out how to overcome the loss of Johnson. History suggests that the offense will be even worse in the weeks to come without its stalwart right tackle. He also needs to instill greater discipline throughout his roster after consecutive weeks with 10 penalties and after falling into a minus-three turnover deficit.
And then there is the preparation aspect. The Eagles did not look ready in the slightest for the Chicago Bears' third-string quarterback, Case Keenum, two weeks ago. Sirianni's game-planning and CEO skills will be put to the test this week when the Eagles play in London. Not only is this international trip out of the ordinary, but it comes against a Jacksonville team that is deeply familiar with playing overseas. If the Eagles look lost in Week 5, much of that could come back to Sirianni.
The Eagles' coaching staff simply needs to keep its team competitive against tough competition and without a myriad of its best players. If Philadelphia comes out of this grueling stretch alive, then there will be enough opportunities on the other side to salvage this season or completely correct its course.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL sets penalty record through Week 4 as tensions flare between teams, officials
summary: Coaches, players and officials have not seen eye to eye during a flag-happy start to the season
full_text:
As important as officials are to the game of football, there is no world in which referees and their decisions should overshadow the players in NFL games . At times over the first four weeks of the 2026 season, it felt as though there was an imbalance in the focus on officials and the teams they moderated. Whether it was a product of poor calls or a lack of discipline from players, the NFL saw a record number of penalties in Weeks 1-4.
According to ESPN , the 963 accepted penalties thus far are the most through Week 4 since play-by-play data became available in 1978. And the 271 accepted penalties in Week 4 alone were the second-most in any week during the play-by-play era.
The following teams last week picked up double-digit infractions.
Twelve teams with at least 10 penalties is an astronomical number. The outlier-level volume of fouls goes beyond just Week 4, though. Perhaps the officials are doing exactly what is asked of them and honing in on points of emphasis. Maybe their quality of performance is at a low. Or possibly teams have been less disciplined in the early going this year than in seasons past. Any of the explanations is possible, or it could be a combination of all of them.
Especially frustrating for teams is that the penalties are not just prevalent but also ill-timed.
According to Warren Sharp , the number of penalties called on third or fourth down in the second half of games is the most in any Weeks 1-4 stretch since at least 2000. The volume of penalties inside the red zone is also a new high. And the 17 touchdowns nullified due to penalties are extremely out of proportion; only five were called back through Week 4 last year, and only four came off the board the year prior. The average over the previous decade was 8.3.
These high-leverage calls halted drives and took points away from offenses. In fact, the uptick in penalties this year strictly impacts the offensive side of the ball. Sharp says the defensive penalty rate is lower in 2026 than in years past, and pass interference calls are below average.
The impact of the rise in penalties — and in some cases, the absence of calls — has been visible through players' and coaches' frustration with officials. In the New England Patriots ' Week 4 win over the Buffalo Bills , coach Mike Vrabel received an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing a pass interference flag that awarded the Bills a first-and-goal situation. Vrabel called referee Bill Vinovich "sensitive" for penalizing him for the use of profanity.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was hit with an Unsportsmanlike Conduct penalty. The Bills tied the game a few plays later. pic.twitter.com/6JsrQWfAeA
The NFL suspended two other officials for what it deemed "unprofessional conduct" toward players in Week 4.
A league review of line judge Jeff Seeman's interaction with Trey McBride determined that the line judge used vulgar language at the Arizona Cardinals tight end. McBride initially pleaded for a pass interference penalty he thought should have been called on a third-down incompletion. CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala said McBride was heated in his plea for a penalty flag but did not use profanity toward the official. Seeman faces a two-game suspension .
The league also issued a one-game suspension to referee Adrian Hill for an incident involving Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson . Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, Hill stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson.
The NFL Referees Association plans to challenge both suspensions .
"NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFLRA executive director Scott Green said in a statement. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye sounds slightly skeptical of the moon landing: 'I'm not 100% sure'
summary: Maye isn't entirely sure whether the US landed on the moon or not in 1969, and he had some other thoughts on conspiracy theories
full_text:
If you've ever wondered what Drake Maye's favorite conspiracy theory is, well, we now know the answer. The Patriots quarterback isn't completely sure that the United States actually landed on the moon back in 1969.
During a Monday interview on WEEI in Boston , the show closed out with a segment called "Ask Maye Anything," and that's when a fan asked the Patriots QB whether there were any "wild" conspiracy theories he "kind of secretly believed in."
At first, it didn't seem like Maye was going to answer the question.
"Wow. How about that?" Maye said. "Let me try not to get too controversial. Let me think."
But then, after thinking it over, the 24-year-old said that he's always been slightly skeptical of the moon landing.
"I don't know about the moon," Maye said. "I can see back in the day of why we would put on the mask if we went there, but I'm not really sure 200% if we went there or not. I wouldn't say I'm leaning one way or the other. I just know I'm a little bit skeptical."
To be clear, Maye isn't saying that he absolutely believes that we never went to the moon; he's just saying he's not so sure. One of the show's hosts seemed thrilled that Maye brought up the moon landing, as he certainly had a few conspiracy theories about it that he wanted to share.
"I think it was Stanley Kubrick who did the entire thing. He has put clues in all of his movies that he was the guy who directed the moon landing," the co-host said. "I absolutely believe we didn't land on the moon."
If you're not familiar with the Kubrick conspiracy theory , some people believe he helped film the "moon landing" on a studio sound stage.
Maye didn't necessarily seem to agree with the Kubrick stuff, but he definitely seemed to be undecided about whether we actually went to the moon.
"Well, I'm not 100% sure," the Patriots QB said.
Before signing off, the former North Carolina quarterback actually revealed an interesting fact about himself: He studied conspiracy theories in college!
"I took a conspiracy class in college, actually, at North Carolina, which was pretty cool," Maye said.
And yes, UNC does actually have a class about conspiracy theories . It's called "Uncertain Truths: Conspiracy Theories, Aliens, and Secret Societies in America." So what did Maye study in this class?
"They studied Hitler being alive and 'are birds real,' some of the classic ones that you hear about," Maye said.
Birds aren't real? If you're wondering what that's all about, Maye has the answer.
"Just like the government has a say in some of the things, you know, birds flying around and whether they're videoing or listening or something along the lines of that," Maye said.
There's actually an entire website devoted to that conspiracy theory .
For the record, Maye didn't actually say that he believed that birds aren't real. He was just pointing out a few things they studied in his conspiracy theories class.
For whatever reason, conspiracy theories tend to be a hot topic in NFL locker rooms. There was once a Rams player who said that he didn't believe in dinosaurs . And more recently, you have Aaron Rodgers , who has turned some of his teammates into conspiracy theorists, including DK Metcalf .
"Yeah, I'm a big conspiracy theorist," Metcalf said in a recent interview with The Athletic . "Shout out to my quarterback."
Metcalf believes that there might be a hidden civilization living in Antarctica.
"You can go to Alaska. You could go to the North Pole," Metcalf said in a recent interview with The Athletic . "But why not Antarctica? Why can't you just book a trip to Antarctica?"
From Antarctica to the moon and everywhere in between, conspiracy theories are everywhere.
"I think there is another civilization inside of Earth," Metcalf said.
author: John Breech

title: Chargers fire sale at NFL trade deadline? Landing spots for Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu
summary: A disastrous start could force Los Angeles to move expiring contracts ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are arguably the biggest disappointment of the 2026 NFL season. After back-to-back 11-6 seasons under Jim Harbaugh, the Chargers enter the month of October still looking for their first victory. They have started 0-4 for the first time since 2017, and are just the third team in NFL history to start 0-4 after back-to-back 11-win seasons.
The Chargers were viewed as the sleeper in the AFC West after hiring former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel to be their new offensive coordinator. However, Los Angeles currently ranks fourth-worst in scoring offense (16.8 points per game) and 12th-worst in total offense (306.8 total yards per game), while Justin Herbert hasn't been playing like a franchise quarterback. He's completing a career-low 59.7% of his passes for a career-low 204.0 passing yards per game with four touchdowns and six interceptions. It's been a disaster.
With games against the Denver Broncos , Kansas City Chiefs and Los Angeles Rams next up on the docket, it's fair to wonder when that first victory is coming for the Chargers. We are in dangerous territory of this becoming a lost season for Harbaugh, as the Chargers' Over/Under win total at DraftKings Sportsbook is currently listed at 5.5.
If things continue to go downhill for Los Angeles, the Chargers could be sellers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. They have a few intriguing trade targets teams will be looking at -- especially when it comes to pass rusher. Let's take a look at some Chargers players who could be traded in the near future, and a couple of potential landing spots for them as well.
Veteran pass rusher Khalil Mack is now 35 years old and playing on an expiring deal. A contender should reach out and see what it costs to acquire the former NFL Defensive Player of the Year.
Mack has actually recorded three sacks in his first four games this season to go along with 14 tackles and 13 pressures. He is just three years removed from his last double-digit sack season, recording a career-high 17 QB takedowns in 2023.
Wouldn't it be something if Mack returned to the Chicago Bears , where he spent four seasons from 2018-2021? He made three straight Pro Bowls in Chicago and recorded 36 sacks in 53 games played.
The Bears have Montez Sweat , Austin Booker and Dayo Odeyingbo -- who leads the team with three sacks. Pass rusher is not the biggest need on the team, but a Mack homecoming would help boost Chicago's defense as the Bears look to repeat as NFC North champions.
The San Francisco 49ers are tied in having the best record in the NFL at 4-0, but have the most games missed due to injury with 76, according to CBS Sports Research. That includes Nick Bosa , who is expected to miss multiple weeks due to a calf injury, and Mykel Williams , who is on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. The 49ers rank in the bottom six in the NFL in sacks with six, as Keion White leads the way with two QB takedowns. John Lynch would be smart to upgrade at pass rusher.
We could see new Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter push to acquire one of his former players in Mack. Trey Hendrickson , Tavius Robinson and Mike Green headline the Ravens' pass-rush group, but it could be better. Baltimore has recorded seven sacks over four games, which ranks in the bottom 10.
The Ravens ranked bottom four in sacks last year, which led them to sign Hendrickson. He's managed just one sack in three games played, and recently underwent surgery on his finger. Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz knows the Ravens organization as well, as he spent 25+ years there working in player personnel and scouting.
While some NFL teams are focused on Khalil Mack, there are others who could be interested in the Chargers' other pass rusher: Tuli Tuipulotu . He made the Pro Bowl last year after racking up a career-high 13 sacks to go along with 20 tackles for loss. It was thought he was holding in for a new deal this preseason, since Tuipulotu is set to make less than $6 million in 2026, but he's been on the field. Tuipulotu has recorded 18 tackles, two sacks, two passes defensed and one interception in four games played this year.
The Chargers front office has likely already spent some time negotiating with Tuipulotu's camp, so they have some idea whether a long-term extension is in the cards. If it's not, it makes sense to acquire draft capital rather than lose a starting pass rusher for nothing. The Chargers did spend a first-round pick on a pass rusher in this past draft with Akheem Mesidor .
Tuipulotu just had a fantastic game against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, recording six tackles, half a sack, his first career interception and one forced fumble. If he were to join the Seahawks, Tuipulotu could come in and immediately join a fun rotation, then get paid and take on a starting role when DeMarcus Lawrence and Dante Fowler Jr. leave this upcoming offseason.
This seems like a Howie Roseman trade. Acquire an underrated pass rusher that is due for a raise, and give him an opportunity to flourish. The Philadelphia Eagles are tied for 31st in sacks this season with four. This Vic Fangio defense as a whole has disappointed, but there's concern for this pass rush. Nolan Smith Jr. is actually the only pass rusher who has gotten to the quarterback this season!
The soon-to-be 84-year-old Jerry Jones is swinging trades left and right for the Dallas Cowboys . He acquired pass rusher Rashan Gary in the offseason, and just made a move for cornerback Joey Porter Jr . last week. Could he continue to wheel-and-deal by scooping Tuipulotu? Despite all of the moves the Cowboys have made, this defense is still struggling. That goes for the pass rush as well, which is tied with the Eagles, Dolphins and Chiefs in having the second-fewest sacks in the NFL this year. As we enter Week 5, the Cowboys rank bottom five in both total defense and scoring defense.
Wide receiver Quentin Johnston had a career year in 2025 with 735 yards receiving and eight touchdowns on 51 receptions. However, he's caught just seven passes for 108 yards and zero touchdowns through four games this season. What could make Johnston tough to move is that the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option for 2027, meaning he will make $18 million fully guaranteed. Maybe there's an interested team out there that will consider giving him a multi-year extension.
There are plenty of teams looking for help at cornerback, and the veteran Donte Jackson could be a potential trade target since he's on an expiring deal. Jackson is in his second season with the Chargers, and has recorded eight tackles and two passes defensed with one forced fumble through Week 4.
Tight end David Njoku is currently on injured reserve, but he could potentially be a sneaky trade target at the deadline. We don't know the extent of his injury, but in the best-case scenario, he could hypothetically return Nov. 1 if the injury isn't long-term. Njoku caught just six passes for 67 yards in his two games with the Chargers, but was an athletic weapon during his nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns . If Njoku is not seriously injured, perhaps a team would be interested in acquiring him for cheap next month.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Referees Association to challenge officials' suspensions for Week 4 conduct
summary: Referee Adrian Hill and line judge Jeff Seeman both face suspensions for 'unprofessional conduct'
full_text:
The NFL had gone eight years without issuing a suspension to a single official before it suspended referee Adrian Hill and line judge Jeff Seeman for their conduct during their Week 4 assignments. The NFL Referees Association said it disagrees with the rare punishment the league handed down and will challenge the severity of both suspensions. Hill faces a one-game ban while Seeman is set to miss two games.
The union argues that the suspensions for unprofessional conduct stretch beyond appropriate punishment. History, to an extent, sides with the union in Seeman's case in particular. His two-game suspension is the longest for an official since 1988, and officials previously suspended for altercations with players each sat just one game.
"NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFLRA executive director Scott Green said in a statement . "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."
A league review of Seeman's interaction with Trey McBride determined that the line judge used profanity at the Arizona Cardinals tight end. McBride initially pleaded for a pass interference penalty he thought should have been called on a third-down incompletion. CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala said McBride was heated in his plea for a penalty flag but did not use vulgar language toward the official.
The NFL said it is reviewing the situation in which an official appears to use profanity at Cardinals TE Trey McBride. The NFLPA Executive Director JC Tretter called for the NFL to hold the official accountable. pic.twitter.com/NuueChAmrx
NFL Players Association president JC Tretter released a statement regarding that play and called for the league to hold officials to the "same standard" as players.
Hill's suspension stems from an incident with Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson . Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II inadvertently shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, Hill stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson.
NFL referee Adrian Hill had a strong reaction when Vikings LB Eric Wilson offered to help him up after their inadvertent collision. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/azDgsIZESY
"Officials are routinely subjected to highly charged interactions and, at times, verbal abuse from players and coaches," Green said. "While that never excuses misconduct by an official, it shouldn't be dismissed as simply part of the game. The League expects the highest level of professionalism from its officials, and it should demand the same from everyone on the field."
Confrontations between officials and players seem to be on the rise. The NFLRA said it plans to meet with the NFLPA leadership team to address the matter and intends to meet with the league's officiating department to discuss disciplinary standards.
"We will defend the principle that discipline must be fair, consistent and proportionate," Green said. "Holding officials accountable while ignoring or minimizing the conduct directed at them is neither fair nor an effective way to address this issue."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Ranking NFL division leaders by which are most vulnerable after opening month
summary: We have some surprising division leaders after the first month, including the Browns and Giants. Will they hold on?
full_text:
Now that the first month of the 2026 regular season is over and done, you might have an urge to go look at the standings throughout the league to see where everyone stacks up. When you do, let me be the first to tell you that you don't need to clean your glasses and your eyes aren't deceiving you. There are some surprising division leaders through the first four weeks.
I mean, if you had the Cleveland Browns atop the AFC North at any point this year, I would like to ask you a few questions. Specifically, I'd like you to tell me this week's winning lottery numbers, since you clearly can see the future. Meanwhile, the New York Giants are another club that is remarkably leading it's division, the NFC East. That wouldn't be surprising if Jaxson Dart was still their starting quarterback, but it certainly is after he went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, which has thrust Jameis Winston under center.
Here, we're going to sift through these leaders and determine which have staying power and which are merely visiting the top spot before making the trek down. To do that, we'll rank all eight first-place teams from the least vulnerable to losing their spot (No. 8) down to the most vulnerable (No. 1).
Odds to win AFC South : -250
Jacksonville is sitting pretty atop the AFC South, and the betting odds support that. The Jaguars are currently the biggest favorite to win their division in the entire NFL , and it's easy to see why. While there are still some undefeated teams across the league, the Jaguars have the makings of a true threat to come out of the AFC. They just went into Cincinnati and beat the Bengals , which continues a white-hot run that dates back to last season. Over its past 12 regular-season games, Jacksonville is 11-1, averaging 31.1 points and allowing just 14.1.
As much as this is a credit to Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence forming quite the head coach-QB pairing, it also speaks to the lackluster nature of the rest of the division. Both the Texans and Titans are 0-4 to begin the year. Houston's offensive line continues to disappoint, and its defense has even regressed a bit from last season, so it doesn't appear to be a legitimate threat. Neither does Tennessee, as it appears destined to have another top-five pick at the NFL Draft . The most competitive division rival appears to be the Colts at 2-2, but even they don't strike fear into true playoff contenders. Daniel Jones doesn't look like the same quarterback he was in the first half of last year before his Achilles injury, and the defense is giving up the second-most total yards in the NFL through four weeks.
Odds to win AFC West: -225
Kansas City has jumped right back into being one of the elite teams in the AFC, with Patrick Mahomes largely not skipping a beat in his return from a torn ACL and LCL last season. The free-agent addition of Kenneth Walker III has also given the offense some much-needed explosiveness and has been a key catalyst for the 4-0 start to the season. K.C. is another division leader that is becoming an overwhelming favorite to keep its grip on the crown, especially after taking down the previously undefeated Raiders in Week 3.
While Las Vegas began the year 3-0 and is building a solid foundation under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, it still feels a year or two away from truly making a push in the division. As for the Denver Broncos , they, in theory, are the biggest challenger to the Chiefs after making the AFC Championship Game last season. However, the offense has been plagued by slow starts throughout the first month, and Bo Nix ranks 19th out of 24 qualified quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. For reference, Mahomes ranks eighth. Even the Denver defense, which is supposed to be the team's strength, ranks 20th in the league in yards allowed per play (5.6). Meanwhile, the Chargers at 0-4 are a virtual non-factor.
Odds to win NFC West: +100
San Francisco plays in the toughest division in the NFL, so putting it this low in terms of being vulnerable should tell you how good it has been through four weeks. Yes, the 49ers will have to fend off the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks and the still-current betting favorite to win Super Bowl LXI in the Rams , but they have the nucleus to do it.
The Niners already beat the Rams in a head-to-head in Australia in the season opener and have jumped out to a 4-0 record. Seattle is right behind at 3-1, and these two square off against one another in Week 5, so either San Francisco can post two marquee division wins over the first five weeks or find itself momentarily looking up at the Seahawks due to the tiebreaker.
When you look at the advanced metrics with the 49ers , it's hard not to have confidence in them. Offensively, they've run the lowest percentage of plays that lose yards at 2.2% (excluding kneels) by any team through four games since 2000. Defensively, they're giving up the lowest percentage of explosive plays (3.5%) by any team through four games since 2000. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked.
If they can keep this level of play up (or even keep it relatively close to these figures), they should win the requisite games to win the NFC West.
Odds to win AFC East: -215
Buffalo has better odds than the 49ers to win the division, but it's hard to ignore the fact that it just lost a pivotal early-season matchup to the Patriots in Week 4. Despite New England's rocky start, that win brought it to 2-2 on the season and within striking range of Buffalo, especially after securing the first head-to-head of the season on the road. The Patriots' schedule also softens up over the next month-plus, so Buffalo will need to be careful not to slip up. That puts an ever greater emphasis on what is slated to be a tough matchup in Week 5 as the Bills travel to Los Angeles to face the Rams on Monday night.
Another element that the Bills shouldn't ignore is that they'll be on the road for a large portion of the second half of the season, specifically down the final stretch. Of their final six games, four will be on the road. While trips to New England and Denver (on Christmas) could be daunting, the Packers currently don't look like a major threat, and the other road trip is to Miami to face a Dolphins team that'll likely be more interested in draft position than anything else.
As for the Jets , they've been pesky through the first few weeks of the season, but they don't pose a real threat to Buffalo in the division race, so it's really only New England the Bills need to concern themselves with.
Odds to win NFC South: +160
Carolina is technically knotted up with the Falcons for the NFC South lead, but currently edges them out thanks to the head-to-head victory from Week 2. The Panthers have flashed their potential at times this season, particularly with Bryce Young . The former No. 1 overall pick leads the NFL in passing yards this season, and his nine passing touchdowns are the most through the first four games of a season in franchise history.
They'll be on the bye in Week 5, so the next time they take the field will be in Week 6 when they travel to Philadelphia to face the Eagles . They'll look to get over .500 for the first time this season and will have a solid rest advantage. Not only will Carolina be coming off its bye, but the Eagles will also be returning from an international game in London against the Jaguars in Week 5.
While Carolina's offense has flashed, its defense still has some questions, allowing the fourth-most total yards per game in the NFL. It's also the seventh-worst red-zone defense (72.7%) in the league. The biggest challenger for the division crown will likely be the Falcons. That initial victory over Atlanta came with Cooper Rush at quarterback for the Falcons. With Michael Penix Jr . back, the Falcons are 2-0 and averaging 40 points per game. They'll come back down to earth in some capacity, but they could be a thorn in their side.
New Orleans has talent, but it is 1-3 through the first…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Michael Penix Jr. has completely revived the Falcons' offense. Can it continue after a hot start?
summary: The Falcons are leading the league in scoring over the last two weeks with Penix, but the question remains whether this is real or a mirage
full_text:
Through the first two weeks of the season, the Atlanta Falcons were the worst offense in the NFL . They scored just 16 total points and did not enter the red zone even once during those two games. Over the last two weeks, the Falcons have led the NFL with 80 total points. They dropped 35 on the Green Bay Packers on "Thursday Night Football" and 45 on the New Orleans Saints on "Monday Night Football."
Atlanta's Bijan Robinson-led run game has exploded in those two contests, totaling 447 yards on the ground. Robinson and No. 2 back Brian Robinson tagged the Packers for 242 yards and the Saints for 205. They also ran pretty well in the first two games (120 yards against the Pittsburgh Steelers and 157 against the Carolina Panthers ), but it's been an entirely different level in Weeks 3 and 4.
However, the main difference between the first two games and the latter two: The Falcons replaced backup quarterback Cooper Rush with starter Michael Penix Jr . starting in Week 3. Rush was dreadful in the first two games, while Penix has largely played well through his two starts. Through four weeks of the season, there are 41 quarterbacks who have thrown at least 30 passes, according to Tru Media. Rush ranks 41st among that group in expected points added (EPA) per dropback, while Penix checks in fifth.
Needless to say, Penix has completely rejuvenated the Falcons' offense. It's worth investigating what he has brought to the offensive attack that Rush couldn't.
Let's start with what's been the same. Penix and Rush have both gotten the ball out extremely quickly. Rush's average time to throw, per Tru Media, was 2.53 seconds, which was fourth-quickest among the aforementioned 41 passers. Penix is getting the ball out even faster, at 2.36 seconds, which is the fastest in the league to date.
A lot of that is because both players have thrown many screens. Rush was 7-of-8 on screens through his two starts, while Penix is 8-of-9. That means screens accounted for 20.5% of Rush's pass attempts and 20% of Penix's. Through the first four weeks of the year, Rush and Penix rank first and second among the 41 qualified quarterbacks for passes that were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage. They're both being schemed for easy completions.
The difference is that Penix has actually opened up some of the stuff farther down the field. Just 23% of Rush's passes traveled more than 10 yards in the air, per Tru Media. That number is 31.1% for Penix. Rush went only 3-of-9 for 56 yards on those pass attempts, while Penix is 9-of-14 for 276 yards and a touchdown.
pic.twitter.com/s1ildLBtnb
pic.twitter.com/nf1wTGHZ1I
Penix has also shown an ability to hit the wide sides of the ball that Rush couldn't access. On throws more than 5 air yards outside the numbers, Rush was just 3-of-5 for 55 yards, per Tru Media. Penix is already 9-of-13 for 213 yards and a score. He's connected repeatedly with Drake London on these types of plays, whether on sail routes, double moves or go balls. It's allowed London to run into open space or use his big body to box out the defensive back and make a play downfield.
pic.twitter.com/Gpcicr1ZGX
pic.twitter.com/NfsKihJ5RY
pic.twitter.com/We9TEiJec4
Being able to make these types of throws also helps the run game, as teams are less willing to devote extra men to the box to stop the rushing attack. Atlanta's rushing success rate with seven or more defenders in the box was just 27% through the first two weeks of the season, third-worst in the league, per Tru Media. In Weeks 3 and 4, that figure spiked to 63.6%, the highest in the NFL.
Perhaps because of that, the Falcons have utilized play action far more often with Penix (20 dropbacks) than Rush (5). Penix is 13-of-20 for 259 yards and a touchdown on those plays, and two of the incompletions were drops. He's thrown deep 15% of the time and created eight 10-plus-yard completions and seven of 20-plus yards. It's been highly effective.
The question, of course, is whether this can keep up. And that's definitely a question.
Penix was tasked with making a lot of the same types of throws during his first two seasons, but he was much less effective. He completed only 59.6% of his passes at an average of 7.2 yards per attempt. He got the ball out quickly and often threw to the sidelines and the intermediate-to-deep areas of the field, but he was off target quite often. That's been less true so far this season, but he's had the good fortune of playing against a couple of friendly defenses.
The Falcons' schedule does include a few games against high-quality defenses through the rest of the year (most notably the Vikings in Week 12), but it's not overly imposing. Penix might have a chance to keep this up, particularly if his accuracy improvement on intermediate and deep passes sticks. If that's just a two-week blip, though (which is certainly possible given the very small sample size and the level of competition), then some regression could be in store for this Atlanta offense.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Seahawks decide not to sign Joe Mixon after physical, per report
summary: Mixon missed the entire 2025 season with a foot injury, but he ran over 1,000 yards and over 10 TD in 2024
full_text:
The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-1) have a running back depth issue with Zach Charbonnet not ready to go after tearing his ACL in January, and first-round rookie Jadarian Price going on injured reserve with a chest injury.
That's why Seattle kicked the tires on signing two-time Pro Bowl running back Joe Mixon to its practice squad after hosting him for a workout on Monday, per ESPN . However, after a physical on Tuesday, the Seahawks reportedly opted not to sign Mixon.
Mixon, who is now 30 years old, missed the entire 2025 season with a foot injury, but he ran for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns on 245 carries as the Houston Texans ' bell cow back in 2024. He has run for over 1,000 yards in five of his eight career NFL seasons played, including three of his last four.
From 2021 to 2024, with the Cincinnati Bengals and the Texans, Mixon's 4,069 yards rushing ranked as the sixth most in the league, while his 40 rushing touchdowns were tied for the fourth-most in the NFL in that span. He will now compete for snaps with veterans Emanuel Wilson and George Holani . Wilson currently leads the Seahawks in carries (53), rushing yards (190 and rushing touchdowns (1) this season.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Grading NFL QBs on rookie contracts: Panthers' Bryce Young earns highest mark, Cam Ward gets 'D+'
summary: Young earns top marks after a dramatic year-four leap in Carolina, while Tyler Shough proves he is the real deal in New Orleans
full_text:
When a franchise has a quarterback on a rookie deal, it's a constant evaluation process. "Is this the quarterback that can win us a Lombardi trophy?" is the question that GMs and fanbases alike ask themselves on a weekly basis. Four weeks into the season, and I'd argue two young quarterbacks have answered that with a resounding "yes" who, prior to the season, we were far more unsure about, while numerous others with high hopes are still waiting for an answer. Here's how every rookie contract starter has graded out through four weeks.
Young has been given arguably the longest leash of any first-round quarterback in modern NFL history and that patience is finally bearing fruit in year four. Last year, Young ranked 27th among starters in EPA/dropback and barely cracked 3,000 yards for the season. Now, no one has more passing yards through four games than Young's 1,268 (317 per game) and he ranks 9th in EPA/dropback. The Panthers have scored 32 or more points in three of their four games after accomplishing that feat precisely zero times a season ago. It's the football equivalent of a caterpillar transforming into a butterfly.
So how did it happen exactly? The answer is obviously a confluence of factors, but I'd argue it's two big things: his ability to diagnose presnap and his postsnap footwork. One of Young's biggest selling points out of Alabama was his ability to create big plays outside of structure, and that's continued in the league, where he's averaged more yards per attempt on dropbacks over 2.6 seconds than under in every season in his career. The problem in the first three seasons, however, was that the inside of structure plays were a disaster. He rarely knew where best to go with the ball in rhythm and averaged 5.5 yards per attempt on throws under 2.6 seconds, his first three seasons. Yikes.
This year, that number is 7.8 and his completion percentage is up 7.0 points from his previous career high on such throws. Below is one of my favorite plays from Young this season, highlighting his presnap improvements (despite it coming in a loss).
Big boy throw by Bryce Young pic.twitter.com/TQfa0tcEkC
A few things to unpack here. The first is his recognition of the blitz and adjustment of the protection by reducing the tight end to get an extra blocker involved. Then he notices that his back and receiver were both in motion at the same time, so he calls for Tetairoa McMillan to come to a set to avoid an illegal motion penalty. Finally, he shows no signs of hurrying in his footwork as he sets up to throw either the corner or out, depending on how the defenders sink, and once they declare, Young puts it right on his receiver's chest.
It's that calm footwork that's the second-biggest area for growth. Young was always more of a loose athletic thrower of the football at Alabama rather than a robotic in-rhythm passer. He didn't need to have his feet perfectly aligned to drop dimes. That habit, unfortunately, didn't give him a consistent base to lean on when things got murky, and you saw his accuracy suffer because of it early in his career. Now he's blending precision footwork with high-end athleticism and the results speak for themselves. Just look at how efficiently he gets from 1 to 2 on the play below.
Bryce Young using the Backpedal Drop from Under Center It's beautiful! 😍 pic.twitter.com/xw0f0s9d0L
And how he manipulates defenders with his feet and shoulders to create a throwing lane for himself.
Bryce young with the shoulder fake to get the flat player to bite and nail the corner route vs C2. game is slow for him the last couple weeks pic.twitter.com/kVBJEmBVls
This is big-boy quarterbacking, not some fluke. Am I betting on Young leading the league in passing yards this season? Probably not. But after what he's put on tape, I would bet that he's going to be the face of the Panthers franchise for a long time.
If you had any doubts about Shough's franchise quarterback worthiness after his rookie season, those should be put to bed emphatically after four weeks. He's turned New Orleans into a top-10 scoring offense despite not having top-10 pick at wide receiver, Jordyn Tyson and with last year's top-10 pick at left tackle, Kelvin Banks, missing the past two games. While it hasn't translated to their 1-3 record, the defense has been to blame, allowing an average of 37 points in their three losses. The poise under pressure is far beyond Shough's years for a second-year quarterback as he's third in passing yards under pressure and averaging 7.2 yards per attempt when pressured.
Tyler Shough has courage. He’ll hang in the pocket and make some Bigtime throws. pic.twitter.com/qAXaP7zsHl
I think the most impressive thing about Shough's start is how well he's handled the volume. He's averaged 53 dropbacks per game this season - far and away the most in the NFL. And I'd argue that he's done a great job taking care of the football, given what he's asked to do, despite four interceptions. Because of those four picks, one was a miscommunication, another was when he was hit by his backup left tackle, and the final one was tipped at the line of scrimmage. So if you are looking for pure efficiency stats, his aren't going to compare to someone like Brock Purdy , who has over 20 fewer dropbacks per game, as a lot of Shough's completions are extensions of the run game, so to speak.
After back-to-back seasons asking what's wrong with C.J. Stroud , it's tragically ironic that the Texans are 0-4 with Stroud looking the best he has since his rookie campaign. He's averaging 7.6 yards per attempt and has yet to throw an interception despite no upgrades to the Texans' supporting cast. The offensive line ranks 20th in PFF pass-blocking grade, #1 receiver Nico Collins has missed two games, #2 receiver Jayden Higgins is out for the year, and the Texans are dead last in rushing success rate.
His game-losing fumble at the end of the Texans Week 1 loss to the Bills is the only thing keeping this grade from being in the A-range and even then he redeemed himself in the clutch with late go-ahead touchdown drives against the Colts and Texans the past two weeks. There's a lot of finger-pointing to go around in Houston, but I'd point at a lot of different parts of this roster before I point at the quarterback.
C.J. Stroud led the Texans 92 yards to take the lead with just over 2 minutes left. Multiple awesome throws on this drive with a 3rd down conversion under pressure to Nico & excellent ball placement to Noel. He’s playing the best ball of his career. pic.twitter.com/4OaT6xOQPl
Maye coming out on top over the weekend in his duel vs. Josh Allen confirmed that there's nothing to be worried about with Maye long-term. Despite being pressured on half his dropbacks against the Bills, according to ESPN, Maye still finished with a .33 EPA/dropback after that figure was -.07 the first three weeks. That early season stretch with six interceptions and nine sacks as the Patriots limped out to 1-2. Of all the quarterbacks on this list, there's still no one else I'd take over Maye if I had to choose one to start a franchise with.
This is a BIGTIME Progression from Drake Maye He works off the Screen & Go to the Backside Glance You rarely see a QB work to the Backside on Screen & Go - kinda looks like a Sluggo Seam Progression. Cool play! pic.twitter.com/Tas9DrlUwG
No one plays down to their competition quite like Nix. It has to be quite the frustrating experience for Broncos faithful. He's fully capable of leading multiple fourth-quarter scoring drives against some of the best defenses in the league and also fully capable of turning into a pumpkin against one of the worst defenses in the league. Through four weeks, it's been more pumpkin than anything else for the 2-2 Broncos, averaging 18.5 points per game.
The obvious question is, after the broken ankle that caused him to miss the AFC championship game last year required two offseason surgeries, could that be a factor in his poor performance?…
author: Mike Renner

title: Former NFL first-round pick abruptly retires after playing 12 snaps in Week 4, per report
summary: The Chicago Bears were hit by a surprise retirement this week
full_text:
After nine NFL seasons, former first-round pick Marcus Davenport has abruptly decided to retire. Davenport played in his first game of the season on Sunday, and he ended up logging a total of 12 snaps for the Bears before making the decision to call it quits.
According to NFL Network , the 30-year-old asked to be released following Sunday's game against the Jets , which the Bears won 23-12. Davenport was credited with making one tackle during his 12 snaps on the field.
Davenport originally signed with the Bears back in mid-August with hopes that he could revive his career in Chicago. He got released on the NFL's Aug. 30 cut-down day, but the Bears did sign him to their practice squad. The veteran pass-rusher didn't see any action during the first three weeks of the season, but Chicago did finally activate him for Sunday's game against the Jets.
Davenport's career began in 2018, when the Saints selected him 14th overall in the NFL Draft . He ended up spending five seasons in New Orleans, and during his time there, he never quite lived up to the hype that comes with being a first-round pick. During his five years in New Orleans, he showed some flashes of his talent at times. In 2019, he started 13 games for the Saints and totaled six sacks. Two years later, he had a career season, racking up six sacks for New Orleans.
The problem for Davenport is that he just couldn't stay on the field. He ended up missing 18 games due to injury in just five seasons with the Saints. Davenport left New Orleans following the 2022 season, and unfortunately, the injury situation never got any better.
In 2023, Davenport sprained his ankle and missed a total of 13 games while playing for the Vikings . He spent 2024 and 2025 in Detroit and missed a total of 24 games with the Lions due to multiple injuries, including a torn triceps.
A big reason Davenport ended up signing in Chicago is that he thought a reunion with defensive coordinator Dennis Allen might help his career. Allen and Davenport spent five seasons together in New Orleans, including 2019 and 2021, when Davenport reached his two highest sack totals.
The fact that the Davenport pick didn't end up working out for New Orleans definitely stung the franchise, because the Saints gave up a lot to get the former University of Texas at San Antonio star.
The Saints went into the 2018 NFL Draft with one pick in the first round at 27th overall. To get Davenport at 14th overall, they had to make a trade to move up 13 spots, and as you can imagine, that wasn't cheap. In a deal with the Packers , the Saints sent their 2018 first-round pick (No. 27), a 2018 fifth-rounder (No. 147) and their 2019 first-round pick in exchange for the 14th overall pick.
After a home run draft in 2017 that included Marshon Lattimore , Alvin Kamara , Trey Hendrickson and Ryan Ramczyk , the Saints took a huge step back with their draft class in 2018.
Davenport's nine-year career will now come to an end with a total of 25 sacks in over 78 games played, which included 43 starts.
author: John Breech

title: Joey Porter Sr. says Steelers 'held us down for three weeks,' celebrates Cowboys victory over Texans
summary: Porter Jr. didn't allow a single target across 25 snaps against Houston as his father, Steelers legend Joey Porter Sr., cheered him on in Dallas gear
full_text:
Joey Porter Jr . made his debut with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday and helped them register a 34-30 come-from-behind victory against C.J. Stroud and the Houston Texans . Porter hadn't played a single snap through the first three weeks of the season and had only a couple of practice days with his new team. But he played 25 defensive snaps vs. the Texans and wasn't targeted while lining up across from Nico Collins , Jaylin Noel and Dalton Schultz .
His debut ended a strange storyline involving a contract dispute with the Pittsburgh Steelers and a back injury. The Steelers traded their young cornerback to the Cowboys in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick last week. And as soon as Porter landed in Dallas, he was ready to rock, new contract or not.
Porter's father, Joey Porter Sr., is, of course, a Steelers legend who spent eight seasons donning the black and yellow. However, he's now ditched the Steelers gear for Cowboys gear. Porter Sr. was in attendance at the Cowboys' huge win in Houston, and he posted a video on Instagram celebrating that he can watch his son play football again.
"I almost forgot what it's like walking through a hostile environment on game day," Porter Sr. said. "They tried to take me away from football for four weeks. I forgot what it feel like. I forgot how intense it gets. It feel like I'm back at home. Walking into a hostile environment. Football is back. They held us down for three weeks; they couldn't hold us down no longer, man."
Who is "they?" One could assume that's the Steelers.
A post shared by Joey Porter (@jportersr55)
It was a thrilling first game for the Porter family, as the Cowboys erased a double-digit deficit in the second half to move to .500. Dak Prescott led an 11-play, 74-yard drive in the fourth quarter, and found CeeDee Lamb on the game-winning touchdown with 40 seconds remaining.
It's been a long road for Porter, who, while he found a change of scenery, is still looking for that next contract. He said he " definitely felt disrespected and undervalued" toward the end of his time in Pittsburgh, but it's all about ball right now.
"Bet on myself. I feel like at the end of the day, you got to always have that in yourself," Porter Jr. said of his 2026 mindset. "Just choose you at the end of the day, and that's what I'm doing."
The Cowboys hope Porter will provide a major boost to a defense that has disappointed up to this point. His 48.1% career completion percentage allowed ranks fourth-lowest in the NFL since he entered the league in 2023 among players with at least 150 passes thrown their way.

title: Tyler Shough reacts to fans booing after Saints blowout loss to Falcons: 'I'd boo, too'
summary: New Orleans was blown out by the Falcons on 'Monday Night Football'
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints were run out of their own building on Monday night as the Atlanta Falcons steamrolled their division rival to a 45-24 victory in Week 4. Given that this is one of the most venomous rivalries in the league, Saints fans weren't happy to see such a lopsided result, especially on a night celebrating the 20th anniversary of the return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina.
And they let the team have it, with boos raining down from the stands.
"Fans understandably are upset," quarterback Tyler Shough said postgame, via ESPN . "We had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of, and you're playing the Falcons, and you lose like that. I mean, I'd boo, too. That sucks."
The game wasn't particularly close, with the Falcons almost instantly jumping out to a 14-0 first-quarter lead. Over that same stretch as Atlanta punched it into the end zone twice, New Orleans went three-and-out, missed a field goal, and fumbled. By halftime, that grew to a 24-7 lead, and Atlanta was effectively off to the races from there.
Cam Jordan candidly said that New Orleans got "punched in the mouth early" and the Falcons "had their way today."
The loss dropped the Saints to 1-3 on the season, leaving them looking up at both the Panthers and Falcons, who finished the first month of the regular season at 2-2.
"I'm disappointed. More than anything, you lose to the Falcons like that and especially on a Monday night game, it sucks," said Shough, who dropped to 0-3 in his career against the Falcons on Monday. "There's nothing you can say, like, 'Ah man, it doesn't suck.' It definitely does. But I do know as a team that we're extremely close, and we're going to keep going and keep our eyes forward.
"We have really good leadership, and our leadership on the team admits that we got to get better... There's no hiding that. But at the same time, it is a long season, and there's a lot of games yet to be played to where we can do that."
Saints' coach Kellen Moore agreed. He called the game "disappointing" for several reasons, including the fact that it was a Monday night matchup with a crowd ready to roll.
"The dome was an incredible night, incredible energy," Moore said . "Didn't coach well enough; didn't play well enough. Obviously, it wasn't good enough.
"It's just disappointing for us, and I know there's frustration for everyone."
The Saints will try to bounce back on a short week as they remain in New Orleans and gear up for a Week 5 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: How non-first-round rookies are faring this NFL season: Denzel Boston among the leaders of the pack
summary: A look at the non-Day 1 selections making an impact on this NFL season, including Browns wideout Denzel Boston and Titans linebacker Anthony Hill Jr
full_text:
The NFL season is nearly a quarter complete, and several teams are already receiving good value on draft selections made in April. The first round represents roughly 12.5% of the selections made in the 2026 NFL Draft, and while they are considered the most likely to contribute early, teams fill out their roster with players selected in other rounds.
Who are those non-first-round picks to take on an important role this season? There are 18 (8 on offense, 10 on defense) who have played 150+ offensive or defensive snaps through four weeks. It's an arbitrary number, but one that serves as a governor for the exercise. Among that sample size, there are six second-round picks, six third-round picks, three fourth-round picks, two fifth-round picks and one undrafted free agent. The undrafted free agent is Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson , whom I wrote about earlier this season .
The Cowboys were an ideal landing spot for Barham because he had played both edge rusher and off-ball linebacker in college. New Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker studied under Vic Fangio with the Eagles . Over the past few years, Philadelphia has had a number of those body types with cross-trained backgrounds, such as Zack Baun , Jihaad Campbell , Nolan Smith , etc.
With Barham, the athleticism jumps off the page, but there are still some inconsistencies in the run game. He has been credited with three pressures by TruMedia, but has not done as well at utilizing his quickness and setting up pass-rush moves as he did at Michigan. The production has been there early, but there is another level he can take his game when Parker grows more comfortable in his role.
Over the past decade, Boston has had the seventh-most receiving yards by a rookie through the first four weeks of the season. Ja'Marr Chase , Justin Jefferson and Puka Nacua are some of the notable names with more receiving yards as rookies through the first four games. TruMedia credits him with zero drops on the season. There have been a few that could have been categorized as such, but the defender was hanging all over him, and a penalty was not called. There were some missed connections with Deshaun Watson that could have manifested even better numbers.
Boston is a big body who can win downfield, but what separates him is the attention to detail in his route-running. He can win at all three levels of the field. When the ball is not coming his way, he is a competent and willing blocker in the run game as well.
He finished the pre-draft cycle as my No. 20 overall prospect.
Notably, Browns right guard Austin Barber is also one of the 18 rookies to meet the criteria. He has been very good despite making the transition from left tackle and looks like a long-term starter for the organization.
Cisse builds speed quickly and is sticky in coverage. There was a blown coverage against Chicago where it looked like he was expecting safety help over the top, but otherwise, he rarely loses leverage.
Cisse had Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels dead to rights in the backfield in Week 4, but he failed to complete the play. He has also not traveled from one side of the field to the other.
Fields has had two receptions and somewhere between two and six targets in each of his four games. On Sunday against the Cardinals , he scored his first touchdown. His two receptions were a byproduct of a lapse in coverage and a scramble drill. Individual catches against the Rams and the Cowboys better represented his potential. He has size and speed, but the route-running has been inconsistent. Fields does bring added value as a blocker in the run game.
He has eight receptions for 126 yards and a touchdown.
Hill was one of my guys leading up to the 2026 NFL Draft. His athleticism is off the charts, and his ability to make an impact extends beyond playing in the box. The Texas product has the range to play sideline to sideline as well as the quickness to thrive as a spot rusher. Hill tends to get stuck on blocks in the box, and improving upon that will allow him to be more effective in fitting run gaps.
Linebacker is a spot where experience is paramount, so starting early in his career allows him to troubleshoot some of his shortcomings, which will benefit him in the long run.
Hurst is more than a space eater in Tampa Bay's offense. He does a good job creating separation and covers ground quickly with long legs. On the season, he has eight receptions for 128 yards and one touchdown, but he had a few deep balls fall haplessly to the ground off his fingertips against Cleveland. Of note, seven of his eight receptions have come to the left side of the field. As the team battles injuries at the receiver position with Jalen McMillan and others, Hurst is a player worthy of a larger target share.
The Buccaneers are now playing undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels in Baker Mayfield's absence.
The younger brother of Chargers quarterback Trey Lance has mostly been a sacrificial player for the Saints : clearing out defenders and blocking in the run game. He generally struggles to create separation, but he has been most effective planting and driving back toward the quarterback.
Lance has four receptions for 50 yards on the year.
Through the first two games, Masses had been targeted eight times and allowed one reception for 16 yards, according to TruMedia. He also had two interceptions in that time period. In Week 3 against the Saints, the rookie out of California was the victim of routes snapped off by Chris Olave . Masses allowed four receptions on the day — all by Olave — for 51 yards. Week 4 is where some of the concerns really took hold. His feet settled a bit at the stem, which enabled his assignment to gain separation, and there was a 42-yard gain to Tyquan Thornton . Masses' eyes lingered in the backfield, and Thornton caught him sleeping on a double move.
Nevertheless, Masses has the size and has met the physical challenge presented by the NFL. His awareness of what is happening around him and his ability to get his eyes back on the ball allow him to make game-changing plays. His performance should inspire confidence from the coaching staff. His potential was evident dating back to his time at Florida International and is one reason why he was a personal favorite in the pre-draft process.
The Jaguars offensive line was a potential problem area coming into the season, but the development of Pregnon, who was my No. 48 prospect overall, has brought stability to the unit. He has a wide, powerful body, and defensive tackles have had a difficult time playing through him; Bengals veterans Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence were a few of the exceptions. Pregnon was inconsistent pulling and engaging blocks in open space, but he has shown improvement as recently as Sunday.
TruMedia credits him with 0 sacks and 6 pressures allowed thus far.
Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley awarded Rodriguez the responsibility of serving as the green dot on defense as a rookie, meaning he communicates defensive calls to the rest of the unit. Rodriguez is an instinctual player who plays square to the line of scrimmage and displays the range to play sideline to sideline.
One year after a fellow linebacker, Carson Schwesinger , broke the drought of linebackers winning Defensive Rookie of the Year, Rodriguez is on the path of building a case of his own. Through four games, he has 46 tackles, including three tackles for a loss and an interception.
Among others in Miami, Dolphins' fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe also met the criteria.
The five other rookies who have played at least 150 snaps, but were not represented on this list, are Buccaneers linebacker Josiah Trotter , Bears cornerback Malik Muhammad , Colts safety A.J. Haulcy , Panthers cornerback Will Lee III and Chargers center Jake Slaughter , who was called into action out of necessity when starter Tyler Biadasz suffered an injury.

title: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB dealing with ankle sprain; Week 5 status still unknown, per report
summary: Jackson injured his ankle in the first half of Sunday's win over the Titans
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens may be without their starting quarterback this weekend. According to a report from NFL Media , Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle sprain that gives him only an "outside chance" to play in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons . Jackson could miss multiple games depending on how his rehabilitation progresses, but the injury is not considered long-term or surgical, per NFL Media.
Jackson got his ankle rolled up on the Ravens' final play of the first half during last week's win over the Tennessee Titans and did not return to the game. Ravens coach Jesse Minter initially seemed to suggest Jackson could have returned to the game had it not already been essentially in hand at the break, but this reporting makes that seem rather unlikely.
The Ravens are 3-1 through the first four weeks of the season, and their offense has been highly explosive under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. That's especially been the case in the three weeks Zay Flowers has been on the field, as Baltimore has averaged 33 points per game in those contests while scoring just 17 in a loss to the New Orleans Saints when Flowers sat out with a hamstring injury.
If Jackson is unable to suit up for Week 5 and beyond, the Ravens will turn to backup Tyler Huntley . Huntley played the second half against Tennessee on Sunday and went 8-of-9 for 63 scoreless yards and ran four times for 16 yards. He's made 16 starts in his career, going 7-9. Across 31 total appearances, he's completed 66.6% of his passes at an average of 5.9 yards per attempt, with 13 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
It's highly likely the Ravens will lean on their Derrick Henry -led rushing attack if Jackson has to miss time, but that could prove difficult in their game against the Falcons. Atlanta has lit up the scoreboard in each of the last two weeks and forced its opponents to play from behind. In such a scenario, it would be much more difficult for the Ravens to mount a comeback without Jackson at the helm.

title: NFC South Week 4 Review: 2 teams pull ahead and 2 fall behind
summary: Like most teams around the league, the division has been hit hard with injuries across the board. Whoever overcomes theirs will be the last team standing. This week, those teams were the Falcons and Panthers, who put on a display of offensive firepower. On the other end of the spectrum, you have the Saints and […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Chuba Hubbard #30 of the Carolina Panthers runs with the ball and scores a touchdown against Detroit Lions during an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Like most teams around the league, the division has been hit hard with injuries across the board. Whoever overcomes theirs will be the last team standing. This week, those teams were the Falcons and Panthers, who put on a display of offensive firepower. On the other end of the spectrum, you have the Saints and Buccaneers, who are now multiple games under .500. Here’s the Week 4 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4) Week 4 Result: Buccaneers 14 – Packers 17 Week 5 Opponent: Dallas Cowboys The Buccaneers are off to their worst start since 2013. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has been unable to get anything going, and Todd Bowles’ seat looks hotter than ever. UDFA Jalon Daniels looked like a UDFA, and Bucky Irving and company have looked quite pedestrian after having success in prior seasons. Fans are sick of Bowles, but his defense hasn’t been the main issue; with Antoine Winfield Jr. expected to miss 2-4 weeks with a broken rib, that could change quickly. There is no rest for the wicked, as the Buccaneers have a quick turnaround against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Carolina Panthers (2-2) Week 4 Result: Panthers 32 – Lions 26 Week 5 Opponent: Philadelphia Eagles Coming into the game, the Panthers injury report had to be posted on two pages. Luckily for Carolina, all they needed was Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan. The duo was unstoppable, racking up 14 completions for 192 yards and 2 touchdowns. The defense did just enough to hold off the Lions, and they kept Jahmyr Gibbs in check on the ground. This team hasn’t been able to stack these performances multiple weeks in a row, but they are in position to win this division. Their next test will be on the road in Philadelphia against an Eagles team that looks like a shell of its former self. BRYCE YOUNG pic.twitter.com/5dq6OdFqrN — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 5, 2026 New Orleans Saints (1-3) Week 4 Result: Saints 24 – Falcons 45 Week 5 Opponent: Minnesota Vikings The Saints have been a volatile product through the first quarter of the season, but they had no high moments in this rivalry game. What started as a celebration ended as a travesty. They had no answer for Atlanta’s run game and surrendered big plays when the Falcons dialed up the deep ball. Kellen Moore’s seat is heating up as the team falls two games below .500. Their season isn’t over, but it will be soon if they can’t sort out their struggles. They’ll host the undefeated Vikings next Sunday. Atlanta Falcons (2-2) Week 4 Result: Falcons 45 – Saints 24 Week 5 Opponent: Baltimore Ravens Week 2 feels like it happened a year ago. The Falcons have been a completely different team with Penix under center. Atlanta spoiled the Saints’ “Domecoming” and dominated from the opening snap. The Robinsons are the league’s best running back duo and accounted for 5 rushing touchdowns and nearly 200 yards. Penix is doing his part by taking care of the football and hitting shots when called upon. You can’t say enough about what Jeff Ulbrich is getting out of this hobbled defense. They pressured Tyler Shough all night and maintained the lead through all four quarters. Everything looks like it’s finally coming together. The Falcons return home for their 3rd straight primetime game and will face off against the Ravens. Bijan Robinson ➖19 carries ➖145 yards ➖2 TDs That guys rocks. pic.twitter.com/ZUCAStw1GJ — That Guy Rocked NFL (@NFLRocked) October 6, 2026 The division is starting to take shape, and the early favorites for the division crown are the Falcons and Panthers. If both teams keep things going, the rest of the league will have to respect the South.

title: Falcons vs. Ravens odds: Opening lines for Week 5 matchup
summary: The Falcons season completely changed complexion over the past two weeks, with Atlanta dominating the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football and the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football. After starting the year as the league’s worst offense behind third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, the Falcons are now the league’s best offense since Michael […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 17: Jase McClellan #30 of the Atlanta Falcons runs with the ball during a NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M & T Bank on August 17, 2024 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons season completely changed complexion over the past two weeks, with Atlanta dominating the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football and the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football. After starting the year as the league’s worst offense behind third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, the Falcons are now the league’s best offense since Michael Penix Jr. returned to the lineup. Talk about a dramatic transformation. Atlanta also continued their elite play on primetime, moving to an astounding 10-1 on Monday Night Football over the past decade. What they did to New Orleans in their home stadium on the anniversary of the Saints return to the Superdome is perhaps their best performance yet. To put it simply, this Falcons team has defied all expectations and are now tied for the NFC South lead at 2-2. That dominance and defiance of expectations are the reason that the Falcons are now 3-point home favorites against the Baltimore Ravens (3-1) on Sunday Night Football in Week 5 per FanDuel. Some of that certainly has to do with the uncertain status of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, who left Week 4’s game with an ankle injury and is considered a long shot to play. Even without that, I would’ve expected to see these odds fairly even given Atlanta’s incredible play over the previous two weeks. We’ll keep a close eye on the injury report going into Week 5, but the Falcons have an outstanding opportunity to get their first winning record of the season this week. The Ravens will not be an easy opponent, even without Lamar Jackson, so the team will need to prepare for a tough battle. Baltimore still possesses a terrific rushing attack headlined by Derrick Henry, along with a stout defense that is currently 10th in total yardage allowed. A defensive slugfest seems to be the expectation given the 43.5-point over/under, but much of that likely has to do with Lamar’s expected absence.
