title: Why Khalil Mack actually makes sense for Chicago Bears to chase at trade deadline
summary: Could the Chicago Bears be in the market for a reunion with one of its biggest stars from the last 10 years? ESPN insider Dan Graziano recently predicted the Bears would be buyers at the November 10 trade deadline, citing their 3-1 record—a promising development given Caleb Williams’ absence for the past two games—and general […]
full_text: The Chicago Bears' Khalil Mack (52) rushes the passer against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 10, 2021, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. (Brian Cassella/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Could the Chicago Bears be in the market for a reunion with one of its biggest stars from the last 10 years? ESPN insider Dan Graziano recently predicted the Bears would be buyers at the November 10 trade deadline , citing their 3-1 record—a promising development given Caleb Williams’ absence for the past two games—and general manager Ryan Poles’ aggressive approach to adding players. “The Bears have needs at defensive back and pass rusher. Assuming they survive this current stretch with QB Caleb Williams injured…the Bears should be on the hunt for the player or two they believe can get them over the top.” One of those players just might be Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack, who started for the Bears from 2018-2021. With Los Angeles circling the toilet at 0-4 and seemingly no end in sight for their struggles in a competitive division, the odds of them holding onto the 35-year-old pass rusher, who signed a one-year, $18 million deal to stay with the Chargers last offseason, aren’t great. Interestingly enough, though, Mack has remained productive as he’s aged (when he’s been on the field). So far, he has three sacks on 14 pressures so far in 2016, and a solid 79.3 grade on Pro Football Focus , which ranks 15th out of 108 edges, and his run defense has held up even better than his pass rushing. Sounds like a guy the Chicago Bears, who have played surprisingly well on defense but still need more able bodies, could use. (No shade to Austin Booker and Dayo Odeyingbo, but Mack would easily clear both of them in this lineup.) The neat part: it would likely come pretty cheap at this point. For one thing, the Bears wouldn’t be on the hook for the whole $18 million of Mack’s contract, which included a $10 million signing bonus. Chicago only has about $7 million in cap space currently, according to Over the Cap , but a quick contract restructure and simply waiting a few more weeks to make a deal, ensuring the Chargers eat more of the money, could keep the monetary costs down. As for trade compensation, a fourth-rounder or something in that range should probably get the job done, especially considering his age and injury issues the past few seasons. In other words, what’s not to like? Mack isn’t what he was when the Bears made that blockbuster trade with the Raiders to bring him to Chicago, where he signed a then-record $141 million contract and tore the league up in 2018. But he doesn’t need to be. He just has to be exactly what he is: a dependable counterpart to Montez Sweat who can stop the run and keep pushing the pocket. This time around, it’d be a lot cheaper to get him in the building. And the payoff for this Bears team in what looks like a wide-open NFL season could be massive for both sides.

title: Bengals Film Room: Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight play well vs. Jaguars
summary: I thought the Cincinnati Bengals defense played well enough to win the game on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A couple of untimely turnovers by the offense did not help their cause. Ultimately, the Bengals were unable to pull out the victory. They lost 22-17 to the Jaguars and fell to 2-2 on the season. […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Barrett Carter (49) celebrates a stop after tackling Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (33) in the first quarter of the NFL Week 4 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I thought the Cincinnati Bengals defense played well enough to win the game on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A couple of untimely turnovers by the offense did not help their cause. Ultimately, the Bengals were unable to pull out the victory. They lost 22-17 to the Jaguars and fell to 2-2 on the season. There are still things to be fixed on the defense. Most notably, they are battling a tackling issue with one of their starting safeties. Overall though, this was a much better performance from the defense than we saw the week before in Pittsburgh. Specifically, I thought Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. had the best game combined of the season for the linebackers against Jacksonville. Demetrius Knight Jr. finished the game with 6 tackles and played much more aggressively at times than we have seen in some previous weeks. When he is aggressively attacking downhill, it is typically when he is playing at his best. We saw him shoot a gap early in the game, ending up with a tackle for loss against Bhayshul Tuten as a result. Explosive tackle for loss from Demetrius Knight Jr. pic.twitter.com/GFjFXhtpSg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Knight and Carter combining for another run stop pic.twitter.com/zeI1paSyDg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Knight and Carter in on another run stop, this time with some help from Dexter Lawrence. That was the best game the young linebackers have both played at the same time this season. pic.twitter.com/4zUb0LhGNh — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Things were not perfect for Knight on the day, as there were still a couple of questionable angles taken during the game. In particular, the touchdown run in the second half was a play that Knight looked out of position coming up near the line of scrimmage. He wasn’t the only one to question on that play, but it was probably his most notable negative play. A lot of guys you can call out on this touchdown run. Knight and Mafe near the line of scrimmage being out of position and then Ivey missing a tackle with Jules getting blocked and Battle taking a poor angle toward the ball carrier. pic.twitter.com/2OWD1psm7o — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 As solid as Knight was during the game overall, I think Barrett Carter might have been even more impressive. Carter finished the game with a team-high 11 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a pass defensed against Parker Washington. Carter was in a really good position on the talented slot receiver for the Jaguars. He did a good job of not turning him at all on the play, which would have certainly drawn a flag from Sunday’s flag-happy crew. Good pass defensed by Barrett Carter. We know what Ron Torbert would have done if this was with the Super Bowl on the line. pic.twitter.com/LHo3PsNekz — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Carter looked very instinctive during the game on Sunday. He was decisive, quick to react against the run, and wasn’t credited with a single missed tackle during the game. Barrett Carter quickly closing off the running lane with Jonathan Allen getting there to finish off the tackle. pic.twitter.com/PEiA20T9Un — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Any game where your linebackers do not record a single missed tackle combined seems like a win to me. The biggest question will be consistency going forward. We need these guys to start doing this week-in and week-out for this defense. If there is a glaring weakness on this defense, it isn’t the linebacker play right now. It is the play of Jordan Battle. The Bengals will have to get healthy to consider replacing Battle in the starting lineup. I don’t think that should be in question for these linebackers. We just need more performances from them like we saw on Sunday against Jacksonville.

title: Bengals News: Chad Johnson believes in the backup wide receivers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading into Week 5 riding a two-game losing streak, and both Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are nursing injuries. The Bengals are facing the Dolphins in Miami on Sunday in a game they need to win to go into the bye week on a high note. It’s currently unclear […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading into Week 5 riding a two-game losing streak, and both Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are nursing injuries. The Bengals are facing the Dolphins in Miami on Sunday in a game they need to win to go into the bye week on a high note. It’s currently unclear as to whether or not Chase and Higgins, the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, will be able to play in Miami. If they don’t, it’ll be Mitchell Tinsley, who was signed off the Texans’ practice squad and rejoined the team last week, and rookie Dohnte Meyers (it’s also possible Colbie Young could play as well) catching passes from Joe Burrow at wide receiver while Mike Gesicki fills in the gaps. One guy who has confidence in the Bengals’ backup receivers is Cincinnati great Chad Johnson, who told Geoff Hobson he’s excited to see the game from his home city of Miami. “And for them, that’s a good thing because if (Ja’Marr) Chase and Tee (Higgins) can’t go., I have the utmost confidence in Tinsley and Myers being able to make plays,” he said, per Hobson . “It’s all up to Zac Taylor understanding their skill sets and what their strengths are, and putting them in positions to be able to make those plays. Even if Tee and Chase can’t go, I mean it’d be a blow, but I still won’t feel that bad understanding how good Tinsley and Meyers are.” Here’s what else is going on: Though there is a small sample size, the Bengals have never lost when wearing orange jerseys, white pants with orange stripes and orange socks. That’s what they’re wearing on Sunday in Miami when they look to bounce back against the Dolphins. They’re 2-0 in that combination, and they’re 28-11-1 in orange jerseys since they were unveiled for the first time in 2004. Bengals’ offensive approach could change. What might be tweaked after 2 straight losses “A very honest and brutal Monday. Which we deserved,” Karras said. “We need to get ourselves back. Wake up. It doesn’t feel like it was a crazy game because we had a chance to win, but I have a pit in my stomach similar to Minnesota last year as an offensive line. That was not very good.” While it isn’t confirmed, it’s possible Colbie Young could suit up on Sunday in Miami. Zac Taylor didn’t rule him out. With Andrei Iosivas on IR, Ja’Marr Chase in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins dealing with an adductor injury that could keep him on the sidelines for an unknown period of time, Young being able to suit up on Sunday could help make sure the Bengals don’t extend their losing streak to three. title: The Bengals’ under-center offense has been a disaster
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals spent the majority of training camp trying to get better at playing under-center offensively. Somehow, all of that preparation has actually made them worse at it. The Bengals are currently dead last in the entire league when going under-center. They are averaging just 3.3 yards per play from under-center. For comparison, they […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals spent the majority of training camp trying to get better at playing under-center offensively. Somehow, all of that preparation has actually made them worse at it. The Bengals are currently dead last in the entire league when going under-center. They are averaging just 3.3 yards per play from under-center. For comparison, they averaged 5.1 yards per play from under-center during the 2025 season. Their running game has not been effective, Joe Burrow does not typically look as comfortable having to operate play-action passes, and they are going under-center at a 54% higher rate than they were during last season. All of that adds up to a more ineffective offense than what we have seen from Cincinnati in the past. At what point do the Bengals just decide to completely scrap under-center unless they have a lead late in the game? To me, it feels like we are getting closer to seeing that happen. If anything, I would like the Bengals to incorporate some up-tempo offense earlier in the game. This team is built to play with a lead. They have the pass rush now to get after quarterbacks, and all of the under-center stuff should be more effective when you have a lead to play with. Theoretically, under-center should help your offense be more effective. It should open up play-action, and it should help keep your quarterback from having to throw the ball 54 times a game. In reality, it actually doesn’t help this team. It keeps them from getting an early lead, the running game is even more bogged down than it is from shotgun, and Joe Burrow is at his best when he can see everything in front of him directly off of the snap. The Bengals will play in Miami this week and be looking to get back in the win column. If they try to continue going under-center a lot, they might just give Miami the confidence they need to get their first win of the season. Regardless of how that game turns out, the Bengals will have to seriously self-scout themselves during the bye week on what type of offense they plan to run primarily going forward. As of right now, I don’t know why they would keep trying to beat a dead horse by using more under-center offense that just isn’t working. The Bengals spent an offseason building an under-center offense. Last year: 5.1 yards a play from it This year: 3.3 Dead last in the NFL on 54% more snaps. pic.twitter.com/3zevwIEJZQ — Stick to the Model (@StickToTheModel) October 5, 2026

title: Browns defense: ‘Jared Verse setting everyone else up,’ man coverage at an ‘absurd’ level
summary: As the Cleveland Browns were busy losing a ton of games the last two years, their defense was playing at an elite level led by DC Jim Schwartz and DE Myles Garrett. When the Browns decided to hire Todd Monken as their next head coach, instead of Schwartz, and the veteran coordinator decided to walk […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns were busy losing a ton of games the last two years, their defense was playing at an elite level led by DC Jim Schwartz and DE Myles Garrett . When the Browns decided to hire Todd Monken as their next head coach , instead of Schwartz, and the veteran coordinator decided to walk away instead of coaching the team, eyes were raised about a possible defensive turndown. Then Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams and everyone expected Cleveland’s defense to get worse by a lot. After a Week 1 destruction, fans were calling for Schwartz to return . Instead of falling apart, the Browns defense came together with a lot of pass rush pressure and a team effort to three straight victories, leading to the top spot in the AFC North . In a video podcast about preseason expectations that were completely off, Cleveland’s defense received a lot of praise: The Browns defense is far from perfect, but they are far less predictable with DC Mike Rutenberg than they were with Schwartz and seem to be playing a more unified approach without the “easy button” of Garrett. With teams no longer double teaming one guy, running away from Garrett, and scheming against one player, different Cleveland defenders have been able to make an impact. After Week 1, where Rutenberg failed to play to his defensive backs’ strength in man coverage, not only did the Browns play in 73% man versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, but Cleveland is lapping other teams in the coverage style for the season: Highest % of defensive man coverage this season Browns 61.0% Bears 49.4% Chiefs 46.6% Patriots 46.0% Giants 45.2% pic.twitter.com/2EiJoUoYz2 — PFF (@PFF) October 6, 2026 Even the best units usually run zone coverage more than 50% of the time, for a variety of reasons. Man coverage is physically hard for players to run consistently, receivers know their routes and have the ability to separate often, and consistent man coverage can get beat with specific route combinations and often leads to quarterback scrambles being wide open. None of that has been a major problem for Cleveland because the defensive backfield is very talented, and the pass rush pressure, starting with Jared Verse and Mason Graham , along with blitzers, has sped up the clock on quarterbacks. Speedy linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams have helped contain the quarterback as well. No Schwartz and no Garrett led to strong convictions that the Browns defense would fall off in 2026. Instead, Rutenberg and the talented players have played at an elite level since Week 1, with more challenges to come.

title: Trade whispers: 2 pass rushers might be available if the Browns are interested
summary: After the Cleveland Browns traded off EDGE rusher Myles Garrett in the offseason, the fanbase was given a dialogue that his replacement, Jared Verse, could fill in nicely. After all, he had two Pro Bowls in each of his years in the league, plus won the “NFL Rookie Defensive Player of the Year” award after […]
full_text: After the Cleveland Browns traded off EDGE rusher Myles Garrett in the offseason , the fanbase was given a dialogue that his replacement, Jared Verse, could fill in nicely . After all, he had two Pro Bowls in each of his years in the league, plus won the “NFL Rookie Defensive Player of the Year” award after a very good rookie season. The narrative was that Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire would hold down the fort on the right side while Verse would wreak havoc on the left. RELATED: MACK’S CONTRACT, SALARY CAP HIT Yet, none of that is happening. The pass rush so far has been very anemic, to say the least, though sacks are not everything . Currently, the Browns rank #23 in overall defense. How can they improve their pass rush? There are two pass rushers who are rumored to become available before the NFL trade deadline on November 11: Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals and Khalil Mack of the Los Angeles Chargers . Should Cleveland GM Andrew Berry attempt to bring in a proven pass rusher this season? Sweat (6’-5”, 265 pounds) was drafted in the fourth round of the 2018 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. When the Eagles’ DC, Jonathan Gannon, became the head coach of the Cardinals, his contract extension expired, and Gannon had his team go after Sweat. The talented defensive end then inked a four-year deal worth up to $76.4 million with $41 million guaranteed. Sweat, age 29, came through last year with 12 sacks. He also had 17 QB hits, 30 total tackles, 13 tackles for loss, I fumble recovery, 2 pass defenses, 4 forced fumbles, 7 knockdowns, 9 hurries, 28 pressures, and zero missed tackles. He played alongside DT Calais Campbell, who was an excellent pass rusher as well, and had 6.5 sacks, 16 QB hits, and 18 pressures, to go along with other stats. The inside/outside pass duo of Sweat and Campbell worked extremely well for Arizona. After losing a franchise-record 14 games, the Cardinals fired Gannon. The two men were close. Sweat was placed on the PUP list early due to a knee injury that was never disclosed. He did not practice at all during training camp or play in any of the preseason games. His first action since the final game of the 2025 season was the Week 1 contest against the Chargers. So far this year, he is a shell of himself. Sweat rarely generates any actual pass rush, although he is going after it every play he is inserted. In 2026, he has just one sack. And that occurred in the last game when the defensive tackle forced the quarterback out of the pocket and into the arms of Sweat. In four games, Sweat has 7 total tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 2 QB hits, 5 pressures, 1 knockdown, 3 hurries, and zero missed tackles. He is being paid $9.78 million this year with a cap hit of $16.4 million. Mack (6’-3”, 269 pounds) is on his third team with the Chargers. Everywhere he has played, the fanbase acts like they just signed Lawrence Taylor. He was selected with the fifth overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft by the Oakland Raiders, and by his second year in the league, he was destroying every offense he faced. In Mack’s final three seasons with the Raiders, he had sack totals of 15, 11, and 10.5, QB hits of 24, 26, and 22, plus double-digit pressures each year. The Raiders then traded Mack, now age 35, to the Chicago Bears in 2018 for two first-round picks, a third, and a sixth. In return, Chicago also received a second-round pick, plus a conditional fifth-round pick. He responded with getting 12.5 sacks in 2018 and 36 during his four years in Chicago. The Bears then traded Mack to the Chargers in 2022 after a foot injury concluded his final year with the Bears. Chicago received a second-round draft pick while Los Angeles received the player plus a sixth-round selection. In his first game with LA, Mack had three sacks plus a forced fumble. He had a career high in sacks in 2023 with 17 sacks. So far this season, he had three sacks, 14 total tackles, 5 QB hits, and 8 pressures, among other stats. For his 13-year career, Mack has played in 183 games and started 181, 676 total tackles, 153 tackles for loss, 116 sacks, 13 fumble recoveries, 36 forced fumbles, 43 batted passes, 201 QB hits, 49 knockdowns, 110 hurries, 239 pressures, and 41 missed tackles. Mack is currently on a one-year $18 million fully guaranteed contract extension. For the Browns, after four games, the pass rush isn’t what it should be. There may be other pass-rushing defensive ends that could be pried from a team’s roster, but these two are rumored to be on the trading block before the NFL trade deadline. 2026 Browns Defensive End Stats: Sacks Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 0 Sam Williams – 1 Derek Barnett – 0 QB hits Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 2 Derek Barnett – 2 Knockdowns Isaiah McGuire – 0 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 1 Derek Barnett – 2 Hurries Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 0 Sam Williams – 0 Derek Barnett – 1 Pressures Isaiah McGuire – 4 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 2 Derek Barnett – 3 Should the Browns trade for either veteran pass rusher? title: Scouting Browns Week 5 opponent: These aren’t the same old New York Jets
summary: As the Cleveland Browns prepare to try to extend their winning streak, the schedule brings them an AFC East opponent in the New York Jets. These two teams played last season, with New York coming out with the victory. Similar to the Browns, the Jets are undergoing a rebuild of their own. Veteran quarterback Geno […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns prepare to try to extend their winning streak , the schedule brings them an AFC East opponent in the New York Jets . These two teams played last season, with New York coming out with the victory. Similar to the Browns, the Jets are undergoing a rebuild of their own. Veteran quarterback Geno Smith is back at the place he started his career. Offensively, the unit has young talent led by wide receiver Garrett Wilson and running back Breece Hall, who could miss Week 5 with an injury. Defensively, the unit has some form of veteran presence after lacking in that department previously. Cleveland is a road underdog heading into Week 5 preparations. Scouting New York ahead of this week’s matchup looks like this Like the Browns, the Jets received a facelift on offense On paper, the Jets offense is much improved from a year ago. For starters, having a veteran quarterback like Smith helps. This unit lacked competent quarterback play, but seems to have it now with Smith, who was in a rough situation last season with the Las Vegas Raiders. Offensively, the unit has a competent offensive line and good receiving talent. Wilson is a top 20 receiver, Hall is underrated, and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq gives New York some versatility in their tight end room. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich isn’t necessarily the best, but he has somehow kept this offense playing at a competent level. HC Aaron Glenn could be coaching for his job It’s hard to say that this is the same Jets team from last year. Head coach Aaron Glenn has gone through the ups and downs, but it’s fair to question whether this will be his last season in Gang Green. On paper, New York is better than last year. However, the team should be 2-2 instead of 1-3. The loss to the Green Bay Packers was more about how the Jets gave the game away instead of the Packers outright winning it. This past Sunday, New York came out flat and were outmatched against a Chicago Bears squad missing superstar quarterback Caleb Williams. People questioned why the Jets chose to bring back Glenn after last season considering how it went, but if New York doesn’t show any improvement as the season goes on, the team will likely make a change with Glenn, perhaps sooner rather than later. The Jets defense is improved (?) Last season, the New York Jets were pretty abysmal on the defensive side of the ball. Before Week 4, the Jets defense had the longest streak without an interception until it was broken by safety Minkah Fitzpatrick on Sunday against the Bears. This season, the unit has veterans on that side of the ball in linebacker Demario Davis and Fitzpatrick, someone Browns fans have high on their dislike list. The secondary has talented pieces in cornerback Azareye’h Thomas and rookie D’Angelo Ponds, however as a collective, the secondary has issues. In terms of their pass rush, it’s lacking. Despite attempting to improve the area in the offseason, the unit is 29th in terms of pressure rate, and rookie David Bailey hasn’t shown the abilities that made the Jets draft him second overall. On paper, the unit appears to be improved, but their on-field performance tells a different story. Whether the defense turns it around is something that is worth monitoring. Overall, the Jets have talent to make things tough on the Browns in Week 5, especially with more veterans on the roster. How concerned are you about the Jets in Week 5 versus the Browns? title: Browns make a potential key move at the QB position
summary: Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry and head coach Todd Monken should be pleased with the current state of the franchise.  The club is riding a three-game winning streak and is tied for first in the AFC North; the defense is finding its footing under defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg; and the rookies are pulling their […]
full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry and head coach Todd Monken should be pleased with the current state of the franchise. The club is riding a three-game winning streak and is tied for first in the AFC North; the defense is finding its footing under defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg; and the rookies are pulling their weight and working to outshine last year’s draft class. Even quarterback Deshaun Watson, though he hasn’t put together a fully productive four quarters yet, has been good enough when the Browns have needed him. This isn’t the first trip around the block for Berry and Monken, of course, and they know that given Watson’s injury history, not to mention his overall poor play since arriving in town, they may need to call on another quarterback at a moment’s notice. Which is why Berry made the mostly unsurprising move on Tuesday to open the 21-day practice window for quarterback Dillon Gabriel, who missed the past four games while on injured reserve with a back injury. Dillon Gabriel and Kalia Davis are eligible to return to practice, and other roster moves 📰 » https://t.co/rylK5uo1wO pic.twitter.com/zN110YYg92 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 6, 2026 The transaction means that the Browns now have three weeks to either add Gabriel to the 53-man roster, put him back on injured reserve for the rest of the season, trade him, or release him. Gabriel was last seen throwing for 186 yards and three touchdowns against the New England Patriots in the preseason finale despite not receiving a single practice rep with the first-team offense all summer. The fact that Cleveland brought Gabriel back from injured reserve as soon as he was eligible could be a sign that Monken wants to ensure he has a viable backup quarterback on hand in case Watson stumbles in the coming weeks. Gabriel was not the only familiar face returning, as the Browns also opened the practice window for defensive tackle Kalia Davis, who has been out since suffering a quadriceps injury during training camp. The defensive tackle position has been dealing with injuries, as Mason Graham was knocked out of last week’s game against Pittsburgh with a sprained MCL and an ankle injury, and Mike Hall Jr. left with an ankle injury, although he was able to return to the field before the game was over and contributed a key sack of Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers. In other transactions, the Browns signed wide receiver James Proche II after a tryout earlier in the day , and defensive tackle Chris Williams to the practice squad, while releasing running back Eric Gray, punter Wes Pahl, and offensive tackle Xavier Truss from the practice squad. Proche was originally drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in 2020. He has played in 71 career games between the Ravens, Browns, and Tennessee Titans. He has served primarily as a kick returner, with 68 punt returns and 68 kickoff returns, although he does have 34 receptions for 364 yards on his account. Williams originally signed with the Indianapolis Colts as an undrafted free agent in 2020. He has played in 44 career games between the Colts and the Chicago Bears. summary: It is Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are officially in the exact middle of NFL power rankings. Around the quarter point of the season, the Browns are in first place in the division, and have turned heads with their young core of players, Deshaun Watson showing more promise, and […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 01: Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the second quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are officially in the exact middle of NFL power rankings. Around the quarter point of the season, the Browns are in first place in the division, and have turned heads with their young core of players, Deshaun Watson showing more promise, and the defense turning things up a notch. Overall, the Browns went up by 4.6 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.1 . Ranking-wise, that is still third in the division. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 16 (up 9 spots) Can you believe they are 3-1 and tied for first in the division? Who saw that coming? Not me. ESPN – No. 19 (up 5 spots) Four words to describe the first four weeks: A rebound beyond belief. The first game of the Todd Monken era got off to an ominous start, with a 24-point road loss to the Jaguars . But instead of crumbling, the Browns responded with three consecutive victories, including a primetime win at home over the Steelers to put them atop the AFC North. Cleveland is back to playing its aggressive, man-to-man style of defense, and QB Deshaun Watson is playing his best football in a Browns uniform. He has led three straight winning drives. NFL.com – No. 17 (no change) Hey, look at that: a three-game winning streak for the Browns, a team I thought might not eclipse four wins this season. They’re tied for first in the AFC North and have regained their defensive identity, harassing Aaron Rodgers all Thursday night. Even better: Deshaun Watson and the offense found a rhythm before the fourth quarter. Cautious optimism reigns here, because I’m not certain Cleveland has beaten a good team yet. Sporting News – No. 17 (up 4 spots) The Browns have done some good work to take down the Buccaneers, Panthers and Steelers during their three-game winning streak. Deshaun Watson is feeling it with his young support all of a sudden and their defense is adjusting well without Myles Garrett. Yahoo Sports – No. 20 (no change) Cleveland should be happy to be on a three-game winning streak. It’s probably not sustainable. The Browns have had three very close wins, with the go-ahead scores coming with 3:51, 1:48 and 10 seconds to play. Their point differential is -14. Their DVOA is 23rd. And still, it’s OK to be excited. The young cast around the quarterback position is flashing a lot of talent. Rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion Jr. already look good, and second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr. is playing well again this season. Deshaun Watson is still very unlikely to be the long-term answer at quarterback but if the Browns get that right in the 2027 NFL Draft, the future is bright. And the Browns are at the Jets next, so a 4-1 start is possible. “This ain’t the old Browns,” Cleveland defensive end Jared Verse said, according to Cleveland.com. “We’ve got new swag.” Bleacher Report – No. 20 (up 8 spots) The Cleveland Browns are sitting at 3-1 a month into the 2026 season, and yet, it’s still a little difficult to take this team seriously. The Browns have won three straight but also by a combined 10 points. Their defense has been more good than great; they’re still trying to get the ground game going, and they overcame an uneven second half by Deshaun Watson on Thursday night. That said, Cleveland is significantly better than pretty much anyone expected coming into the season and has a legitimate chance to move to 4-1 against the New York Jets next week. USA Today – No. 12 (up 6 spots) Kardiac Kids Part Deux? Deshaun Watson is the first Browns quarterback since Brian Sipe, the league MVP in 1980, to engineer a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter of three consecutive games. full_text: While Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry knows no bounds when it comes to making adjustments to the team’s rosters, this is not the Luke Floriea post many fans are hoping to see at some point. The Kent State star and training camp hero is still unsigned after only one reported workout . Berry is reportedly bringing in a former Browns receiver for a workout on Tuesday. With veteran Tylan Wallace injured , Cleveland’s depth chart lacks a lot of veteran presence outside of ( possibly on the trading block ) Jerry Jeudy to help support the young star receivers at the position. James Proche III could help fill that role if his workout goes well on Tuesday: Free agent WR/PR James Proche is working out for the Cleveland Browns today, per source. Proche was with the Browns previously (2023-24). — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 6, 2026 A sixth-round pick of the Baltimore Ravens in 2020, Proche has played for three teams, including last year with the Tennessee Titans. Primarily a kick return specialist, Proche has only caught 34 passes for 364 yards in 71 career games. He has returned 68 punts and 60 kicks, including 41 punt returns for Cleveland spread over two seasons. So far in 2026, RB Raheim Sanders and WRs Malachi Corley and KC Concepcion have taken on the return duties for the Browns. Do you think the Browns should add a punt returner to keep Concepcion fresh? title: Browns trade talk: Khalil Mack’s contract, salary cap hit, and performance review
summary: With the Cleveland Browns 3-1 and at the top of the AFC North heading into Week 5 as underdogs on the road against the New York Jets, everything around the team is more fun. Talk of trading away a wide receiver or quarterback is about what is best for the team, not just about adding […]
full_text: With the Cleveland Browns 3-1 and at the top of the AFC North heading into Week 5 as underdogs on the road against the New York Jets , everything around the team is more fun. Talk of trading away a wide receiver or quarterback is about what is best for the team, not just about adding draft capital for the future. With the NFL trade deadline over a month away, the Browns have five games to make a decision about what direction they see the team going after the deadline. That doesn’t mean GM Andrew Berry will wait. DE Khalil Mack is already rumored to be on the market and fits a role that Cleveland could use help with: pass rush. Berry spent most of the offseason trying to add another edge player, and that was before DE Alex Wright was lost for the season due to injury. The 35-year-old Mack, who signed a one-year deal to return to the Los Angeles Chargers, may be the first big domino to fall as his team has floundered to a 0-4 start. Mack’s $18 million contract seems big, but a trade would only cost the Browns a portion of the $8 million in base salary, as the Chargers paid $10 million as a signing bonus. As Jack Duffin of The OBR explains, how much it would cost Cleveland depends on when a deal happened: How does the cap work for team acquiring Mack. $10m signing bonus stays with the Chargers as dead cap The remaining $8m is base salary. So 1/18th of it for each week of the season. Trade now 4/18 Chargers & 14/18 new team. In two weeks 6/18 and 12/18 https://t.co/xJsqA4cyWy — Jack Duffin (@JackDuffin) October 5, 2026 Quick math says that acquiring Mack this week would cost just over $6 million in cap space and that would drop about a million every two weeks. At the start of the season, Berry had over $12 million in cap space to work with and could get creative with Mack’s contract if the two sides were amenable. Is Mack’s performance at age 35 worth it? So far, the veteran has three sacks, five QB hits, and five tackles for loss in four contests. Pro Football Focus has him ranked 13th in total pressures in the NFL and gave him an 86.1 grade in Week 4 : Mack produced one sack and four pressures while leading the team with four stops. He also posted an 82.0 in run defense and a 69.6 in pass rush (second best on the team). Suffice to say, Mack continues to produce. Given his age, production, and salary, Los Angeles is likely to receive a high Day 3 pick for the veteran pass rusher. It is also possible, especially for a team like the Browns with a lot of young players, that the Chargers attempt to do a player-for-player swap instead of draft capital. Are you in favor of the Browns trading for Mack? If so, how high of a draft pick would you be willing to give up? If not, who do you think the team should be looking to add in a trade? title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Still looking for answers against the Buccaneers
summary: In the NFL, you take any win, no matter how many warts it has. And make no mistake, there were warts all over the Dallas Cowboys’ 34-30 win over the winless Houston Texans. From the way the defense struggled at so many points in the game to the anemic run offense outside of the redzone, […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images In the NFL, you take any win, no matter how many warts it has. And make no mistake, there were warts all over the Dallas Cowboys’ 34-30 win over the winless Houston Texans. From the way the defense struggled at so many points in the game to the anemic run offense outside of the redzone, there clearly is much to work on. Now they face another winless team, the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. This comes on a short week as it is on Thursday Night Football . With so many questions still to be answered, here are some areas Sean Martin and Tom Ryle have concerns. Tom – Some context is important here. By beating the Texans, the Cowboys kept themselves in the thick of the NFC East race. The New York Giants are somehow keeping at the head of the division without Jaxson Dart, the Washington Commanders are trailing everyone else but hope to have Jayden Daniels back this week, and it is with great sadness that I observed what can only be called a meltdown by the Philadelphia Eagles against the Los Angeles Rams that may bode ill for them. The playoffs are hardly out of reach for Dallas at this point. But some things really need to change. And forgive me for venting a bit about something. I didn’t like the whole ‘Greatest Offense There Is’ idea from the start. Not only was it unoriginal and clumsy, it seemed to have been created while willfully ignoring something very important. Yes, the Cowboys offense was tearing it up all offseason and leading up to the regular season. But it appears Dak Prescott put out of his mind it was looking so good working against a defense that was simply pitiful last season. And the first four games have shown that the supposed improvements during the offseason have not panned out as well as we were hoping. It leaves the offense still having to carry this team. That was certainly the case in Houston, but it was just half the offense, or more precisely, it was the Dak-to-CeeDee Lamb connection being on absolute fire. Yes, Javontae Williams scored three touchdowns, but he still mustered a paltry 3.3 yards per carry. That, to me, is not a sustainable formula for making any kind of a playoff run. Sean – Well, it’s good to be talking to you after a win Tom. I wish I could say it was 2-2 over the weekend, but I’m sure we’ve all seen what happened at this point to my Bobcats at Idaho. You make a great point about the GOTI offense for the Cowboys, and Prescott pushed that further by saying he expected a blowout win against the Texans. All we can say about that now, is that at least he came up clutch when it mattered and the ball was firmly in the offense’s court. We have CeeDee Lamb’s historic day to thank for that. I think we learned with the Cowboys this week, and in many other places around the league, that we’re at a point where it’s important to not get too high or too low. This win had all of the thumbprints the Cowboys would like on it, Schottenheimer redeeming himself and calling the right plays in crunch time, the defense getting some key pressures, overcoming two missed field goals and a deficit, and winning late. There’s going to be talk of the “culture” being fixed because of this, of the Cowboys righting all their wrongs, almost as if Brazil didn’t happen. We have to pair these last two games together, all of the crazy highs and lows, and try to paint a more realistic picture of where this team is at with a short week to get back to work. Mix it all together and a winning record before we even get to the weekend is still in sight, so sign me up for that. Having the intensity to hand a winless, desperate team another loss was nicely done though, and exactly what the Cowboys will need to do again as the headline for the Buccaneers is that they also fell to 0-4 on Sunday. Tom – The problem is that I’m not sure what it really proves to get wins over winless teams, especially close ones like Sunday. I know that on any given Sunday something something, but Dallas needs to really assert itself. Tampa Bay offers a great opportunity for just that. But if they don’t breeze to a comfortable win, then we have to worry very much about what will happen when the competition is more formidable. And after facing the Texans and Buccaneers back to back, that is exactly what is coming. A win is a win, of course, but unless we see the offense really clicking without Prescott and Lamb, or maybe George Pickens have to be superheroes, and the defense shows it can put the clamps on a team that is having its own struggles, we should have a sense of trepidation. A strong showing against Tampa Bay would not only make us feel better about the overall performance of the team. It could set Dallas up to be a real challenger to win the division and get back to the playoffs. Sean – I am going to disagree with the general premise of style points mattering right now, but the thing I can’t possibly disagree with is that this team still has a lot of work to do. Luckily, so does every team right now as we’re a long way from knowing who will be the last one standing in February. We’ve seen Cowboys teams that won with style points in the regular season before not even make it to January, and the league is on a heater when it comes to games being decided by one score across the board right now. The Texans win can’t ease all of our woes about playing better competition, but the level of competition the Houston defense gave the Dallas offense in the first half sure was challenging, and they built a ten-point lead off of it. Within the same 60 minutes, the Cowboys turned it around and won, so maybe that will be something we look back on for evidence of getting it done against top defenses. I also think the easiest room for improvement to play even better on offense is the play-calling consistency right now, which is fixable if there’s still trust to be had in Schottenheimer. That trust will be back down to near-zero if the Cowboys are upset by the Bucs. The cruel reality is that it also won’t skyrocket back up with a win against this very depleted Tampa squad, but that Todd Bowles defense is going to bring pressure and play a bit reckless I think. The offense will need to show poise yet again. It’s a bye week on Saturday for the Bobcats, and a free Sunday for us Cowboys fans to watch other teams. Should be a nice weekend if they handle business on Thursday!
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Houston comeback, Nick Sorensen, defensive sacks
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  What was most convincing about the comeback win?  Mike – The most convincing part was Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas looked flat, stuck, and […]
full_text: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. What was most convincing about the comeback win? Mike – The most convincing part was Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas looked flat, stuck, and out of answers in the first half, but Schottenheimer helped flip the game after halftime. The play-calling became much better, the offense found rhythm, and the team clearly still believed it could win even when Houston had control. Credit has to go to the head coach when adjustments work and the team responds. This was not just Dak Prescott or CeeDee Lamb dragging Dallas out of trouble. It was a coaching staff finding answers, and Schotty did that. Dyllan – If teams choose to eliminate the quick death by focusing on George Pickens, Dallas is happy to methodically beat you with CeeDee Lamb the entire game. And don’t forget about Flournoy, by the way, who is completely capable of key chain moving grabs. This WR room reminded the NFL why they’re so dangerous. Jorge – The offense genuinely looks like a force of nature, and I still don’t think it’s firing on all cylinders yet. To Dyllan’s point, the WR room may be the deepest and most capable in the league, and they are getting the job done when called up and asked to deliver in the clutch. Oh, and QB Dak Prescott ain’t playing too bad either. Tom – I’m not sure there was anything convincing besides the obvious potency of the passing attack, and a nice bit of evidence that CeeDee is indeed among the elite at his position. But a couple of other things were at least encouraging. The red zone offense found a way every time. And the Cowboys had half the penalties, not their normal result. Oddly, those two are kind of interconnected, because on one touchdown the Texans just refused to get off the field without getting a flag. Sean – The offense not being denied in crunch time. The margin for error on some of Dak’s biggest throws of the game was slim to none, and every point the Cowboys put up ended up being needed. We can keep hoping and dreaming to see this offense with a little less pressure on their backs to score almost every time they touch it, but for now they’re scoring at an elite rate anyway, and it’s good enough to be right in the thick of things going into mid-October. Are we happy with how Nick Sorensen is coaching the special teams unit? Mike – In my opinion he needs to go. Brandon Aubrey is elite, but Aubrey’s leg should not cover up the wider special teams problems. The unit has too many messy moments, too many avoidable mistakes, and too many situations where Dallas either loses hidden yards or puts unnecessary pressure on the rest of the team. Special teams should be the cleanest, most reliable phase, not something that constantly feels like it is one mistake away from hurting the Cowboys. At some point, the coordinator has to own that. Dyllan – The FG unit needs to learn how to block things up in a hurry. They nearly had a second kick blocked on the PAT at the end of the game. But I do love their mastery of the dirty kick. The hidden yards in field position is extremely important for the growing defense. And Turpin is quietly putting up solid return numbers. I’m fine with Sorensen but they do need to figure out how to block on the FG attempts. Jorge – No. Special teams was an issue last year, and continues to be this year. The kickoff penalties are unacceptable, and blocked field goals played a hand in a loss this year. Aubrey’s special ability to nail those long kicks will be neutralized if the Cowboys can’t shore up protection on these field-goal attempts. Tom – It is more tolerable than satisfying. Those blocks and near blocks are potential game changers and must be avoided. Return yards are a plus, but we still haven’t seen the big return for a score or to get on the doorstep of the end zone. Sean – The Texans hurt themselves more than the Cowboys with special teams penalties in this game, but the Cowboys left an opportunity to push this differential even further with some sloppiness in the third phase themselves. For a coach that’s been here for a minute now, that’s a tough thing to swallow, and they’ll need to get it corrected. Is this the game where the defensvie line have to turn pressures into sacks? Mike – Yes, absolutely. Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks in four games, so if there is ever a week for the Cowboys’ defensive front to arrive, it is this one. Pressures are nice, but against a struggling protection unit, Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashaan Gary and the rest of the edge rushers have to finish plays this week. If the Buccaneers offensive line gives them chances and the Cowboys still cannot turn those chances into sacks, then the concern level goes way up. Dyllan – The game against Houston was the one where I thought they’d rack up the sacks. And they did finish with two. But I thought it’d come together sooner and more frequently. I’m losing confidence that the current room will be able to get after passers this season. Jorge – I agree with Dyllan; I’m not sure this group has what it takes to consistently bring the opposing quarterback down. They looked much better at the end of the game and on third down, but we still aren’t seeing much in the rush. I think that Christian Parker has to start maximizing their ability to rush the passer beyond asking them to beat their blockers with their skill/athleticism, so I’m talking more vigorous rush plans, and maybe even more blitzes. Tom – The lack of sacks is only concerning when paired with the failure to get a single interception. One can offset the other, but when neither is happening, it just increases the concern about whether this team can ever put it all together on D. Sean – To Tom’s point, rookie starter Jalon Daniels was sacked three times by the Packers on Sunday, but also threw two interceptions, so the impact plays could go either way, and both would be welcome from Parker’s defense. I would lean towards forcing this quarterback to throw into coverage as much as possible, so the chance for edge rushers to win matchups straight up will be there. I think they’ll get some, but not enough for us to feel drastically better about the EDGE group coming out of the game. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Dyllan – George Pickens gets on the board first the week. Jorge – CeeDee Lamb Tom – Javonte Williams, rapidly becoming a red zone machine Sean – I think it’s time for me to start picking Pickens until it hits, so Pickens. CeeDee Lamb receptions, over/under 9.5 Dyllan – Under. This is the week Pickens faces more solo coverage and comes alive. Jorge – Yeah, under. Tom – Ditto Sean – Ride the hot hand, over for me. Javonte Williams rushing yards, over/under 79.5 Dyllan – Over. I think Dallas gets up early and it becomes kill the clock time. Jorge – Over, for the reasons Dyllan mentioned. Tom – I’ll stick with the under until this team proves it can run the ball effectively outside the red zone Sean – Under. Dallas sacks on Jalon Daniels, over/under 3.5 Dyllan – Under. The pass rush is still very suspect regardless of opponent. Jorge – Under Tom – Ditto again Sean – Under Cowboys margin of victory, over/under 9.5 Dyllan – Over. 10 points is a huge line in the NFL but I think Dallas piles on the points and the defense nets them extra possessions. Jorge – Under, I’m still not convinced with this coaching staff. Tom – Over, just because they are about due for a blowout of an outmanned opponent Sean – Over would sure be nice True or false? Dallas forces multiple turnovers this week on defense. Dyllan – True. And I see your multiple turnovers and raise you one defensive touchdown. Jorge – False Tom – False until proven otherwise Sean – Probably false.

title: Cowboys offensive plan: Attack the Buccaneers corners early and often
summary: Coming off the most exciting win of the 2026 season, the Dallas Cowboys offense has a quick turnaround in week five, hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a pivotal NFC conference matchup. The Cowboys offense started out slow in their 34-30 win over the Houston Texans, but unleashed on a quality Texans defense in the […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Coming off the most exciting win of the 2026 season, the Dallas Cowboys offense has a quick turnaround in week five, hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a pivotal NFC conference matchup. The Cowboys offense started out slow in their 34-30 win over the Houston Texans, but unleashed on a quality Texans defense in the second half to seal the victory. A lot of went right for the Cowboys offense in the second half against Houston should be heavily leaned on in this Tampa Bay matchup. The Cowboys took a more conservative approach in the first half against the Texans and that led to struggles putting up touchdowns and sustaining drives. In the second half, they came out and played their typical style of football. They aggressively pushed the ball downfield while getting better pass protection. The Tampa Bay defense has played pretty well to start their season, despite their 0-4 start. Their defense currently ranks fifth in EPA/play and sixth in success rate. With that said, the Cowboys passing game should look to attack the Tampa Bay corners early and often. The Buccaneers starting three corners showcase rookie Keionte Scott in the slot, and Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum on the outside. Scott and Parish have played well to start the season, but both players are young and undersized compared the Cowboys trio of wide receivers. Scott is feisty nickel who does most of his damage as a run defender and blitzer, but he can be had in coverage and will lineup across from CeeDee Lamb on a high percentage of snaps. That is a clear advantage for the Cowboys and they should look to involve Lamb in all areas of the field, just like last week, and take advantage of the rookies inexperience against arguably the best wide receiver in football through four weeks. On the outside, George Pickens will also have an advantage over Parrish and McCollum. To make matters worse for Tampa Bay, they will be without their best secondary player in Antoine Winfield Jr., limiting their ability to control the middle of the field. While we should expect the Cowboys top two receivers to feast in this game, the matchup for all the pass catchers favors the Cowboys. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter has been fantastic to start the season, but getting tight ends Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford matched up on him in coverage with Winfield out gives the Cowboys more size advantages against the Buccaneers coverage defenders. Through four weeks, the Cowboys have seemingly needed to score 30+ points to win these games. Even with Baker Mayfield not expected to play, the Cowboys passing game will likely need to carry the weight of this game again, but they should have a much easier matchup in week five than they had in week four.
author: Connor Livesay

title: Cowboys Week 5 opponent: Looking at the 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys don’t have much time to enjoy their comeback victory over Houston. After Dallas erased a 10-point halftime deficit to beat the Texans 34-30 on Sunday, they immediately started prepping for a Thursday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Tampa Bay enters the game at 0-4 after a 17-14 loss to the […]
full_text: Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys don’t have much time to enjoy their comeback victory over Houston. After Dallas erased a 10-point halftime deficit to beat the Texans 34-30 on Sunday, they immediately started prepping for a Thursday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Tampa Bay enters the game at 0-4 after a 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers, while Dallas comes in at 2-2. The Buccaneers’ record doesn’t tell the whole story of where this team stands, though. Tampa Bay has dealt with injuries, inconsistent quarterback play and an offense that has struggled to turn opportunities into points, while its defense has kept the team competitive through the first month of the season. And now, with just three days between games, Tampa Bay will arrive in Dallas without the quarterback it expected to lead it through the season. So what exactly are the Cowboys getting on Thursday night? Baker Mayfield won’t be there Baker Mayfield was supposed to be the centerpiece of Tampa Bay’s offense this season, and through the first three games, he had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while completing 63.5% of his passes. He also added 65 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. Those numbers haven’t produced the kind of offensive explosion Tampa expected, but Mayfield’s absence still changes the complexion of this game. He suffered a dislocated right thumb in Week 3 and is expected to miss at least three games, meaning he will not be available Thursday night against Dallas. That leaves rookie Jalon Daniels as the Buccaneers’ starter. Daniels made his first NFL start against Green Bay in Week 4, completing 19 of 30 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also ran nine times for 64 yards, giving Tampa a slightly different look when their QB scrambles. There were some encouraging moments for Daniels against Green Bay, but the Buccaneers ultimately couldn’t capitalize on their opportunities. He also threw an interception that helped set up a Packers field goal, and Tampa’s final possession ended without the game-winning drive the team needed. That makes Thursday a very different quarterback challenge for Dallas than the one it would have faced against Mayfield. Instead of dealing with an experienced veteran who has played more than 100 NFL games, the Cowboys will be facing a rookie quarterback making his second career start on a short week and on the road. Jalon Daniels' first career TD! 🙌 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MKQijt4XeA — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Tampa still has plenty of weapons The quarterback situation may have changed, but Tampa hasn’t suddenly become an offense without playmakers. Bucky Irving remains one of the Buccaneers’ most important offensive pieces. Through four games, Irving has rushed for 241 yards on 56 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per carry, and has added 61 receiving yards. Chris Godwin Jr. is another veteran Dallas will have to account for. Godwin has 16 catches for 142 yards through four games, while second-year receiver Emeka Egbuka has emerged as another important part of the passing attack with 15 receptions for 154 yards and a touchdown. Then there is Cade Otton. The Buccaneers’ tight end currently leads the team in receiving yards with 157 on 15 receptions, averaging 10.5 yards per catch. He has become an increasingly reliable target for Tampa’s quarterbacks, and his involvement could become even more important with Daniels now running the offense. The Buccaneers have also gotten production from receiver Ted Hurst III, who has eight catches for 128 yards and a touchdown. His 16.0 yards per reception average is actually the highest among Tampa players with multiple receptions. So while Tampa’s offense has struggled to score consistently, Dallas can’t afford to approach Thursday as though it is simply facing a struggling offense with a rookie quarterback. There are too many legitimate weapons available for the Buccaneers to create problems if the Cowboys’ defense isn’t disciplined. Jalon Daniels hole shot to Ted Hurst pic.twitter.com/jNdNK0n5mP — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 6, 2026 Tampa’s defense has quietly kept the team alive If there is one thing the Buccaneers have done well through the first four weeks, it is keeping games within reach. Tampa has allowed fewer than 300 total yards in three consecutive games, including just 283 against Green Bay in Week 4. The Buccaneers also forced multiple turnovers against the Packers, recovering a fumble and intercepting Jordan Love during the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers have only allowed their opponents to score nine touchdowns in the first four games. David Walker leads the team with two sacks, while Alex Anzalone and Anthony Nelson each have one. Tampa has also gotten strong early contributions from linebacker Josiah Trotter, cornerback Keionte Scott and cornerback Zyon McCollum, who lead the team in tackles with 17, 16 and 15 respectively. The defense has essentially kept giving Tampa opportunities to win games that the offense hasn’t consistently been able to finish. The Cowboys just demonstrated against Houston that they can overcome defensive problems by scoring 34 points, but Tampa’s defense has shown that it can make opponents work for every possession. Tampa’s defense will also be missing one of its most important players. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. suffered a rib fracture during Sunday’s loss to Green Bay and is expected to miss two to four weeks. Winfield had recorded 24 tackles through the first four games and has been one of the Buccaneers’ most important defensive players since entering the league. Tampa Bay’s defense does it again! #WeAreTheKrewe pic.twitter.com/Hq5dtapFvM — Matty B (@mattthew_jordan) October 4, 2026 A Thursday night game with two very different teams The Cowboys and Buccaneers enter Thursday night in very different places. Dallas is 2-2 and coming off its highest-scoring comeback of the season. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a historic performance, Dak Prescott just threw for 335 yards against Houston, and the Cowboys have scored at least 20 points in every game this season. Tampa Bay is 0-4 and has already had to change quarterbacks because of injury. Even still, the Buccaneers have a legitimate running back in Irving, productive receiving options in Godwin, Egbuka and Otton, and a defense that has consistently kept opponents under 300 total yards. The Buccaneers have been close in every game, and their defense has proven capable of keeping them within striking distance. If Dallas wants to improve on its 2-2 record, Thursday night is an opportunity to do exactly that. Now the Cowboys get a Tampa Bay team that may not be able to match them offensively, but has spent the first month of the season proving that it can make a game uncomfortable for anybody.
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott says team will be ready for quick turnaround
summary: In the words of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the NFL blessed the Dallas Cowboys with three games in 11 days after they returned from a ten-hour flight to Rio, Brazil. So far, they are one of two teams to beat the Houston Texans on the road, but they lost to the Baltimore Ravens on the […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images In the words of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the NFL blessed the Dallas Cowboys with three games in 11 days after they returned from a ten-hour flight to Rio, Brazil. So far, they are one of two teams to beat the Houston Texans on the road, but they lost to the Baltimore Ravens on the road. The Cowboys have their first Thursday night game of the season, and after two physical, down-to-the-wire matchups, Dak Prescott is confident his team will be ready for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dak Prescott promises Cowboys will be ‘100’ percent for TNF vs. Buccaneers – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys need to win Thursday night if they want to keep pace with the New York Giants—what a world. “Oh, it’s gonna be 100. It’s gonna be 100,” said All-Pro Dak Prescott when asked if the Cowboys will be ready in a short week after two emotionally and physically draining matchups. “That’s how much I love this game, how much I put in this game throughout my life. Through the offseason, you prepare and you condition, and you do a lot of things for these types of moments. How Jerry Jones helped a Cowboys’ player make it to the birth of his first child – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Congratulations to Shemar James and his entire family. At halftime of the win, James was informed by the Cowboys’ director of security, Cable Johnson, that James’ wife was going into labor. The team and James quickly talked through options, and the way that got him to the delivery room the quickest was actually to wait until after the game and ride back on Jerry Jones’ private jet. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Joey Porter Jr. was a ‘boundary eraser’ in Cowboys debut. Could he be even more than that? – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News If the Cowboys can get an All-Pro season from Joey Porter Jr., this defense could turn things around quickly. Porter didn’t hesitate to say he’d be willing to solely cover a team’s No. 1 receiver. “When a team gives you that ability to go out there and lock in on a No. 1 guy, that means they really trust you out there,” Porter said. “Whenever I get that call, that’s an exciting task for me.” The Parker Report: Defense’s growth continues – Dyllan Rivers, Blogging the Boys Christian Parker’s defense is making baby steps forward in the right direction. Final grade: C I really wanted to give this defense a B- for their efforts against the Texans run game. It was by far their best effort of the season in that regard. Yes, the Texans have been pitiful while attempting to run the ball this season. But at the end of the day, you can only play who the schedule says to play. This unit did their job and made the Texans mostly one-dimensional throughout the day. The problem was that the Texans single dimension proved to be quite difficult for Dallas to slow down. Cowboys making changes on field goal unit after consecutive weeks with blocked kick – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News After back-to-back weeks with blocked field goals, the Cowboys are making a change to their field goal unit. “Yeah, moving some pieces around,” Schottenheimer said without getting into specifics. “We were going to move some pieces around anyways because it hasn’t been very good. We’ve got a good rotation going, but at the end of the day, we just got to clean some things up from a technical standpoint.” The Cowboys are tied for the second most field goal attempts (11) in the NFL with two kicks blocked.

title: Cowboys report card: Grading Week 4 vs the Texans
summary: When the Dallas Cowboys schedule was first released, it looked like they’d beat the New York Giants and Washington Commanders, but lose back-to-back to the Baltimore Ravens and Houston Texans. Turns out, getting to 2-2 would be a lot more topsy-turvy than we expected, especially with the New York Giants sitting alone at the top […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the Dallas Cowboys schedule was first released, it looked like they’d beat the New York Giants and Washington Commanders, but lose back-to-back to the Baltimore Ravens and Houston Texans. Turns out, getting to 2-2 would be a lot more topsy-turvy than we expected, especially with the New York Giants sitting alone at the top of the NFC East for the first time in over a decade. That’s a topic for another time. The Cowboys went into Houston in full-on desperation mode, looking to avoid a 1-3 start. The only caveat was that the Texans were desperate too, which meant they’d throw everything they had at Dallas’ high-powered offense. Dallas walked out with a win, showing they were the tougher team by finishing strong on offense and holding it together (barely) on defense. A lot of high grades are being handed out on the report card this week. A grades: CeeDee Lamb (A++) This was a signature game from CeeDee Lamb. 17 receptions for 189 yards, and the game-winning touchdown is a good day at the office. When the Cowboys needed a play on offense, especially in the second half, they looked to Lamb. Schottenheimer kept the Texans’ defense on their heels by moving him all over the formation and not keeping him to one side. The play design to get him the ball was brilliant, using screens and double moves to exploit his matchups. Dallas won the battle of Texas on the back of their star wide receiver. Dak Prescott (A+) After a week of noise about the Cowboys’ GOTI offense not finishing drives against the Baltimore Ravens, it was almost like the football gods wanted to give Dak Prescott a chance at redemption. Like the Rio game, Dallas had little time on the clock and three points to tie the game, or a touchdown to take the lead. A field goal wouldn’t do it this time. Not if they are trying to learn from their mistakes. After a should-have-been interception that landed in the dirt between two Texans defenders, Prescott went to work. Lamb’s final touchdown wasn’t just for the lead. It shook off the narrative that Dallas can’t do it in big moments on offense and gave them confidence for when they find themselves in the same moment again. It took him until the second half to heat up against a vaunted Houston defense, but Prescott finished 32 of 45 passing for 335 yards and one touchdown. Not bad at all. Tyler Guyton (A) 😤😤😤 Up Next 📺: #TBvsDAL 10/8 on Prime Video https://t.co/Zb82Klo3hO pic.twitter.com/SwUT7biOom — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) October 5, 2026 Tyler Guyton’s development has been one of the biggest storylines around the Cowboys through the first month of the season. Things look like they are coming together for the former first-round pick. He still loses a couple of matchups, but that’s life as a tackle in the NFL—nothing is perfect, but consistency is key. Through four weeks, Guyton has allowed no sacks and has just one penalty: a false start against Houston. The Cowboys offense has benefited from not having to worry about Prescott’s blindside, and their investment in first-round offensive linemen continues to deliver success other teams dream of. The ball of clay isn’t molded to perfection just yet, but Dallas has to be ecstatic about how their left tackle has played so far this season. Javonte Williams (A) Javonte Williams had some dirty yards between the 20s, but it was a career day in the red zone. The Cowboys running back had three touchdowns, and the impressive part was that none of them were easy. The Cowboys paid Williams this offseason not just for his leadership, but for how productive he can be in this offense. He is the team’s true bell cow and has shown this year he’s almost unstoppable in short-yardage situations. Dallas struggled in the red zone last year because the play calling was not right. This year, there have been questionable moments, but one thing is clear: if Dallas has the ball inside the five-yard line, hand it off to No. 33. Otito Ogbonnia (A) Ogbonnia is tied for first among all IDL in run stops with 10, and he's 7th in run stop rate through 4 weeks, per PFF. https://t.co/KhjG17HxCE — John Owning (@JohnOwning) October 6, 2026 The big man deserves some love. Defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia is starting to show up each week as a run defender. When the Cowboys signed him in free agency this offseason, no one made a big deal of it because run-stuffing defensive linemen don’t pop the same way a cornerback trade does. However, Ogbonnia has been very good for Dallas’ defense and a big reason why they’ve been better at stopping the run in back-to-back weeks. He’s like a younger Jonathan Hankins. B grades: George Pickens (B+): George Pickens may have had just two catches in the game, but they wee among the most important catches. His 53-yard, no-look, over-the-shoulder, I-couldn’t-believe-my-eyes reception was the turning point. Dallas scored on their opening drive of the second half, but Houston responded with a touchdown of their own. The dink-and-dunk offense needed a spark for most of the day, and GP found it by doing what he does best. Pickens’ second reception came on the game-winning drive for 22 yards when Prescott found a hole in the coverage and hit him on the left side of the field. Pickens looks more locked in this year, even though he hasn’t received the same targets as last season. His time is coming, but for right now, he’s doing everything he can to help his team win. Quinnen Williams (B+) Williams had another really nice game for Dallas and looks to be settling in nicely in Christian Parker’s scheme. He has played in a similar scheme before, but you would have to go back to college to find that film. After being taught something different for so long, it may have taken a few weeks for him to finally feel comfortable. Williams showed up in the run game, but his biggest play came on a critical third down where he got to Stroud and took him down for a sack. That’s the type of impact defender Dallas not only traded for, but signed to a massive extension in training camp. Momentum looks to be building for Williams, which would be big for the defense if they want to turn things around. Joey Porter Jr. (B) Credit to Joey Porter Jr. for diving into the playbook on short notice and playing meaningful snaps on Sunday. You could tell he was playing with a spring in his step, as a player who missed being on the grass. Porter Jr. is a competitor and isn’t shy about showing it. After DaRon Bland was harassed all game by Nico Collins, Porter Jr. got more snaps in coverage against Collins to limit the damage . C.J. Stroud had to change his approach and look elsewhere. It was a small sample size, which is why he ends up with a B grade. However, it shouldn’t define him because I’m sure he’ll have many A-grade games this year, since that’s the player Dallas hoped they’d be trading for. Rashan Gary (B) Hello, Rashan Gary. It took a couple of weeks, but he finally showed up on defense. His sack on Stroud as he ran to the sideline helped reset the tone on defense after Houston led 10-6. Gary was active all game and put consistent pressure on Stroud in the pocket. Dallas gave up a late-round draft pick for Gary, but expectations have been higher than what he showed three weeks into the season. On Sunday in Houston, he met those expectations. Hopefully it’s a sign of things to come. Sunday was the best game that Rashan Gary has had with the #Cowboys . 5 pressures, 2 stops, and 1 sack. I thought his effort was outstanding. pic.twitter.com/hMwGcEvleU — Marcus Mosher (@Marcus_Mosher) October 5, 2026 KaVontae Turpin (B) Not too often does an All-Pro/Pro Bowl player fly under the radar, but KaVontae Turpin has done just that. He hasn’t had too much of a role on offense with the emergence of Ryan Flournoy form last season, so it’s shifted to him being a big part on special teams. His kickoff return to start the second half really jump started the offense and gave them the boost they…
