title: How does Justin Herbert’s painful reality become an ‘insult’ to Jim Harbaugh?
summary: Unless you live under a rock, you probably are aware of the recent exchange between Jim Harbaugh and ESPN’s Chargers beat reporter Kris Rhim. But if you haven’t here’s the quick TL/DR plus the accompanying posts from X: Here is the post from Rhim with the transcript and a video of the exchange: So I’m […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Unless you live under a rock, you probably are aware of the recent exchange between Jim Harbaugh and ESPN’s Chargers beat reporter Kris Rhim. But if you haven’t here’s the quick TL/DR plus the accompanying posts from X: Following the latest loss to the Seahawks where Justin Herbert was consistently smacked around due to a lack of pass protection, Harbaugh raved about Herbert’s “warrior play” that’s he’s had a front row seat to for over two seasons. Since this “warrior play” only arises when Herbert has to overcome incredibly tough circumstances and an offense that let’s him down more often than not, Rhim understandably asked Harbaugh why this is still happening after roughly 2.5 seasons under his watch Harbaugh took the question as an insult and proceeded to answer the question with a complete non-answer, showing some contempt after being confronted with some harsh reality Rhim and Harbaugh went back and forth before Rhim realized he wasn’t going to get a serious answer from Harbaugh Here is the post from Rhim with the transcript and a video of the exchange: Q to Jim Harbaugh after he praised Justin Herbert's "warrior" play that he's been watching for two and a half years: "Part of that is just him taking a ruthless beating because of, I don't know if it's the group in front of him, his protection, what's going on, but when you… — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) October 5, 2026 So I’m just going to be frank about this: This may have been the most cringe-inducing presser for Harbaugh since he became the head coach in 2024. And no, not the kind of cringe that comes with the latest Harbaugh-ism or wacky metaphor that we’ve all become accustomed to when he’s at the microphone. This was a coach who, from the very beginning of his tenure in LA, has taken an approach with the media to never actually answer any question with a straight-forward response. There’s always a story, an analogy, or a metaphor that stretches like it’s about to take a run at the vault in the Olympics. All of Harbaugh’s -ism’s were ingested and palatable due to the results he had over the past two seasons which were 22 wins and two playoff appearances. There were some gripes and other things to nitpick over that span but it all became irrelevant for the most part due to the results. That’s how this business tends to work. At the end of the day, a coach can do whatever he wants, say whatever he wants, and be whoever he wants to be as long as he’s winning. With a record of 0-4 to begin his third season — on top of exactly how the team has become 0-4 — that is no longer the case with Harbaugh, this fan base, and the media who have covered the team the past two-plus seasons. Justin Herbert is the greatest thing on God’s green Earth to Harbaugh. He’s the son he wished he had and the most magnificent player of football he’s ever laid eyes on (or something along those lines, he’s said a lot of things about his quarterback since 2024). So it should be quite understandable that someone who has kept their eyes on every single move and decision this team has made since his hiring has a question or two about what’s going on when the team’s record is 0-4 in Year Three while Herbert is being pummeled at an alarming rate. That is VERY understandable and something Harbaugh should have actually expected to talk about at some point this year. Instead, he acted shocked and appalled that someone would have the audacity to point out the giant, purple, feather-covered elephant in the room. Bringing it back to the initial question posed by Rhim, he didn’t even point a finger at any one thing. He offered up that he wasn’t exactly sure what the issue was, but the reality is that Herbert’s only showing you his “warrior play” because he’s having to fight through hell in the first place. So Rhim points that out and follows it with the “charges” that were placed upon Harbaugh and McDaniel when they were respectively hired by the Chargers. Harbaugh’s charge was to protect Herbert with a good offensive line. It was the whole “tip of the spear” monologue. So far, the spear has been shattered multiple times in two-plus years and isn’t poking anyone nonetheless capable of being used to protect his quarterback. McDaniel’s charge was to make things easier for Herbert so he wouldn’t have to be a superhero every game to give the Chargers a chance. What’s wild here is that Herbert did not have to be as much of a hero the last two seasons because the defense was also that elite. Now, McDaniel seems to have taken the offense back several steps and aided in putting Herbert back into his hero ball state of mind. (General manager Joe Hortiz also deserves a ton of blame for his actions thus far, but we’re sticking to Harbaugh as much as possible to not lose the plot.) Both of these things are apparent and obvious when the team takes the field each week. So for Harbaugh to listen to Rhim’s words and still come away believing they were meant as an insult? That’s ONE THOUSAND PERCENT on Harbaugh for taking it that way. If pointing out an objective truth is insulting, then that tells you everything you need to know about his internal dialogue. If Harbaugh believed he has done everything in his power to hold tight and accomplish the goal he was charged with, he would have explained how he’s gone about doing that and what may have been out of his control that has led the team to this position. And for those of you who cannot understand this concept, Harbaugh can still offer explanations and answer these types of questions without “throwing someone under the bus.” He can also be the one to actually shoulder the blame because that’s what leaders do. The buck stops with him. No ifs, ands, or buts. Whether it is or is not directly because of him, the team’s record and performance falls on him. There’s a lot of gray area in all of this obviously, but at the podium and in front of the football world, it is on Harbaugh. He knows this and I’m shocked he seemed so taken aback at being confronted in such a lukewarm manner. Anthony Lynn went through this. Brandon Staley sure went through this. The tough questions come with the tough times. If you’re a well-seasoned head coach, you should understand the game at this point. Play well, the media will toss you some underhand pitches and move on. Play not so well and you’re going to be met with a few fastballs you may not have prepared for. Either way, it’s up to you to take a calculated swing when the time comes. Before I wrap this whole thing up, I just want to shout out Rhim once again for having the steel within him to ask the questions that need to be asked. It has become such an archaic mindset within the sports media space to bend the knee to teams during media availabilities and only ask the questions that have zero chance at ruffling feathers. Players and coaches need and deserve to be pushed. Regardless of already knowing what their response will more than likely be, reporters still need to hold their ground. Respect is important for both sides. I don’t want to be remiss of that fact. But if we’re, again, being frank about all of this, Harbaugh’s way of answering question could also be viewed as lacking respect. If the head coach gets to (not) answer as many questions as he wants, then Rhim or any other reporter has the right to ask the questions he REALLY doesn’t want to answer. And once again for the record, as many times as Harbaugh wants to say he answered Rhim’s initial question, he most certainly did not. Harbaugh isn’t likely to break or change up his approach anytime soon, but he’s going to feel the pressure all the same if things do not change. In a results-based business, the results should be free game to discuss, no matter how much the head coach…

title: Rams vs. Bills features rare MVP matchup
summary: When the Los Angeles Rams face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, the game will feature the last two MVP winners. Josh Allen won the award in 2024 and Matthew Stafford won the award in 2025, and this will be the fourth time that the quarterbacks have played against one another. It will also be the […]
full_text: When the Los Angeles Rams face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, the game will feature the last two MVP winners. Josh Allen won the award in 2024 and Matthew Stafford won the award in 2025, and this will be the fourth time that the quarterbacks have played against one another. It will also be the first time since 2015 that the last two MVPs have faced off against one another and they don’t play in the same conference. Inter-conference MVPs have not faced off since Aaron Rodgers played against Peyton Manning in 2015. QBs with the highest passing yards O/U for Week 5: Jared Goff 280.5 Matthew Stafford 280.5 Jacoby Brissett 270.5 Dak Prescott 263.5 Josh Allen 244 Jordan Love 233.5 C.J. Stroud 231.5 Trevor Lawrence 229.5 Drake Maye 227.5 Sam Darnold 227.5 — Parlae | Fantasy Desk (@parlaeio) October 7, 2026 MVP quarterbacks who play in the same conference is obviously more common, but still doesn’t happen every year. The last four instances featured either Lamar Jackson or Patrick Mahomes: 2025 Allen vs Jackson 2024 Jackson vs Mahomes 2020 Jackson vs Mahomes 2019 Mahomes vs Brady 2017 Matt Ryan vs Cam Newton (twice) To find the next-most recent example of quarterbacks in different conferences before Rodgers-Manning, you have to go back to the 1976 Super Bowl between the Vikings and Raiders; Fran Tarkenton and Ken Stabler. In Allen’s 10th career start, he faced Stafford’s Lions and won 14-13. The next time they faced off was 2022, as the Bills blew out the defending Super Bowl champions 31-10 in Week 1. Two years later, Allen had 342 yards and three touchdowns against the Rams in Week 14 and scored three more touchdowns on the ground. However, the Rams won 44-42, holding off Buffalo’s comeback attempt. Allen still won MVP that season, a controversial close victory over Lamar Jackson. The Bills lost to the Chiefs in the AFC Championship game. In 2025, Stafford led the league in passing yards and touchdowns and won an even closer MVP vote over Drake Maye. Allen finished third. The Rams lost to the Seahawks in the NFC Championship. Allen is off to another crazy start, as he leads the NFL with seven rushing touchdowns, which is even more than his six touchdown passes. Home teams are 8-2 in the 10 previous meetings of the last two MVP winning quarterbacks.

title: What did you think of Makai Lemon against the Rams?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams could’ve taken Makai Lemon instead of Ty Simpson in the latest NFL Draft, so it was fitting that Lemon took on the Rams in Week 4 to give him a chance and the show the Rams what they missed out on. How did you think he did? Lemon didn’t have the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams could’ve taken Makai Lemon instead of Ty Simpson in the latest NFL Draft, so it was fitting that Lemon took on the Rams in Week 4 to give him a chance and the show the Rams what they missed out on. How did you think he did? Lemon didn’t have the biggest day as the Eagles offense as a whole struggled. He did make a few catches including a nice fourth down conversion. No, Lemon hasn’t lit his rookie season on fire to this point, but he has played more than Simpson, and that may not sit right with some fans who wanted the Rams to get players who can help them in 2026. Perhaps the Rams didn’t think Lemon could help them enough. It will be interesting to see if Lemon catches fire at some point this year, or ever, really considering the Rams could’ve had him. It’s all rather interesting when it comes to the NFL. Rams Rookie Report Cards After Week 4 (And an Update on the Ones That Got Away) (si.com) “The player that many wanted the Rams to take at 13th overall was wide receiver Makai Lemon. Given the Rams’ shift to 13 personnel and the fact that he would have been WR3 at best, Lemon didn’t make sense at that spot. Lemon struggled during the summer with the Philadelphia Eagles and through four games, he has 10 receptions for 65 yards. The Rams’ current third wide receiver, Konata Mumpfield, has six receptions for 112 yards. Now, Lemon is undoubtedly the better player than Mumpfield, but the early production proves that the Rams were right not to take the USC wide receiver.“ The rare fiery Sean McVay moment that saved Rams’ season from spiraling vs. Eagles (clutchpoints) “ESPN’s Lindsey Thiry called out one fiery moment from head coach Sean McVay that sparked the impressive fourth quarter comeback. “Yeah, I definitely think this is really helpful. And the moment I think we will all look back on if the Rams go on the run that they’re expected to go on is Sean McVay gathering that offense around,” Thiry said on Tuesday via Good Morning Football. “… He was proving as the head coach what he’s always preaching to his players and they needed something to really get them going. And you don’t really see that from Sean McVay. You don’t see him get the entire offense around in the middle of the game and get after them like that. But he did and it clearly sparked a change in that team.” Week 5 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Are Rams Contenders or Pretenders After Comeback Win? (si.com) “With 8:16 to play, the Rams had a 3.2 percent chance to win, and they somehow overcame the odds to come out on top 24-20. Quarterback Matthew Stafford led another fourth-quarter comeback and the two late touchdown drives were enough. Still, how the Rams are winning is not sustainable. Stafford has thrown an interception in every game this season. He currently ranks 20th in EPA per pass and needs to be better, especially as the Rams get ready to play the Bills. Let’s take a look at how the media feels about the Rams in this week’s consensus power rankings. ESPN – 7th The Rams don’t move this week in ESPN’s Power Rankings and stay in the No. 7 slot after coming back from 10 points to beat the Eagles. Again, one of the biggest questions around this Rams team is its consistency. The Rams haven’t found a way to play for 60 minutes outside of their Week 2 win against a New York Giants team that was led by Jameis Winston for most of the game.“ Rams Week 5 Power Rankings Round-Up: LA Stays Mostly Amid Top 10 (sports.yahoo) “ NFL.com sees no change for the Rams from Week 4 to Week 5. The publication points to what was written above: the team found a way not to fold when it mattered. One of the glaring issues that remains is quarterback Matthew Stafford. The reigning MVP threw another two interceptions on Sunday, pushing his total to six for the season. He had a total of eight in the 2025 regular season. Yahoo! Sports – No. 8 Yahoo! Sports has the Rams as being a top 10 team, but they have fallen two spots down from No. 6.“ Former Chargers 14-Game Starter Signs with NFC West Practice Squad (sports.yahoo) “According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, former Bolts linebacker Eric Kendricks has signed with the LA Rams’ practice squad. “Rams signed veteran ILB Eric Kendricks to their practice squad.” Kendricks signed with the Chargers to a two-year, $13.25 million deal in the 2023 free agency, but was released after one season. In his only season with the Bolts, the linebacker logged 117 total tackles, 3.5 sacks, six pass deflections and a forced fumble. Now, after three years, Eric Kendrick returns to the City of Angels with the opportunity to play for a Super Bowl contender.“ BEST PHOTOS: Kyren Williams’ back-to-back touchdowns, Byron Young’s critical sacks & more | Best of the Rams’ Week 4 road win over the Eagles (therams.com) “The Los Angeles Rams beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 at Lincoln Financial Field. Browse through photos from the Rams’ 24-20 comeback win, including running back Kyren Williams’ back-to-back touchdowns, outside linebacker Byron Young’s critical sacks, wide receiver Puka Nacua’s return to the field, and more.” Rams’ Sean McVay Calls Out His Own Assistants for ‘Unacceptable’ Behavior Toward Eagles Fans (sports.yahoo) “A Super Bowl-winning Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed sideline behavior after a viral video showed team staff taunting opposing fans during a tense fourth-quarter comeback win. Several assistant coaches were seen pounding on glass windows and gesturing toward spectators seated below their stadium box. Sean McVay said he spoke directly with his staff about maintaining professional standards. He stressed that emotion must come with composure, insisting the behavior will not happen again.“ Rams report card: Grading every position after first 4 games (ramswire) “That’s what makes now a good time to share a report card from the first quarter of the season. We graded each position group, evaluating their performance through Week 4. Quarterback: B- Matthew Stafford hasn’t been at his best this season. He had five interceptions in the Rams’ first 15 games last season and he already has six this year. His eight turnover-worthy plays rank as the fourth-most in the NFL this year, though he’s also tied for seventh with seven big-time throws.“ NFL Power Rankings, Week 5: Cowboys, Pats rising at quarter mark; unbeaten Vikings fall out of top 10 (nfl.com) “For three quarters, serious, nearly existential questions began to build for these Rams. They’d fallen behind in Philadelphia and couldn’t get out of their own way offensively, raising the specter of a 1-3 start to a season that began with immense hype. But Sean McVay’s squad proved something amid the chaos of a fourth-quarter comeback: L.A. is not going to lay down, no matter the odds. Matthew Stafford needs to be better, though.“ Eagles OT Lane Johnson announces retirement from NFL amid 14th season (nfl.com) “Having long been an advocate for mental health, Johnson explained that it’s time for him to focus on his own emotional well-being. “I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season,” Johnson’s statement read, in part. “But after a lot of reflection, I’ve realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed. title: Aaron Donald, Jaylen Watson trending upward on injury report
summary: The Los Angeles Rams could be getting two key defensive reinforcements back at exactly the right time. Head coach Sean McVay provided encouraging injury updates Monday on defensive lineman Aaron Donald and cornerback Jaylen Watson, expressing optimism that both players could return for the Rams’ Week 5 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Both players suffered […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD,CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams stands for the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams could be getting two key defensive reinforcements back at exactly the right time. Head coach Sean McVay provided encouraging injury updates Monday on defensive lineman Aaron Donald and cornerback Jaylen Watson, expressing optimism that both players could return for the Rams’ Week 5 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Both players suffered injuries during Los Angeles’ Week 3 Sunday Night Football loss to the Denver Broncos. 🚨 RAMS INJURY UPDATES 🚨 Rams head coach Sean McVay provided several injury updates on Monday ahead of the team's Week 5 matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. Jaylen Watson (Shoulder): McVay is optimistic Watson will return against the Bills after missing… pic.twitter.com/JFriOPL9DA — RambLAng Man (@RambLAngMan) October 7, 2026 Watson exited the Denver game with a shoulder injury that was later identified as a dislocated shoulder. The starting cornerback was subsequently ruled out for Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, giving him an additional week to recover. Watson had already recorded 10 tackles and three passes defensed through the first three games before the injury. McVay is hopeful Watson can return to practice this week, with the expectation that he could be ready to play if his shoulder responds well. The Rams are particularly motivated to get him back with Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills’ talented passing attack coming to SoFi Stadium for Monday Night Football. Donald, meanwhile, dealt with back soreness following the Denver game. Rather than risk aggravating the issue, the Rams held the future Hall of Famer out of their Week 4 victory over Philadelphia as a precaution. McVay made it clear that Donald was willing to play, but the organization ultimately decided protecting him from further injury was more important than putting him on the field at less than full strength. That decision appears to have paid off. McVay said Monday that Donald’s return is “trending” in the right direction, while the team remains hopeful about Watson’s availability as well. Getting both players back would be a major boost for a Rams defense preparing for one of its toughest challenges of the season. Donald’s presence can change the game at the line of scrimmage, while Watson’s return would strengthen a secondary that will have its hands full with Allen and Buffalo’s receiving weapons. For now, the Rams will take a cautious approach. But after sitting out Week 4, both Donald and Watson appear to be trending toward a return when Los Angeles needs them most.

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams signed linebacker Eric Kendricks to the practice squad on Tuesday, potentially setting up a potential change to the game day roster in the near future. Kendricks played for the San Francisco 49ers down the stretch last season, helping with several losses they had at linebacker during the season, and he had 19 tackles in two playoff games. That includes three tackles for a loss. Rams signed veteran ILB Eric Kendricks to their practice squad. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 6, 2026 The 34-year-old veteran has been a free agent for all of 2026. This could be a situation similar to 2025, when Kendricks was added to the 49ers practice squad in November and then joined the team in December. A second-round pick out of UCLA in 2015, Kendricks spent eight seasons with the Minnesota Vikings prior to stops with the L.A. Chargers, Dallas Cowboys, and 49ers. The Rams are his fifth career team, but first he needs to get onto the game day roster, either as an elevation or signing to the 53-man roster. The Rams may not be completely satisfied with what they’ve seen by Omar Speights, but Nate Landman hasn’t been worth every penny of the three-year, $22 million contract he signed either. This is a competition that continues to see action.

title: Rams’ 2-2 start isn’t as concerning as it seems
summary: The Los Angeles Rams sitting at 2-2 through four games likely isn’t what fans envisioned, given lofty expectations entering the 2026 campaign. Despite several injuries and inconsistent performances through the first quarter of the season, slow starts haven’t doomed recent Super Bowl champions, even if they’re uncommon. Since 2016, eight Super Bowl champs have started […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams sitting at 2-2 through four games likely isn’t what fans envisioned, given lofty expectations entering the 2026 campaign. Despite several injuries and inconsistent performances through the first quarter of the season, slow starts haven’t doomed recent Super Bowl champions, even if they’re uncommon. Since 2016, eight Super Bowl champs have started with three wins or better through the first four games. Only the 2019 Chiefs began their respective campaign with an unblemished 4-0 start, which propelled them to their second Lombardi Trophy. Generally, those teams have started hot, including the ‘21 Rams. However, there have been a couple of exceptions, as evidenced below: 2016 Patriots: 3-1 2017 Eagles: 3-1 2018 Patriots: 2-2 2019 Chiefs: 4-0 2020 Buccaneers: 3-1 2021 Rams: 3-1 2022 Chiefs: 3-1 2023 Chiefs: 3-1 2024 Eagles: 2-2 2025 Seahawks: 3-1 The 2018 Patriots and 2024 Eagles were the lone champions in that grouping to start 2-2. Deep playoff runs had seemingly caught up to New England, as it was coming off its second straight Super Bowl appearance. Philadelphia was breaking in new coordinators Kellen Moore and Vic Fangio, so things weren’t smooth early on. However, the Eagles recovered nicely by winning 16 of their final 17, two at LA’s expense. Yeah, we’re not bitter over here about it or anything. Even the best teams, or ones expected to be stellar, are prone to being blown out. The Rams found that out the hard way after losing by 20 to the 49ers in Australia to begin the season. Half of the Super Bowl champions in the last decade suffered a double-digit loss within the first four games, with the ‘18 Patriots again standing alone as the only team to suffer multiple such losses in that span. LA’s last Super Bowl team is included in that group after rolling through the first three weeks of the Matthew Stafford era before running into trouble against Arizona. Remember, the 2019 Chiefs are excluded here since they had to be different and win their first four games. Get a load of those guys, am I right? Team Year Loss(es) Patriots 2016 16-0 to Bills (Week 4) Eagles 2017 27-20 to Chiefs (Week 2) Patriots 2018 31-20 to Jaguars (Week 2) 26-10 to Lions (Week 3) Buccaneers 2020 34-23 to Saints (Week 1) Rams 2021 37-20 to Cardinals (Week 4) Chiefs 2022 20-17 to Colts (Week 3) Chiefs 2023 21-20 to Lions (Week 1) Eagles 2024 22-21 to Falcons (Week 2) 33-16 to Buccaneers (Week 4) Seahawks 2025 17-13 to 49ers (Week 1) These teams lost by an average of 9.4 points, though the data is slightly skewed due to the multiple double-digit losses. The most interesting thing about the findings is that a third of the losses came in Week 1, showing that it’s not always about how you start, but how you finish. Plus, if last year’s Seahawks are any indication, the Rams now know that it’s possible to bounce back from a season-opening loss to the Whiners and be just fine. Slow starts like the Rams have endured this season can be overcome, as the Patriots and Eagles proved over the last 10 years. Super Bowl champions since 2016 have mostly started hot and maintained that momentum for the rest of the season. LA has yet to play consistently enough to find any momentum, but the team has enough talent and a solid coaching staff to turn a corner sooner than anticipated.

title: Les Snead got it right with Rams contract extensions
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have made plenty of aggressive moves under general manager Les Snead, but some of the best roster-building decisions have come from knowing which players are worth keeping around long term. Quentin Lake, Trent McDuffie, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams represent four different examples of the Rams investing in players who can […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Quentin Lake #37 of the Los Angeles Rams smiles after an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have made plenty of aggressive moves under general manager Les Snead, but some of the best roster-building decisions have come from knowing which players are worth keeping around long term. Quentin Lake, Trent McDuffie, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams represent four different examples of the Rams investing in players who can provide significant value. While the contracts vary considerably in size and structure, the early returns suggest Los Angeles has gotten these decisions right. Quentin Lake The Rams rewarded Quentin Lake with a three-year, $38.25 million contract extension in January 2026, keeping him under contract through the 2028 season. The deal included $25.7 million in guarantees, with $8.5 million fully guaranteed. Lake also received a $1 million roster bonus at signing, while additional guarantees were tied to his remaining on the roster in future league years. That investment looks even better now. Through four weeks of the 2026 season, Lake has emerged as one of the highest-graded safeties in football. Quentin Lake currently lists with a 90.0 grade, second among 93 qualified safeties. His coverage grade is an even more impressive 91.6, which ranks first at the position. This is what I was talking about from yesterday @DariusJButler pic.twitter.com/ikBJkUBkLG — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) October 5, 2026 Lake’s versatility and ability to play multiple roles have made him an increasingly important piece of Chris Shula’s defense. Snead recognized that value before the market forced the Rams to pay significantly more. Trent McDuffie, CB The Rams took an even bigger leap of faith with Trent McDuffie. Los Angeles traded for the former Kansas City Chiefs cornerback during the offseason and then immediately committed to him with a four-year, $124 million extension. The contract includes $100 million in guarantees, with $50 million fully guaranteed at signing. McDuffie also received a $14 million signing bonus. An underrated thing that the Rams are getting out of Trent McDuffie is his ability to tackle in space. Rams blitz forces Hurts to get the ball out quick to Cooper, but he doesn't get any extra yardage because McDuffie makes the immediate tackles. Didn't have that last year. pic.twitter.com/PkEERFGyiL — Blaine Grisak (@BGMediaOnSI) October 6, 2026 That was a massive commitment for a player who had yet to play a snap in Los Angeles. So far, however, the Rams have received exactly what they paid for. McDuffie has established himself as a legitimate No. 1 cornerback and a foundational piece of the secondary. Trent McDuffie currently has him at a 89.1 overall grade, second among 103 qualified cornerbacks. The price was enormous, but so was the talent Snead acquired. Tyler Higbee, TE Tyler Higbee represents another example of the Rams understanding their own roster. Los Angeles re-signed the veteran tight end to a two-year deal in 2026, and Higbee has quietly become an important part of the passing game. Through four games, Higbee has 15 receptions for 141 yards and a touchdown on 19 targets. His 15 catches rank third on the team, while his 19 targets trail only Davante Adams among Rams pass catchers. That production has become particularly important with injuries and changes at the skill positions. Higbee may not receive the same attention as Adams or Puka Nacua, but his ability to consistently work underneath coverage and move the chains gives Matthew Stafford another reliable option. Tyler Higbee passed Tom Fears (400) for seventh on the franchise's all-time receptions list. Higbee also passed Marshall Faulk (4,071) for the 13th-most receiving yards in franchise history. #Rams | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/9ZEIDYapto — Los Angeles Rams PR (@TheLARamsPR) October 4, 2026 Kyren Williams, RB Kyren Williams may ultimately be one of Snead’s best recent investments. The Rams signed Williams to a three-year, $33 million extension in 2025, with $15.145 million fully guaranteed. At an $11 million average annual value, the Rams are paying Williams like a significant offensive piece—and he continues to prove that he deserves that investment. Williams was outstanding in the Rams’ Week 4 comeback against Philadelphia, finishing with 80 rushing yards and two touchdowns while adding 10 receptions for 67 yards. Week 4 SumerStar: Kyren Williams Most receptions for a Rams RB since Todd Gurley in 2018 pic.twitter.com/aiE3Iz5MRp — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 5, 2026 Through four games, he has already accumulated 294 rushing yards and another 173 receiving yards, giving him 467 total yards from scrimmage. Recap The Rams’ roster has been built through trades, free agency and the draft, but identifying which players deserve second contracts is just as important. Lake was a sixth-round pick. Williams was a fifth-round pick. Higbee was a fourth-round selection who developed into a longtime contributor. McDuffie was acquired through an aggressive trade and immediately became one of the highest-paid players at his position. The common denominator is simple: Les Snead and the Rams have identified players who fit the team’s vision and then committed to them before the opportunity disappeared. That is how sustainable contenders are built. And if their early 2026 performances are any indication, the Rams’ recent contract extensions are looking like some of Snead’s best work yet.

title: Kyren Williams is a weapon in the passing game: Rams Film Room
summary: The Los Angeles Rams needed Kyren Williams to come up big in Week 4, and the veteran running back did just that. In a win over the Philadelphia Eagles that was anything but pretty for the Rams offense, Williams became a vital outlet for the passing game while also being his typically efficient self on […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams #23 celebrates scoring a touchdown during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams on October 4th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams needed Kyren Williams to come up big in Week 4, and the veteran running back did just that. In a win over the Philadelphia Eagles that was anything but pretty for the Rams offense, Williams became a vital outlet for the passing game while also being his typically efficient self on the ground. This was especially important in a game where Los Angeles’s second-best pass catcher, Davante Adams, struggled uncharacteristically and frustratingly. Williams caught a career-high 10 passes against the Eagles, six of which were “successful” (based on generally accepted calculations for success rate), while three turned into new first downs for the Rams (another would have led to a manageable 4th-and-1 situation but was aided by a penalty on the Eagles). We’re going to look at one play in particular from this week’s fourth-quarter comeback, in which Sean McVay and L.A. weaponized Williams against an ill-equipped Philadelphia linebackers group. And the end zone view: The Rams will always be happy with Kyren Williams matched up one-on-one in space against Jihaad Campbell (11). These choice routes are a staple of McVay’s offense and in this situation it sets up a scoring opportunity moments later. Williams is even with Campbell after releasing from the backfield with a gaping hole in the middle of the field. The veteran running back takes the inside option, running the angle route across quarterback Matthew Stafford’s face and beating Campbell to the spot. The linebacker didn’t gain any depth here, leaving him no margin for error before the running back breaks inward. He’s dropped at the one-yard line but punched it in to cap the 98-yard scoring drive. HB Angle on the goal line is always a good call, but when you’ve got a linebacker on skates from the start you’re in excellent shape. McVay and all the coaches from his tree (Kyle Shanahan and his coaching descendants included) thrive on putting linebackers in conflict. Again, the Rams are going to attack Campbell or a similar player every single time in this spot. If this concept looks at least vaguely familiar, it should. It led to a Williams touchdown reception in Week 2 against the New York Giants. The setup here is very similar to this week’s case study. The Rams are in 11 personnel both times, the only difference being the tight end is aligned to the right of the formation in Week 4 instead of the left like he is in Week 2. It’s out and up out of the backfield for Williams, once again putting a linebacker, in this case rookie Arvell Reese, in conflict. That’s where we start to see some differences. Here, Reese does gain depth and also has help in between the hashes, putting a lid on the potential for Williams should he take the inbreaking option. That depth, however, opens a huge passing lane for Stafford as his running back takes the vertical option instead. Reese and co. took away the angle, but Williams still split him and the boundary defender with a seam route for a 10-yard touchdown snag. The great Dan Casey broke down this particular play on Twitter as part of a longer deep dive on the Rams, which is worth your time. McVay and the Rams offense have a great deal of trust in Williams, and it allows them to pick defenses apart in the low red zone. You can’t do this with every running back, but with one with good hands and a legitimate route tree it opens up so many potentially explosive opportunities. Los Angeles needed someone to step up on offense to beat the Eagles this week, and Williams, paired with an old faithful option from the playbook, answered the call.

title: Tonka Hemingway becoming key figure on defense
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 666 percent of the snaps Sunday. […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 666 percent of the snaps Sunday. Jeanty, who appeared to be bothered by his ankles, finish fairly strong after a slow start. He had 58 yards on 15 carries and he added six catches for 68 yards, his highest receiving yardage output. The Raiders’ ground game has struggled, but at least, Jeanty made an impact in the receiving game. Jeanty is leading the NFL with 10 runs for negative yardage. Jack Bech: The second-round pick is on the injured reserve with a fractured forearm and will likely be out for several more weeks. Darien Porter: The third-round pick, a former starting cornerback, played three defensive snaps and 20 on special teams. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick started at right guard when Jackson Powers-Johnson out with a groin injury. He struggled against the Chiefs’ star defensive tackle Chris Jones, Rogers gave up five pressures. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense, but logged six snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, is on the injured reserve. The team is hopeful he can return soon. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 65 percent of the defensive snaps, the most of any Raiders’ defensive tackle. He had three tackles, a quarterback hit and knocked down pass. He is making plays. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the first time this season and for the 10th time in his career. He played seven snaps on defensive and seven on special teams. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 19 snaps on special teams.

title: How Kenneth Walker II ran all over Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 to Kansas City Chiefs
summary: While the Las Vegas Raiders are certainly ahead of schedule and exceeding expectations in the early stages of the 2026 season, the Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs is a tough pill to swallow. With first place in the AFC West on the line, the Raiders let Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker rush […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Las Vegas Raiders are certainly ahead of schedule and exceeding expectations in the early stages of the 2026 season, the Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs is a tough pill to swallow. With first place in the AFC West on the line, the Raiders let Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker rush for 177 yards , 8.0 yards per carry and a pair of touchdowns in the 30-27 defeat. To be fair, Walker has been tough for all of Kansas City’s opponents to stop. But the numbers above were season highs and his yardage was a career high. Additionally, that was the most rushing yards Las Vegas’ defense has given up so far, and the unit didn’t allow a single player to crack triple digits during the first three games of the year. The Raiders also had their lowest team run defense grade of the season from Pro Football Focus , coming in at 46.7, after being above the baseline (60.0) in each of the first three weeks. How did that happen? Let’s flip on the tape and dive into a few examples find out. Kenneth Walker is averaging 10.2 ypa around the left end this season (per PFF), and the #Raiders couldn't contain him -Kelce's motion forces LBs to slide over -Backside T/E stunt creates a soft edge -Masses in man coverage & gets inside release -Easy 11 yards & 1st for Walker pic.twitter.com/uqfD79LoO5 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 5, 2026 According to PFF , 174 of Walker’s 543 rushing yards (32.0%) have come around the left edge, and he’s averaging 10.2 yards per attempt on such runs so far this season. That’s the most yards and second-highest rate he has to a specific direction/gap, and the Raiders contributed to the problem last Sunday. Here, it’s second-and-10, and Kansas City comes out in 11 personnel with tight end Travis Kelce in-line on the short side of the field before motioning across the formation and creating a three-by-one set as a slot receiver in the bunch formation. As a result, Las Vegas’ linebackers, Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker, slide over to mirror Kelce, taking Dean out of the box and forcing Walker to be in the middle of the offensive line. In other words, the Chiefs are creating a softer edge by pulling defenders away from the direction they want to run. Additionally, the Raiders get caught running a T/E stunt, meaning the defensive end works inside, where the offense wants him to go, and cornerback Hezekiah Masses appears to be in man coverage. Since Masses gets an inside release from his receiver, he also isn’t in a position to contain and to force Walker inside. By the time the corner recognizes the run, it’s too late, and he has a tough time getting off the block, creating an outside rushing lane for the running back to get an easy 11 yards and pick up the first down. To be clear, the rookie is far from the defense’s biggest problem here, as several factors led to the chunk run, primarily getting beaten by the play call. Kenneth Walker "only" forced 5 missed tackles (via PFF) against the #Raiders , a season low for him But just about all of them came on this 22-yard run pic.twitter.com/nDlIAl2qqH — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 5, 2026 We’ll take a look at another run around the left edge in the clip above, but Walker’s ability to make defenders miss is the biggest factor on this rep. He leads all running backs with 39 missed tackles forced this season, 14 more than Jahmyr Gibbs in second place, per PFF . Technically, Vegas did a decent job of getting the NFL rushing leader on the ground, where he forced a season-low five misses on Sunday. However, just about all of them came on this 21-yard run. This time, the motion actually works against the Chiefs, since it brings an extra linebacker (Quay Walker) into the box. Additionally, the Raiders fit the power run pretty well, where defensive end Kwity Paye spills the puller to force the running back to bounce outside, while the linebacker and safety are inside of their blocks to continue to spill the ball toward the sideline. That sets up Masses with an opportunity to make the tackle to keep the run to a two- or three-yard gain. However, the rookie corner lunges and doesn’t bring his feet with him on the tackle attempt, allowing Walker to make him miss. Then, it’s just a collection of bad angles, overpursuits and more missed tackles from several other defenders to put the offense at midfield. Kenneth Walker's 22-yard TD run -Chiefs in 13 personnel, #Raiders match with base but leave 2 CBs in the game w/ Quay & Stokes on the edge -Walker sets up Dean by stepping downhill -Quay gets caught w/ TE on arc release and pushed vs. RT -Stokes can't set the edge vs. TE pic.twitter.com/fl84jqHEgU — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 5, 2026 This next run is around the right end where Walker hasn’t had as much success, with 40 rushing yards (22 coming on the play above) and 5.0 yards per carry, according to PFF . However, the result here wasn’t any different than the two previous runs. Kansas City comes out in 13 personnel, and Las Vegas matches by bringing base personnel into the game. However, with a three-tight end formation and only one wide receiver in the game, the Raiders don’t need to keep four defensive backs on the field and would be better off matching with heavy personnel by adding an extra defensive tackle or linebacker, or at least another strong safety. Instead, they end up getting into a front where Quay Walker and cornerback Eric Stokes are on the edge, while Kansas City runs outside zone right at them. The result is Quay Walker getting caught up with the inside tight end, who is arc releasing up to the linebacker (Dean), so Quay Walker isn’t in a position to take on the right tackle’s block and gets pushed out of the way. Additionally, Stokes is at a significant size disadvantage and can’t set the edge against the outside tight end. On top of that, Kansas City has a subtle wrinkle to a standard play call, where the running back steps downhill and looks like he’s attacking one of the A-gaps. That sets up the linebackers because it gives them the illusion that the play call is inside zone. So, Dean steps downhill and ends up getting caught in the trash with the tight end working up to him, as Walker bounces outside and takes advantage of the soft edge for a touchdown. 2nd & 3, Kenneth Walker gets an easy 6 yards for the 1st -WR motion pulls Nakobe Dean out of the play -Foley Fatuaski lets the C & RG scoop him & ends up in the opposite B-gap -Big rushing lane in the playside A-gap pic.twitter.com/7ex0BbzWba — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 5, 2026 Another reason why Las Vegas struggled to stop the run is that Foley Fatukasi, the team’s best run-defending defensive tackle, had his worst game of the season, in my opinion. Fatukasi posted a 54.9 PFF run defense grade and really struggled against combo blocks throughout the afternoon. It’s second-and-three here, and the Chiefs run mid zone while motioning a receiver across the formation. That forces Dean to slide over and takes him out of the play, as the call is designed to hit in either the weak-side A- or B-gaps. With Kwity Paye lining up as a 4i-technique and doing a decent job taking the left guard’s block, the B-gap is closed. However, Fatukasi, who is at nose tackle and shaded on the center in the weak- or play-side A-gap, gets a scoop/combo block from the center and right guard, and lets the two offensive linemen get to his outside shoulder. As a result, Fatukasi isn’t close to his assignment and ends up in the back-side B-gap, creating an interior rushing lane with no linebacker to fill the hole. So, Walker just makes a small cut up the field and gets an easy six yards. Also, Jeremy Chinn can be more aggressive and trigger downhill to replace Dean once he sees the run play, rather than staying deep and waiting for the receiver to come block him. Kenneth Walker's 76-yard run vs. #Raiders -Foley Fatuaski gets blocked into the 2nd level by the combo block -Nakobe Dean gets caught in…

title: Week 5 NFL Power Rankings note Klint Kubiak building something special with Las Vegas Raiders
summary: There may not be any moral victories in the NFL, but the Las Vegas Raiders falling 30-27 to the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday is as close as it gets. A hard-fought loss has many in the media singing the Las Vegas Raiders’ praises in the Week 5 NFL Power Rankings, while noting that new […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There may not be any moral victories in the NFL, but the Las Vegas Raiders falling 30-27 to the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday is as close as it gets. A hard-fought loss has many in the media singing the Las Vegas Raiders’ praises in the Week 5 NFL Power Rankings, while noting that new head coach Klint Kubiak is building something special in Las Vegas. Sports Illustrated 10. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 9 Column on the arrival of Mark Davis finally making a coaching hire who lets his actions do the talking . — Conor Orr In Orr’s column, he references Kubiak as the league’s “early shoo-in for Coach of the Year.” Obviously, the Raiders have to swap out “moral victories” for actual victories on the scoreboard during the brutal stretch of the schedule that they just started. But if they do and continue to stay in the playoff conversation throughout the season, Orr’s claim is going to be hard to argue with. The rookie head coach hasn’t been perfect and showed signs of his inexperience during his first four games. But this is a team that was picking first in the draft just six months ago, had very low expectations heading into the season, and just went toe-to-toe with a legitimate Super Bowl contender. ESPN 11. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 14 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Something special is brewing. Even after the Raiders’ heartbreaking loss to the Chiefs, there’s a sense that first-time coach Klint Kubiak is building something special in Las Vegas. The Raiders were competitive for four quarters against Kansas City. They are better than expected and should be a competitive team each week, especially with quarterback Kirk Cousins playing at a high level. With the Chargers 0-4 and the Broncos 2-2, it’s not crazy to suggest Las Vegas can make a playoff run in Year 1 of the Kubiak era. — Ryan McFadden It’s only been a quarter of the season and, of course, the Raiders have to finish strong. However, they’ve put themselves in a good spot to earn an AFC Wild Card spot by currently sitting as the sixth seed, with the 3-1 Baltimore Ravens owning the early tiebreaker. In the same vein, this week’s game matters even more because who owns the seventh spot in the conference right now? The 2-2 New England Patriots . The Athletic 13. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 12 Concern level: Concern? What concern? The Raiders lost, but they’ve got to come away from Sunday’s game feeling pretty good. They’ve already matched their win total from a year ago. New coach Klint Kubiak is exceeding expectations, and even 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is slinging it. There’s not a lot to be worried about in Vegas given what this season could’ve looked like. — Chad Graff, Josh Kendall The last line is key here. The Raiders certainly aren’t perfect and have a handful of issues that probably can’t even be addressed until the offseason, but the coaching has been able to mask some of their problems. Continue to add talent to the roster, and Kubiak and Co. should be able to return the organization to prominence. In other words, the spotlight is going to be on general manager John Spytek moving forward, and Spytek’s 2026 offseason additions should inspire more confidence. NFL.com 12. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 There are no moral victories here, but the Raiders sure have plenty to be proud of after their narrow Week 4 loss to Kansas City. The upstart Las Vegas squad battled with big brother for four quarters and nearly handed the Chiefs their first loss of 2026. Kirk Cousins is playing fantastically, and the defensive additions have helped transform the team from an also-ran into a squad that deserves a ton of respect. I’m not sure how the story will end, but I’m glad we’re along for the ride. — Nick Shook I hate the idea of calling the Chiefs “big brother”. However, let’s be real: Patrick Mahomes is 14-2 against the Raiders and has played in five Super Bowls (winning three of them). So, he/they have earned that distinction. But if last Sunday is any indication, the Silver and Black finally have the regime that can help close the gap and take over as top dog in the division down the line. Bleacher Report 10. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 11 For the first time this season, the Las Vegas Raiders came up short, losing to the Kansas City Chiefs, but their contender credentials are genuine after entering last week at No. 11 in our power rankings. In the third quarter, on 4th-and-2, Las Vegas passed up a 41-yard field-goal attempt and turned the ball over on downs. In the final quarter, kick returner Dareke Young fumbled, which allowed league-leading rusher Kenneth Walker III to score on a short field. While aggressive, the Raiders will miss the mark at times, but they’re good enough to hang with the NFL’s upper-echelon teams. Keep in mind that playoff-caliber clubs have a better chance of capitalizing on Las Vegas’ mistakes. — Moe Moton To Moton’s point, turnovers were the difference in the game against Kansas City, with the fumble leading to a late two-possession lead and an interception sealing Las Vegas’ fate. The good news is that the Raiders lead the NFL with nine takeaways, per The Football Database , despite not getting any on Sunday. The bad news is that they failed to get a turnover against the best team they’ve played so far and are now only plus-three in differential. A pick or fumble recovery (or both) in New England this weekend can help ease concerns.

title: Raiders-Chiefs: Tell the truth Tuesday
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 loss at home to the Kansas Cify Chiefs was both eye-opening and a validation of things to come. While there is absolutely no reason to panic, in order to continue playing winning football, some questions and issues need to be addressed.  The rest of the NFL landscape is now seeing […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) The Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 loss at home to the Kansas Cify Chiefs was both eye-opening and a validation of things to come. While there is absolutely no reason to panic, in order to continue playing winning football, some questions and issues need to be addressed. The rest of the NFL landscape is now seeing that the Raiders are for real. They are a well coached team that plays aggressively disciplined football. This loss was more about them not converting their opportunities and making a single mistake than it was the Chiefs doing anything special. The running game The heart of Ashton Jeanty should not be questioned, but his durability can be. Jeanty has been playing hindered since the end of kickoff weekend against the Dolphins. Jeanty has always been the volume-type player who needs his touches in order to get going. However, as other teams have tailored their schemes to sellout for the run his ailments have become more and more pronounced. The smooth sharp cuts are labored and gradual, he’s not forcing many missed tackles if any. Most notably absent is any burst through the hole to hit them when he sees them. Those who have been around football understand when his preventative treatments wear off. He has replenished the treatment either during halftime or in-game, but it isn’t maintaining its effect for 60 minutes of football. Mike Washington Jr. as explosive as he has shown himself to be during both the preseason and last week versus the New Orleans Saints, was swarmed each and every time he touched the football. Nine carries for 18 yards is hardly the production expected of him, given his previous success. Even though Jeanty is playing his heart out, with him being compromised, Washington may be called on to shoulder the load sooner rather than later. The offensive line Many factors contribute to the running game being ineffective. Equally the amount of hits quarterback Kirk Cousins is taking is both ramping and piling up week by week. Singling players out is an easy thing to do, however there are larger factors at play. The left side of the line is underperforming as a whole, despite the phenomenal coaching job done by Rick Dennison. Left tackle Kolton Miller allowed George Karlaftis six hits on Cousins. The right side has been better at pass protection; however, numbers and superior physical talent over the course of the last two weeks have resurfaced issues thought to be corrected. Power can only take the Raiders so far when players are overmatched and outnumbered. Without getting much of a push the rushing attack has suffered, and the timing of everything is disrupted. Opponents are displaying a complete lack of regard towards the passing attack. Consequently, opponents’ fresh and rotating defensive lines are maintaining a healthy advantage over the offensive line. The wide receiver room It’s time the Raiders picked up the phone and reached out to Arizona and Jacksonville to see what it would take to finagle Marvin Harrison Jr and/or Brian Thomas Jr. It is blatantly obvious, to the detriment of the team the only pass catcher worthy of schematic adjustment is Brock Bowers. That has to change. It’s far too early to be using the “P” word (playoffs), but with what the Raiders have shown, good-to-great production from the wide receiver position can certainly push them towards it. Trey Tucker is not a big enough threat. An injured Jack Bech can’t provide dividends as a blocker in the slot or a quick-hitting slot receiver. Jalen Nailor’s most productive plays have been as a decoy and getting his clock cleaned on a hospital ball. Cody White’s blocking isn’t good enough and he’s still improving as a #3 option. Malik Benson has all but disappeared over the last couple of weeks. Dareke Young caught one pass on two targets yet failed to make an impact downfield blocking. Raiders had the numbers on this misdirection toss, but Dareke Young wiffs on his block, and Delane makes a great tackle. pic.twitter.com/w5gCQ3ZRbC — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) October 5, 2026 No disrespect is intended and perhaps this oversimplified look may be a bit narrow-minded, but a wide receiver’s number one job is to get open and catch the football. There just isn’t a lot of that going on right now. Donte Thornton isn’t going to come back on a white horse from the injured reserve list and save them either. Both Harrison and Thomas were former first round picks and bonafide studs in college. They have also been nearly completely phased out of the lineup by coaches who didn’t draft them and don’t value their abilities. The fact that you could potentially get both of them for day 2 or 3 picks in the 2027 draft is something to capitalize on. If for nothing else but to look the part and provide better decoys and take pressure off the offensive line and run game. Best case scenario two mid round picks bring in highly motivated players eager to resume playing at the high level they are capable of. Or even one of the two should make a sizeable difference in alleviating coverage on Bowers. Never in a million years did I think Kirk (at this stage of his career) was capable of this play. Every part. The feel. The escape. The throw on the run. And the arm. The effortless flick downfield on the move dotting his man in stride. This is not normal 38-year-old stuff. https://t.co/L5bsELJRv4 — Alex Monfreda (@AlexMonfreda) October 5, 2026 Is Kirk Cousins showing his age Cousins, through the first ¼ of the season is still tied for the NFL lead with 11 passing touchdowns and had his biggest output yardage wise of the season. He’s been playing really solid ball, arguably some of the best in his career. However there are a few glaring shortcomings he’s been using smoke and mirrors to overcome. Cousins was called out for being slow in training camp and walking in the field. He responded by sprinting unimpeded the next few days. That was cute, but when opportunities to run for yardage his team needed against the Chiefs or any other team arose, he either can’t or won’t do it. Instead he has opted for some very poor decisions in throwing into coverage in the middle of the field. Sometimes off balance, or away from his body in ways that are inexcusable and fundamental No-No’s. Moreover, his ability to slide in the pocket and escape an initial rush has been satisfactory yet pushing the ball downfield to anyone other than tight ends remains a problem. Driving throws beyond the intermediate outside of the numbers and hashes remains a point of concern. Managing games and completing high percentage throws is how he’s been able to be successful. However, declining pocket times and being hit in the middle of throws are causing him to miss open receivers. As the hits keep coming, what kind of toll is it taking on his body? Against the Chiefs, Cousins was hit 10 times, including one that earned a roughing the passer penalty. He took a beating. How long can he continue to endure remains to be seen. Rob Leonard got got You can call a perfect game, and not get a perfect result. Somewhere between 85-90% of what Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard worked to perfection. Yet 98 yards and both touchdowns of Kenneth Walker’s 22 carries and 177 yards came on two plays. Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy both gashed the Raiders for 55 and 41 yards respectively against cover-0. In short yardage pick plays and bunches crossed up off coverage and hit the Raiders for two touchdowns The long and the short of it is, the Raiders did almost everything right, but against the Chiefs perfection is required. The Chiefs won because their situational football was better. A true learning experience for Raiders coach Klint Kubiak and his football team. Tackling One thing and one thing only was going to lead the Raiders to their doom and that was missed tackles. On one play, Walker broke five tackles, making the defense look silly. What quick-throw offenses specialize in is getting the ball…

title: Mike Washington couldn’t ignite run game in Week 4
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick served as […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. He hasn’t played all season. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick returned from being out with a concussion in Week 3 and he played all 60 defensive snaps. He nearly had an interception and finished with two tackles. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played five offensive plays in a Jumbo set and he played two special teams snaps. He missed some time with an injury, but he returned. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 17 snaps on special teams. He didn’t play defense for the third time in four games. He has played 18 defensive snaps this season. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played a season-high 18 snaps and he had a season-high nine carries. He finished with just 18 yards. He has 24 carries for 110 yards. He also had his first catch for minus-1 yard receiving. While he didn’t get anything going Sunday, it wouldn’t be a surprise if the Raiders use Washington more gain at New England in an attempt to spark a lacking ground game. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was active for the first time. He played 12 special-teams snaps. It will be interesting to see if he continues to be active. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played all but two snaps against the Chiefs. He flashed as usual for the most part. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played seven offensive snaps with no targets. He had one punt return for four yards.

title: Jeff Hafley remains confident in direction of Miami Dolphins
summary: The Miami Dolphins have started the 2026 NFL season with four straight losses, but despite the team’s hardships, head coach Jeff Hafley still believes in the direction of his organization. On Tuesday, Miami’s rookie head coach spoke with the South Florida media and discussed why he believes his squad will turn things around moving forward. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins looks on during the first quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have started the 2026 NFL season with four straight losses, but despite the team’s hardships, head coach Jeff Hafley still believes in the direction of his organization. On Tuesday, Miami’s rookie head coach spoke with the South Florida media and discussed why he believes his squad will turn things around moving forward. “Everything that we do is towards winning, but if we have the right guys in the building, and they keep improving, and if they keep trusting in their teammates and trusting in themselves, and develop, they’ll continue to go forward and give their best, and do everything they can, because they respect and love their teammate, and go after it, and get better and win a game.” Hafley continued: “It’s what I just told them downstairs in the team meeting. I told the guys very clearly that this was going to be a tough journey that we were all going to go on. I told them that if they weren’t up for it, then they can go talk to [Jon-Eric Sullivan]. This is the time to find out, as we build this thing and grow, who are the real guys? Like, who are the guys that we can trust — that want in the boat — because when we flip this thing — and we will flip this thing — that we want to have around? The only way you find out those things is going through adversity together. And we’re going to find a lot about the guys.” Does Hafley believe he already has the right guys in the building? “The way we’re building this thing and the way we are talking about the process and the way we’re playing together, and the way we’re getting better, and the energy that we’ve played with, and the toughness that we’ve played with, I do believe we have the right guys, more or less, that will help us get to that point.” It’s clear that Miami’s coach believes in his team and trusts they aren’t too far away from being a consistently competitive squad. Though the Dolphins remain winless on the season, they are trusting in their process and have faith that the results will start to show in the win/loss column soon. Their next opportunity to finally claim a victory will come this Sunday when Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals visit Hard Rock Stadium.

(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As a part of the Miami Dolphins’ 2026 roster rebuild, the team moved second-year guard Jonah Savaiinaea from the left to his natural right-side position. The guard has responded to the move, but it may not be the only reason he looks like the player Miami hoped to get when they selected him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. According to Savaiinaea, the move actually has nothing to do with his growth and improved play. According to a report from Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson, Savaiinaea identified several other areas that have led to his improvement, which includes not having allowed a sack so far this season after leading all guards in sacks allowed last year: Even though Dolphins coaches have said he seems more comfortable playing right guard (his position at Arizona) after playing left guard as a rookie, Savaiinaea said changing sides has had “zero impact” on his growth. So what has been the difference? He cited a few factors: game experience, increased confidence, helpful tips from offensive line coach Zach Yenser and a determination not to get beat inside, which was perhaps his biggest of several problems last season. “Most of my beats, when I got beat, were [on] the inside” last season, he said. “My plan this year is to not get beat inside. That’s the minor change I’ve put into my game this year. There are a lot of good rushers out there who know how I’m setting. It’s minor improvements like not getting anywhere with my first step.” Savaiinaea would go on to talk about new offensive line coach Zach Yenser and the game slowing down for him. title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
summary: The Dolphins hung tight with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game, but somehow that game never felt close.  The Dolphins not only had a chance in this game against Minnesota, but they also actually held a lead.  Well, for about 30 seconds.  Still, this one was a heartbreaking loss because unlike the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II (0) celebrates with running back Jaylen Wright (5) after scoring a touchdown during the second half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dolphins hung tight with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game, but somehow that game never felt close. The Dolphins not only had a chance in this game against Minnesota, but they also actually held a lead. Well, for about 30 seconds. Still, this one was a heartbreaking loss because unlike the previous 3 games, they felt like they could win. There were some more positives, but plenty of negatives. Here’s what I saw on a quick watch. THE OFFENSIVE NEEDS… WORK First, I will give credit where credit is due. The Vikings have one of the best defenses in the NFL. They generate a ton of pressure and have the best scoring defense in the NFL. They have held better offenses to less. The Bears scored 59 points in week one against the Panthers. The Vikings held them to 3 points at their home. The Vikings have only allowed 4 TDs all season, one of which was to the Dolphins. That said, the Dolphins’ offense was nothing short of terrible on Sunday. Willis struggled mightily, going 9-17 and 85 yards. He was sacked twice, though one of those sacks was a “strip sack” where the ball hit a defender’s helmet right before Willis was able to throw it. Despite the best pressure defense in the league, the Dolphins mostly kept Willis clean. The bigger issue in my opinion is the lack of playmakers helping their QB (hat tip to JUK). Willis targeted 6 WRs in the contest and only Malik Washington was the only one to contribute in a meaningful way. Rookie Chris Bell was blanked on 3 targets. Greg Dulcich wasn’t even targeted. Without Caleb Douglas, the Dolphins don’t have the weaponry to consistently move the chains and have a productive offense. Some of the blame will go to Willis and rightfully so. But he doesn’t have the help he needs either. This would be the same for a rookie this season OR next season. Unless Miami goes out in FA and signs a big time WR or TE – unlikely – then whatever rookie QB they draft will also struggle thanks to the skill players around him. THE DEFENSE ALSO NEEDS WORK DESPITE SOME POSITIVES There is a lot being made about how the defense stepped up in this game. They finally got home to the QB getting 4 sacks after getting shutout the previous 3 games. The Dolphins were able to generate pressure all game long. Linebackers Rodriguez and Brooks had a combined 31 tackles, with the rookie getting 18 total and 9 solo tackles. The Dolphins kept the Vikings out of the end zone, forcing 5 FG attempts. But… The Vikings were an even worse offense than the Dolphins entering this game. In week one, the Vikings QBs passed for 151 yards. In week 2, that number was 143. In week 3, they went for 168 yards. Against Miami, Murray went for 247 yards. In the previous 3 contests, the Vikings barely topped 62% CP in one game and 55% or below in the other 2. Murray went 27-37 against the Dolphins, for a whopping 72.9%. Wildly, that’s lower than what Miami had been allowing at over 80%. But they couldn’t contain what had been the worst passing offense in the league. The Vikings were able to do it without Justin Jefferson also. The damage came from tight end TJ Hockenson, whom the Dolphins could not stop. He caught 13 passes on 13 targets for 119 yards and would have scored a TD at the end but slid to force kneel-downs and end the game. Considering the Vikings #2 WR Jordan Addison was quietly 4-52, you would think the Dolphins would have forced Murray to look at someone other than Hockenson. But no. Not only that, but the Dolphins had been tighter against the run in the 1st 3 games. But they allowed Aaron Jones to go 20 carries for 94 yards. Murray went 6 for 16, but lost 5 yards on 3 kneel-downs, so he gained 21 yards on 3 actual attempts. The Dolphins kept the Vikings out of the end zone and were able to get on the board for sacks. But they will face much better QBs and offenses in the next few games and they don’t appear to have solved the issue of keeping QBs from getting easy completions. They also couldn’t get off the field when they needed to. If I asked you how many plays the Dolphins had in the fourth quarter, could you tell me without looking it up? I’ll tell you now: 3. That’s it. Three plays was all the offense had. We can argue about how bad the offense was and argue about where Willis should have thrown the ball on his final attempt. What we REALLY need to discuss is the fact that Minnesota got the ball at the end of the 3rd quarter – running one play in the 3rd – went on a 14 play drive to get a FG, leaving Miami with 6:41 on the clock. Miami went 3-and-out and that’s bad. But Minnesota got the ball back with 5:48 left and proceeded to end the game with a 10-play drive that should have ended with a TD, but they had 3 more plays to kneel out the game. Miami’s offense was bad. But Miami’s defense allowed Minnesota to run 26 plays – 26 FREAKING PLAYS – and burn 14 minutes in the FOURTH QUARTER ALONE!!! We can whine about the OL and QB play and all of that until the cows come home. But another easy way to help the QB is for the defense to GET. OFF. THE. FIELD! That was an embarrassment. THIS AND THAT They say football is a game of inches, but in this contest, it was a game of millimeters. Or perhaps microns. Malik Willis and Chris Bell had a highlight reel TD play wiped off the board because Bell’s toenail was across the line out of bounds. The Dolphins were going to get a first down due to roughing the kicker, but the defender got a fingernail on the ball to tip it. Ollie Gordon was “touched down” on a run despite the replay showing the defender merely wafted in his general direction. That negated what would have been a big run, possibly a TD run. All of these were game-changing plays that could have been the difference in the outcome. The toe being out of bounds cost a TD. The tipped punt that could have extended a drive resulted in a FG drive for Minnesota. That’s a 10-point swing in a game decided by 5 points. Not to mention the possible TD run stolen from Gordon. The discussion about the Dolphins offense is different today if the final was say… 24-20 in Miami’s favor. The officials were WAY too prevalent in this game. This isn’t a complaint about Miami getting screwed, although that argument could be made. Minnesota had more penalties than the Dolphins. There was a total of 20: 9 for Miami, 11 for Minnesota. That’s way too much laundry on the field for an NFL. There were other officiating issues across the league. It has become a very visible problem . I would say in this game, it was due to 2 crappy offenses more than anything else. But fans across the league are taking notice. Not only that, but two officials, including the referee for the Dolphins game have been suspended by the league for conduct towards players on Sunday . Ollie Gordon II had his breakout game, and he should be the starter moving forward. Last week, I was going to write about how OG2 seems to struggle with vision and doesn’t have the burst needed to be a full-time starter. But I waited to see what he’d do in this game. He ended up with 100 yards even on 9 carries. Most of that came on a 53 jaunt early in the third quarter. As usge, I like to exclude a long run or pass play from the stats (or a long negative play) because it can skew the averages, making something that’s actually negative look like a positive. I shall name this “The Kalen Ballage Rule”. Going 100 yards on 9 carries is an 11.1 YPC average and looks nice. But excluding the 53-yard run, he went 47 yards on 8 carries for a 5.9 YPC average. Which is also nice. That means he was effective overall despite one stat-skewing…
