full_text: The Coyote after the Vikings game OK, my ears must hear different things than the broadcasters who say “Look at what Jeff Hafley is building. Just wait until he gets the players!” They didn’t say “Let’s aspire to be the Green Bay Packers! The ACME of NFL franchises.” I have a question: be TOTALLY honest and don’t cheat! What does the word ACME actually mean? Don’t cheat! Be honest with your answers which will makes things funnier in the comments! To end my digression: go see Coyote vs Acme!!!! The Ghost of Vikings Passed Back to aspiring to be the Green Bay Packers! What the hell has the Green Bay Packer organization done since winning the Super Bowl with Aaron Rogers in 2011. Yes, 2011! Is that what we want to aspire to? Really, we were whipping their asses when Tua injured his noggin for the 8 th time. I don’t get it. Maybe I don’t understand what the goal is? Would you rather be the NY Giants and win 2 Super Bowls with Eli but suffer like 11 years of mediocrity in return or maybe you would rather be the KC Chiefs under Schottenheimer and go 11-5 every year but never even SNIFF the Super Bowl. The Phins were once like that too and the stadium in the 80s used to flash these graphics showing the Phins were the most successful sports franchise ever! Highest winning percentage! Ha! Those were the days. And don’t forget we lost 2 AFC Championship at home under Marino. But with #13 we were never out of the game. And that right there keep me faithful. I keep hearing that the GB cap situation is good, blah blah blah. What does that have to do with winning Super Bowls? Phincidents! I am watching what the Saints did with Drew Brees and Sean Payton. It eats me alive; I must admit. I also remember a classic episode of South Park in 2004 where Cartman dons a carboard box pretending to be a robot called Awesome-O. During the episode, Awesome-O is asked “who’s gonna win the Super Bowl?” Awesome-O answers “The New Orleans Saints” to mocking laughter from the crowd and myself at the time. Guess what? Awesome-O was correct, just like the Coyote during his trial! Devon Godchaux (Miami Dolphins 5 th round pick 2017) is still playing for the Saints! Wow! God Bless Him! Laissez les bon temps rouler! And the halftime show! Wowwie wow Wow! Back to this coaching staff; I have heard some strange statements like “Miami has trouble covering TEs.” This is an untrue statement, giving too much credit to the Phins. The statement should be “Miami has never heard of the TE position and doesn’t believe that it exists.” I have never watched a game or heard of a game where the TE was targeted 14 times(whatever) and every target was caught(Until Sunday). Is this what Coach Hafley is bringing to the Phins? This is a pure unadulterated embarrassment. On the last 3 rd down play, I was screaming “Don’t fall for the brush block and drift garbage that was taught to me in 1974.” I thought the great Green Bay standard bearer Jeff Hafley would have done SOMETHING to slow down this average TE. He isn’t Gronk, Jason Witten, Tony Gonzales or even Russ Francis (look him up). Where is the “secret sauce” that Hafley is bringing; where are the strategems! I have played in hundreds of pick-up games where I would “bird dog” that play and bait the QB into throwing that pass. But my God, he would have scored in a “tag” game. How can we take this organization seriously when they don’t know what a TE is? Do they cover TEs in Green Bay? Is that something they teach in year two of the rebuild? Do they play special teams in Green Bay? The word is out on the street, the Phins special teams play is hot garbage and there are opportunities to exploit. The TE position on the opposing team is the Road Runner and we’re never gonna catch him.
author: Paulie Dorsal

title: Vikings Autopsy: Daily Norseman Week 4 Postgame Roundtable (A 15-10 win over the Dolphins)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 4 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off another ugly one, this time a 15-10 win at home over the Dolphins, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 4-0. How much longer can the offense ride the defense’s coattails? Did the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Dolphins 15-10. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 4 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off another ugly one, this time a 15-10 win at home over the Dolphins, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 4-0. How much longer can the offense ride the defense’s coattails? Did the fourth quarter show an offense starting to figure some things out? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Dolphins in Week 4, 15-10. Brandon Warne : I’m going to take a little bit of a different tack here. While many are saying “they can’t keep winning like this” and things of that nature, I’m going with this: They have four wins — and those aren’t going anywhere. Good, bad or otherwise, they won those four games and nobody can take that from them. If you assume a team needs to go 10-7 to be in the playoffs this year, then if they can go 6-7 the rest of the way, they should be good to go. In a division that is by no means insurmountable with games against the Saints, Commanders, Colts, Jets and Falcons remaining, I’m choosing positivity. Now, that’s not to ignore the elephant in the room that they can’t keep winning games this way — which is likely more true than false — I also fall back on one of my most-used sports adages: No matter what, things will not stay the same. They’ll get better, or they’ll get worse — but they will not remain the same. It’s easy to fall into a thought process of “this won’t work if things don’t change,” but that’s rooted in a concept that I’ve never felt was true in sports — that things won’t change. Warren Ludford : It was another somewhat ugly win over a struggling team, so it was frustrating. On the other hand, the offense showed signs of improvement later in the game, especially with Kyler Murray. Defense and special teams continue to be great; the offense is still anemic, but there are some positive signs for the future. Craig Williams : Painful to watch. The Vikings could be the 2000 Ravens if they had average QB play. I wish Murray was mid. Shawn C. : Fortunate (again). Between the lucky breaks and penalties, we’re really playing with fire if the offense doesn’t turn the corner. Kyler Murray found his rhythm in the 4th quarter, which hopefully signals the consistent success many envisioned all offseason. Performances like these may be enough to get past the combined 0-8 Bucs and Dolphins, but teams like the Bills and 49ers will eat our lunch if the offense can’t hold up its end of the bargain. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have to go with T.J. Hockenson. Love ‘em or hate ‘em, a 93.2 PFF score really tells the story here. A safety valve is so vital with a quarterback still trying to find his identity within an offense, and that’s exactly what Hockenson provided — and not only in general, but with the top wide receiver in the NFL sidelined, besides. WL : T.J. Hockenson. He had his best game post-knee injury. The Vikings will need him with Jauan Jennings being a non-factor at this point. CW: Will the Thrill Reichard is the best kicker in Vikings history and this team’s biggest weapon. Aaron Jones and Dallas Turner are in consideration as well. SC : Dallas Turner. Another amazing day for Turner, who is now on pace for like 23 sacks. I expected improvement, but this is just ridiculous now. It seems like his name is being called on every pass play ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I’m going to go with Jauan Jennings. With Jefferson sidelined, it stood to reason that someone would have to find their way in the passing game to pick up the slack. And if I’m honest, I think Hockenson was third on my pecking order behind Jordan Addison — who was fine but not great with four receptions and 52 yards — and Jennings, who caught his only target for eight yards and graded out poorly in pretty much every facet of the game. WL : Johnny Hekker. He shanked two punts… CW : Wes Phillips. Waste of salary. SC : This one is tough, but I gotta go with Harrison Smith, who had a rough outing. Hoping it’s simply a matter of getting back into football shape after missing the entire offseason. ————— Question 4: For the second week in a row…where do you stand on Kyler Murray right now? BW : Baby steps — pun unintended. I think we expect an awful lot out of quarterbacks on a weekly basis, and there’s a lot of nuance that a signal-caller has to pick up on in the playbook, within the offense/communication with the coaching staff, and also with the supporting cast (both the pass-catchers and also the line, as well). I’ll also lean on his fourth-quarter stats as a reason for optimism: In the final stanza Sunday, Murray went 12-for-13 for 112 passing yards (92.3 percent), zero touchdowns/interceptions, zero sacks (!), 8.6 yards per attempt and a passer rating of 102.6. It’s…. something. WL : Kyler Murray is getting more acclimated and improving. His accuracy against the Dolphins was 90%, which is elite. And no turnovers. Sacks are still an issue, not 100% his fault in every case, but he built a rapport with T.J. Hockenson, which will serve him well down the road. The Dolphins played cover-2 most of the game (which they hadn’t done much this season), which limited the deeper passing game. But overall, he showed signs of getting more acclimated to the offense and becoming a bit more comfortable in his second full game. CW : We’re standing shoulder to shoulder with Donovan McNabb…in Minnesota, not Philly. SC : Optimistic. Murray played out of the shotgun much more this week, and I don’t think it’s a coincidence that he finally looked like the quarterback I thought he’d be since the spring. The fourth quarter looked like a completely different player. Getting Justin Jefferson back will be fun to watch. ————— Question 5: T.J. Hockenson — Is he “back” or do you still need to see more? BW : He’s BACK back. I think the most impressive thing to me is that he secured all 13 of his targets, making him the first pass-catcher with a 100.0 percent reception percentage on at least that many throws since CeeDee Lamb caught 13 of 13 targets for 98 yards and two scores on Jan. 7, 2024 against the Commanders. He’s also the first Vikings player to do so in team history. That’s right, a team with as rich a history as the Vikings when it comes to pass-catchers. That’s pretty special. WL : I think he’s back. He may not be targeted as much as he was against the Dolphins, but he showed he can be more dynamic than he has been in the past couple of years, and I don’t think he pulled that out for just one game. It may be as much mental as physical for him. But once he got it back, I don’t think he’ll lose it again in future games barring injury. CW : He’s never truly lived up to the expectations. A very nice game; let’s see if he can keep it up. SC : Oh, he’s back. If he stays healthy, he could have a 2023-type season. Murray loves throwing to tight ends, and a healthy, elite WR group will force defenses to pick their poison. It’s the perfect storm for Hockenson to thrive the rest of the way.

title: Will Reichard Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
summary: While the Minnesota Vikings’ offense can’t seem to find its way into the end zone, the National Football League has recognized the one guy on the roster who doesn’t seem to have any problems putting points on the board. On Wednesday, the league named kicker Will Reichard the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after defeating the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Minnesota Vikings’ offense can’t seem to find its way into the end zone, the National Football League has recognized the one guy on the roster who doesn’t seem to have any problems putting points on the board. On Wednesday, the league named kicker Will Reichard the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week. This means that a member of the Vikings has been named the Special Teams Player of the Week for three weeks in a row after Isaiah Rodgers won the award in Week 2 and return specialist Myles Price took home the honors in Week 3. Reichard accounted for all of the Vikings’ scoring in the team’s 15-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon at U.S. Bank Stadium, connecting on field goals of 50, 47, 41, 33, and 29 yards on the day. It’s the second time in his career he’s hit five field goals in a game, equaling the feat he accomplished in Week 7 last season against Philadelphia. Going back to last season, Reichard has now hit 31 consecutive field goals, which is the currently longest streak in the NFL and ties him with Fuad Reveiz for the third-longest streak in Vikings history. Counting extra points, he has converted 56 consecutive kicks, with his last miss* coming on a field goal attempt against the Los Angeles Chargers last season. (Yeah, I put a * next to “miss” there for a reason.) Reichard was also named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for the final month of the 2025 season. Reichard’s award makes the Vikings the fifth team in NFL history to bring home three consecutive Special Teams Player of the Week awards, and the first to do it since the San Francisco 49ers did it in 2011. The other teams to have done so are the 2007 San Diego Chargers, the 2004 New Orleans Saints, and the 2003 Kansas City Chiefs. Congratulations to Will Reichard on being named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season!
author: Christopher Gates

title: Vikings Sign Odell Beckham Jr., Jeshaun Jones to Practice Squad
summary: With a couple of open spots on the practice squad, the Minnesota Vikings filled them on Wednesday with a pair of wide receivers, one of which you may have even heard of before. Well, if you’re a Vikings fan, you’ve heard of both of them, but one of them. . .yeah, didn’t see this coming. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Odell Beckham Jr. #13 of the New York Giants walks off the field after losing the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a couple of open spots on the practice squad, the Minnesota Vikings filled them on Wednesday with a pair of wide receivers, one of which you may have even heard of before. Well, if you’re a Vikings fan, you’ve heard of both of them, but one of them. . .yeah, didn’t see this coming. The Vikings have announced the signings of wide receivers Jeshaun Jones and Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad. The Vikings brought Jones back after he served his three-game suspension for violating the league’s substance abuse policy and waiving him earlier in the week, but you don’t care about that at the moment, do you? Beckham Jr. really needs no introduction. He was drafted by the New York Giants out of Louisiana State in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft, after which he won the NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Year Award and has twice been named a Second-Team NFL All-Pro (2015, 2016). In his career, he has 575 receptions for 7,987 receiving yards and 59 touchdowns. His career has dropped off significantly since 2020, when he suffered a torn ACL midway through the season as a member of the Cleveland Browns. He returned to Cleveland for the 2021 season but had disagreements with the way he was being used in the Cleveland offense, leading to his release. He landed with the Los Angeles Rams and was a part of their Super Bowl championship team. He scored a touchdown in that Super Bowl, but he suffered another ACL injury during that game as well, one that caused him to miss the entire 2022 season. In 2023, Beckham signed with the Baltimore Ravens and had 35 receptions for 565 yards and three scores. He was released by the Ravens ahead of free agency in 2024 and signed with Miami. He started the season on the Physically Unable to Perform List and wound up being released in December, appearing in nine games and making just nine catches. He did not play in 2025, and for part of the 2025 season served a six-game suspension for violating the league’s performance-enhancing drug policy. Beckham attempted a comeback with the Giants this season and made the 53-man roster out of training camp, but was released after three games without recording a catch. I’m not sure how high the expectations should be for OBJ at this point in his career or how much juice he has left in the proverbial tank. But he’s a member of the Vikings now, so what does everyone think about this development?

title: The Re-Education of Kyler Murray and the Outlook for the Vikings Offense
summary: Kyler Murray’s first pass as a member of the Minnesota Vikings was a hail mary thrown under pressure to a double-covered Jauan Jennings. Not surprisingly, it was intercepted. That was on a second-down with less than a minute elapsed in the first quarter of a 0-0 game. A few offensive plays later, he was knocked […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before kickoff against the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyler Murray’s first pass as a member of the Minnesota Vikings was a hail mary thrown under pressure to a double-covered Jauan Jennings. Not surprisingly, it was intercepted. That was on a second-down with less than a minute elapsed in the first quarter of a 0-0 game. A few offensive plays later, he was knocked out on a scramble which caused him to miss the rest of that game and the next one. Those two plays encapsulated most of the trials and tribulations of Kyler Murray over his seven years in Arizona: hero ball and injuries. Hero ball was ingrained to some degree by the Air Raid scheme Murray ran in college and his early years in Arizona, but also to some degree by necessity – playing for a team that frequently lacked a capable defense and forced to come back from deficits or win shootouts. Injuries happened on Murray’s scrambles, although they were typically non-contact injuries. A More Conservative Kyler Murray But one can surmise, based on Murray’s week one performance, the strengths of this 2026 Vikings team and Murray’s subsequent performance, that there was a conversation between Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and Murray before he returned that might have gone something like this: KOC: Kyler, now that you’re back on the field, let me remind you of a couple things. First, since I’ve been head coach, we’ve won at least 13 games in seasons when we’ve had a healthy starting quarterback. And we win 90% of the games when we tie or win the turnover battle. Kyler: Okay, I get where you’re going with this. KOC: Good. We don’t need you to play hero ball. Just take what the defense gives you. Scrambling is okay when there’s nothing available, but we’re not looking to make that a big part of the offense. Working from the pocket and being on schedule is what we’re after. But when you do scramble, avoid contact and slide. We don’t want the risk of you getting hurt trying to get an extra yard or two. Throwaways are fine too when there’s nothing there. Kyler: Got it. KOC: Don’t forget, you’ve got a defense you can lean on here- I know that’s something you haven’t had as much in the past. Kyler: thanks Coach- that makes my job a lot easier. Since Murray has come back after week one, he’s been more conservative. He’s been careful with the football- no turnover-worthy plays according to PFF- and has been more judicious with his scrambling- avoiding contact and sliding the few times he did scramble. There’s also been a couple times he’s wound up to throw into a tight window but thought better of it. That’s not to say he’s avoided all tight window throws or hasn’t taken some shots downfield- he has- but it’s been in the context of taking what the defense gives him rather than forcing a throw into double coverage. Getting Acclimated? Still, there have been some instances where rhythm or timing has been a bit off, causing Murray to miss a throwing window or the throw to be off the mark. Murray has also shown some rust, particularly in his first full game against the Bucs, when his accuracy (adjusted completion percentage) was just 66.7% – well below his career average- and his average time to throw was 3.35 seconds- well over his career average. But in the Dolphins game, Murray’s average time to throw fell to 3.07 seconds- still above his career average but an improvement over the previous week. And his accuracy jumped to 90.6%, albeit on a shorter depth of target, as the Dolphins focused on taking away the deeper part of the field with their coverage – probably after seeing the deep shots Murray had to Jordan Addison the previous week. Murray also seemed to get into a bit of a rhythm late in the Dolphins game, developing a rapport with TJ Hockenson that should serve him well down the line. Murray now ranks 5th in adjusted completion percentage and 4th in turnover-worthy play rate on the season. Still, the Vikings offense is hardly hitting on all cylinders after four games, as it still ranks near the bottom of the league in most major metrics. Outlook for the Vikings Offense A month into the season, Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson have been on the field together for just 17 plays. Clearly having Carson Wentz play two games at quarterback while Justin Jefferson missed all but one drive of Kyler Murray’s last two starts has had an impact on the Vikings offense. Not to mention Jordan Mason being out the last three games. All of these injuries has made just about everything more difficult for the offense and it has shown. Additionally, Murray’s acclimation process was delayed by the two games he missed. But going forward, there is reason for optimism and improvement. Return of Justin Jefferson. The return of Jefferson, which could be this Sunday, is important not simply because of his production, but because his presence makes it more difficult to defend the rest of the Vikings offense. Return of Jordan Mason. Mason will return after the bye-week and he’s the Vikings best back. He’ll also take the load off of Aaron Jones, who’s done reasonably well in Mason’s absence but having Mason back will improve the Vikings ground game. Kyler Murray continuing to acclimate to the Vikings offense. It’s only been two games, but we’re starting to see Kyler Murray get a little more comfortable and acclimated to the Vikings offense and develop rapport with his receivers, most recently TJ Hockenson. We’ve only seen a couple passes from Murray to Jefferson, but Murray started working on his rapport with Jefferson in training camp so that might be further along despite the lack of playing time together. His rapport with Addison isn’t quite there yet, despite some key receptions. There have been some other instances where the opportunity was there but the timing was off. More reps will help across the board. It’s still very early. Next Opponents Lack Strong Defense . The Vikings offense will have the opportunity to gel against opponents over the next four games that rank in the bottom half in terms of pass defense DVOA, which is helpful. The Saints, Colts, Lions, and Bills all rank in the mid-20s in pass defense DVOA. The Saints, Colts, and Lions also rank in the bottom six in run defense DVOA. The Bills rank 17th. The loss of Josh Oliver and now Donovan Jackson for the season are significant ones, but Joe Huber looks like he can fill in without a big drop off in production. It looks like the Vikings may replace Oliver in part with an extra lineman (Caleb Tiernan) but Gavin Bartholomew and Max Bredeson could see more snaps as well. Jauan Jennings looks like a bad fit now. Before the season started, the acquisition of Jauan Jennings seemed like a perfect fit for what the Vikings wanted to do offensively. He had been a big, tough receiver for the 49ers who could block, move the chains catching underneath passes and make contested catches in the end zone. He’s done none of that so far. Part of the problem is that Kevin O’Connell has him running a different set of routes that he’s not good at. Jennings is not an athletic receiver or a good detailed route runner. He’s more of a tight end in that respect. He can run shallow crossers, slants, stops, and flat routes and make contested catches with his size. But he’s running downfield routes now and not gaining separation- as expected. Worse, he’s the lowest graded run blocker on the team so far this season according to PFF. At this point, Tai Felton or Myles Price look like better WR3 options. Price has the third best run blocking grade on the team, albeit on just 15 reps. Maybe Jennings can be salvaged, or maybe he will be replaced, but there is an opportunity for improvement at WR3 that could help the offense moving forward. Bottom Line It’s been a slow start for the…

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. So, we want to know how everyone is feeling after how this past Sunday unfolded. As we saw, Kyler Murray hit T.J. title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: You Play To Win The Games!
summary: The Vikings handled their business against the Dolphins and stacked another win although you would not know it based on a lot of the comments here (and elsewhere). It does not matter that the team has been without one of the best receivers in the NFL for basically the last two games. It does not […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) throws the ball during the first half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Vikings handled their business against the Dolphins and stacked another win although you would not know it based on a lot of the comments here (and elsewhere). It does not matter that the team has been without one of the best receivers in the NFL for basically the last two games. It does not matter that the main running back that shares duties with Aaron Jones has been out. It does not matter that the left tackle got a stinger and concussion and missed most of the game. It does not matter that the starting left guard tore is meniscus and missed most of the game and now will be out for the season. All that matters is that Kyler Murray is not playing like an All Pro Quarterback, KOC is not calling a great or even good game (as if these commenters would know – they dont), and the team “gave up” on JJ McCarthy. It is going to take time for folks to get over the fact that the people who were with JJ every day, in all the meetings, on the practice fields, etc. decided that it was time to move on. I am not worried about the offense nor do I expect it to be at peak level right now. Assuming they make the playoffs, I want to see the offense peaking right before the playoffs which is 13 more games from now. Any complaints now are premature and just silly. The offense has not had all the presumed starters together yet. Hopefully, Jefferson will play this week so at least he and Kyler can start to build more chemistry. He caught two passes on two targets for 38 yards before hurting his ankle which is a good sign. Once they get Mason back it should be even better. Missing Donovan Jackson is going to hurt but maybe there is a move that can be made to bring in some extra linemen. It never is the move you expect though. Just like after the draft when the team signs undrafted free agents. Quite often they sign players I never heard of to be honest. I am wondering if there is a lineman the team could trade for either as a backup to Huber or maybe even to start? The team did sign Trevor Keegan who is 6’6″ 320 and started 37 games for Michigan winning the title there too. He was drafted in the 5th round by the Eagles in the 2024 draft. The Eagles released him in August of 2025 but their line is tough to crack. He is on the Vikings 53 man roster so the new GM, Nolan Teasley thinks highly of him. I doubt they make any moves besides maybe adding someone to the practice squad. The Saints game will be a tough test for sure and the offense needs to pick it up more. I expect they will especially if Jefferson is back. I don’t know but when Kyler Murray can complete 27 out of 37 passes (73%) for 247 yards without Jefferson while not turning it over then that is a very good thing and I am hoping he does similarly the rest of the way. That is all the team needs right now. Just incremental improvements as the season progresses. I know it wont stop the hand wringers but what can you do? You play to win the games! View Link Minnesota Vikings News and Links Kevin O’Connell Updates Donovan Jackson Injury, Recaps Kyler Murray’s Final Stretch Against Miami https://www.vikings.com/news/kevin-oconnell-updates-donovan-jackson-injury-dolphins After a strong start to the season, Donovan Jackson’s second NFL campaign is being cut short. The Vikings left guard injured his knee against the Dolphins Sunday, and imaging taken Monday confirmed a torn meniscus that will require surgery. Vikings Head Coach Kevin O’Connell spoke to media members and said the injury will “likely end his regular season” based upon early prognosis. “Donnie’s gotten off to a great start this year. Unbelievable offseason and ascending player,” O’Connell said. “A temporary setback for him, but very, very excited about Donovan Jackson the player, and we’ll support him and love him up, and he’ll still be a big part of that O-line room and culture here as we move forward.” Though it will be a challenge to replace Jackson, O’Connell spoke highly of the job Joe Huber did stepping in for him and noted coaches have been “really excited” about the interior lineman since signing him in 2025 as an undrafted rookie. “He’s physical. He’s a smart player, has spent a lot of time really diving in, working,” O’Connell said. “Whether it’s been with [center] Blake [Brandel] or his reps he’s taken at center, I think it’s opened up his viewpoint and his ability to impact at [multiple positions]. “But yeah, it’s definitely going to be something we’ve got to work through, and Donnie, I would definitely say was an impact player for us,” O’Connell added. “High expectations for Joe. I know his teammates have him, [offensive line coaches], they have high expectations for him, and we’ll do whatever we can to support him and expect him to play well.” According to analytics site Pro Football Focus, Huber did not allow a sack or hit of Kyler Murray in 71 snaps. Ryan Van Demark, who played 36 snaps in place of left tackle Christian Darrisaw, also was not assessed with allowing a sack or a hit. Darrisaw exited the game in the second quarter with a neck injury but then returned. He later left again, however, to be evaluated after a different play and is now in the concussion protocol. “Working through initial stages on that,” O’Connell said. “I’ll keep you posted throughout the week on where he’s at.” Center Michael Jurgens and tight end Ben Yurosek, who have been on Injured Reserve, will begin practicing this week and be evaluated. No 1. Murray’s final stretch O’Connell described encouragement after watching the way Kyler Murray finished Sunday’s game. The Vikings QB completed 12 of 13 passes in the fourth quarter, highlighted by gains of 27 and 22 yards, respectively, to Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. O’Connell said he and Murray are spending “more and more time together” either in 1-on-1 situations or working on game plans and playbook processing. “Even though we’re in Year 5 [of this offense] and we may call it something all of our players know, it might be the first time since either an install in the spring or training camp he’s hearing it,” O’Connell said. “I thought there were some plays where he was really comfortable in a game where the Dolphins pass rush — whether it was via stunts or some of the pressure packages — they were able to get to him a few times. “There was a firm feeling to his footwork and his drop and then getting through progressions,” O’Connell added. “I thought he had some huge backside throws to move the chains to T.J. late in the game, and then he used his legs a couple times to create some extra time and put the ball in play or take off and get us some yards.” No 4. Defense at another level Minnesota’s defense has been playing at an incredibly high level through the first four games. Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores has had success with his unit since joining O’Connell’s coaching staff in 2023, but are there reasons the group seems to be even more effective early this season? O’Connell said he’ll take time over the Week 6 bye to break that down even more with defensive coaches, but he provided a high-level answer Monday. “I think I’ve felt the impact of the d-line, the fits of guys and their roles within the defense … it can sometimes look like chaos, but it’s an organized symphony of guys making sure [in regards to stopping the run, whether we’re pressuring to it, away from it … it feels like we’re doing some fundamental things at a really high level,” O’Connell said. “Building a wall, defeating blocks, guys defeating double teams, the cutback player being right where they’re supposed to be. title: 2026 NFL Week 5: Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints
summary: The Minnesota Vikings will look to remain among the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated as they travel to the Big Easy to face off with the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. Despite another game where the offense failed to find its way into the end zone, the Vikings stretched […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 12: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the second quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings will look to remain among the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated as they travel to the Big Easy to face off with the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. Despite another game where the offense failed to find its way into the end zone, the Vikings stretched their undefeated streak to four games, and nine in a row going back to last season, with a 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium last Sunday. Will Reichard connected on five more field goals and Brian Flores’ defense put together another masterful effort, holding the Miami offense under 100 yards passing and ensuring that the Vikings would remain one of just three teams in the league without a loss over the season’s first four weeks. The Saints come into this one with a record of 1-3 and are coming off of a pretty rough loss in Week 4, getting blown out by their division rivals from Atlanta on Monday Night Football by a final score of 45-24. The Saints will be looking to avoid a third consecutive home loss, as they were defeated at the Caesars Superdome by the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3 by a score of 35-27. The Saints’ lone victory so far came in Week 2, when they engineered a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens in Baltimore. That is currently the lone blemish on the Ravens’ record this season. The statuses of Vikings’ wide receiver Justin Jefferson and left tackle Christian Darrisaw are both in doubt for this one. Jefferson missed the victory over Miami with an ankle injury he suffered in the team’s Week 3 win over Tampa Bay, while Darrisaw is currently in the league’s concussion protocol and will be monitored throughout the week. We know that Minnesota will go into this one without guard Donovan Jackson, who suffered a torn meniscus in the first quarter of the Miami game and is set to undergo surgery that will likely end his 2026 season. After a couple of weeks in the late Sunday window, this game will find the Vikings back in the noon Central Time window on Sunday afternoon, with coverage being provided by the FOX family of networks. We’ll be keeping all of our stories relating to this week’s game in this stream for you, so be sure to keep checking back for the latest. summary: The Minnesota Vikings and the New Orleans Saints are both well-known “dome” teams. And yet, somehow, their game on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans could be affected by the weather. We’ll explain. After a very quiet Atlantic hurricane season to this point, there’s now an area that has been named Invest 92L […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 03: A general overall exterior view of Caesars Superdome ahead of the NFL Super Bowl 59 football game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Kansas City Chiefs on February 03, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and the New Orleans Saints are both well-known “dome” teams. And yet, somehow, their game on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans could be affected by the weather. We’ll explain. After a very quiet Atlantic hurricane season to this point, there’s now an area that has been named Invest 92L that is sitting in the Bay of Campeche off of the coast of Mexico. Over the next couple of days, this area is being forecast to organize into, at the very least, a tropical depression and start making its way into the Gulf of Mex. . .the Gulf of Am. . .into the Gulf. You know which Gulf I’m talking about. If the tropical depression manages to get organized enough, it could develop into Tropical Storm (or even Hurricane) Isaias. And while it’s too early to tell the exact path the storm might take, early indications have it headed right for the Gulf Coast. Here are the “spaghetti models” from the 12Z (approximately 7:00 AM Central) runs of the various models this morning, courtesy of the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee . At the 96-hour mark, or early Saturday morning, a lot of the models have the storm parked right off of the coast or relatively close to it. Obviously, the storm isn’t going to have enough time to develop into a Category 4 or 5 hurricane or anything like that, but it could still be significant enough to potentially cause issues for, say, a football team whose plane is attempting to land at Louis Armstrong International Airport or something. If something slows the storm down and it doesn’t start impacting the area until later on in the day, it could make things even trickier, if not potentially impact the game itself. I’m not saying that this depression/storm/potential hurricane is definitely going to impact the game on Sunday afternoon in New Orleans. I’m just saying it’s something that shouldn’t completely be ignored at this point.

(Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Drake Maye has been named AFC Offensive Player of the Week following his resurgence at Highmark Stadium. The New England Patriots captain completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns in last Sunday’s 29-26 AFC East upset against the Buffalo Bills. He added a team-high and season-high 54 rushing yards to lead the conference’s quarterbacks by the end of Week 4. Week 4 belongs to @DrakeMaye2 🙂‍↕️ pic.twitter.com/ifqG8dU3mI — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 7, 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Foyesade Oluokun and Kansas City Chiefs punter Matt Araiza joined the QB as AFC Defensive Player of the Week and AFC Special Teams Players of the Week, respectively. Entering last Sunday’s divisional matchup with one touchdown and seven turnovers on the campaign, Maye was intercepted once and lost a fumble on the lone occasion he was sacked in Orchard Park. But the 24-year-old delivered two scoring strikes to Romeo Doubs and hit the right glove of Efton Chism III for the game-winning TD with 1:50 remaining in the fourth quarter. And with that, the unbeaten Bills went to 3-1 while the Patriots went to 2-2. For the No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, it marks the second career AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor. Maye finds himself the fifth quarterback in franchise history to get the call multiple times, joining 30-time winner Tom Brady, six-time winner Drew Bledsoe as well as two-time winners Matt Cassel in Tony Eason. The North Carolina product also joins running back Willie Parker and tight end Alge Crumpler as the only Tar Heels to twice be named AFC Offensive Player of the Week during their careers. A reigning second-team All-Pro who paced the NFL in passer rating and completion percentage on the way to Super Bowl LX, Maye will cross paths with the Las Vegas Raiders next Sunday. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots strength of schedule talk is back on the menu
summary: One of the biggest talking points surrounding the New England Patriots last season was the supposedly easy schedule they played on their way to a division title, playoff berth, and ultimately the Super Bowl. While some of it was naturally hyperbole, there was some truth to the fact that the team benefitted from its fourth-place […]
full_text: One of the biggest talking points surrounding the New England Patriots last season was the supposedly easy schedule they played on their way to a division title, playoff berth, and ultimately the Super Bowl. While some of it was naturally hyperbole, there was some truth to the fact that the team benefitted from its fourth-place schedule and a generally weak year in the AFC. This season was supposed to be different. Entering 2026, the team was set to go up against an above-average slate of opponents. Based on win-loss totals from a year ago, their scheduled ranked as the sixth-hardest; based on projected win totals, they ranked 10th. Turns out, their schedule might be a lot easier than that if we use the first four weeks of the season as an indication. Using traditional win-loss rate, only three other clubs have it easier down the stretch than the current 2-2 team. And here we go — Ben Baldwin (@rbsdm.com) 2026-10-05T14:09:03.560Z Even if we use a more complex methodology — Pro Football Focus’ point spread rating — we can see that New England’s schedule from here on out becomes a lot more manageable. Strength of schedule data via PFF. Lower number is tougher opponents. So for instance, the Raiders, Chiefs, and 49ers have had the easiest schedule so far, will have the toughest going forward (they all play each other). The Lions had easy so far, will stay that way. pic.twitter.com/uYARXVWqTB — Shaun Newkirk (@Shauncore) October 6, 2026 That does not mean the Patriots’ remaining 13 games won’t have their pitfalls and potential for problems. Whether it is teams getting healthier at key positions (i.e. Chicago Bears) or hitting their stride at the right time (i.e. Green Bay Packers), or challenging circumstances due to scheduling (i.e. two Thursday night games) or location (i.e. Detroit Lions in Germany), anything can happen even if the projection works in New England’s favor at the moment. Still, what this shows more than anything is that the Patriots have a chance to build some momentum after a challenging four-game stretch to open the season. Given that they are 2-2 and currently inside the AFC playoff picture , they have the potential to keep making some noise. It starts with internal improvement both performance- and health-wise, but the schedule certainly could help with that as well. Again.

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Raiders ahead of Week 5
summary: There’s the Josh McDaniels connection. There’s the Tom Brady connection. And then there’s those in the AFC East and AFC West locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for Sunday have been both New England Patriots and Las Vegas Raiders during the NFL journeys. Here’s a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Adam Butler #69 of the Las Vegas Raiders enters the field during player introductions prior to an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s the Josh McDaniels connection. There’s the Tom Brady connection. And then there’s those in the AFC East and AFC West locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for Sunday have been both New England Patriots and Las Vegas Raiders during the NFL journeys. Here’s a glance through the list of the formers leading up to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium. LAS VEGAS Phillip Dorsett II, wide receiver — Dorsett has not made appearance beyond the preseason since 2023. But the No. 29 overall pick in the 2015 NFL draft has continued his career in Las Vegas as a member of the practice squad over the past two campaigns. That’s after making a previous stop there when New England’s current offensive coordinator held the title of head coach. The 33-year-old wide receiver has caught 151 passes for 2,001 yards and 12 touchdowns since entering the league out of the University of Miami more than a decade ago. In 2017, he landed in Foxborough at the 53-man roster deadline as the Indianapolis Colts landed quarterback Jacoby Brissett. From there, Dorsett reeled in 73 passes for 881 yards and eight touchdowns across 45 games in the regular season. The playoffs stretched additional 126 yards and two trips to the end zone. A Super Bowl LIII ring followed. Adam Butler, defensive tackle — Butler entered the league at Gillette Stadium as an undrafted free agent in 2017. The former Vanderbilt convert from the offensive line to the defensive line went on to appear in 63 games, starting 12, while having a hand in 96 tackles, 15 sacks and nine batted passes. After being retained on a restricted tender in 2020, the Super Bowl LIII champion moved on to another corner of the AFC East. Yet Butler was released by the Miami Dolphins with a failed physical designation in 2022 and spent the year out of football. The 32-year-old defensive tackle has since found his footing in Las Vegas over the past four seasons. Butler’s time in silver and black has spanned 53 games, 32 starts, 152 tackles and 11.5 sacks. He’s also knocked down six passes, forced two fumbles and recovered two fumbles. Patrick Johnson, defensive end — Now on the 53-man roster for the Raiders, Johnson had seen his agreement in Foxborough expire in February. The 28-year-old edge rusher joined the practice squad of the 2025 AFC champions during preparations for Super Bowl LX. Originally entering entering the NFL in the seventh round of the 2021 draft at No. 234 overall, Johnson was a member of the Philadelphia Eagles’ Super Bowl LVII team and has also spent time with the New York Giants as a waiver claim. The Tulane product has checked into 74 games in the regular season while totaling 50 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and one recovery as well as a pair of starts. Cameron McGrone, linebacker — The Patriots called McGrone’s name in the fifth round of the 2021 class at No. 177 overall. But with a redshirt year on deck after the Michigan product sustained a second torn ACL during his final Big Ten season. McGrone started and finished his rookie campaign on the non-football injury list despite having his 21-day practice window open. After going through the waiver wire unclaimed at the end of the 2022 preseason, McGrone was brought back on New England’s practice squad. He’d depart for a 53-man roster spot in Indianapolis that winter, however, and the 26-year-old linebacker’s stay in the AFC South stretched into 2025. A stint with the Cleveland Browns followed before heading to the desert in May. McGrone then joined the Raiders’ practice squad at its formation. His NFL career includes 27 appearances and 13 tackles through 51 snaps on defense and 390 snaps on special teams. NEW ENGLAND Mack Hollins, wide receiver — The 33-year-old Hollins agreed to terms with the Patriots on a two-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. The move reunited the veteran wide receiver with his head coach from 2022. Hollins found four touchdowns and career highs with 94 targets, 57 receptions and 690 yards while a member of McDaniels’ Raiders that season. He now stands 131 games, 56 starts, 223 catches, 2,828 yards and 17 touchdowns into an NFL run that began in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 118 overall. The former North Carolina Tar Heel won a Super Bowl LII while a rookie in Philadelphia. Tours with six different NFL clubs have been logged. He leads his current club in receptions and receiving yards while also being tied with Romeo Doubs in targets, but did not finish the first game of October due to a calf injury. Ben Brown, guard — Back in the starting lineup amid attrition, Brown has appeared in 30 games since New England signed him to the 53-man roster off the practice squad of Las Vegas in the fall of 2024. Taking the field at center, left guard, right guard and jumbo tight end, the 28-year-old offensive lineman has handled 1,086 downs on offense for the organization. He’s also gotten the nod for 15 starts, with the first of his NFL career coming same week he left Las Vegas and the latest in place of two veterans on injured reserve. Brown made his initial stops with the Cincinnati Bengals, Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals after going undrafted in 2022. The Ole Miss product reached a contract extension in December and returned to the active roster shortly after being released in a procedural move in August. Greg Van Roten, guard — The 36-year-old Van Roten visited Gillette Stadium during training camp and circled back to sign a one-year deal after the aforementioned backup interior lineman suffered a multiweek injury. He started at right guard in New England’s first game without incumbent Mike Onwenu. But a thigh injury has since sent the NFL veteran of 147 games and 106 starts to IR, as well. Van Roten began his career as an undrafted rookie with the Green Bay Packers in 2012. The All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn has been a member of nine different NFL teams as well as the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts over the years since then. And in 2023, his lone year in Las Vegas, he started all 17 games before going wire-to-wire in 2024 and 2025 with the New York Giants. Robert Spillane, linebacker — Spillane finds himself a back-to-back team captain for the Patriots after reaching a three-year pact entering the 2025 league year. The 30-year-old Western Michigan alum has appeared in 103 games, starting 67, since entering the NFL in 2018 as an undrafted tryout at rookie minicamp with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans. Spillane went on to spend four seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers before heading to Las Vegas in 2023. From there, the linebacker became a Raiders captain and started every game across two campaigns, respectively posting 148 and 158 tackles as well as 1,101 and 1,095 defensive snaps. A veteran of 623 tackles and 9.5 sacks, Spillane’s NFL odometer includes three forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, eight interceptions and one touchdown return.

title: Patriots vs. Bills position grades and film review from Week 4
summary: Talk about a bounce-back. Failing to perform at an adequate level in all three phases, the New England Patriots were seemingly in the gutter following their Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. And things did not look much better either with a 1-2 record in hand, traveling to Buffalo to take on an unbeaten […]
full_text: Talk about a bounce-back. Failing to perform at an adequate level in all three phases, the New England Patriots were seemingly in the gutter following their Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. And things did not look much better either with a 1-2 record in hand, traveling to Buffalo to take on an unbeaten Bills team that had a strong case as the best in the AFC if not the entire league. And yet, it mattered not. The Patriots set the tone from the early first quarter on and managed to overcome a hostile environment as well as a rollercoaster ride of momentum. The end result was a 29-26 victory that saw a team much more in line with the preseason expectation. Our weekly film review backs this up, and the grades look accordingly. Patriots film review from NFL Week 4 Quarterback: Talk about confident quarterback play. Drake Maye didn’t eliminate the turnovers on Sunday, losing a fumble and throwing an interception — although he is only partially to blame for both — but he bounced back from those and a handful of other shaky moments in impressive fashion. That is the biggest takeaway from the win over the Bills, and it directly impacted how he operated on the field and within a well-structured and sequenced game plan. Maye anticipated passing windows more consistently, spread the ball around well, maneuvered the pocket well in the face of pressure, and was a threat as a runner. The entire offense looked much more in-sync in Week 4, and it started with a quarterback who hasn’t performed on this high a level since late during the 2025 regular season. | Grade: A- Drake Maye's first TD throw to Romeo Doubs came on a classic screen-pump concept. Great job by Maye to progress to the backside here, ball is out right as Doubs is leaning into his break and before the pass rusher can get home. pic.twitter.com/Atedvpp9jO — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 6, 2026 Running back: The final numbers for Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson did not look particularly impressive, with neither posting a positive expected points added per play or reaching 4.0 yards per carry. That being said, both backs ran hard and had some positive moments. Stevenson had successful runs twice in short-yardage, including a 1-yard touchdown, and was quick to the hole on a well-blocked trap run, whereas Henderson operated well when designed to get in space (see: his second-quarter reverse run for 11 yards). They also broke a combined five tackles between them and did not give up a single pressure in 10 total pass-blocking reps. | Grade: B- Patriots Trap run working as intended. DT had no idea what hit him. pic.twitter.com/P29QrLt5uC — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 6, 2026 Wide receiver: Already down A.J. Brown, the Patriots entered Week 4 with a starting duo of Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins. However, the latter was lost to a non-contact calf injury in the early third quarter, forcing the team to adjust at the position once again. They did by inserting Efton Chism into the lineup, and the second-year receiver made two of the game’s biggest receptions on the game-winning drive — including a 23-yard touchdown with one hand to give New England the decisive lead. Chism’s exploits made him a popular player postgame, for better or for worse , but so should have been Romeo Doubs. Playing his best game as a Patriot, the offseason signing showed good chemistry and timing with Maye as the a pair finished with six connections for 58 yards and a pair of scores. DeMario Douglas contributed 15 yards on two consecutive catches, with the second an excellent toe-tap on the sideline to move the chains on 3rd-and-5, while Kyle Williams was once again quiet — in part because Maye over-shot him on a go ball just before the Chism touchdown. | Grade: A – Tight end: Hunter Henry played his best game of the season on Sunday, which is good news for an offense needing him as a security outlet capable of exploiting soft zones and staying on the same page as his quarterback on extended plays. His five catches for 62 yards were both a season-high and included the game-clincher in the fourth quarter. Most encouraging, however, might have been his performance as a blocker. Eli Raridon was actively involved but not quite as successful in either areas of his position, while also missing some reps with an ankle injury. | Grade: B- Offensive line: Even though the offense as a whole operated at its highest level to date, the offensive line did not. The unit was particularly susceptible to pressure in the run game, with left tackle Will Campbell playing his most uneven game of the season against a talented edge rotation. He mostly limited the damage but on the whole allowed the operation to be disrupted on multiple occasions, either through pressures or penalties. Elsewhere along the line, the consistency was similarly lacking. Alijah Vera-Tucker was shaky as a pass blocker but had some good run blocks; Jared Wilson had two bad snaps but is seemingly starting to settle down as a pass protector; Ben Brown had some unsurprising highs and lows in his first start and needs to build better chemistry with Morgan Moses on line games, while Moses himself whiffed on a 5-yard tackle for loss but generally looked better than he did last week. | Grade: C- Defensive line: Even with Christian Barmore sidelined, the interior defensive line looked improved compared to last week’s loss in Jacksonville. Milton Williams continues to be stout without making the impact plays just yet, while Leonard Taylor worked his way into the backfield to pressure Josh Allen twice. Meanwhile, the edge trio of Dre’Mont Jones (pressure on Allen’s INT), Elijah Ponder (sack, fumble recover) and Gabe Jacas (multiple impressive reps vs. Pro Bowler Dion Dawkins) continues to contribute in a positive and most importantly disruptive way. There are still some questions about the overall group’s ability to slow down the run, though, with James Cook finding some perimeter success in the second half and the nose tackles — be it Cory Durden or DaQuan Jones — still getting pushed back too much. | Grade: A- Something else I love about this play: The Bills get extra bodies on Milton Williams and Elijah Ponder off PA, but Cory Durden and Gabe Jacas win their 1v1 matchups to reach Josh Allen Also appreciate Durden wrapping over Jacas to keep the QB pinned pic.twitter.com/OJ1NynPolt — Taylor Kyles (@tkyles39) October 5, 2026 Linebacker: Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss continue to play some solid football at the second level of New England’s defense. The former was all over the place, notching a forced fumble, quarterback pressure and run stuff all while disguising looks well and helping cover Josh Allen’s favorite target heading into the game, tight end Dalton Kincaid (1 catch, 7 yards). Elliss continued to be quick to the ball, either as a spy against Allen or as a enforcer against crossing patterns; Dawson Knox probably still feels the hit the veteran had against him in the first half. | Grade: B+ Cornerback: One would imagine that some of the Bills’ big passing plays would not have happened if the Patriots had Christian Gonzalez available; especially Buffalo’s final touchdown, when Keon Coleman fully exploited Charles Woods’ outside leverage with a stutter move. Woods in general had some uneven moments, as had starter Carlton Davis; both were beaten at some point for sizable gains. Davis, however, showed his instincts and ability to play downhill again. Marcus Jones was solid in coverage but he missed a pair of tackles and his run defense looked dubious at times. All in all and given the circumstances, however, the unit still faired reasonably well. | Grade: B- Safety: Craig Woodson capped his return after a one-week absence by hauling in a big interception in the late fourth quarter. Both he and fellow starter Kevin Byard however, were badly positioned on multiple of Buffalo’s big plays. Not every team has the quarterback to take advantage, but those…

title: The Number Crunch: Patriots’ win in Buffalo a tale of 2 quarterbacks
summary: This past Sunday was arguably one of the biggest regular season wins in recent memory for the New England Patriots. Not only did it put them “back in the race,” according to head coach Mike Vrabel, but the uneasiness surrounding the team’s offense and quarterback Drake Maye in particular has finally subsided for the time […]
full_text: This past Sunday was arguably one of the biggest regular season wins in recent memory for the New England Patriots. Not only did it put them “back in the race,” according to head coach Mike Vrabel, but the uneasiness surrounding the team’s offense and quarterback Drake Maye in particular has finally subsided for the time being. Let’s dive into the statistics that resulted in this much-needed bounce-back win over the Buffalo Bills. Drake Maye’s resurgence Without a doubt, Maye’s much-improved play in Week 4 was the key to the Patriots’ win at the brand-new Highmark Stadium. While still not perfect, the increased confidence, sharper decision-making, and better ball placement was all on display for last year’s MVP runner-up. From Week 4, of all quarterbacks who logged as many plays as Maye, the Patriots’ third-year QB ranked second in expected points added at 0.33. To put this in perspective, over the first three games, Maye had the fourth-worst EPA in the NFL, at -0.07. The only quarterbacks with a worse EPA up to that point were Justin Herbert, Aaron Rodgers, and Baker Mayfield, whose teams were a combined 2-7 through the first three weeks. To boil it down even deeper, Maye’s rushing has been prominent this season, and he proves every week that it is one of his greatest qualities. He was the lead rusher for New England in this game with eight carries for 54 yards and added 0.87 expected points per rushing attempt. For comparison, Rhamondre Stevenson had -0.01 and TreVeyon Henderson -0.14. The Bills seemingly had no answer for it, allowing Maye to pick up three first downs with his legs, including a 26-yard rush where he nearly reached the end zone. The numbers are even more impressive when you zoom out. Among quarterbacks, Maye ranks first in scramble yards with 127, on just 13 runs, which ranks 26th. His running ability has always been a dangerous part of his gam and so far, the opposition is yet to limit it, leading to numerous extended drives off of broken plays. One-dimensional Josh Allen Unlike Maye’s explosive rushing, Bills quarterback Josh Allen didn’t see nearly as much success as he’s used to on the ground. Allen, who won league MVP back in 2024, had his scrambling disabled by the Patriots’ defense. Through the first three games of the year, he rushed for 114 yards, and got into the end zone twice in each game. This past Sunday was the first game of the year he didn’t score with his legs multiple times, and didn’t have double-digit rushing yards. In five carries, Allen gained a measly 4 yards. This was his lowest amount in a game since November 20, 2024 against the Titans, where he had just 1 yard. Of course, Allen still has incredible arm talent and can make any throw he wants at any time. But to keep a great rusher like him in the backfield makes it much easier to defend him, since he is also prone to costly mistakes here and there. It’s safe to say the New England defense made the Bills’ superstar impatient, similar to Drake Maye in the beginning of the season. On what ended up being his last throw of the day, Allen soared a ball to Joshua Palmer that was intercepted by Craig Woodson. Buffalo had all three timeouts and 1:14 still left on the clock at their own 40-yard line. The ball traveled 41 yards through the air, marking his longest pass of the game. What allows Allen to be so dominant is his dual-threat abilities, and the Patriots took that away, leading to the win against their division rivals. As gloomy as it was looking for New England, it is now two years in a row that they put themselves on the map with a win against an undefeated Bills team. With a considerably better performance from their quarterback, hope has seemingly been restored within the Patriots fanbase as the team heads back home to take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5.
author: Dylan Klayman

title: Former second-round O-lineman among Patriots’ latest group of tryouts
summary: The New England Patriots had an active day on Tuesday. Besides releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to free up a second open spot on their 53-man roster, the team also made change to their practice squad. In addition, they had six players in town on a tryout basis. One of those — cornerback Al’zillion Hamilton […]
full_text: The New England Patriots had an active day on Tuesday. Besides releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to free up a second open spot on their 53-man roster, the team also made change to their practice squad. In addition, they had six players in town on a tryout basis. One of those — cornerback Al’zillion Hamilton — was added to the practice squad. The others currently remain unsigned. That group consists of running back Jamaal Williams, tight end Josh Kattus, offensive linemen Cody Ford and Jaren Kump, and defensive back Stephen Hall. Ford, 29, is the most notable player from that group. A second-round draft pick out of Oklahoma in 2019, he spent his first three years in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills and later also had stints in Arizona and Cincinnati. During that time, he appeared in a combined 102 regular season and playoff games with 43 starts. The 6-foot-3, 345-pounder has seen extensive action at both tackle spots and both guard spots playing 400-plus snaps at each of those positions. Williams, 31, offers similar experience. A fourth-round draft choice in 2017, he has played 121 games with 46 starts during his time in Green Bay, Detroit and New Orleans. The NFL’s leading touchdown-scorer in 2022 has remained without a team since March 2025. Kattus, Kump and Hall all entered the league as rookie free agents earlier this year. The Patriots will host the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium this week. Kickoff between the two teams is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: What releasing Jose Ramirez means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots made a change to their 53-man roster on Tuesday, releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez. The 27-year-old will now hit the waiver wire and if going through it unclaimed could return via the team’s practice squad. For now, however, let’s assess what letting him go means from a big-picture point of view. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots made a change to their 53-man roster on Tuesday, releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez . The 27-year-old will now hit the waiver wire and if going through it unclaimed could return via the team’s practice squad. For now, however, let’s assess what letting him go means from a big-picture point of view. Edge turnover continues The Patriots originally brought Ramirez in via their practice squad in early September, and decided to promote him to their active roster later that same month. That particular move came shortly before the team decided to place fellow edge Quintayvious Hutchins on injured reserve. Hutchins, who had suffered a knee injury in Week 2, has to remain on IR for at least two more games. Meanwhile, team captain Harold Landry is now eligible to return from the physically unable to perform list even though he has yet to make his practice debut this season. Regardless of his and Hutchins’ status, waiving Ramirez means more turnover at a position that has faced questions about depth going all the way back to the offseason. At the moment, said depth consists of Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas on the active roster, and Xavier Holmes and Benton Whitley on the practice squad. Quiet tenure over Ramirez getting released does not come as a particular surprise, especially considering that the Patriots might need some roster spots soon (more on that in a second). His tenure on the 53-man squad, after all, was relatively quiet. In two games, he played 30 total snaps. All eight of his defensive snaps came late in a blowout loss to Jacksonville in Week 3, while the other 22 were spent on special teams against both the Jaguars and Bills. He registered one kicking game tackle along the way, and saw time on four special teams units, primarily on kickoff coverage and the two return teams. Ramirez wasn’t actively bad, but he was a depth player in the truest sense of the word. Apparently, the team feels as if said depth is better allocated elsewhere. Second open roster spot Probably the biggest takeaway from the move is that it gives the Patriots two open spots on their 53-man roster at a time when several players have become eligible to be activated from various injury lists. The aforementioned Harold Landry, who remains on PUP, is just one of five players in the same boat. Safety Brenden Schooler (NFI), offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (IR), linebacker Khalil Jacobs (IR) and punter Bryce Baringer (IR) are also now cleared to return. Schooler seems like a safe bet to be brought back fairly recently, which would fill one of those two spots. As for the other, it probably wouldn’t be used on Baringer because who needs two punters? If he is activated, it likely will signal the end of the road for stand-in punter Mitch Wishnowsky. This means that Landry, Bryant and Jacobs are likely to eventually fill the other opening. Of course, the Patriots could also opt to sign somebody else — especially with Mack Hollins’ injury outlook TBD — or leave one spot open through Week 5 and with a potential A.J. Brown activation on the horizon.

title: Chris Olave continues to shine despite Saints’ ugly loss
summary: The New Orleans Saints had very little go right in Monday night’s 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, but Chris Olave continued to show why he should be considered one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. Olave finished the night with eight receptions for 116 yards on 12 targets. with a long reception […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints had very little go right in Monday night’s 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, but Chris Olave continued to show why he should be considered one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. Olave finished the night with eight receptions for 116 yards on 12 targets. with a long reception of 44 yards, leading the Saints in all three categories. This marked Olave’s third 100-yard receiving game through the first four weeks of the season and his second consecutive game surpassing that mark. He has now recorded at least eight receptions in all four games this season while reaching double-digit targets in each contest. That consistency has made Olave one of the few dependable pieces of the Saints’ offense that has had a difficult start. Through four games, Olave has 35 receptions for 491 yards (second league-wide) and one touchdown. He is averaging 14 yards per reception and has already established himself as the focal point of the Saints’ passing attack. Against Atlanta, Olave’s 116 receiving yards accounted for more than one-third of New Orleans’ 320 total yards. While the Saints ultimately could not keep pace with Atlanta, Olave’s performance was another reminder that New Orleans should feel comfortable with their investment in the wideout. For a team searching for answers after falling to 1-3, Olave has been one of the few constants. His production has not slowed despite the Saints’ struggles, and Monday night was the latest example.
author: Nic Jennings

title: Is Kellen Moore’s seat hot after loss to the Falcons?
summary: The New Orleans Saints’ 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night felt different. It was completely embarrassing. It was not just another loss. It was a total failure across all three phases on a night that was so special to the city and the fanbase. The Saints had an opportunity to make a […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints reacts to a call during the second half of an NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 13, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints’ 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night felt different. It was completely embarrassing. It was not just another loss. It was a total failure across all three phases on a night that was so special to the city and the fanbase. The Saints had an opportunity to make a statement in front of a nationally televised audience, and they blew it. And now, it’s fair to ask how hot Kellen Moore’s seat is after a 1-3 start. Moore did not hide from the performance afterward. He repeatedly acknowledged that the Saints were not prepared for Monday night’s game, which is frustrating to hear after knowing how important this game was and how much it meant to the organization. It would be easier to accept if it were an isolated occurrence. But it hasn’t been. The Saints under Kellen Moore have now trailed by double digits 16 times since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the NFL over that span. Monday night was another example, as Atlanta jumped out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter and extended it to 24-7 by halftime. The problem isn’t simply that New Orleans has fallen behind. It’s that Moore has been asked repeatedly why his team continues to struggle to open games, and his answers have consistently come back to some version of needing to look at things, make adjustments and figure out what went wrong. At some point, those answers have to turn into results. The Saints scored just six total first-quarter points through their first four games and have been forced to play from behind in every game this season. Under Moore, New Orleans has failed to score in the first quarter 14 times. That puts immense pressure on Moore to fix the preparation and execution issues that have followed his team into another season. There is still plenty of football left to play, and firing a head coach after four games would be an extreme move. But this is also Year 2 for Moore, so there’s no excuse of this being his first rodeo. The Saints expected progress after a six-win first season, and instead they are 1-3 after getting embarrassed by their biggest rival on Monday night. Moore has repeatedly said the Saints need to look at themselves. Now, the question is how long the organization will continue waiting for the answers to translate onto the field before they take a look at him.

Another winnable game was in front of them, but they basically gave it away. This team is 0-4 going into Week 5 with Baker Mayfield injured, bad coaching, roster issues everywhere, and a lack of run game. Green Bay also looked like they wanted to lose this game, and maybe if Mayfield was playing, they would have, but hope is lost with this team. Tampa Bay has a tough matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, so it looks like this team is going 0-5. Carolina Panthers On the opposite end of the division, Carolina did really well on Sunday Night Football against the Detroit Lions. The offense was really consistent and picked the Lions apart all night, with Tetairoa McMillan having a career night, and the run defense did really well against Jahmyr Gibbs. That same defense allowed Jared Goff to throw for more than 400 yards, so it wasn’t perfect, but it was impressive nonetheless. In Week 5, the Panthers have a winnable game, but the defense will need to do a bit better against the Jalen Hurts-led offense. Atlanta Falcons Now to our NFC South matchup of the week. The Falcons came into this game as an unknown, and they left fighting for first place in the division. Atlanta’s offense had the easiest day of their life, basically seeing zero resistance in the run and pass game, and the defense didn’t have to worry about the Saints’ rushing attack once. The Falcons have not seen a challenge in the past two weeks; maybe that will change in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens. New Orleans Saints On the other side of the matchup, the Saints were embarrassing in this one. Just a horrible loss in a game with so much emotion, and now, the team is 1-3 with hope ripped away from the fan base. Tyler Shough, Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Juwan Johnson are still the top guys on this team and it’s clear, but besides that group, it has not been great and now the Saints will have to go up against the Minnesota Vikings. NFC South standings: Carolina Panthers (1-2) Atlanta Falcons (2-2) New Orleans Saints (1-3) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4)
