title: Game Recap: Saints host Falcons in MNF clash
summary: The New Orleans Saints were hoping to bounce back after losing a second-half lead to the Las Vegas Raiders last week as they hosted the Atlanta Falcons in a primetime showdown on Monday night. Here’s a recap of the action. First Quarter The Falcons began with the ball, and Michael Penix Jr completed his first […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints celebrates a first down against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were hoping to bounce back after losing a second-half lead to the Las Vegas Raiders last week as they hosted the Atlanta Falcons in a primetime showdown on Monday night. Here’s a recap of the action. First Quarter The Falcons began with the ball, and Michael Penix Jr completed his first two throws to Drake London and Austin Hooper for nice gains. Then, Bijan Robinson broke off a 59-yard touchdown run to give Atlanta the lead. Trailing 7-0, the Saints went three-and-out before Atlanta had a brief drive of their own and punted back to the black and gold. Tyler Shough then found the first chunk play of the game for the hosts with a 23-yard pass to Juwan Johnson, before Alvin Kamara did the bulk of the drive’s work on a number of plays both on the ground and through the air. But having been limited to a field goal attempt, Daniel Carlson missed his kick wide left from 52 yards. Tyree Wilson sacked Penix on the ensuing possession, which resulted in another three-and-out. But New Orleans gave the ball right back to the visitors, as Kendre Miller fumbled. Atlanta took advantage of getting the ball back on the edge of the red zone, and within a few plays Bijan Robinson was in the end zone again for a 4-yard score. Trailing 14-0, Shough found a response straight away as a 44-yard connection with Chris Olave gave the Saints 1st-and-goal. Second Quarter A play later, Alvin Kamara found the end zone with a 3-yard touchdown run to get New Orleans on the board. But Penix and the Falcons responded straight away, with Brian Robinson Jr finding success running the football to move the drive into Saints territory. Shortly after a 27-yard pass from Penix to London, Brian Robinson ran in the 4-yard touchdown to give Atlanta a 21-7 lead. The Saints then went three-and-out again, and on the first play of the ensuing series, Penix threw to London for 37 yards to get to midfield. Both Robinsons then got touches and continued to run at will against a depleted Saints defense. New Orleans did eventually limit the visitors to a field goal attempt, which Nick Folk converted from 29 yards. Shough did make two throws to Olave and Johnson for a combined 30 yards as the Saints sought a response, but he was sacked on the edge of field goal range, and the black and gold had to punt again just before halftime. Third Quarter Receiving the ball to begin the half, New Orleans embarked on a 13-play, 59-yard drive during which Shough found a variety of receivers, including two throws to Olave for 10 and 11 yards, respectively. But an incompletion intended for Devaughn Vele on third down meant a short field goal attempt, which Carlson converted from 27 yards to put the score at 24-10. However, Atlanta continued to move the ball at will, with runs from Bijan Robinson and a 23-yard catch by Jahan Dotson getting the drive near the red zone. Penix converted a 3rd-and-10 with a pass to London, before Brian Robinson ran in an 8-yard touchdown to extend the visitors’ lead to 31-10. A defensive pass interference rescued the Saints from facing another 4th down straight away on the next possession. But after three incompletions, Shough did face 4th-and-10, a play on which he found Vele for 18 yards to extend the drive. Fourth Quarter A pair of offensive penalties at the end of the third meant the Saints would face 3rd-and-18. Shough found 17 of those yards with a pass to Vele, before Kamara ran for two yards on 4th-and-1. A few plays later, Kamara was in the end zone again with a 5-yard touchdown run to put the score at 31-17. But New Orleans just couldn’t buy a stop. Penix found Pitts for 28 yards to begin the ensuing drive, and a few plays later he found Dotson with a 31-yard touchdown strike to seal the game for Atlanta. Down 38-17, the Saints instantly turned it over on downs as Shough was sacked on 4th-and-6 deep in his own half. Brian Robinson ran in another touchdown from 11 yards out to extend the lead to 45-17. New Orleans then put together a 76-yard touchdown drive as time ran down, which was capped off by an impressive catch by Vele in the back of the end zone. Penix knelt out the clock after that, as the Falcons secured a 45-24 victory. Attention for the black and gold now turns to Week 5, as the Saints host the Minnesota Vikings.

title: Saints vs. Falcons Game MVP
summary: In all honesty, after getting your teeth kicked in the way the Saints just did in primetime, there really isn’t a player of the game. It is worth noting that Chris Olave played great again, but that’s not worth much when the team gets embarrassed the way it just did. The true MVPs of this […]
full_text: In all honesty, after getting your teeth kicked in the way the Saints just did in primetime, there really isn’t a player of the game. It is worth noting that Chris Olave played great again, but that’s not worth much when the team gets embarrassed the way it just did. The true MVPs of this game, however, were the fans. Shoutout to the entire city of New Orleans, which was on 10 from the moment the sun came up. New Orleans was ready and excited for what this game represented: the 20-year celebration of the reopening of the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. The atmosphere inside the Dome at kickoff was electric. I spoke with former Saints wide receiver Lance Moore after the game, and he said the Dome felt like the Dome again. And that is exactly what it should be. The fans were ready to roll. The excitement was there, and every single one of you, whether you were at home, at work, or at the stadium, just wanted that moment to shout, “Who Dat!” The Saints did a great job of having Steve Gleason lead the Who Dat chant at the start of the game, with his son by his side raising his hand. The emotions were nearly overwhelming as a fan, seeing all of the pageantry that went into this game. The former players from 20 years ago were present on the sideline for kickoff. It was beautiful to see. And then the game started. All of that went away because, for the next three hours, the play on the field did not match the expectations and hope that Saints fans had going into the night. Who Dat Nation, you all are this week’s Canal Street Chronicles MVP.

title: NY Giants’ CB Deonte Banks is NFC Defensive Player of the Week
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after his game-saving interception for the New York Giants in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Banks intercepted Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal at the 4-yard line, returning the ball 98 yards for a touchdown. Banks said after […]
full_text: Deonte Banks | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after his game-saving interception for the New York Giants in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Banks intercepted Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal at the 4-yard line, returning the ball 98 yards for a touchdown. Banks said after the game that he had called his shot during the week . “They was giving me a tight end and a receiver set all day. I’ve been thinking a slant all day and they haven’t been giving it to me,” Banks said. “That time I just knew they were going to give it to me. It was just a matter of time because they kept running it. “I knew I was going to take it. I’ve been calling it all week. I’m going to pick a slant this week.” “My guy. Tae Banks!” Wink Martindale’s belief in Deonte Banks never wavered. He talks about the Giants’ excellent “cat coverage” corner & breaks down his Pick-6 “Wednesdays with Wink” is up NOW on the Talkin’ Ball with Pat Leonard @YouTube Channel 👀 Brought to you by… pic.twitter.com/M8uCHu0g9K — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) October 7, 2026 Banks also had four passes defensed, tied for the most in a game by any player this season. A first-round pick in 2023, Banks had a promising rookie season. The last two seasons, though, have been difficult, and there were questions entering the season about what role Banks might have. He has, though, responded to the opportunity given to him by head coach John Harbaugh. “We just taught the defense really and talked to him about playing technique the right way, and he was just really amenable to it,” Harbaugh said. “We didn’t really have any kind of an in-depth conversation about the past. You know, that really wasn’t part of it. Just said, ‘Hey, man, we know what you’re capable of, let’s go play some good football.’ And maybe that was just all it took, maybe that’s all that was really needed. I do think he felt the confidence. I think he felt happy about the opportunity, maybe. Maybe he was freed up a little bit from the past, whatever happened. I mean, he had a great year his first year. So, maybe he leaned into that a little bit more. I’m not really sure, but it just wasn’t something we thought too much about. We just made it about the football, probably, more than anything.”

full_text: Jake Haener | Getty Images The New York Giants are signing backup quarterback Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network . This fills the roster spot opened by the loss of wide receiver/kick returner Braxton Berrios . The Giants singed Haener on Aug. 17 following some disastrous preseason performances by Brandon Allen. Haener, 27, is a former fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints in the 2023 NFL Draft. He spent time as the Saints’ starting quarterback in 2024 after Derek Carr’s Week 14 injury, but was waived and signed to the Saints’ practice squad in 2025. Haener played well enough for the Giants in the final preseason game and was ultimately signed to the practice squad instead of Allen. Haener now likely becomes the Giants’ primary backup while J.J. McCarthy gets up to speed. This does raise the question as to whether or not the Giants will employ their “McCarthy package” against the Washington Commanders. This also opens up a spot on the Giants’ practice squad. The Giants did have a visit on Tuesday from wide receiver Dontae Fleming , who spent last season on the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad.

full_text: Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings announced Thursday morning that they’ve signed former New York Giants star wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad. The Giants originally signed Beckham to their 90-man roster back on June 1, and while the ball didn’t find Beckham in games, he looked solid in practice and preseason. He ultimately made the Giants’ initial 53-man roster after final cutdowns. However, he only saw 20 snaps over the first three games with the Giants before being released prior to Week 4. Beckham remained a fan favorite in New York, receiving ovations every time he got on the field, but his second stint as a Giant ended with no catches. It was reported that Beckham had no interest in signing with the Giants’ practice squad and wanted to go somewhere where he had a better chance to play. The Vikings are looking for a spark on offense, and head coach Kevin O’Connell is familiar with Beckham from their time together with the Los Angeles Rams.

title: Cornerback Greg Newsome explains the Giants’ ballhawking ways
summary: There were plenty of stories that came out of the New York Giants 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4. One of the biggest was how the Giants’ defense transformed itself after the Cardinals’ second drive. The story of the game has been how the Giants’ front seven took over the game, but […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II intercepts a pass against the Arizona Cardinals. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There were plenty of stories that came out of the New York Giants 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4. One of the biggest was how the Giants’ defense transformed itself after the Cardinals’ second drive. The story of the game has been how the Giants’ front seven took over the game, but the development of the secondary was just as important. Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome II has been a steady presence on the outside for the Giants, and was one of three players to intercept Jacobi Brissett on Sunday. His experience and demeanor has led to him becoming one of the leaders on the back end of the Giants’ defense. He was careful, though, to credit front seven players like Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, and D.J. Reader. “Guys are hunting,” Newsome said. “Guys are giving us chances to get our hands on footballs. It’s also great in the secondary that we’re playing tight coverage. We’re getting our heads around and just trying to find the football. But, like I said, once again, it’s rush and coverage working together, so without those guys up front, we wouldn’t have 14. Shout out to those guys up front.” We anticipated before the season that Dennard Wilson would want to base his defense on “Step” coverage — that is, coverage with the cornerback within a step of the receiver. The philosophy is to challenge quarterbacks to consistently make tight window throws. Each of the Giants’ corners has upside in press-man coverage, and Newsome has been one of the best in the NFL in playing tight coverage. Here's a look at how cornerbacks have been in coverage through the first three games of the season. Trent McDuffie on another planet right now in his first season with the Rams. — Ben Baby (@bbaby41.bsky.social) 2026-10-01T17:06:17.213Z The tight coverage combined with the pressure generated by the Giants’ front seven has the Giants among the league leaders in takeaways. The Giants are tied for third with eight total turnovers and tied for first in the NFL with six interceptions. Newsome explained that the Giants’ secondary makes a point of practicing taking the ball away during the week. “First, our coaches. Just how we structure practice,” he said. “We’re always doing takeaway things before we get into team activities and things like that. Obviously, I think our d-line, our front seven, the guys that are blitzing. I think they’re doing a great job of just pressuring the quarterback, affecting the quarterback, and just giving us a chance to make plays out there.” It didn’t look so good to start the game against the Cardinals. The Giants’ defense made some plays, but were ultimately little more than a speedbump on the Cardinals’ first two drives. While the interior of the Giants’ defense was stout against Arizona’s runs, the perimeter proved vulnerable to well-schemed off-tackle runs. The game was flipped on its head when Dennard Wilson began to call a much more aggressive defense and used the Giants’ speed to disrupt the Cardinals’ running game as well as their passing attack. That put the ball in Brissett’s hand and Brissett in less advantageous positions. “Them stopping the run makes teams one-dimensional,” Newsome said. “It helps us out on the back end. It helps the linebackers not have to bite up on play fakes and things like that. I think with them doing such a great job up there with the front seven, it definitely helps our job, and just getting them on passing downs, allowing our guys to go up there and attack, so I think they’ve been doing an amazing job.” This Giants team is playing with much more confidence and tenacity than fans are used to seeing from their squad. It shows in how they’ve won their last two games: Walk-off interceptions in the closing seconds of the game. However, John Harbaugh seems to be channeling Han Solo and is coaching his players to not let their confidence turn into cockiness. “We’re underdogs every week, so that’s enough humbling for us,” Newsome said. “We’ve got to continue to keep going 1-0 each week. We don’t get too high, we don’t get too low. It’s a long season, so it’s great to be 3-1, but we have a lot of football left to play.” Newsome mentioned “going 1-0”, which has been the message from the Giants’ front office and coaches. Observers noticed that the Giants’ brass was wearing tee shirts emblazoned with a “1-0” prior to Sunday’s game. The message is that the players need to focus on getting to a 1-0 record each week. The team seems to have bought into the mantra while they embrace the underdog mentality. “I think we have a lot of vets in here that have played meaningful football that know how much each win matters,” Newsome said. “So we just focus on the next opponent. We don’t really care too much about the last game. It’s in the past, and now we’ve got to find a way to go 1-0 this week.” The Giants have a 3-1 record and lead the NFC East, but you wouldn’t know it from how Newsome says the team is carrying itself. “For sure you can play with an underdog mentality,” he said. “3-1 can easily turn into 3-14. That can easily do that. If you’re not careful enough, and if you have too much – if you’re not humble, you will get humbled. So, at the end of the day, we have to continue to have that mindset that we had in the beginning of the season, and we’re going to carry it the entire way. We definitely will keep that mindset.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 5
summary: No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (4-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The 49ers went into Denver and defeated the Broncos, 24-14. It was a defensive 3-3 game until the end of the third quarter, when Brock Purdy led a nine-play, 28-yard drive that ended in a one-yard touchdown to Deebo Samuel. The 49ers are […]
full_text: Has Bryce Young turned a corner? | Getty Images No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (4-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The 49ers went into Denver and defeated the Broncos, 24-14. It was a defensive 3-3 game until the end of the third quarter, when Brock Purdy led a nine-play, 28-yard drive that ended in a one-yard touchdown to Deebo Samuel. The 49ers are now undefeated at 4-0, with wins against the Rams, Dolphins, Cardinals, and Broncos. No. 2 — Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) | (3rd) 📈 1 spot The Chiefs scored 21 points in the fourth quarter to secure a victory over Las Vegas in Week 4. The defense held the Raiders to two field goals in the fourth quarter, while forcing a special teams fumble and an interception. It was a complementary win where all three phases did their duty, and Patrick Mahomes only had to complete 15 passes ( of 30 attempts ). Kansas City may reunite with Tyreek Hill too after the terrible injury to Tyquon Thornton. This was a strange, but important, win for the Chiefs against a quality 3-1 Raiders team. No. 3 —Buffalo Bills (3-1) | (1st) 📉 2 spots The New England Patriots came to play! The Bills’ defense surrendered 405 yards in the game, but a late Josh Allen interception, followed by a 12-yard Hunter Henry catch on third-and-ten, secured the victory for New England. The 49ers jump the Bills here, but Buffalo is still a top-three team in the NFL. No. 4 — Seattle Seahawks (3-1) | SAME The Seattle Seahawks defeated the Chargers, 30-23, with Emmanuel Wilson as the number one running back as Jadarian Price was placed on I.R. Seattle was up 27-3 and 30-13 in the game at the start of the fourth quarter, and Los Angeles was able to score 10 points to make the game slightly more interesting, but the Super Bowl champions controlled the game. No. 5 — Los Angeles Rams (2-2) | SAME The Rams went into Philadelphia and scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns while forcing two turnovers on downs from the Eagles. The Rams won 24-20 in a game with 10 punts. Puka Nacua caught nine passes for 125 yards on 12 targets. No. 6 — Minnesota Vikings (4-0) | (7th) 📈 1 spot The Vikings took down the Miami Dolphins, 15-10, in an uninspiring win led — of course — by Brian Flores’ defense. Kyler Murray threw for 247 yards, but it still left so much to be desired. The Vikings kicked five field goals to win the game. I don’t love having this team in the top-six, to be honest, but their defense is elite, and they’re a well-coached team that just needs more from their quarterback position. No. 7 — Chicago Bears (3-1) | (9th) 📈 2 spots Ben Johnson is fun! The Bears possessed the football for more than 42 minutes; the Jets had 157 total yards on just 32 plays! New York wasn’t disciplined, committing 12 penalties for 76 yards. Quarterback Tyson Bagent did enough to secure the win, but former Rutgers running back Kyle Monangai led the offense with 146 yards on 30 rushes and two scores. A funky, rainy Week 2 loss is the only thing keeping the Bears undefeated. No. 8 — Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) | (11th) 📈 3 spots The Jaguars’ defense forced two turnovers and a turnover on downs for Cincinnati to end the game, but allowed 437 total yards, while Joe Burrow threw the ball 54 times without Ja’Marr Chase. Jacksonville had a long Bhayshul Tuten touchdown called back for a dubious penalty. Overall, Jacksonville is now 3-1, and they’re playing well under Liam Coen. No. 9 — Baltimore Ravens (3-1) | (6th) 📉 3 spots Baltimore handled its business against the Tennessee Titans, 24-18, with the Titans scoring 11 points in the second half; the story of the game, however, was Lamar Jackson leaving the game at halftime with an ankle injury. The severity of the injury is still unknown, which is why the Ravens fell in the rankings. If it’s an extended absence, they more than likely will continue to fall, asthe offense looked poor with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. No. 10 — Dallas Cowboys (2-2) | (15th) 📈 5 spots Dallas’ defense remains a problem. C.J. Stroud performed well, throwing for 347 yards and two touchdowns against Dallas, but Dak Prescott matched him with 335 yards and a score, while also completing 17 passes to CeeDee Lamb. Javante Williams punched in three rushing touchdowns. Dallas is 2-2, but they’re a solid team; if they can fix that defense, they’d be a threat in the NFC. No. 11 — Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) | (14th) 📈 3 spots Sure, they lost, but Kirk Cousins has the Raiders playing well, and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has done well all season. Patrick Mahomes only completed 15 passes, and the Raiders had one too many errors in the second half, but they played well. Klint Kubiak has this team sitting at 3-1. No. 12 — Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) | (10th) 📉 2 spots The Bengals lost to the Jaguars at home and also lost Ja’Marr Chase to a head injury. The Bengals still had a 437-yard offensive performance. Cincinnati just could not run the football; Chase Brown gained 10 yards on nine carries — abysmal! Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards on 16 targets without Chase. The Bengals defense was solid again, but Zac Taylor’s squad didn’t do enough to secure the home win. No. 13 — Denver Broncos (2-2) | (10th) 📉 3 spots The Broncos’ offense looks inept for far too long in these games. Bo Nix’s team had three points until the fourth quarter, and San Francisco was able to put 21 fourth-quarter points on the Broncos. There’s no denying Denver’s talent level, but the Broncos disappear offensively too much. No. 14 — New England Patriots (2-2) | (27th) 📈 13 spots The Patriots are moving all over this board. New England looked terrible for three weeks, despite defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2, but they went into Buffalo and defeated the Bills 29-26. Drake Maye still made mistakes, but he found Romeo Doubs for two touchdowns, and Mike Vrabel’s defense did enough to stop the Josh Allen train. They host the Raiders next week. No. 15 — Carolina Panthers (2-2) | (22nd) 📈7 spots Am I being fooled by the prime-time victory — maybe! But the Panthers’ free-agent defensive additions are proving successful. They’re 2-2, and just beat the Lions 32-26, with Bryce Young throwing for 329 yards and two scores. Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards. The Panthers are looking solid early in 2026. No. 16 — Detroit Lions (2-2) | (12th) 📉 3 spots The Lions are 2-2 with losses against the Panthers and Bills. They won their two home games against the Jets and Saints. Kelvin Sheppard’s defense is an issue, but the offensive firepower is undeniable. Brighter days are ahead for Detroit, with the Packers, Cardinals, Dolphins, and Buccaneers on the schedule over the next six games. No. 17 — Atlanta Falcons (2-2) | (25th) 📈 8 spots The Falcons have won two in a row after a 0-2 start where Cooper Rush was their starting quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. didn’t do much against the Saints, but he provides the Falcons with a much-needed level of competency at quarterback. Atlanta has a strong defense and a solid offensive line, so they jumped up the rankings significantly after their Week 4 road victory against the Saints. No. 18 — Cleveland Browns (3-1) | (24th) 📈 6 spots The Browns are on a three-game winning streak, and Todd Monken has this team playing a physical style of football that suits the NFC North. Deshaun Watson is playing competent football, and the offensive line is doing a solid job up front. Defensively, the Browns forced two interceptions. The Browns defeated Pittsburgh, 27-24. title: 6 storylines for NY Giants-Washington Commanders: Prepping for Jayden Daniels
summary: The NFC-East leading New York Giants (3-1) travel to Landover, Md. Sunday to face the 1-3 Washington Commanders. What are the storylines to watch this week, beyond the Giants trying to defend a solo grip on first place for the first time since November of 2015? Let’s take a look. Jayden Daniels: ‘Looks like we’re […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels | Getty Images The NFC-East leading New York Giants (3-1) travel to Landover, Md. Sunday to face the 1-3 Washington Commanders. What are the storylines to watch this week, beyond the Giants trying to defend a solo grip on first place for the first time since November of 2015? Let’s take a look. Jayden Daniels: ‘Looks like we’re going to get him’ Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels has not played since dislocating his left, non-throwing, elbow in Week 2 against the Philadelphia Eagles. That is the second time in two seasons Daniels has suffered that injury. Head coach John Harbaugh and the Giants are expecting to see Daniels behind center on Sunday. “We’re going to have to prepare for Jayden. I mean, that’s got to be, until they say he’s not playing, we’re assuming he’s playing and we’ll be preparing for all the things he does, as if he was 100 percent healthy,” Harbaugh said. “They’re not going to put him out there if he’s not ready to play. So, that’s the way we’ll approach it. The Commanders have used now-injured veteran Marcus Mariota and seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis, formerly of Rutgers, at quarterback in Daniels’ absence. They surprisingly won a game against the Seattle Seahawks with Mariota at quarterback, but Daniels, the 2024 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year, is a difference-maker. “He’s different. He’s a premier quarterback who can operate just in all those modalities. Is that a good word? I mean, he can RPO. He’s quarterback driven. It’s drop back pass. It’s under center. It’s under center, play-action, downhill run game. He does it all. He’s a very accurate passer. Outside throwing lanes, especially accurate, which is tough. Nice touch underneath,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, he’s proven himself to be a very, very dangerous quarterback, obviously. So, yeah, premier guy and it looks like we’re going to get him, so we’re going to have to be at our best.” Who’s at center? Bryan Hudson made his first NFL start on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals after John Michael Schmitz missed a couple of late-week practices due to the birth of a child. Hudson played well in what was his first meaningful NFL action. So, now the question is whether or not he played well enough to displace Schmitz, a decent player but one who has never lived up to his status as the 57th overall player taken in the 2023 NFL Draft. Harbaugh was non-committal on Monday. “We’ll see. We haven’t really talked about it yet today,” Harbaugh said. “So, we haven’t had that personnel meeting yet, but I’ll say Huddy (played really well, and we were excited about him going in. So, maybe create some options for us, but JMS was playing really well too. So, a very good problem to have.” How will the Giants solve it? I think Hudson starts against the Commanders. Why? I believe the Giants know that Schmitz, in the final year of his rookie contract, is not their answer at center beyond this season. Unless something changes drastically, I can’t see Schmitz getting a second contract from New York. They will almost certainly need a new center for 2027, and it would be a shame if they didn’t give Hudson an extended run to determine if they already have their answer in place. Harbaugh said something interesting on Monday that applies to the center position, even though he was responding to a question about potentially having to fill Braxton Berrios’s roster spot. “We’ll turn over every stone,” Harbaugh said. “But sometimes the best stones are right under your feet.” That, I think, is the best explanation for why Hudson needs an opportunity to play. Hitting the road The Giants are 3-0 at home, and establishing a home field advantage is an important step in becoming a truly good football team. You do, though, have to win some games on the road. The Giants have gone 3-14 on the road the past two season, including 1-8 in 2025. They got manhandled by the Los Angeles Rams on the road in their only loss so far this season. Showing the ability to win games that matter on the road would be another step in the evolution of a team still trying to transition from down-trodden loser to truly dangerous contender. Are the Giants ready to take that step? ‘Protect the football at all times’ The Giants have already fumbled the ball seven times this season, but have been fortunate enough to lose only two of those. Cam Skattebo has three of those fumbles in 76 touches. That kind of sloppiness with the ball will eventually cost the Giants games “Sometimes you try too hard. Sometimes you try too hard to get the extra couple yards, to break out of the pile, to get the run game going. And then the ball becomes a little bit vulnerable in there and I just think we just stick (to it),” Harbaugh said. “You watch what Skatt and Najee have been doing, too. But protect the ball at all costs. The yards are going to come. Make that the first priority. Don’t forget that. Play to play. Keep reminding each other of that.” Harbaugh said holding on to the ball is a priority for everyone. “We have these heavy balls now that we bring in, and they carry this. But it’s not really punishment. They do it all anyway. They carry them around. We punch them out. They’ve got to hold them behind the line. But that’s what all the guys do anyway,” Harbaugh said. “So even our managers have to not fumble the ball. They’ll punch it out if they’re holding it loose. So, it just kind of needs to be like an organizational priority. You protect the football at all times if it’s in your hands.” Something else Harbaugh said might be considered a warning shot for quarterback Jameis Winston , who has three touchdown passes and three interceptions since taking over for the injured Jaxson Dart . “It’s definitely a priority for us. The priority for us,” Harbaugh said. “Not turning the ball over, whether it be fumbles or interceptions. If we’re going to accomplish the things we want to accomplish, that has to get done. That is the number one priority offensively. Everybody knows it. We all know it. We have to know it and do it.” ‘3 yards and a cloud of dust’ That has, more or less, been the Giants’ rushing attack so far this season. Skattebo is averaging 3.5 yards per carry. On 68 rushing attempts, his longest gain is 13 yards. Over the last three games, he has gained just 154 yards on 50 carries, 3.08 yards per attempt. Najee Harris is averaging 4.0 yards per carry (22 rushes, 88 yards). His career average, though, is just 3.9 yards on more than 1,100 attempts. The Giants want to grind teams down with their running game, but overall they are 23rd in the league at 3.7 yards per rush. The Giants’ rushing Expected Points Added (EPA) is -15.6, 26th, per NextGenStats. Their 37.8% success rate is 22nd. The Giants are at -45 in rushing yards over expected, 26th in the league. Remember when the Giants were flirting with Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker in free agency, or considered a legitimate landing spot in the draft for Jeremiyah Love ? This is why. They don’t have a home run hitter in their backfield. The closest that they have is Tyrone Tracy , who has a career average of 4.3 yards per carry, but he has carried only four times for 16 yards this season. In an effort to create some chunk plays, the Giants might need to give the ball to Tracy more often. They might also have to turn to this: The J.J. McCarthy package The Giants manipulated their roster against the Arizona Cardinals is such a way that McCarthy was QB3, with Harbaugh saying it was “unrealistic” for J.J. McCarthy to be able to function in a full backup role. Harbaugh, though, admitted that there were “certain plays that we had prepared for” McCarthy. They ended up choosing not to use them. That could change this Sunday. Harbaugh said on Monday that McCarthy being the No. 2 quarterback behind Jameis Winston this week is “definitely on the table.” McCarthy is not the runner Jaxson Dart is. In 10 games, he has averaged 3.7 rushes per game for 4.9 yards per carry. Dart, an…

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to hit the road to Washington this week. McCarthy — an intriguing third-year quarterback just acquired via a trade — could be the backup for the game, rather than the third stringer. “I think that’s a possibility,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll see how it goes during the week, but that’s definitely on the table.” For all of McCarthy’s flaws — and he has plenty — his mobility would let the Giants run the offense they envisioned running with Dart. And perhaps coordinator Matt Nagy could turn McCarthy into more of a game manager — within a run-focused offense — than Winston can be. John Harbaugh during the final play of Sunday’s game "You want the pressure?" John Harbaugh was ready for somebody to make a play, and then Deonte Banks did just that. @insidetheNFL Week 4 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/9ygrscqeE2 — NFL (@NFL) October 6, 2026 John Harbaugh set a Giants standard everyone is already meeting | New York Post It is quite something that Deonte Banks made a game-sealing interception and en route to turning it into an emphatic pick-6, he reached a speed of 21.85 mph on his 98-yard return. No ball carrier in the NFL has run faster than that this season, according to NextGen Stats. John Harbaugh says New York Giants’ backs must clean up fumbling issues | USAToday.com Still, that’s too many times for Harbaugh’s liking. This past Sunday against Arizona, it was running back Najee Harris who coughed up the ball on the Cardinals’ 43 yard-line, killing a second-half drive. It amounted to nothing in the end, as Arizona ended up punting the ball back to the Giants, but it could have been a game-changer. “Najee’s never been a guy that fumbles too much,” Harbaugh explained to reporters on Monday. “And sometimes you try too hard. Sometimes you try too hard to get the extra couple yards, to break out of the pile, to get the run game going. And then the ball becomes a little bit vulnerable in there, and I just think we just stick (to it). You watch what Skatt and Najee have been doing, too. But protect the ball at all costs.” Early NFL All-Rookie Team: Which 2026 draft picks have excelled so far? | The Athletic First team: Arvell Reese, Giants (Round 1, No. 5); Jacob Rodriguez, Dolphins (Round 2, No. 43). This is a crowded position for rookies, but Reese’s dominant performance against the Cardinals on Sunday clinched his spot on the first team. The No. 1 prospect for me this past draft, Reese finished with nine tackles (all solo) and now leads the NFL (not just rookies) with 27 solo tackles. Reese also had a tackle for loss, three passes defended and his first career interception in Week 4. He is the NFL’s only non-defensive back with at least four passes defended and one interception this season. Arvell Reese nominated again for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week | Giants.com The linebacker was nominated for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week, the second time he has been up for the award in as many games, after he led the Giants with nine solo tackles, three passes defensed, one tackle for loss and his first career interception. Fans can vote for Reese on Instagram or X ( @NFL ) through Thursday at 11 a.m. ET to determine who will bring home the championship belt for Week 4. The winner will be announced later that day. After the regular season, four players will be nominated for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Year honors. Jermaine Eluemunor Island No OT has been left on an island more than Jermaine Eluemunor this season (71.4%) And he's winning a ton too (93.7%) @JEluemunor is a boss pic.twitter.com/QXrJQRzo3n — PFF (@PFF) October 6, 2026 Ranking NFL division leaders by which are most vulnerable after opening month | CBSSports.com 2. New York Giants (3-1). New York’s schedule isn’t daunting, but with a backup quarterback like Winston (or J.J. McCarthy), no game is guaranteed, which opens the doors for division rivals. Dallas is currently the betting favorite to win the division at +134 and does feel like the most complete team in the NFC East at the moment. The offense is tied for the second-highest scoring unit in the league, averaging 30.5 points per game. The Cowboys are also the fourth-best on third down (51.02%) and the third-best in the league in the red zone (81.25%) through the first month. Their defense is still a major question, but the addition of corner Joey Porter Jr. should help improve the secondary. Buyers or Sellers for the NFL’s Most Surprising Teams 1 Month From Trade Deadline | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Buyers. With quarterback Jaxson Dart on season-ending injured reserve, the New York Giants are going through the Jameis Winston experience and still winning games. Currently atop the NFC East, Big Blue should bring in a veteran quarterback in case Winston implodes with turnovers. Keep in mind that J.J. McCarthy struggled in his second season, which was his first year as a starter with the Minnesota Vikings. He may not be equipped to take over on short notice in New York. Because of Brian Burns’ season-ending knee injury, the Giants should also look to add an edge-rusher, which is ironic given all the trade buzz around Kayvon Thibodeaux this past offseason. Versatile rookie first-rounder Arvell Reese has pass-rushing ability, but he’s a starting inside linebacker alongside Tremaine Edmunds. title: NY Giants’ PK Dominic Zvada shares secret to early success
summary: Not many rookies start their career as hot as Dominic Zvada has so far for the New York Giants. Through four weeks, Zvada has yet to miss any of his five extra-point attempts or his nine field goals. He scored every point in the team’s Week 3 victory against the Tennessee Titans and came in […]
full_text: Not many rookies start their career as hot as Dominic Zvada has so far for the New York Giants. Through four weeks, Zvada has yet to miss any of his five extra-point attempts or his nine field goals. He scored every point in the team’s Week 3 victory against the Tennessee Titans and came in clutch with three more field goals in the team’s Week 4 victory against the Arizona Cardinals, including kicks of 50 and 52 yards. Zvada may be just a rookie, but he doesn’t have the mindset of one. He spoke to the media about how he is adapting to life in the NFL, part of which was set up for him during training camp. “Throughout training camp they were doing a really good job of trying to get us in as much of a game-like situation as possible with just a little bit of fun hostility. And so, yeah, they did a great job, and it really helped prepare all of us for the preseason, and then obviously the season,” Zvada said. “It kind of got us ready for that early so that when we got to the games, we were already used to that sort of thing, so I thought it was great work, and hopefully they continue to do it.” Zvada has stuck with a routine he developed as a college kicker. “Throughout college I was able to kind of get into a good routine and I’ve kind of stuck with that,” he said on Tuesday. “Really the focus going into the season was just to come in and get better every single day and stay focused on the task at hand.” Zvada won a training camp competition with Ben Sauls, and has come in clutch for the Giants throughout the season. Zvada and the Giants are back in action in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside Northwest Stadium. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

full_text: ﻿The New York Giants celebrate after a touchdown | Getty Images The New York Giants have emerged from the first month of the 2026 season with a 3-1 record. That much isn’t surprising and is in line with many preseason predictions. What wasn’t expected is that the Giants not only have sole possession of first place in the NFC East, but they’ve done it without Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns. Most expected the Giants to fold once they lost their franchise quarterback and star pass rusher. Instead, the Giants have kept fighting, literally down to the closing seconds of the last two games, and new stars have emerged. Arvell Reese is positioning himself in the race for defensive rookie of the year, while Abdul Carter has been a devastating pass rusher. At the same time, Jevon Holland, Deonte Banks, and Greg Newsome II have been playing much better in the secondary than many expected. Elsewhere in the NFC East, meanwhile, the other teams have issues. The Philadelphia Eagles are short-handed and a mess on offense. The Dallas Cowboys have one of the most potent offenses in the NFL, but a defense that is still porous. Finally, the Washington Commanders don’t know what to expect from Jayden Daniels and there are questions elsewhere on their offense and defense. So that brings up the question… Can the Giants stay resilient, hold off their division rivals, go from Worst To First, and win the NFC East? title: The Jets should change their running back approach
summary: Over the last couple of years, one thing that has frustrated me with the Jets’ approach to offense has been their insistence on using Breece Hall as a do it all back. Hall is a very talented player, but I think it’s clear that he isn’t a complete back. He is an explosive play threat […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 01: Isaiah Davis #32 of the New York Jets celebrates his touchdown with teammate Braelon Allen #0 in the first half against the Seattle Seahawks at MetLife Stadium on December 01, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the last couple of years, one thing that has frustrated me with the Jets’ approach to offense has been their insistence on using Breece Hall as a do it all back. Hall is a very talented player, but I think it’s clear that he isn’t a complete back. He is an explosive play threat on outside runs and is a capable receiver out of the backfield. When he is decisive and hits the hole hard, his size makes him tough to bring down. But he struggles to read blocks, which makes him inconsistent on zone runs and sometimes leads him to play smaller than his 217 pound frame. (He also has a tendency to be caught from behind on breakaway runs, but that feels like nitpicking.) With Hall out of the lineup in Week 4 against the Chicago Bears, Braelon Allen took over the lead running back role. There wasn’t much that went right for the Jets offensively in that game, but Allen played some solid football. While there were no highlight reel runs, Allen ended the day with a very respectable 59 yards on 14 carries. In many ways that has been the story of Braelon Allen’s young career. The 2024 fourth round pick out of Wisconsin has a career average per rushing attempt of 3.7 yards, which is underwhelming. Allen’s career long run is only 20 yards. But he pairs it with an above average success rate of 51.7% on runs. (Success rate tells you what percentage of a running back’s carries end in gaining at least 40% of the yardage needed to move the chains on first down, at least 60% on second down, or a third or fourth down run resulting in a first down. It is a test of how frequently a running back keeps the offense on schedule.) Against the Bears, Allen was steady if unspectacular. He posted a robust 57% success rate despite not breaking a run longer than 10 yards. If the Jets passing game had shown more competence, Allen’s ability to keep the offense on schedule might have garnered more notice. It’s difficult to completely judge a back with 143 rushing attempts over a three year career, but at this point it looks like Braelon Allen is an unflashy back who can grind out yardage for moderate gains. There’s nothing wrong with that. I think a back like this does have some value, but you also would like to see some explosive plays in the run game. In that game against Chicago, fellow 2024 day three pick Isaiah Davis did not receive a single carry. You might remember that Davis dealt with an injury in training camp, but he was active for the game. He got in for two plays on offense and 15 on special teams. Where Davis might be particularly helpful is in adding a bit more juice to the Jets run game. Again we are living in the world of small sample sizes for inexperienced players, but in 73 NFL carries, Davis has a success rate of 47.9%, a tick below average. Where he has thrived so far is in producing splash plays. Of those 73 carries, 13 would be considered “explosive” runs of 10 yards or more. You might wonder whether a 17.8% explosive run rate is good. Well, Breece Hall is known as a big play threat in his own right. To this point in his career, Hall has an explosive run rate of 11.2%. Once again, sample sizes matter. Nobody should immediately declare that Isaiah Davis is a better big play threat than Breece Hall. It will be almost impossible for Davis to maintain that rate over the long haul unless the Jets secretly have one of the best big play runners in NFL history sitting on their bench. Humility is important here. As their respective workloads increase, our perceptions of Allen’s and Davis’ skillsets could change dramatically. But based on what we’ve seen so far, there’s a case to be made that they would be a duo that complements each other. Allen could be the reliable guy when you just need to grind out a few yards to keep the offense on schedule. Davis could go in when you need something more dynamic. That’s if the Jets will ever give more than one running back a chance.
author: John B

title: Cam Jurgens trade: Eagles send center to Ravens for draft picks
summary: Well, here’s a massive Eagles offensive line development for the second day in a row: Philadelphia is trading Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for multiple draft picks. The full terms of the deal, as first reported by NFL insider Adam Schefter: EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick RAVENS RECEIVE […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens (51) warms up before the game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles on January 04, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Well, here’s a massive Eagles offensive line development for the second day in a row: Philadelphia is trading Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for multiple draft picks. The full terms of the deal, as first reported by NFL insider Adam Schefter: EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick RAVENS RECEIVE — Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick Wow. Safe to say no one saw this coming. Coming off a down season in 2025 where he inexplicably still made the Pro Bowl, the Eagles were hoping Jurgens would bounce back in 2026. Along with fellow starting offensive lineman Landon Dickerson, Jurgens made an offseason trip to Medellín, Colombia for stem cell therapy. After beginning the season at his normal center position, the Eagles decided to move Jurgens to left guard with Dickerson massively struggling and landing on injured reserve after Week 1. To no surprise, Jurgens massively struggled at a new position where he had no previous experience. There were calls for the Eagles to bench him in favor of Willie Lampkin. Jurgens was expected to miss Week 5 after self-reporting a concussion. But no one expected him to be off the Eagles’ roster entirely. Howie Roseman clearly saw an opportunity to get good draft pick compensation in return for a player with a questionable outlook moving forward. The Ravens were clearly desperate for center help after losing Tyler Linderbaum in free agency and seeing their next three replacement options get injured. Kudos to the Eagles’ general manager for taking advantage of this opportunity. It is a shame that Jurgens’ Eagles career came to such an abrupt end. He was drafted to be Jason Kelce’s successor and it once looked like he was going to have a long career in Philly. Jurgens should always be remembered fondly for toughing it out through a back injury in an NFC Championship Game win over the Washington Commanders and the team’s Super Bowl LIX victory during the 2024 season. With Jurgens gone and Lane Johnson retiring, the Eagles’ offensive line is clearly in flux . That’s not really ideal in the short-term. But Roseman’s trade signals that the team has a long-term focus in mind. While I don’t think the Eagles are ready to completely throw in the towel on the 2026 season, the Jurgens trade seems like an acknowledgement that 2026 might just be a down year for this franchise. The Eagles are now set to have four picks in the first two rounds of the 2028 NFL Draft: their own first-round pick, the New England Patriots’ first-round pick (via the A.J. Brown trade), their own second-round pick, and the Ravens’ second-round pick.

title: Eagles News: Reflecting on Lane Johnson’s legendary career
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Lane is a legend. While I do think he’s properly getting his flowers following his retirement announcement, I do wish the damper of “How do the Eagles replace him?” wasn’t also a necessary discussion right now. Wish he could’ve made the […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 09: Lane Johnson (65) of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with owner Jeffrey Lurie after Super Bowl LIX against the Kansas City Chiefs at Caesars Superdome on February 09, 2025, in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Eagles defeated the Chiefs 40-22. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Lane is a legend. While I do think he’s properly getting his flowers following his retirement announcement, I do wish the damper of “How do the Eagles replace him?” wasn’t also a necessary discussion right now. Wish he could’ve made the decision back in the offseason to allow more space for celebrating him without interruption. To be clear, this isn’t to criticize Lane. He clearly wasn’t ready to make the call back then. That’s understandable. Things change. You can’t always anticipate how you’re going to feel down the road. In any case, here’s to one of the greatest Eagles players we’ll ever see. Glad we all got to witness his excellent career and come to know him as a fellow human. I know offensive linemen aren’t the most popular jersey choices for fans but I do hope to see more No. 65s out in the wild. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles legend Lane Johnson retires: Five thoughts on the announcement – PHLY Eagles 1) Lane Johnson is the best player I’ve covered in my eight years reporting on this team. He was the type of ruthlessly efficient offensive tackle that didn’t always grab your attention on a down-in, down-out fashion, but the consistency with which he singlehandedly erased even the league’s top edge rushers solidified his status as one of the best offensive linemen in modern NFL history. Johnson went whole seasons without allowing not only sacks, but pressures during his career. And he did so in a way the Eagles built an entire offensive philosophy around. They’d have two of the league’s best offensive tackles, and they’d leave them both isolated on islands in pass protection as a result. Perhaps that arrangement didn’t get the recognition it deserved throughout Johnson’s career; his five All-Pro honors somehow feel insufficient for the player he was and the impact he had on the game. So did his omission from the NFL’s Top 100 players going into this season (something that didn’t seem lost on him upon his return to training camp a few months ago). None of this should change what most in Philadelphia already know: Johnson was one of the best players of a generation and belongs in the Hall of Fame. Lane Johnson gave the Eagles greatness. To Philadelphia, he meant something more – The Athletic “The best …” I can’t tell you how many times during the past decade I’ve heard that word used to describe Lane Johnson — from teammates, coaches, executives. “No question about it in my mind that he’s the best player I’ve ever been around,” Nick Sirianni said. “He’s the best offensive lineman that’s f—ing come through the Eagles,” Cam Jurgens said. “One of the best players ever to play his position in NFL history,” Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie said. “Best tackle in the NFL,” team security chief Dom DiSandro said. “For the past decade, Lane has been the best right tackle in the NFL,” Jason Kelce wrote Tuesday. Saquon Barkley called him the best player on the team. Howie Roseman called him one of the greatest to play the game and said he changed how the NFL views right tackles. Take their word for it. Know Lane Johnson had better *statistical* seasons than 2017, but for my money that was his best season, and maybe the best individual campaign of any #Eagles player I've covered in my years on the beat. Consider the primary edges he faced at right tackle that year, around the… — Jeff McLane (@Jeff_McLane) October 7, 2026 Taking stock of the Eagles’ offensive line after Lane Johnson’s retirement – BGN The Eagles’ offensive line situation right now is far from ideal. As a unit, they already weren’t playing very well while healthy. And now they’re losing their best player with Johnson retiring. And it’s not like Jeff Stoutland is here to help get the most out of the remaining talent. The Eagles have had seasons from hell in the past when their offensive line has gone to crap. Unfortunately, 2026 might just be another one of those years. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 196: Week 5 Preview | Cowboys on TNF | Eagles in London – NFC East Mixtape A new week is upon us and it is a quick one at that. The Dallas Cowboys will be in action shortly as they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. Can they get above .500 for the first time this season? Elsewhere in the division, the Philadelphia Eagles are on the verge of falling apart and a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London just might be the tipping point. Finally, the New York Giants will visit the Washington Commanders and if the home team loses… is their season over? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss on the latest episode of the NFC East Mixtape! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Jaguars keep climbing in NFL power rankings entering Week 5 – Big Cat Country The respect is finally coming. After taking care of business in Week 4, the Jacksonville Jaguars now sit at 3-1. They have a convincing first-place lead in the division — and their chances to earn the top seed in the conference continue to rise. “I don’t think we really care about the credit,” safety Antonio Johnson said Monday. “We’re going to go into each week, and if you don’t look at us as an imposing defense, then we’re going to impose our will on you. If you don’t respect us, then we’re going to make you respect us. I know personally, in the rooms that I’ve talked to the players, we don’t care about the respect. You don’t respect us, cool. We’re going to make you respect us, so we’re not even tripping about that.” As Week 5 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally. Eagles player review: Markel Bell’s debut against the Rams – PhillyVoice I don’t think Bell is ready to start. Opposing defenses are going to throw everything they can at him, and my guess if that we’re going to see him struggle. I also think the Eagles should just start him anyway. Let him get as many reps as he can, allow him to improve, see what he has, and let his performance guide whether or not the team still needs a replacement for Johnson next offseason, or if Bell shows enough that he can be the guy. However, I do think there’s a chance that the coaching staff might prefer to play the far more experienced Fred Johnson if they still have delusions that they are Super Bowl contenders. Of course, Johnson missed the last two games with a knee injury, so that might not even be an option, for now. NFL Week 5 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we’re hearing – ESPN Are any coaches’ seats warming a little early? […] Graziano: Yeah, barring a massive turnaround, you have to think someone ends up in trouble with the Chargers. Head coach? GM? Quarterback? All of the above? Also, what happens if things turn really bad in Philadelphia? Obviously, the Eagles aren’t afraid to move off an offensive coordinator after one disappointing season, but could things get bad enough that Super Bowl-winning head coach Nick Sirianni has to start watching his back? […] Fowler: With Philly, it has been proved that if owner Jeffrey Lurie and GM Howie Roseman identify a problem on the field, they will find a solution. Sometimes that involves the head coach. Another up-and-down season would inevitably keep Sirianni’s name in the leaguewide conversation, despite him winning 70% of his games and having a Super Bowl ring. But…

title: Vic Fangio says it’s possible the Eagles are playing Jalen Carter too much
summary: The Eagles are having a rough week, and as they prepare for the Jaguars in London, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters about their late-game struggles against the Rams, what he thinks of the secondary, and about Jalen Carter’s work load with a cast. As the injuries continue to stack up, Fangio was asked […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles are having a rough week, and as they prepare for the Jaguars in London, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters about their late-game struggles against the Rams, what he thinks of the secondary, and about Jalen Carter’s work load with a cast. As the injuries continue to stack up , Fangio was asked how he feels about the depth on defense: “It’s being challenged right now, so we’ll see. But I think in certain places we’re good and others, you cross your fingers.” When later asked about which positions lack depth, he coyly replied, “You’ll have to figure that out yourself.” Here’s what else the DC had to say: On the late game struggles Fangio said that they struggled to make a play and he struggled to make the right call late in the game against the Rams, and with a veteran QB like Matthew Stafford, that’s a bad combination. “We didn’t get it done. You know, we played great for 10 drives, but the last two, we didn’t.” The DC clarified that the defense played 83 total snaps, including penalties, and while it might have a small affect on things, ultimately, they need to find a way to finish. On the secondary Fangio thought that Michael Carter did a good job on Sunday. He was asked about Jonathan Jones having to come in after Quinyon Mitchell was sidelined, and the DC said he was happy with how the CB stepped up. “I thought [Jonathan Jones] did good for really his first action in a long time. If you remember, he missed the tail end of training camp and hadn’t had any action since whenever, one of the early preseason games and though he’d come in there and did a good job. He does a good job preparing and he was ready to go.” The DC said that they are hopeful that Quinyon Mitchell will be available this weekend, but said they’ll find out more as the week goes on. He was also complimentary of new DB Kenny Moore and how he’s preparing to contribute. “[Kenny Moore]‘s getting closer. He’s done a great job learning, [we’re] trying to get him to learn two positions to be part of nickel or dime, and safety. But he got in there for a play or two at the end.“ On the pass rush “I thought it was inconsistent.” The DC said that they haven’t been consistently really good in one-on-ones, and while they might be affected by chips, when they are getting one-on-ones, they’re not getting it done on a consistent basis. Ultimately, though, Fangio said that he’s still confident that the pass rush will get to a level that he wants to see. “I just believe in the guys. A lot of times too, we’ve lost two sacks the last two games due to penalties. Sometimes the ball’s coming out quick, like previous some games. I know you guys have a love affair with the sack stat, but the ball’s coming out quick a lot.” On playing time for players Fangio said that LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr. played very well against the Rams, and probably earned some more playing time as a result. The DC was also asked about Jordan Davis only taking 35 percent of the defensive snaps, to which Fangio admitted that they probably need to get him on the field more. He explained that it was more of a result of personnel the Rams were in — they had been playing a lot of three tight ends in the weeks before the Eagles game, but then went with more three receiver looks on Sunday, which changed the game. He admitted that Jalen Carter ’s wrist injury affected him more on Sunday against the Rams than in previous games, and when asked if the DT is playing more than he should be, Fangio replied, “Possibly.” On the Jaguars offense “They’re really good on offense. The quarterback is athletic, got a big arm, he’s got a good group of receivers to throw it to. Their running back, 33 [RB Bhayshul Tuten] runs really good, kind of a new guy on the scene and they do a good job. They got a very varied running game, a lot of different types of runs, multiple run game and they’re good at it.” Other notables Fangio said that safety Andrew Mukuba has been playing well all season, and he’s real pleased with where he is in his development. He noted that Jalyx Hunt just needs to continue doing the little things consistently. The DC said LB Jihaad Campbell has been coming along, and is getting better each game against both the run and pass game.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles roster news: Tank Bigsby to IR, practice squad changes
summary: Four Philadelphia Eagles transactions were included on the official NFL personnel notice from Tuesday, October 6. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. TANK BIGSBY Bigsby to IR was first reported on Monday evening. With Saquon Barkley dealing with a hamstring injury, Bigsby likely would’ve started at running back in […]
full_text: GLENDALE, AZ - JANUARY 08: OL James Brockermeyer #52 of the Miami Hurricanes points to defenders before a snap during the Miami Hurricanes versus Ole Miss Rebels College Football Playoff Semifinal at the Vrbo Fiesta Bowl on January 8, 2026, at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, AZ. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Four Philadelphia Eagles transactions were included on the official NFL personnel notice from Tuesday, October 6. Here’s an overview: RB Tank Bigsby was placed on injured reserve. LB Anfernee Orji was released from the practice squad. LB Chance Campbell was released from the practice squad injured list with an injury settlement. C James Brockermeyer had a free agent visit with Eagles. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. TANK BIGSBY Bigsby to IR was first reported on Monday evening. With Saquon Barkley dealing with a hamstring injury, Bigsby likely would’ve started at running back in his absence. Instead, Bigsby will miss at least four games as a result of undergoing core muscle surgery. Those games: Week 5 at Jacksonville Jaguars Week 6 vs. Carolina Panthers Week 7 vs. Dallas Cowboys Week 8 at Washington Commanders He might miss a little longer considering he’s reportedly set to be back in “six weeks or shorter.” With Barkley injured and Bigsby on IR, the Eagles currently have one running back on the active roster: Will Shipley. They do have three running backs on the practice squad: Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue. I’d expect Pierce to be the first man up from that trio. Bigsby to IR and Lane Johnson retiring (not yet on the official transaction log) means the Eagles are set to have two open roster spots. ANFERNEE ORJI The Eagles originally signed Orji to their practice squad on October 1. Now he’s gone. Perhaps his departure signals that Zack Baun will be ready to return from his concussion this weekend. CHANCE CAMPBELL The extent of the injury that landed Campbell on the practice squad injured list is unclear. And now he’s gone after previously being temporarily elevated to the roster for the Eagles’ Week 3 game. JAMES BROCKERMEYER Brockermeyer came to Philly for a visit and the Eagles are signing him to their practice squad, according to a report from Matt Zenitz. Brockermeyer is a 24-year-old rookie who signed with the Atlanta Falcons after the 2027 NFL Draft. The Falcons waived him in late August only to bring him back on the practice squad for a couple weeks … before cutting him again. Dating back to college, Brockermeyer has exclusively played center. The Eagles apparently wanted more depth at that spot. Cam Jurgens could very well miss Week 5 due to a concussion. And he wasn’t playing very well when he was healthy. Here’s a scouting report from Brockeymere from NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein : Undersized center prospect with NFL bloodlines, admirable grit and above-average intelligence. Brockermeyer has the technique and core strength to fight as a downhill blocker but his impact in the run game is likely to be limited to occupying/neutralizing. In protection, his success rate climbs against pure bull-rushers thanks to his hand usage and protection know-how. However, a lack of length will limit his ability to redirect athletic rushers if they find his edge. Brockermeyer was outstanding at the Senior Bowl, but he’s a one-position player, so he’ll have to fight hard for a roster spot. For what it’s worth, Brockermeyer ranked 39th out of 53 centers graded by Pro Football Focus during the 2026 preseason. Willie Lampkin was first! Fun fact: Brockermeyer was Markel Bell’s teammate at Miami in 2025. MORE ROSTER MOVES COMING The Eagles will likely announce some more transactions on Wednesday, which will be the team’s first practice ahead of Sunday’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Taking stock of the Eagles’ offensive line after Lane Johnson’s retirement
summary: With Lane Johnson announcing his retirement, let’s take stock of the Philadelphia Eagles’ current offensive line situation. THE PLAYERS Here are the current projected starters entering Week 5: Here are the current backups on the active roster: Here are the current practice squad offensive linemen: OFFENSIVE TACKLE Lane Johnson’s absence puts Markel Bell in line […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Markel Bell #72 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Lane Johnson announcing his retirement , let’s take stock of the Philadelphia Eagles’ current offensive line situation. THE PLAYERS Here are the current projected starters entering Week 5: Left tackle — Jordan Mailata Left guard — Willie Lampkin Center — Drew Kendall Right guard — Tyler Steen Right tackle — Markel Bell Here are the current backups on the active roster: OT Fred Johnson OG Micah Morris Here are the current practice squad offensive linemen: C/G Jake Majors OT Kiran Amegadjie OT John Ojukwu OFFENSIVE TACKLE Lane Johnson’s absence puts Markel Bell in line to start at right tackle again this week and potentially moving forward. The Eagles also have Fred Johnson on their roster … but he’s missed the last two games with a knee injury. Bell also outplayed Big Fred in the summer and offers more upside than the 29-year-old veteran, who will be a free agent once again after this season. Still, getting Fred Johnson back would be ideal from the standpoint of having a swing tackle behind Mailata and Bell. Because there’s currently no other tackle on the active roster. On that note, the Eagles’ lack of tackle depth will likely prompt them to promote Ojukwu and/or Amegadjie to the roster. The Eagles currently have two roster spots to fill with Lane’s retirement and Tank Bigsby being placed on injured reserve. Another potential internal option is to move Tyler Steen to tackle and play rookie Micah Morris at guard. But that doesn’t seem likely. INTERIOR OFFENSIVE LINE Cam Jurgens is reportedly in the concussion protocol . While it’s possible that he’s cleared in time to start at left guard on Sunday, it seems like he might miss at least one game. And there have been calls to bench him with how poorly he’s played out of his normal center position. Jurgens ranks 77th out of 79 guards graded by Pro Football Focus this season. Assuming Jurgens is out, Willie Lampkin will make his first career NFL start. The 5’11”, 290 pound blocker is something of a curiosity given his lack of prototypical NFL size. But his diminutive stature hasn’t prevented him from playing well in training camp and preseason settings. It’ll be interesting to see if he can carry that success over to the regular season. We’re also assuming that the Eagles will keep Kendall at center and put Lampkin at left guard. But maybe the Eagles could flip them to get Lampkin in at center? We’ll see. Landon Dickerson is currently ineligible to play for the Eagles while on injured reserve. He will be able to return from IR as soon as Week 6, though it’s unclear if he’ll actually be healthy enough to play then. And even if he can suit up, it’s unclear if he’s actually able to still play well at all. The Eagles could look to either sign Majors to the roster or temporarily elevate him from the practice squad to give them more interior depth. Majors took a lot of reps with the second-team offensive line during training camp and preseason games. The 2025 undrafted rookie free agent signing has never played in a regular season game. EXTERNAL OPTIONS? I would think the Eagles aren’t looking to trade for a rental to help replace Lane. The only way I see them paying a significant price for a veteran is if they have the potential to be a long-term option. But which teams are trading a high quality starting tackle during the season? Maybe Taylor Decker is a name to watch? He’s available after requesting his release from the Detroit Lions earlier this year. The 33-year-old has only really ever played at left tackle, though. Long-time starter Cam Robinson is also still on the market. Ditto for Jonah Williams. The problem with signing a short-term veteran is that it blocks Bell’s development. But the Eagles also aren’t going to play Bell if he’s struggling to the point where they’re concerned Hurts could get injured as a result. Or if they feel like winning in the short-term is better than a long-term focus. Other external options could involve the Eagles poaching practice squad player(s) from other teams. Less likely to get an instant starter that way but there could be some players with upside that are worth taking a chance on. ALL TOLD The Eagles’ offensive line situation right now is far from ideal. As a unit, they already weren’t playing very well while healthy. And now they’re losing their best player with Johnson retiring. And it’s not like Jeff Stoutland is here to help get the most out of the remaining talent. The Eagles have had seasons from hell in the past when their offensive line has gone to crap. Unfortunately, 2026 might just be another one of those years.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Lane Johnson retires: Eagles right tackle announces decision to leave team
summary: Philadelphia Eagles legendary right tackle Lane Johnson is retiring, according to an official announcement from the two-time Super Bowl champion himself. Things have been complicated with Johnson for the better part of the last year. He was sidelined with a foot injury that unexpectedly ended his 2025 season. There were rumors about him potentially retiring […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Lane Johnson #65 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field against the Washington Commanders following an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles legendary right tackle Lane Johnson is retiring, according to an official announcement from the two-time Super Bowl champion himself. Thank you. 🦅 pic.twitter.com/up2kH1K40p — Lane Johnson (@LaneJohnson65) October 6, 2026 Things have been complicated with Johnson for the better part of the last year. He was sidelined with a foot injury that unexpectedly ended his 2025 season. There were rumors about him potentially retiring in the offseason but the 36-year-old decided to return to an offensive line room that didn’t include Jeff Stoutland for the first time in his 13-year career. After a few days into training camp, Johnson left the team for personal reasons. He eventually returned and talked about his increased focus on family and announced that 2026 would probably be his final season. Things changed on Sunday morning ahead of the Eagles-Rams game in Week 4 when it was abruptly announced Johnson would be inactive and miss the game due to personal reasons. It was a huge loss for an already struggling offensive line, and rookie Markel Bell had to step into some big shoes on incredibly short notice. Now, Johnson is deciding to call it a career after four games into the Eagles’ 2026 campaign. From a personal standpoint, the Eagles and their fans wish the best for him. Johnson will go down as one of the best players in franchise history. The two-time first-team All-Pro, three-time second-team All-Pro, and six-time Pro Bowler deserves a spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. From a football standpoint, the Eagles are in MUCH worse shape without him. Bell is now presumably the team’s starting right tackle. He can make himself into a long-term fixture by excelling in this role but it won’t be easy for the rookie. Sitting at 2-2 after two straight losses, there’s plenty of time left in this season for the Eagles to turn things around. But with the way things are trending at the moment, the team’s outlook isn’t looking very good, especially now that Johnson is gone. UPDATE: Statement from Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie. pic.twitter.com/T39yp5Phnd — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 6, 2026
