title: The Steelers offense can be great, but they need to lean into what’s working
summary: Inconsistency has been the name of the game for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense and defense through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season, leading to a fitting 2-2 record through four weeks. And after another recent low point, a 27-24 loss to the rival Cleveland Browns and Deshaun Watson last Thursday, Read and React […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inconsistency has been the name of the game for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense and defense through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season, leading to a fitting 2-2 record through four weeks. And after another recent low point, a 27-24 loss to the rival Cleveland Browns and Deshaun Watson last Thursday, Read and React is here to take a look at if there might be a light and the end of the tunnel to one of the Steelers’ struggling units. Is there hope for the Steelers’ offense? RP : The Steelers have been an undoubtedly frustrating watch through the first quarter of the NFL season. While their record of 2-2 is certainly not reason to give up on the season — they are just one game back from the division lead after all — we can certainly empathize with any fans who think this Steelers team has proven they aren’t good enough to be taken seriously. You could argue the offense has only played one good game this year, Week 3’s win over the Bengals. That’s a tough pill to swallow considering the organization’s hiring of offensive-minded coach Mike McCarthy was supposed to finally fix what has been the glaring weakness of this team for the entirety of the 2020s. But what makes the whole thing more maddening is that there have been glimpses of a promising offense. The Bengals game was a stellar performance from start to finish, and even the Browns game featured an immaculate first drive of the game, as well as a late-game surge that saw the Steelers score two touchdowns in the fourth quarter to tie the game. The issue again and again has been that the Steelers have lacked consistency. On one drive they’re Jekyll, the next they’re Hyde. Naturally, fans are left wondering why that is. Are the players simply not good enough? Or are the coaches failing to utilize them well? Truthfully, the answer lies somewhere in the middle, but for the sake of this column, we’d like to argue, with film and data, that there is still a chance for this offense to be not only a fun one, but maybe even an above average one too. But to do so, the two most influential people in this offense, McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers, need to put ego aside, and embrace not the offense that they’ve enjoyed in the past, but the offense this roster is currently built to be. The Steelers need to lean into playing bully ball. And by that, we mean they need to get under center more and, to use an old coaching adage, they need to run the damn ball. Steelers are starting to embrace their size up front, their skill position players willingness to scrap, and even Warren's running style. They ran the Duo run concept 12 times last night against the Browns with 8 of them ending up successful, per @NextGenStats . Bully ball! pic.twitter.com/FMs7nQd7L0 — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 2, 2026 The Steelers gotta lean all the way into playing bullyball. Washington and Nowakowski handle the EDGE, DK Metcalf gets a solid block on the LB, and then Fautanu and Mason McCormick really help spring this run pic.twitter.com/7zKZtvTeBF — JP Acosta (@acosta32_jp) September 30, 2026 But it’s more than just what the eye test is telling us. The Steelers have been dominant when they line up under center. Whether it’s run or pass, Pittsburgh is averaging 6.8 yards per play when they do so. That trails only the Kansas City Chiefs through the first four games of the season. Steelers aren’t just a good offense when they’re under center, they’re literally the 2nd best under center offense in the league https://t.co/1EnJbRiB7c — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) October 6, 2026 RB : Under center isn’t a magic bullet fix to an offense, but it does offer some advantages over shotgun in certain instances (and vice versa, of course). The most obvious is a more direct, downhill run game. The quarterback-center exchange is cleaner, the running back gets a running start and a wider field of view, and linemen have a tick longer to land their blocks. The results can be a fun watch, even if some more of less boil down to hitting a narrow crease at full speed for four or five yards. Steelers under center run game pic.twitter.com/4N11KtLxI4 — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 7, 2026 And the Steelers have the personnel to pull this style of play off. The addition of Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor on the Steelers’ offensive line has added a much-need infusion of extra physicality to a group that already includes maulers Mason McCormick and Zach Frazier, as well as a good left tackle in Troy Fautanu. Tight end Darnell Washington is, of course, one of the biggest bullies at his position in the NFL, and both running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle (when healthy), are physical ball-carriers with the latter having even more of a decisive, downhill playing style. And while this hasn’t been a great postgame week regarding the reputation of the Steelers’ wide receiver room, names such as Germie Bernard, Michael Pittman Jr. and Ben Skowronek have been putting some work in as blockers in recent weeks (including a lot of C-gap inserts), upping the “bully ball” potential of the offense as a whole. Yeah the Steelers O-line can be pretty cool, but check out these receivers in the run game pic.twitter.com/Xk8ySEGiGn — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 7, 2026 But why under center? A mid-September article from ESPN’s Bill Barnwell further broke down why the league as a whole has been seeing increased usage of this concept. The explanation matches the eye test — defenses have become incredibly modern, and to beat them, sometimes you have to break out the old-school concepts. Defenses have become unpredictable, meaning offenses need to follow suit. And under-center runs have far less tells of where the run will go as the running back is directly behind the quarterback to start the play. And in the passing game, play action and ball fakes are easier to pull off. Barnwell points out that the uncertainty of reacting to an under-center offense has been the “natural response” to NFL defenses using increasingly exotic zone coverages. As the adage goes, it’s a game of inches, and hard play-action fakes can provide the extra millisecond of hesitation in the secondary needed to break a big play. Little bit of hesitation from the safety opens up big play to DK Metcalf pic.twitter.com/UUgJAh9G9k — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 7, 2026 The Steelers have been especially productive in this aspect of the game. According to DK Pittsburgh Sports’ Chris Halicke , the Steelers run play action on 89% of their under-center drop backs — meaning almost every snap from that alignment starts off looking like a run play. As uninteresting as the Steelers’ offense has looked at times, the under-center concepts have found some success in confusing opposing defenses. RP : Frankly, for as impressive as the Steelers look under center, they’ve been just as dreadful from shotgun. Here's how effective NFL offenses have been when under center vs. shotgun pic.twitter.com/9zbgy01Xda — Ben Baby (@Ben_Baby) October 5, 2026 Historically, both McCarthy and Rodgers have preferred not only a passing-dominant approach to offense, but they’ve preferred a heavy dose of 11 personnel (three wide receivers) and from shotgun. But as the chart above indicates, this version of Rodgers, mixed with this current collection of players, is simply not built to live in that style of offense. A recent article from Mike DeFabo of The Athletic pointed out some of the key data points that can help contextualize the struggles we’ve seen play out on the field: The Steelers have used 11-personnel at 10th highest rate (63.8%) When doing so, they rank 30th in EPA per dropback (-0.23) That ranking drops to 31st when the defense rushes 5 or more (-0.68) 12 of the Steelers 13 sacks allowed have come while using 11 personnel When using 12 personnel, the Steelers improve to 18th in EPA per dropback (-0.05) They also improve against 5+ rushers in 12…

title: Steelers get positive injury update on Jamel Dean
summary: There may be some encouraging signs for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean. Dean was reportedly seen without the walking boot inside the Steelers’ facility Tuesday, an encouraging development as Pittsburgh prepares for Sunday’s matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. Dean aggravated an ankle injury during last Thursday’s loss to the Cleveland Browns and did not return […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images There may be some encouraging signs for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean. Dean was reportedly seen without the walking boot inside the Steelers’ facility Tuesday, an encouraging development as Pittsburgh prepares for Sunday’s matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. Dean aggravated an ankle injury during last Thursday’s loss to the Cleveland Browns and did not return to the game. He had initially been dealing with the same ankle issue heading into the Browns matchup, and reports indicated he could miss multiple weeks. Pittsburgh could certainly use the veteran cornerback against Indianapolis, particularly with the team already dealing with significant turnover at cornerback. If Dean cannot go, Asante Samuel Jr. and rookie Daylen Everette will continue to see expanded roles. The fact that Dean is already out of the boot is a step in the right direction, but his practice participation will be the biggest indicator of whether he has a realistic chance to return Sunday. title: Steelers Week 5 power rankings roundup: Pittsburgh falls after loss to Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers fell to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 by a score of 27-24. Despite erasing a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter, the Browns got the last laugh with a game-winning field goal with just seconds remaining. Pittsburgh is now 0-5 all-time in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. […]
full_text: (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers fell to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 by a score of 27-24. Despite erasing a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter, the Browns got the last laugh with a game-winning field goal with just seconds remaining. Pittsburgh is now 0-5 all-time in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. It’s time for our weekly look around the internet to see where various media outlets place the Steelers among the rest of the NFL in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.22 (No. 14 Last Week) “Aaron Rodgers’ last ride is certainly turning into a wild one. His deep throws wobble more than their place in these rankings and his mobility is completely shot. But as he showed in the second half of Week 4 against the Browns, he can still be stellar. The problem is, the Steelers need him to be consistent, because neither the Jaylen Warren-led running game nor the T.J. Watt-led defense are very good.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.20 (Last Week No.14) “This isn’t how things were supposed to go. Aaron Rodgers’ reunion with Mike McCarthy in the head coach’s hometown was supposed to be a feel-good success story, a nice way for Rodgers to go out and for McCarthy to return. Instead, we’re left with McCarthy apologizing after the game for the profane on-field exchange between the two that was caught by TV cameras.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.21 (Last Week No. 13) “Losing to the Browns on the road opens up the question about whether they can compete for a division title. They have to be more consistent on offense.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.14 (Last Week No. 13) “The best-case scenario is 9-8. The worst-case scenario is they’re giving Will Howard or Drew Allar game reps after Thanksgiving.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.25 (Last Week No.19) “The Steelers’ offense fell back into a rut for most of Thursday night, and the relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy seemed to sour further — that is, until a desperate fourth quarter saw Rodgers and DK Metcalf suddenly torch Cleveland’s secondary for a game-tying score. The late outburst doesn’t paper over the earlier issues, though, and Pittsburgh’s defense failed to get after Deshaun Watson despite facing an offensive line that was missing two of its starters (and replaced one with a rookie). The jury is still out on the Steelers, who seem like a middling-at-best team right now.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.21 (Last Week No.17) “The days of this Steelers defense scaring anyone are probably over. Pittsburgh is 15th in defensive DVOA through Sunday’s games, 14th in EPA allowed per play, 23rd in success rate allowed and 13th in yards per game allowed. Pittsburgh allowed Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson to go 14-of-17 passing for 181 yards and a touchdown in the first half last Thursday night, then let him put together a game-winning drive.” “It’s just an average defense. The Steelers had the second-oldest defense in the NFL coming into the season by average age, so it’s not like there’s an obvious turnaround coming with a young unit. The offense’s upside is limited with a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers at quarterback. The ceiling is not very high for this team.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.19 (Last Week No.16) “Time will tell if their hardline negotiating policies cost them too much following the departure of Porter … but sure could have used him in Cleveland.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.20 (Last Week No.17) “Coach Mike McCarthy’s phrase of choice — “herky-jerky” — is an apt description for the Steelers through four weeks. Neither the offense nor defense has established an identity. Even special teams has struggled, as kicker Chris Boswell is 7-of-10 on field goal attempts. QB Aaron Rodgers and the passing attack have been inconsistent, and while the run game found a spark in Jaylen Warren, the playcalling has often put the ball in Rodgers’ hands. He has 167 dropbacks; the Steelers have run the ball just 86 times. The league’s highest-paid defense has allowed 24.7 points per game over the past three weeks” – Brooke Pryor After an embarrassing primetime loss in front of the entire nation in which your head coach and quarterback were caught yelling profanities at each other, it’s no shock to see the Steelers take a tumble in the power rankings. The Steelers will likely be a pretty volatile team in these power rankings until they show any week-to-week consistency, which may never happen this season. full_text: (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Chicago bears cornerback Terell Smith off the Washington Commanders practice squad, per Nick Farabaugh of PennLive . Smith joins fellow veteran Sean Murphy-Bunting as new signees that will be on the Steelers’ 53-man roster straight away, as the team quickly became very thin at the cornerback position following the trade of Joey Porter Jr and an ankle injury to Jamel Dean. title: 5 cool things the Seahawks did in Chargers win that they haven’t done in years
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may not have played their cleanest football (to put it kindly) against the Los Angeles Chargers, but they still won the game and had some cool moments along the way. Not everything has to be focused on the penalties or the dueling interceptions to start a game, not when the Seahawks did […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks may not have played their cleanest football (to put it kindly) against the Los Angeles Chargers, but they still won the game and had some cool moments along the way. Not everything has to be focused on the penalties or the dueling interceptions to start a game, not when the Seahawks did some good things we haven’t seen from them in a good while! The first Seahawks running back screen pass touchdown in six years Their first touchdown came on a screen pass—yes, a “screen pass”—to Emanuel Wilson, who recorded his first Seahawks TD on a 23-yard scamper. It’s only the second receiving touchdown of Wilson’s NFL career. 23-YARD TOUCHDOWN BY 2️⃣3️⃣ 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/GZLhRD0LMB — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 4, 2026 The Seahawks passing game is not known for featuring running backs as receivers. Brian Fleury was supposed to get the backs more involved as passing targets, and so far there’s been at least some semblance of an effort even if it’s not in high volume. It’s a running joke among Seahawks fans that the team is/has been notoriously bad at screen passes, particularly to the backs, such that the Wilson TD felt like something from a parallel universe. What’s the last Seahawks screen pass touchdown to a running back? You have to go back to the cavernous feeling of the 2020 pandemic season, when fans were either not allowed in the stands or there in limited capacity. Chris Carson’s second receiving touchdown of the quarter from Russell Wilson couldn’t have been much easier. You can even hear Atlanta Falcons defenders and coaches yelling “SCREEN!” as they hopelessly chase a lost cause. Emanuel Wilson's screen pass touchdown against the Chargers was Seattle's first RB screen touchdown since Chris Carson on opening day of the 2020 season (aka the Let Russ Cook year). pic.twitter.com/42PLXdkzXc — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 5, 2026 Ernest Jones IV pulls a Bobby Wagner daily double Seattle’s elite middle linebacker destroyed the Chargers offense. Whether it was stopping the run, getting after Justin Herbert, defending receivers in the pass game, or creating turnovers, Jones might end up with an NFC Defensive Player of the Week award come Wednesday. Jones picked up his first sack of the season on a blitz that the Chargers had seven in protection for and didn’t come remotely close to stopping. No time 😤 @ErnestJones SACK! 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/0Alv03yx3k — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 4, 2026 The next possession was Jones’ first interception of the year, one that might as well have been catching practice given Herbert threw the ball directly in his lane. 20-YARD RETURN ON THE PICK 😮‍💨 @ErnestJones Welcome to The Dark Side. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/eOq36faKS2 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 4, 2026 Jones became the first Seahawks linebacker since Bobby Wagner to record a sack and an interception in the same game. Wagner did it in 2018 against the San Francisco 49ers, sacking Nick Mullens before setting a franchise record with a 98-yard interception return for a touchdown. Bobby also had a sack and a pick against the Minnesota Vikings in 2013. PICK-SIX BOBBY WAGNER!!! Incredible play by @Bwagz . Jumps in front of the pass to the running back and brings it back for the score. Longest in team history for the #Seahawks . 98 yards… Well worth the delay of game penalty lol. #SFvsSEA pic.twitter.com/WQazBbSf9r — Samuel Gold (@SamuelRGold) December 3, 2018 Seahawks score 30+ points in three straight games for first time since 2020 Ahhh the Let Russ Cook year. Might have been a blessing in disguise given what soon transpired out of that season. Seattle started the year scoring 38, 35, 38, and 31 points out of the gate, starting the season 4-0. They also put up 34, 37, and 34 points later in the season, but lost two of those games and so went the LRC movement. It might not feel like it, but the Seahawks have scored 92 points (31, 31, and 30) over the past three weeks. The offense hasn’t been at its sharpest but they are scoring. The Seahawks have scored 30+ points in three straight games. Would you believe that has not happened since 2020? Even with some rough edges, they have outscored the Klint Kubiak offense through four games while missing their starting QB for two of them. pic.twitter.com/WEWRjm9xa9 — Brian Nemhauser (@hawkblogger) October 6, 2026 Rashid Shaheed is the first Seahawks receiver to get a rushing TD since… Shaheed finally got his first offensive touchdown in a Seahawks uniform. No, it wasn’t on a catch, but he impacted the run game with a couple of carries for 33 yards. His 28-yard touchdown run is Seattle’s longest rush of the season. Electric speed 🔥 @RashidShaheed to the end zone for a 28-yard TOUCHDOWN. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/ZBTqi9wCSk — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 4, 2026 A Seahawks receiver scoring a touchdown isn’t something that we have seen a lot more recently than the other facts. You just probably don’t remember that the previous WR rushing touchdown was scored by… JAKE BOBO! Yes, Bobo received a handoff near the goal line and scored against the Cleveland Browns back in 2023. The first touchdown in our Throwback went to Jake Bobo. Who's next? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/XsTgqulLYI — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 4, 2024 Before Bobo, the last Seahawks rushing touchdown by a receiver was Tyler Lockett’s 75-yard jet sweep score in the 2016 win over the Carolina Panthers. Drake Thomas’ first play pick Justin Herbert clearly loves him some Seahawks linebackers, because before Ernest got his INT, Drake Thomas snagged Herbert’s first throw of the game. Drake Thomas will not get fooled by your play action attempts. pic.twitter.com/gf3Rq6cCt1 — Billy M (@BillyM_91) October 4, 2026 Yes, we know the Seahawks wasted this with an immediate interception at the other end, but this was an excellent start for the defense after not forcing any takeaways last week. It’s the first time the Seahawks have recorded a first play INT since supreme ball-hawk Quandre Diggs got Derek Carr in a 2022 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Maybe it’s an AFC West thing. “INCREDIBLE INTERCEPTION HERE!!” Greg Gumbel & @AdamArchuleta call Quandre Diggs picking off Derek Carr on the FIRST PLAY from scrimmage 🫣 📺 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/3CGZQHchFn — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 27, 2022 So while it’s easy to be steamed at the very real issues we saw in the Chargers game, Seattle still produced some significant performances and highlights worth praising. They’re still 3-1, they’re still the reigning Super Bowl champions, and you know Mike Macdonald and that locker room will not be complacent with “a win is a win” mentality.

title: 49ers-Seahawks: 3 major differences from last year’s roster
summary: The San Francisco 49ers faced the Seattle Seahawks three times in 2025. Kyle Shanahan’s offense had 30 drives against Mike MacDonald’s defense. They scored two touchdowns. In the first matchup, Ricky Pearsall had over 100 receiving yards, while Zach Charbonnet led Seattle in rushing. Neither player will be in uniform this Sunday. In the second […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers faced the Seattle Seahawks three times in 2025. Kyle Shanahan’s offense had 30 drives against Mike MacDonald’s defense. They scored two touchdowns. In the first matchup, Ricky Pearsall had over 100 receiving yards, while Zach Charbonnet led Seattle in rushing. Neither player will be in uniform this Sunday. In the second matchup, the 49ers’ leading receiver was Jauan Jennings. Cornerback Riq Woolen had a pass breakup. Those two are on different teams. In the playoff matchup, Kenneth Walker ran for 116 yards, while Jake Tonges had a team-high in receiving for the Niners. Walker is with the Chiefs, while Tonges is on the injured reserve. Having a WR1 like Mike Evans Even in that Week 1 matchup, 45 of Pearsall’s 108 yards came on one play. Christian McCaffrey and Kyle Juszczyk each had 25-yard receptions. For the most part, the passing attack was held in check because, as they showed in the next two games, no wideout could consistently get open. Mike Evans is seventh in the NFL in EPA per target and fifth in targeted success percentage. He’s what a true WR1 looks like. The only reason he’s seventh in Sumer Sports’ impact plays metric is because he’s only been targeted 24 times. For reference, the six receivers ahead of Evans have at least 39 targets. Kyle Shanahan moves Evans around the formation enough that defenses can’t key in on him. That has led to incredible efficiency. Of Evans’ 17 receptions, 14 have resulted in either a first down or a touchdown. The struggles against Seattle are why you go out and get a receiver of Evans’ caliber. In Week 18, the 49ers wide receivers were Jauan Jennings, Kendrick Bourne, Demarcus Robinson, and Skyy Moore. It’s a completely different group this time around. There’s speed around Evans, which has opened things up and allowed the 49ers to stretch the field both vertically and horizontally. Evans isn’t catching intermediate passes with Bourne or Jennings on the field, because teams like Seattle aren’t threatened deep. Brock Purdy will also have George Kittle and Deebo Samuel, two players who weren’t available in the playoffs. A little better at linebacker In those final two matchups, the 49ers started two players who had signed to the roster as recently as Thanksgiving, plus Dee Winters. The fact that the Niners were so eager to move on from Winters this offseason, despite his rookie contract, tells us how they felt about him internally. Raheem Morris views Garret Wallow as a nickel linebacker, while Kendricks is 34. There were plays where Seattle ran to the outside, and Kendricks, understandably, was a step slow. Wallow would get swallowed up, while Winters’ best work came on plays right at him or in coverage. Quietly, the 49ers have been one of the best teams at defending outside zone — the Seahawks run some variation outside of the tackles 60% of the time. The Niners have allowed 3.7 yards per play on outside zone runs, with a -0.045 EPA per play. On 16 attempts, they’ve had nine defensive stops. It’s been a mix-and-match of players on the edge. They’ve done their jobs, but Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw are winning the foot race when running backs try to beat them to the sideline. In Week 18, Tatum Bethune and Winters combined for three missed tackles. Seattle torched Bethune in coverage, to the tune of 64 yards. Bethune allowed six of his seven targets to be completed. Wallow got lost on one play in coverage, leading to a critical first down. It goes without saying that Warner will impact where Sam Darnold throws the ball. If he targets Warner seven times, Raheem Morris will take that all day. The upgrade at linebacker cannot be undersold heading into this matchup. Interior pressure + an edge presence Yetur Gross-Matos was the only player to generate interior pressure against the Seahawks during the regular season. In those three games, five defensive tackles recorded seven run stops and five missed tackles. Let’s look at the past two games this season, since those are the defensive tackles who will play this week for the 49ers. Osa Odighizuwa has eight pressures. Gracen Halton and Sebastian Valdez have five impact plays. Naquan Jones has a couple of run stops and is holding his ground. The four defensive tackles on the field this year are all upgrades from last year. One of the most impressive areas from Week 3 was seeing the edge players play the run. Matt Judon played one snap, and it looked great. Romello Height is wiry strong, while Keion White has been a pleasant surprise. The edge presence who didn’t play in the final two games is Mykel Williams. The 49ers’ run defense allowed a half-yard-per-play more with Mykel off the field last season. The first-down rate and EPA per play were marginally better. What you can’t quantify is having a player his size going up against tight ends. Those are wins for Williams. Or having Mykel take on pulling blockers instead of your designated pass rushers, like Height. Even if Williams plays only 30 snaps, you get to keep Height, Okoronkwo, and Khalid Kareem fresh. The domino effect of getting a first-rounder back has immense benefits for the Niners’ defense.

title: 3 quarter season takeaways for the 49ers: How the Niners are putting it all together so far
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are just about a quarter of the way into the season, and they’re undefeated so far, starting off 4-0 with wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. Through four games, the 49ers have been exceptional offensively, ranking first by a wide margin in EPA/play, while […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers calls a play in the huddle in the second quarter against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are just about a quarter of the way into the season, and they’re undefeated so far, starting off 4-0 with wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. Through four games, the 49ers have been exceptional offensively, ranking first by a wide margin in EPA/play, while coming together strongly defensively, all while dealing with a large number of injuries. Still, they’ve beaten two contenders, while establishing themselves as a real threat in the NFL behind MVP-level play from Brock Purdy. So, through four weeks, let’s look at five quarter-season takeaways for the 49ers. Brock Purdy excelling in several key categories The Brock Purdy train has taken off, as the quarterback is currently the odds-on favorite to win MVP, being No. 1 on NFL.com’s MVP Ladder through four weeks. He’s played extremely well thus far, including in a performance against the Denver Broncos where he still played quite well despite it being his “worst” game of the season. Purdy kept the ball out of harm’s way, took what the defense gave him, and still threw for 218 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions. Through four weeks, Purdy is the clear leader in EPA per play and success rate at quarterback. He’s No. 1 in QBR. And he is also leveling up in key moments. Breaking it down by quarter, Purdy is the NFL’s top quarterback in EPA per play in both the third and fourth quarter, while ranking third in the NFL in the first quarter. Purdy is also pushing the ball downfield, ranking first in yards per attempt, while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes and ranking fourth in completion rate over expected. One category really caught my eye, though: Purdy’s excellence against the blitz. Thus far, when blitzed, Purdy has completed 27 of 35 passes for 427 yards and seven touchdowns when blitzed, while not being sacked once on 11 pressures. He’s been the NFL’s best quarterback against the blitz and has seen the field very well, not making any turnover-worthy plays, which have been the issue in years past. In 2025, Purdy’s completion rate dropped to 62.6 percent, and he had six of his 13 interceptions when blitzed, despite being blitzed on just 26.6 percent of his dropbacks. This year, he’s being blitzed at a 31.5 percent rate, and playing even better. The story is simple: Purdy is making the plays while not taking any negative plays, regardless of situation. The 49ers run game has a foundation The Niners’ run game was an issue in 2025. They ranked 29th in EPA per rush and 24th in rushing success rate, as the explosives just weren’t there on the ground. This season, the 49ers are 10th in EPA per rush and eighth in rushing success rate. Thus far, the 49ers are averaging 4.8 yards per carry, seventh in the league, while getting to 137.3 rushing yards per game, a top-six mark in the NFL. That’s happened while Christian McCaffrey has averaged just 4.4 yards per carry and Kaelon Black has averaged 3.9 yards per carry, thanks to the wrinkles in the run game with Deebo Samuel and Brock Purdy’s ability to extend plays with his legs. More importantly, the 49ers run game seems to have built a foundation again. San Francisco’s offensive line has done a really good job over four weeks of keeping Brock Purdy up and limiting the pressure from opposing defenses. But they’ve also paved the way in the run game. San Francisco ranks fifth in yards before contact per rush (1.93 yards), and they’re also not getting negative plays in the run game, which was an issue last year. Instead, the 49ers also rank sixth in percentage of runs with zero or negative yards before contact at 37.2 percent. So, they’re avoiding negative plays and averaging nearly five yards per tote. The explosives still need to come. Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black also rank 24th and 45th, respectively, in yards after contact. But the 49ers are doing better on the ground and have a foundation there this year. Limiting explosive plays The 49ers have been the best team in the NFL at limiting explosive plays this season. In fact, their 3.5 percent explosive play rate allowed is the best of any team through four games since 2000. And that’s with a banged-up defensive line. Raheem Morris has been exactly what the 49ers needed, and I’m slowly starting to compare him to DeMeco Ryans back during that monster 2022 defensive campaign. The 49ers are the No. 5 team defensively in DVOA, which, matched with the No. 1 rank on offense, has created a clear-cut contender. Now, the 49ers are 26th in pressure rate, but part of that is attributed to teams looking to get the ball out quickly. Subsequently, they’re sixth in ESPN’s pass rush win rate, and it helps to limit explosive plays when linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw fly to the ball. I’ve been impressed with how Morris has created pressure with his personnel up front on the defensive line, but also with how the 49ers have played coverage through four weeks. After struggling last season at times, the 49ers secondary has looked the part in a big way so far. That includes growth from safeties Marques Sigle and Malik Mustapha, as well as from Renardo Green and the newcomer Jack Jones, who have all played roles in the secondary so far. Overall, you’re starting to see a defense gel in a new scheme, and this unit should only get better with healthy players. It’s been a very promising start to the 49ers season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Brock Purdy atop MVP leaderboard through four weeks
summary: It’s been only four weeks, but San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been playing the best football of his career so far here in 2026. Through four games, Purdy has thrown for 1,007 yards, 11 touchdowns, and only one interception, while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes and averaging 8.9 yards per attempt. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers throws a pass against the Denver Broncos in the third quarter at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been only four weeks, but San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has been playing the best football of his career so far here in 2026. Through four games, Purdy has thrown for 1,007 yards, 11 touchdowns, and only one interception, while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes and averaging 8.9 yards per attempt. While the 49ers receiving core has been hit with a flurry of injuries, Purdy hasn’t lost a step, leading this team to a 4-0 start as he’s done a good job of taking what the defense has given him. His main issue coming into the year was turnovers and some poor decisions that could overshadow a quality game. Well, he’s got just one interception this year, coming back in Week 1, and has continued to find ways to extend plays behind a strong offensive line. That’s why it’s not a surprise that Purdy sits atop the leaderboard of the MVP race through four weeks in NFL.com’s MVP tracker. “Purdy is on fire to open the season, and the catalyst for the 49ers’ 4-0 start,” NFL.com’s Kevin Patra wrote. “Playing pristine in Kyle Shanahan’s system, Purdy’s performance is a culmination of time on task, innate deft touch, exemplary pocket manipulation and heady playmaking. Each week he seems to drop a dime that makes me yelp and wonder how in heaven the ball got through to its target. “Through four games, Purdy is tied for the league lead with 11 touchdown passes and has allowed a banged-up 49ers offense to continue operating at a high level without a trove of assets. Sure, he still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to lean on, but the receiver corps has been decimated, including Mike Evans clearly playing through a painful rib issue. Lesser QBs have crumbled. Carrying a club through injury is MVP pixie dust.” While Purdy didn’t have the biggest stat line against the Broncos on Sunday, he didn’t hurt his MVP case, and remains sack-free through four weeks while avoiding negative plays. “Sunday’s outing against Denver wasn’t his best of the year, but did little to take the shine off. Purdy still hasn’t been sacked this season,“ Patra continued. ”If we’re willing to say sacks are a QB stat when blaming players who take them in droves, we should credit Purdy’s uncanny ability to shake free and avoid negative plays. Avoiding disaster has been a Purdy specialty through four weeks. He’s thrown two touchdowns without an interception for the third straight week. He also became the first 49ers QB to start the season with multiple touchdowns in each of the first four games since Steve Young in 1998 (seven straight), per NFL Research. “Purdy has used keen accuracy to blow away the rest of the QBs through the start of the season. He’s No. 1 in passer rating (126.2), QBR (89.6) and net yards per attempt (8.9). His EPA per dropback of 0.53 is by far the top ( Lamar Jackson is No. 2 at 0.29), and his success rate of 60.7% is best among QBs with at least 100 dropbacks. There is nary an advanced stat Purdy isn’t dominating right now. Knock his opponents if you must, and yes, there could be a clunker coming, in which he splashes a couple of interceptions on high passes over the middle, but entering Week 5, no one is playing the position at Purdy’s level in 2026.” That final sentence has been echoed by a few national reporters this season. Purdy has been playing on a different level than his peers, as he’s pushed the ball downfield, been accurate, carried his offense, and avoided negative plays. Behind him on the MVP leaderboard are Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker III, Trevor Lawrence, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba to round out the top five. It’s only a quarter of the season in. But Brock Purdy has been playing at a very high level, and people are taking notice.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Who has been the unsung hero this season for the 49ers?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. Who has been the unsung hero? The 49ers have become all too familiar with unsung heroes under Kyle Shanahan. Injuries have led to depth players being […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris of the San Francisco 49ers speaks with the media after a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. Who has been the unsung hero? The 49ers have become all too familiar with unsung heroes under Kyle Shanahan. Injuries have led to depth players being elevated into starting roles. There have been plenty of examples over the years of a player the outside world may have never heard of rising to the occasion. Last week, it was Sebastian Valdez at defensive tackle: Sebastian Valdez is forcing Raheem Morris's hand. He impacted/won on 40% of his snaps. Drew a flag. Found the ball. Made stops. Held his ground. Split doubles. Caused chaos. Cover the name on the back of the jersey, you'd think this was one of the DTs the 49ers drafted in '25. pic.twitter.com/i8yGgcoQyH — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) October 6, 2026 Raheem Morris quickly learned how ridiculous the 49ers’ injury luck is. He’s lost multiple starters and depth pieces before the season began. That continued into the season. Valdez wasn’t supposed to step onto the field, but injuries to Alfred Collins, CJ West, and James Thompson Jr. have opened the door for Valdez. The 49ers are 10th in passing success rate defensively without the player the pass rush revolves around. They’ve been stingy in the passing game and limit teams to field goals, as shown by their 6th-best red zone scoring percentage. One positional group that has not been banged up, knock on wood, is the offensive line. Sacks are largely a quarterback stat, but Brock Purdy has been pressured on 33.3% of his dropbacks, which is the fourth-lowest in the NFL. Christian McCaffrey is averaging 1.72 yards before contact, the fifth-best mark in the league. It’s a unit that shouldn’t even be in this category, as they’re one of the strengths of the team. However, they do not get the credit they deserve. The other options are the benefit of three home games in the first month, the schedule, and the return of Deebo Samuel. author: Kyle Posey

title: Kyle Shanahan ‘real excited’ with Malik Mustapha ahead of Week 5 start
summary: The 49ers will be forced to make a change to their starting secondary for their huge Week 5 matchup with the Seattle Seahawks. After Marques Sigle suffered a high-ankle sprain in Sunday’s 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos, the 49ers will have a different starting safety duo in Seattle, though thankfully the replacement is a […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Malik Mustapha #6 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates on the field during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers will be forced to make a change to their starting secondary for their huge Week 5 matchup with the Seattle Seahawks. After Marques Sigle suffered a high-ankle sprain in Sunday’s 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos, the 49ers will have a different starting safety duo in Seattle, though thankfully the replacement is a player in whom they have great faith. Malik Mustapha is set to come into the lineup and fill in for Sigle, the 2024 fourth-round pick having lost his place in the starting lineup due to injuries during training camp. But, even as Sigle and Ji’Ayir Brown have held on to their starting spots through the first four weeks of the season, Mustapha has continued to play defensive snaps, featuring on 49 so far this campaign. Mustapha played 21 defensive snaps against Denver owing to the injury to Sigle and, as head coach Kyle Shanahan articulated in his Monday conference call, made a significant contribution to an impressive defensive showing from San Francisco. The game saw Mustapha register his first pass breakup of the season, and it was a huge one as it got Denver off the field after the Broncos reached San Francisco territory on their penultimate drive of the second quarter. Incredible drive and play on the ball from Malik Mustapha. pic.twitter.com/Vv0Aa0lLIO — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 6, 2026 Mustapha read the eyes of quarterback Bo Nix perfectly, got a great drive on the ball and arrived at the catch point at the perfect angle to get in front of intended target Evan Engram and make a diving deflection that prevented the Broncos from adding to a 3-0 lead. That play served as a reminder of the coverage instincts and athleticism that — along with his physicality — are key components of Mustapha’s skill set. And, after helping hold the Denver offense largely in check, Shanahan praised Mustapha’s efforts in limited playing time as he prepares for his first start of the year. Asked if Mustapha had made improvements since Week 1, Shanahan said: “Yeah, definitely. Malik just had some unfortunate injuries during training camp, so he got a late start, but got his first practice out there in Australia and I think he’s been awesome this whole month. That’s why we’ve been mixing him in there more regardless, even with all those guys healthy. We started mixing him in last week trying to get him some series and stuff. Every time he’s come in, I think he’s played at a high level. I thought he did that yesterday and made one of the biggest plays in the game yesterday on that third-and-five when he broke that pass up. I’m real excited with Malik and how he’s looked.” Shanahan also had kind words for Sigle, a fifth-round pick last year, and how he has played to start his second year. He added of Sigle: “I think he’s been playing his ass off in the run and pass game. The way he’s filled on some of these tackles, just how solid he’s hit people and how quickly he’s done it getting up in there. I thought he’s done it good in the pass game too. He did a lot of good stuff last year, but I think he has taken it to another level, just playing a little bit faster, hesitating less, knowing what he’s doing and really playing well before that injury.” It will be several weeks before Sigle is able to return, giving Mustapha an opportunity to establish himself in the lineup. Mustapha has some fond memories of playing in Seattle, with his first career interception as a pro coming in the Niners’ 2024 win over the Seahawks. As the 49ers seek a fifth consecutive regular-season road victory over the Seahawks, his ability to build on the flashes he has shown this season will be crucial to their hopes of improving to 5-0 and taking a stranglehold on the NFC West with the third division triumph of the campaign.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw fined for taunting and cussing at the Broncos sideline

Whether he was pointing, gesturing, or smack-talking, Greenlaw went out of his way to make it a point to Broncos head coach Sean Payton […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dre Greenlaw’s emotions were running high in the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos. If Greenlaw had a chance to let Denver’s sideline know, he took it. Whether he was pointing, gesturing, or smack-talking, Greenlaw went out of his way to make it a point to Broncos head coach Sean Payton during the game. Aaron Wilson reported the NFL fined Greenlaw $11,941 for taunting and cussing at Payton: Greenlaw, after the game, yelled at Payton: “Hey! You get the f-ck off my field!.” He told reporters: “I told him to get the f–k off the field. “That’s it: ‘Get the f–k off the field.'” Greenlaw said he was upset about being released by and not being called by Payton. “The disrespect,” Greenlaw said. “He couldn’t be man-to-man and call my phone and say, ‘We’re going to cut you.'” Payton didn’t add fuel to the fire during his post-game press conference. “I think the world of him. I love everything about him,” Payton said. “He plays with that emotion and so, all good.” Greenlaw told reporters after the game he didn’t like “the disrespect” and was upset Payton didn’t call him when the Broncos released him last offseason: “He couldn’t be man to man and call my phone and say, ‘We’re going to cut you.'”
author: Kyle Posey

title: Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy explain those bizarre fourth-and-1 calls against the Broncos
summary: We’ve always had a few plays after a 2026 San Francisco 49ers game where we asked: “What the hell was that?” In their 24-14 victory over the Denver Broncos, a couple errr, “apparent” moments were on fourth down. The first fourth down was in the first half on fourth-and-1. A very long “1,” mind you. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Kaelon Black #26 of the San Francisco 49ers gets tackled by Jahdae Barron #23 and Brandon Jones #22 of the Denver Broncos in the third quarter at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve always had a few plays after a 2026 San Francisco 49ers game where we asked: “What the hell was that?” In their 24-14 victory over the Denver Broncos , a couple errr, “apparent” moments were on fourth down. The first fourth down was in the first half on fourth-and-1. A very long “1,” mind you. The 49ers lined up to do their trademark QB sneak—the one that works on shorter fourth-and-1s. The 49ers failed to convert on the QB Sneak pic.twitter.com/3QXRUukrH9 — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) October 4, 2026 So it’s a QB sneak with Christian McCaffrey in the backfield doing whatever he’s supposed to do. If you said, “What the hell?” you are not alone. “It was a little long,” Kyle Shanahan said after the game. “We had the look we wanted. And when you get the look you want, sometimes we get like 3 to 4 yards on those.” How this would go four yards is a mystery. Not every play can be like last week against the Arizona Cardinals, where Christian McCaffrey does his best Thomas the Tank Engine impersonation, taking the whole offense and powering through for nine yards. Shanahan praised the Broncos for defending it, but one has to wonder if that would have fooled anyone. The other fourth down was equally surprising, but had a much happier ending. On fourth-and-1 at the Broncos’ 18-yard line, this, well, whatever it is, happened: Heads up play by Kaelon Black. Unreal lucky first down on 4&1 pic.twitter.com/y30AKLMHFE — Christian (@ChristianR_Vill) October 4, 2026 What the hell was that?! I can only imagine the arguments at watch parties over whether this was planned. The ball somehow gets diverted from Brock Purdy and goes into the hands of Kaelon Black. Since Black has awesome awareness, he takes a 1-yard dive and picks up the first down. It’s not nearly as good as Frank Gore’s fumble touchdown against the New England Patriots over a decade ago, but it’d definitely be up there. “It was a bad snap,” Shanahan said. “We didn’t call a direct snap.” Brock Purdy had more detail on what went down. “The ball just like, hit Jake’s [49ers center Jake Brendel] butt,” Purdy recalled. “It popped back up, and I was like, ‘oh gosh,’ I went to go get it, and he [Black] just snatched it and then kept going on his running back track for the run.” Purdy later confirmed the play was supposed to be a handoff to Black—not Black taking the snap like what happened. If it wasn’t supposed to be a handoff, Black sure made you wonder if that was how it was drawn up to begin with. As you can see from the video above, he catches the ball and makes his dive. The alternative? I don’t want to think about it. The game was 3-3, and another failed fourth down would have left fans irate after what we saw on the first play. Points were at a premium, and keeping the game close like this would have been maddening. Instead, the 49ers converted, setting up what would be a Deebo Samuel touchdown a few plays later. While what happened is interesting, it’s another point of how Kaelon Black has been as a rookie. We’ve praised his ability to spell Christian McCaffrey (something others have failed to do), but his awareness on a play like this to make the dive is invaluable. While the 49ers are 4-0, plays like these, even with Black’s awareness, carry a bit of luck. Just like the fumble earlier, that’s one reason teams make it to a championship.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: Week 5 NFL Power Rankings: Where do the 49ers rank among undefeated teams?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are only one of three NFL teams that have started the season 4-0 in 2026, joining the Kansas City Chiefs and the Minnesota Vikings. Thus far, their +58 point differential leads the NFL, and they also have two big wins on their resume: the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball after a catch against the Denver Broncos in the fourth quarter at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are only one of three NFL teams that have started the season 4-0 in 2026, joining the Kansas City Chiefs and the Minnesota Vikings. Thus far, their +58 point differential leads the NFL, and they also have two big wins on their resume: the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos. The 49ers have had some flaws, with injuries being the biggest issue. San Francisco is well short at wide receiver and defensive line, going deeper and deeper into their practice squad pool. But they’ve been even better than advertised through four weeks, taking advantage of an early three-game home stand. There were several teams that had impressive wins in Week 5. The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Cincinnati Bengals. The Dallas Cowboys put up 34 points on the Houston Texans. The New England Patriots came from behind to beat the Buffalo Bills on the road. So did the Rams against the Philadelphia Eagles. Remaining undefeated, where are the 49ers in this week’s power rankings? ESPN: No. 1 “The 49ers have again been hit by a slew of injuries,” ESPN’s Nick Wagoner wrote. “On the defensive line, star defensive end Nick Bosa is out because of a calf issue. At receiver, they’ve lost Ricky Pearsall (knee) for the season and promising rookie De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) for 10 weeks. “And yet the Niners are one of three undefeated teams. Quarterback Brock Purdy has emerged as an early MVP candidate, as the offense has done most of the heavy lifting. But Sunday’s win showed the Niners can lean on their defense and special teams when they aren’t lighting up the scoreboard.” The Chiefs, Seahawks, Bills, and Jaguars rounded out the top five. USA Today: No. 1 “Given their largely tremendous start, would have put them in the top spot sooner if not for concern regarding their latest rash of injuries, FB Kyle Juszczyk the most recent star to go down,” USA Today’s Nate Davis wrote. “However, the Niners are certainly safeguarding early MVP candidate Brock Purdy, becoming the first team since Peyton Manning’s 2005 Colts to permit zero sacks through four games. Beat Seattle on Sunday, and San Francisco will have already taken down three of last season’s final four teams. Unbeaten through four games for the third time under Kyle Shanahan, now the longest-tenured coach in franchise history, the 49ers leveraged those other two hot starts into Super Bowl berths.” Here, the Chiefs, Seahawks, Broncos, and Rams closed off the top five. CBS Sports: No. 1 “At 4-0, they are rolling, and beating good teams in the process. The defense came up big in the victory over the Broncos, which is a good sign,” CBS’s Pete Prisco wrote. Behind them were the Chiefs, Vikings, Seahawks, and Jaguars. Overall, most places had the 49ers initially at No. 2, bumping them to No. 1 after their win over the Broncos and Buffalo’s loss to New England. San Francisco will get a big challenge, though, in Week 5, as they take on the Seattle Seahawks on the road. They’re currently three-point underdogs ahead of kickoff.

title: How to win, how to lose: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys week 5 game preview
summary: This week the Buccaneers play on Thursday Night Football, a national spotlight for a team that does not deserve it. Tampa Bay is 0-4 (only two games out of first though, just ask coach Bowles) with a spiraling feeling surrounding the organization. The Bucs are not yet lifeless, but the trend is nearing that point. […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - JANUARY 16: Vita Vea #50 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during the first half in the NFC Wild Card playoff game at Raymond James Stadium on January 16, 2023 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week the Buccaneers play on Thursday Night Football, a national spotlight for a team that does not deserve it. Tampa Bay is 0-4 (only two games out of first though, just ask coach Bowles ) with a spiraling feeling surrounding the organization. The Bucs are not yet lifeless, but the trend is nearing that point. Losers of 11 of their last 13, Tampa is flatly not good right now and does not appear to nearing a solution or a corner to turn in the near future. The team has a coach on the hot seat, a quarterback in a thumb cast, and a familiar vibe starting to set in. “We’ve got to coach it better, we’ve got to play it better.” – Todd Robert Bowles How can the Buccaneers win? The Buccaneers will be entering Thursday’s game with a minute margin of error. In order for Tampa to win their first game of the season, not only will they need their A-game, but they will likely need that A-game to be accompanied by a few breaks— Breaks Daniel LaRusso would be proud of (Tampa may be given similar odds as well). The Bucs will be pitted up against a team with legitimate championship aspirations that is need of a victory. Dallas is just 2-2, leagues ahead of the prey they’ll see on Thursday night, but not near where expectations would have placed them at the year’s start. There is no denying that the Buccaneers are going to struggle to match the Cowboys’ personnel. Tampa has injuries, youth, and just general lethargy going against them. Perhaps this will be the week that the team will in fact coach it better and then wind up playing it better, however, a more likely outcome is Bowles’ bunch will look much like it has thus far in 2026, meaning their straightest path towards victory will be turnovers. The Dallas Cowboys have two games this season where they have played a clean game— They are 2-0 in those contests. Subsequently, they’ve played two games where their heralded offense has given the ball away to its opposition— Dallas is 0-2 in these games. Simple data, but its data that is tied back to a tale as old as time— If you win the turnover battle, you win the game. Todd Bowles’ Buccaneers have little to no chance at winning this game in many people’s eyes, however, any chance they do have is going to rest on taking care of the ball offensively and taking the ball away from Dak Prescott to give that offense more opportunities to find points of their own. Can this coaching staff guide an undrafted rookie quarterback away mistakes without handcuffing him to first down runs every sequence? Can Todd Bowles generate some pressure and force Dak Prescott into a mistake, or two… Or three? “You can’t win a game, if you don’t score any points.” – John Madden How can the Buccaneers lose? Let’s set the table. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are heading into a primetime matchup, on a short week, up against one of the most explosive offenses in the NFL, while they wield an offense that has been as dull as a school-lunchroom spork. In four games, Dallas has been held under 30 just one time and has never been kept beneath 20. Factually, the Cowboys can score points and it is unlikely Todd Bowles’ defense will be able to keep the lid on Dak and co. for the entirety of this game. The Buccaneers will need to score. There is not a single NFL game where you don’t need to score (if you plan on winning), but this Thursday in particular, they will touchdowns. The issue is, undrafted rookie quarterback or not, the Buccaneers’ offense doesn’t really spend a lot of time scoring. So far, 2026 hasn’t really been about touchdowns for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ offense. Operating as essentially an antonym for Dallas’ output, the Buccaneers haven’t hit the thirty-point mark in any game this season— They’ve only broken 20 one time, way back in week one. For context that 27-point explosion against the Cincinnati Bengals was aided by a defensive score when Josiah Trotter pick sixed Joe Burrow. It is extremely unlikely that the Bucs are going to be able to steal a victory totaling 16 points which is what they’re averaging since that week one performance. The easiest way the Buccaneers can lose this game is most obvious way the Buccaneers can lose this game— The prediction that anyone prepared to watch this game would make. Dallas is going to score points, they may score a lot of points— Can the Buccaneers’ offense do something it has not been able to all season and score touchdowns to be able to keep up wth them? That will be the question for Zac Robinson and his floundering unit on Thursday night.

title: Where is TE Gunnar Helm in this Titans offense?
summary: Tennessee Titans fans entered the 2026 season believing sophomore tight end Gunnar Helm would play a big role in the offense. Fast forward through Week 4 and that hasn’t been the case. Let’s examine Helm’s early involvement in Brian Daboll’s offense. Helm ranks third on the Titans in receptions, but has just nine catches. The […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Gunnar Helm #84 of the Tennessee Titans runs out prior to an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tennessee Titans fans entered the 2026 season believing sophomore tight end Gunnar Helm would play a big role in the offense. Fast forward through Week 4 and that hasn’t been the case. Let’s examine Helm’s early involvement in Brian Daboll’s offense. Helm ranks third on the Titans in receptions, but has just nine catches. The former Texas standout is also third in targets (12), but ranks fourth in receiving yards (60). Rookie Carnell Tate has essentially dominated all air-yardage opportunities, especially after his breakout performance in Week 4 further skewed the numbers. Helm has not scored a touchdown, but was on the receiving end of Cam Ward’s two-point conversion on Sunday. Helm has surprisingly not seen a single red-zone target. In fairness, the Titans have consistently run the football, even stubbornly, once inside the 20-yard line. Extrapolating Helm’s current production into a 17-game sample size, he’s currently on track for fewer receptions, yards, and touchdowns than he accumulated as a rookie in 2025. He was productive last campaign, catching 44 balls for 357 yards and two scores. Even his yards per reception (6.7) is down (8.1). The Titans signed veteran tight end Daniel Bellinger to a three-year, $24 million contract in free agency. His annual $8 million price tag suggested he might eat into Helm’s workload, but that hasn’t necessarily been the case. Helm has outsnapped Bellinger 179-85. Helm has been on the field for 78.85% of the offense’s snaps. That’s a noticeably bigger workload than his rookie season included (50.47%). Yet his production is way down. The Titans appear hellbent on using Helm as a blocker more frequently than they did last season. That’s confusing, because he’s a better pass catcher, and the presumption was Bellinger was signed to primarily handle in-line blocking duties. PFF has Helm with 67 run-blocking snaps, compared to Bellinger’s 49. The ball isn’t finding Helm enough in the passing game. Coach Daboll could also make personnel-related changes to how Helm is being deployed. The Titans’ inconsistencies on offense and time of possession issues surely haven’t helped, but Daboll hasn’t put Helm in the best imaginable positions to be successful yet.

(Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 7 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Sonny Styles vs Colts [The video of the play described in the excerpt below is embedded in the tweet that is also pasted below] Despite the Commanders suffering another disappointing loss and falling to a 1-3 record, there were some positives to take out of this game. One of the biggest positives, in my opinion, was the play of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles. Styles has been playing well all season, winning NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his performance against the Seahawks [the week before]. He made some flash plays against the Eagles a few weeks prior too, and his coverage ability has already stood out as one of the best coverage linebackers in the NFL. But against the Colts, we saw a step forward from Styles in another area of his game. Styles is an incredible athletic and is terrific in coverage, but he’s still fairly fresh to the linebacker position, having transitioned from safety to linebacker in college a few years ago. So while he’s been fine in the run game, there has certainly been some room for growth in his first three performances. In this game though, we saw what was comfortably the best performance we’ve seen from Styles against the run. So let’s break it down to see why he was so good. Commanders rookie LB Sonny Styles had another impressive performance on Sunday. It was perhaps his best outing against the run so far. I broke it all down: https://t.co/AzV7Q767u5 pic.twitter.com/uh8OwqgWKh — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) October 7, 2026 This time the Colts run a gap scheme inside with the fullback kicking out the edge and the tight end working up to block Styles inside. Styles reads the run quickly and you can see how compared to Luvu, he’s the quicker linebacker to read the run and react. He identifies the tight end working up to him and closes the gap, using his momentum to get into the chest of the block and stack him up. Styles arrives at the block with a thump, landing both hands on the blockers chest and standing him up. From there, Styles has control of the block. He looks into the backfield and sees running back Jonathan Taylor cutting his run outside, so Styles works off the block and reaches out with one arm to make the stop for a one yard gain. Perhaps his most impressive play against the run came later on in the game in the second half. Commanders.com Kaliakmanis’ NFL debut contained plenty of lessons Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo didn’t make life easy on Kaliakmanis. He didn’t blitz the quarterback an excessive amount — per Pro Football Reference, Kaliakmanis was pressured on only 20% of his dropbacks — but he did choose moments in which Kaliakmanis needed to make a play. Most of the pressure came off the edge and led to a sack on third-and-9 that knocked the Commanders out of field goal range. Other times, Kaliakmanis got the ball out but was punished for it with hard hits on his release. But plays were open downfield thanks to that pressure, and Kaliakmanis started letting the ball fly in the second half. He tied with C.J. Stroud for the highest average depth of target at 14.1 yards and had six passes of at least 30 yards — the most for a quarterback in a single game so far this season. Two of those passes found their mark — a 48-yarder to Dyami Brown and a 47-yarder to Treylon Burks that resulted in his first career touchdown pass. The current expectation is that Kaliakmanis will not be under center for the first snap against the New York Giants this coming weekend. Daniels is expected to have a full week of practice, and if everything goes well, he will start and try to get his team one game closer to .500. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Do Commanders need to look outside the organization for a short-term veteran backup QB? Kaliakmanis will be available to stabilize the room in week five with the hope that Daniels anchors the room once more, yet given the Commanders have already watched its starting quarterback go down in two of the first four games in 2026, whether an addition needs to be made is the question. The irony? A familiar name looms as an available option given 33 year old Jeff Driskel, who also joined the Commanders’ practice squad to close last season, is an available name. Jimmy Garoppolo and Brandon Allen are two others who remain available, albeit both have limited experience over the last two seasons to add a question whether they would serve as viable stopgaps. Could Washington pull a page from last season’s book and sign someone off another team’s practice squad? Josh Johnson, who started the final two games of last season, is on the Bengals’ practice squad to serve as a low risk move. The upside is unlike Washington, the question isn’t about finding an answer atop the unit, rather ensuring depth is in place as offensive coordinator David Blough looks to find consistency [in the 2 games] ahead of the bye week. Given that Washington is currently 0-2 in the division and dealing with injuries large and small throughout the lineup, it’s not actually that simple. But Daniels always has been the most important person in the Commanders’ building, and Washington’s need for him to save the season has only grown since Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday’s loss to the Colts. In the first half of Washington’s Week 2 loss at Dallas, Daniels was playing his best football since his rookie year of 2024. He needs to be both on the field and playing at that level for the Commanders to overcome everything that faces them — a 1-3 start, a long-term injury to left tackle Laremy Tunsil, short-term injuries to wide receiver Terry McLaurin and guard Sam Cosmi and an upcoming schedule that features games against the 49ers, Eagles and Rams before the midway point.
