title: Is there cause for concern with Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt?
summary: The Commanders run game is a quandary.   The commitment to it is fine. Offensive coordinator David Blough continues to call for runs at an appropriate rate. The numbers look just sort of okay.   You take away the quarterback runs, though, and an eybrow gets raised. We aren’t talking about a nuclear winter, here. […]
full_text: The Commanders run game is a quandary. The commitment to it is fine. Offensive coordinator David Blough continues to call for runs at an appropriate rate. The numbers look just sort of okay. You take away the quarterback runs, though, and an eybrow gets raised. We aren’t talking about a nuclear winter, here. We’re just making folks aware that the bedrock of this offensive system isn’t hitting on all cylinders. The bottom line stats, as we’ve mentioned, can also be skewed by mobile quarterbacks. Here’s what we’re trying to get to in this long introduction: the curious case of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who is averaging less than four yards per carry over four games. That number dropped to less than two over the last two games, with Rachaad White unavailable on Sunday against the Colts. The prevailing theory was that Croskey-Merritt would fit well with Blough’s rushing scheme, which is predicated on outside zone runs. That hasn’t been the case to this point. Look, I’ll just put this out there. I’m not a “tape guy” and I’m not going to pretend to be one. We have Mark Tyler and Jamual Forrest and John Portis for that stuff. But I have been around the game for a super long time and can analyze the numbers and the advanced metrics, and, frankly, I know a good player when I see one. I covered LaDainian Tomlinson for goodness’ sake, so I have a gold standard. It also doesn’t take a rocket scientist to see that the Commanders aren’t efficient running the football at important times. Nor is their lead back. Croskey-Merritt’s explosiveness might be his best feature, as we saw several times last year. So is his decisiveness and burst into the second level. But, outside a single play negated by penalty, we haven’t seen that this season. He’s still in prove-it mode, considering it’s just his second season. But…the fact we saw Rachaad White average 4.4 yards per carry vs. Seattle to Croskey-Merritt’s 1.9 isn’t great. Neither is the fact that Austin Ekeler has now joined the roster, and was efficient with his opportunities. Is it the back, or is it the system, or the line and the operation? Evaluate that in the article comments below. But it’s fair to wonder how long the Commanders stick with Croskey-Merritt and whether this is a temporary issue or a major cause for concern. I bring this all up for a discussion point, as the Commanders head into a now vital Week 5 contest with the New York Giants. Is it time to pivot higher carry counts towards Ekeler or White? Or am I overreacting? Let’s discuss.
author: Scott Bair

title: NFL Power Rankings: Commanders return home to an uphill battle for their season
summary: The Washington Commanders are 1-3 and the high from a win over last season’s Super Bowl winners quickly faded when Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury that ended his London game in the 1st quarter. One step forward, and two steps back for a Commanders team that continues to deal with a high […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 07: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders runs for a first down against the New York Giants during the fourth quarter of the NFL 2025 game at Northwest Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Jess Rapfogel/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 1-3 and the high from a win over last season’s Super Bowl winners quickly faded when Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury that ended his London game in the 1st quarter. One step forward, and two steps back for a Commanders team that continues to deal with a high number of injuries. Mariota is expected to miss time after reinjuring his MCL and Jaylin Lane is done for the year after a serious injury. The hope lies in the returns of Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin, and Sam Cosmi this week. A much needed injection of starters back into the offense’s starting lineup. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis made his debut last week after Mariota’s injury, and became the first rookie to throw his first NFL touchdown in an international game. Tress Way will love that little piece of NFL trivia, but if all goes to plan, Jayden Daniels returns this week, and Kaliakmanis doesn’t play another snap this season unless its for kneel down duty in a blowout win. Plans don’t always work out, and the Commanders are currently a bottom of the league team clinging to hope for a miracle run after a rough start to the season. The NFL Power Rankings consortium doesn’t see that hopeful scenario happening, and has them averaging out as a bottom 8 team in the league. They don’t have a lot of time to change that perception because another loss puts their odds of climbing out of this hole off the board. The Commanders return home for their third division game in the first five weeks off the season. They are 0-2, and face the improbable division leaders, the New York Giants. Win this week and on the road against the 49ers and they’re 3-3 heading into the bye. Lose the next two weeks, and the calls for Dan Quinn’s job might actually reach majority owner Josh Harris’s desk. High: 20 Low: 28 Average: 25.4 #20 NFL Trade Rumors (Woodie) You have to feel for Marcus Mariota. The Commanders offense was humming early with Mariota at the helm, although they failed to score a touchdown in two redzone trips. Then he sprained his MCL on a sack and the wheels fell off. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis had a couple of very impressive throws and big plays, but ultimately Washington was just outmatched without Mariota. The good news is that starting QB Jayden Daniels is hopeful to play in Week 5 after dislocating his elbow in Week 2. Last week: 20 Walter Football The poor Redskins had to go to Athan Kaliakmanis in London. The good news is that Jayden Daniels will be back this week, which is why Washington has risen so much. The bad news is that this means that Daniels is bound to get hurt again soon, too. Last week: 29 #22 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) Jayden Daniels’ return can’t come soon enough after the Commanders were stuck relying on third-string QB Athan Kaliakmanis for most of Sunday morning in London. The Greek Rifle had a moment or two, but not enough to convince anyone he can help the Commanders win. If Daniels does return Sunday against the Giants, there might be time to salvage this season. If not, it’s time to start preparing for the draft, and maybe a coaching search, too. Stat To Know : The Commanders have allowed 122 points through four weeks, tied for the second most in the entire NFL. Last week: 24 #23 SB Nation As for the Commanders, this is some course correction. We were bullish on Washington returning to form in 2026, but there’s been nothing to indicate they’re worthy of faith. Moreover, the team is getting worse as time goes on, struggling more against worse opponents — and the injury bug is creeping in. It’s a shame, but this is shaping up to be another lost season for the team. Last week: 17 #24 USA Today (Davis) Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis became the first NFL quarterback to throw his first career TD pass in an international game. Cool. But this team can’t get Jayden Daniels back fast enough. Last week: 20 Sporting News (Iyer) The Commanders are having trouble keeping key offensive players such as Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin, Laremy Tunsil and Rachaad White healthy. Then they also lost Marcus Mariota to a knee injury, forcing rookie Athan Kaliakmanis into action. Daniels may not be ready to return from his elbow injury in Week 5, either. They have a shot at the Giants next to try to stay in the NFC East race early. Last week: 20 #25 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Maybe if Marcus Mariota hadn’t gotten injured, the Commanders might have won and been a promising 2-2. They were about to take an early 6-0 lead on the Colts early in the game when Mariota sprained MCL in his right knee. The Commanders’ defense played pretty well but Washington’s offense couldn’t do much with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis in for Mariota and an inactive Jayden Daniels. And 1-3 is a tough hole to dig out of. With Mariota hurt and the Commanders in danger of having their season slip away further, there has to be tremendous urgency for Daniels to return from a dislocated left elbow. “That’s the hope for us for sure, Jay coming back,” Commanders coach Dan Quinn said . “He’ll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That’s the goal: that he could get into that space.” Last week: 21 Bleacher Report The Washington Commanders are in real danger of having their season slip away because of injuries for the second straight season. They managed to beat the defending champion Seattle Seahawks with Marcus Mariota at quarterback in Week 3, but they lost Mariota to a knee injury in London on Sunday. Rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis had a few bright moments against the Indianapolis Colts, but he made his fair share of rookie mistakes, too. Washington’s defense showed some signs of progress against Indy, too, but it couldn’t stop the ground game late, and the Commanders now sit at 1-3. Next week’s matchup with the rival New York Giants has become a veritable must-win. Last week: 24 Clutch Sports (Johrendt) With Jayden Daniels already out, the Washington Commanders lost Marcus Mariota to a first-half injury, forcing them to hand over the keys to Athan Kaliakmanis. The former Rutgers QB found Treylon Burks for a long touchdown, but the WAS offense struggled when Mariota was forced out. It remains to be seen which QB will be Washington’s starter in Week 5. Last week: 23 The Score Amik Robertson: With the Commanders still waiting for Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson to heat up on the edges, Robertson has arguably emerged as the team’s top defensive performer. He’s tied for the league lead with seven pass breakups and ranks among the best in separation allowed. Last week: 20 New York Post (Dunleavy) Last week: 23 #26 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Concern level: High as Jayden Daniels nears a return It seems their exciting young quarterback is going to opt against surgery on his elbow, which both breathes hope into this frustrating season and brings a fair amount of risk over the possibility of reinjury. Concern will be high as he returns to the field, possibly as early as next weekend. Last week: 23 Sports Illustrated (Orr) I enjoy reading updates about Commanders third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis from the perspective of a Greek news outlet . While the return of Jayden Daniels will ultimately deprive us of a Greek Tommy DeVito-like run, we can always hope in silence. Last week: 26 Sharp Football Analysis (Summerlin) The Commanders continue to have rough injury luck, this time losing Marcus Mariota in the first half against the Colts. Jayden Daniels , Terry McLaurin , Sam Cosmi , and Rachaad White were inactive, and Laremy Tunsil is on injured reserve. Washington could get some of those players back for the Giants this week, but it has been a rough start to a pivotal season.…

title: Future Hogs – Week 5: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: In last week’s article, I mentioned how Ole Miss went from signature win over LSU to huge loss to Florida. This past weekend, it was Florida’s turn to tumble down the rankings after a loss to Missouri. The Gators fall to #16 with that loss, one spot ahead of a Mississippi State team that was […]
full_text: In last week’s article, I mentioned how Ole Miss went from signature win over LSU to huge loss to Florida. This past weekend, it was Florida’s turn to tumble down the rankings after a loss to Missouri. The Gators fall to #16 with that loss, one spot ahead of a Mississippi State team that was dominated by Alabama. Miami faced Clemson, but it was not much of a contest with the Hurricanes continuing to roll. The same is true for Ohio State who passed a road test behind an incredibly productive day from star receiver Jeremiah Smith and beat Iowa and their stingy defense. There will be a couple of rivalry games this weekend that should be exciting. First, the Red River Rivalry between #1 Texas and Oklahoma is always entertaining. Although the Sooners are not ranked, Arch Manning and Texas have looked beatable. Second, a ranked-on-ranked top-10 matchup between #2 Georgia and #6 Alabama could go a long way to establishing what team makes it to the SEC Championship. #13 Oregon will host an undefeated #21 UCLA that has looked like one of the Big Ten’s best teams. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to comment with players that stood out to you. Gio Lopez | QB | RS Junior | Wake Forest Another week, another quarterback injury. Marcus Mariota exited the Commander’s game with a knee injury and was replaced by seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis. While the rookie did some good things in the pass game, it was clear that many of the plays that take advantage of Jayden Daniels and Mariota’s mobility were off the table. Adding a mobile developmental QB would allow the offense to run many of the same plays for the backups. In his first year at Wake Forest after a year at UNC, Gio Lopez is a big part of why Wake Forest looks like a contender in the ACC. Lopez has less than ideal height at 6’0”, but he’s sturdily built at 220 pounds. He has a quick release and he makes accurate passes with good ball placement. Lopez is also capable of making plays with his legs in the run game. He’s not an elite runner at the position, but he will keep a defense honest and make them pay if they play man coverage against him. Lopez has an average arm, but is a quick and accurate passer that can somewhat mitigate a lack of arm strength. Lopez went 20 of 27 for two touchdowns and added 88 yards and three touchdowns on the ground in a win over Stanford. Jamal Roberts | RB | Senior | Missouri The Commanders have not received much help from its run game. Austin Ekeler was arguably the best running back against the Colts and he just got the playbook last week. Bill has flashed, but he has not been consistently productive. White, who wasn’t healthy enough to go against the Colts, provides a boost in the passing game, but not much on the ground. Jamal Roberts, the Tigers’ 6’, 216 pound lead back, was supposed to be the backup to Ahmad Hardy this season. An unfortunate incident to Hardy before the season started opened the door for Roberts and he has been special. Mizzou uses a lot of zone blocking schemes and Roberts excels behind it. He has excellent burst through the line of scrimmage once he identifies the hole. Roberts will break off long runs but can be caught from behind. He has enough power to push the pile on short yardage situations, but he is more of a straight line runner in the open field with little elusiveness. Roberts had 211 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries in the Tigers’ win over Florida. Missouri backup* RB Jamal Roberts: 24 rushes, 211 yards, 3 TD Florida RB Jadan Baugh: 12 rushes, 13 yards Any. Given. Saturday. In the SEC pic.twitter.com/oWOeyLGc1b — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) October 3, 2026 Missouri’s offensive line putting in work today against Florida. Jamal Roberts has run for over 200 yards on the Gators (Missouri has more than 500 yards) pic.twitter.com/r7oX1GIyCx — Bobby Football (@Rob__Paul) October 3, 2026 Umari Hatcher | WR | RS Senior | Syracuse Injuries are starting to be more of an issue for Terry McLaurin as he missed the game against the Colts. Jaylin Lane’s dislocation and ankle fracture keeps him out the remainder of the season. A player like Syracuse’s Hatcher could be an interesting addition to the Commanders’ receiving room. He would be a large target at 6’3”, but at only 190 pounds, there could be legitimate concerns about his play strength. His long strides help him close space between defenders in off coverage. It also allows him to run by them or break off routes short and make himself available to his quarterback. His competitiveness at the catch point and ability to adjust to passes are attributes Hatcher possesses. Route diversity and route polish would go a long way to helping Hatcher contribute at the next level. In an overtime win over UConn, Hatcher made 12 catches for 142 yards and three touchdowns. Hatcher was the go-to guy all day 🍊 Umari Hatcher caught 12 passes for 152 yards and three TDs in Syracuse’s 42-41 overtime thriller against UConn. His 17-yard TD on 4th-and-17 in OT kept the Orange alive and set up the game-winning conversion. @CuseFootball | @Cuse | #Cuse pic.twitter.com/fN8WElTJfN — ACC Digital Network (@theACCDN) October 3, 2026 Randy Pittman Jr. | TE | Senior | SMU Despite a healthy Chig Okonkwo, the Commanders struggled to get the tight ends involved in the passing game in London. Randy Pittman, Jr. could help because he is more of a big wide receiver. He’s 6’2”, 240 pounds, and lines up in various places to create mismatches for the Mustangs. He can find the soft spot in zones and settle down or beat a defender in man. At the catchpoint, Pittman, Jr. shows very good body control by adjusting to catches outside the frame of his body. I haven’t seen much of him as a blocker, but I wouldn’t expect a lot out of him in this regard given his size. Pittman, Jr. made three catches for 23 yards and a touchdown as SMU beat Boston College. . @SMUFB finds the end zone after the turnover! Kevin Jennings ➡️ Randy Pittman Jr. pic.twitter.com/dwltpsOfyQ — The CW Sports (@TheCW_Sports) October 3, 2026 Bruce Mitchell | C | RS Senior | BYU We have discussed the woes of the Commanders’ interior offensive line ad nauseum. Starting Matt Gulbin did not help matters. A player that might solidify the middle of that line is Bruce Mitchell. One reason might be because Mitchell is an older prospect. He did a three-year mission and is a redshirt senior, so I suspect he could be 25, maybe 26, on draft day. That also means Mitchell has a mature body and the requisite strength for the position at the next level. In the run game, Mitchell can push defenders downfield, turning them away from the play to create rushing lanes. BYU uses a gap scheme run game, but Mitchell looks to move well enough for zone blocking duties. In the pass game, Mitchell has a solid anchor and mirrors defenders well. Oh my goodness Bear Bachmeier will not be denied 🤯 📺 ESPN x @Big12Conference pic.twitter.com/x5ZLHq3OyN — CFP (@CFBPlayoff) October 4, 2026 Ahmad Moten | DT | RS Senior | Miami The Commanders front did a commendable job containing Jonathan Taylor and pressuring Daniel Jones. The line could use more talent that can beat blocks and make plays in the backfield without blitzing. Ahmad Moten, Sr. is part of arguably the most talented defensive line in the country. While he plays 3-technique for Miami, his quickness at 6’3”, 300 pounds, and his hand usage would allow him to play defensive end in a 3-4 front. Along with that quickness is Moten’s superb hand usage. It allows him to defeat blocks and disrupt action in the backfield. Moten had two tackles, half a sack, and a forced fumble in Miami’s win over Clemson. Ahmad Moten is out here swimming with the fish. #NFLDraft | @CanesFootball pic.twitter.com/l8z812XpnC — Newt Westen (@NFLDraft_Westen) October 6, 2026 Ahmad Moten did a great job PUNCHING THAT BALL OUT‼️🗣️💪🏽👊 💥👊🏈👊💥 pic.twitter.com/hkmQsmb4mM —…

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 5
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 5? We made our 1-32 list and sized up each franchise's performance so far.
full_text:
After four weeks of the  2026 NFL season , there are only three undefeated teams left: the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings. And last season's 14 playoff teams are off to a rocky start, with a combined record of 30-26 this season. That's the lowest winning percentage through four weeks by the previous season's playoff teams in the past 15 years, per ESPN Research.

 So why are those teams struggling -- and how are San Francisco, Kansas City and Minnesota still unbeaten? We're stacking all 32 teams entering Week 5. And in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to reflect on the first month of the season. Which teams are meeting or exceeding expectations? Which teams are already in jeopardy of a failed season? 

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Jaguars secured their second straight win over an AFC opponent Sunday to move into the top five of our rankings. That was despite 125 penalty yards in Cincinnati , which marked their most in a single game since Week 7 of 2019, per ESPN Research. And the Jaguars saw some positive play from third-year receiver  Brian Thomas Jr ., who scored on his first red zone target this season. 
 The Eagles are out of the top 10 after a shocking defeat to the Rams at home. According to ESPN Analytics, Philly had a 97.4% chance to win when it led by 10 with a third-and-goal with 8:17 left in the fourth quarter. The loss marked their second straight game with no points in the second half. 
 The Browns climbed into the top 20 of our list after their third straight win -- a 27-24 decision over the Steelers on Thursday night. Cleveland won three games as an underdog for the first time since 2021, per ESPN Research, and is tied with Baltimore for first place in the AFC North, though the Ravens could run into some trouble after QB  Lamar Jackson   injured his left ankle  Sunday. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with a different No. 1 team from last week.

 1. San Francisco 49ers (4-0) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Broncos 24-14 
 Week 4 ranking: 2 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Not surviving but thriving.

 

 The 49ers have again been hit by a slew of injuries. On the defensive line, star defensive end  Nick Bosa is out because of a calf issue . At receiver, they've lost Ricky Pearsall ( knee ) for the season and promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling ( ankle ) for 10 weeks. And yet the Niners are one of three undefeated teams. Quarterback Brock Purdy has emerged as an early MVP candidate, as the offense has done most of the heavy lifting. But Sunday's win showed the Niners can lean on their defense and special teams when they aren't lighting up the scoreboard. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Raiders 30-27 
 Week 4 ranking: 3 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks:  In Walker we trust.

 

 Coach Andy Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy have no excuses to ever abandon the running game as long as running back Kenneth Walker III is healthy and on the field. Walker has completely transformed the Chiefs' offense, allowing quarterback Patrick Mahomes to make more deep completions. Walker leads the NFL with 537 rushing yards and the team with six total touchdowns. The Chiefs should continue to rely on Walker following the bye week after injuries to receivers  Tyquan Thornton (dislocated left ankle) and Rashee Rice (right hamstring).  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 3. Seattle Seahawks (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Chargers 30-23 
 Week 4 ranking: 4 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Eventful -- not always positive.

 

 Quarterback Sam Darnold sustained a glute injury  on the season's fifth play and missed most of the first two games. No. 1 running back  Jadarian Price , Seattle's first-round pick, lost fumbles in consecutive weeks and is now on IR because of a chest injury . The Seahawks won in Week 4 despite a franchise-record 150 penalty yards. Throw in coach Mike Macdonald's interview mishap -- which resulted in an apology to Broncos coach Sean Payton -- and the reigning champions haven't traveled the smoothest road so far. But the first month was also defined by some stellar performances, such as  Drew Lock 's fill-in stint and Jaxon Smith-Njigba continuing to make his case as the league's best receiver. -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 4. Buffalo Bills (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Lost to the Patriots 29-26 
 Week 4 ranking: 1 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Might've established unsustainable expectations.

 

 The Bills opened the season with 77 points and 855 yards in two weeks. Quarterback Josh Allen looked unstoppable against Houston and Detroit , two teams with Super Bowl aspirations. Now the Texans and Lions are a combined 2-6, and the Bills are coming back down to earth. Coach Joe Brady's offense has been held to 25 points per game over the past two weeks and turned the ball over seven times. There's no question the Bills can compete in the AFC. But the steamrollers who looked poised to break NFL scoring records seem like an artifact from the start of the season. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Bengals 22-17 
 Week 4 ranking: 10 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Defense is getting overlooked.

 

 Heading into this season, there was plenty of hype around Year 2 of the Liam Coen offense. But defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile has made a name for himself early in the season, which could lead to attention in next year's head-coaching cycle. The Jaguars rank among the top eight in the NFL in sacks, run defense, turnovers, red zone efficiency and third-down defense. With a run defense ranked second in the NFL (74.3 yards per game), Jacksonville has given up just nine first-half points. -- Michael DiRocco 

 

 
 

 6. Baltimore Ravens (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Titans 24-18 
 Week 4 ranking: 5 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: First place but hurting.

 

 The Ravens are meeting expectations with their best start in three seasons, which puts them in a first-place tie with the Browns atop the AFC North. But it has come at a cost. Quarterback Lamar Jackson is considered  day-to-day after injuring his left ankle Sunday , and his offensive line isn't faring much better. Injuries have left Baltimore with its No. 4 option at center ( Olaivavega Ioane ) and its third-string right guard ( Emery Jones Jr .). "We're not going to make excuses," coach Jesse Minter said. "We're going to figure out the guys that we have and put them out there and give ourselves the best chance to be successful." -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 7. Los Angeles Rams (2-2) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Eagles 24-20 
 Week 4 ranking: 7 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Not a superteam ... yet.

 

 The Rams came into the season with sky-high expectations after adding defensive end Myles Garrett , cornerback Trent McDuffie and defensive tackle Aaron Donald to a team that already had the reigning MVP in quarterback  Matthew Stafford . But Los Angeles needed an improbable comeback victory Sunday to avoid a 1-3 start. The Rams have been inconsistent and missed significant players because of injuries, including Garrett (three games), Donald (one) and wide receiver Puka Nacua (two). Los Angeles might not be playing like a Super Bowl contender right now, but it could be later in the season, especially once Garrett is back from knee surgery . -- Sarah Barshop

 Week 4 result: Beat the Jets 23-12

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

 
 See more on the NFL draft 

 
 

 First-round picks that have been traded: 

 
 The Green Bay Packers ' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade . 
 The Indianapolis Colts ' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade . 
 The Los Angeles Rams ' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade . 
 The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade .

title: NFL Week 5 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: Could injuries to Saquon Barkley, Lamar Jackson and others derail their teams? Which AFC teams should trade for a WR? Which coordinators could get head coach interest?
full_text:
It's already Week 5 of the  2026 NFL season ! Insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 Injuries are starting to pile up as we hit the quarter mark of the season, and a few important players went down Sunday, including Lamar Jackson , Pat Surtain II , Ja'Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley . Which teams could be in trouble if they have to go without one of their stars? And which teams might have to make a trade sooner rather than later to either replace an injured player or quickly fix a weak spot in the roster? The trade deadline is approaching fast -- it is under five weeks out.

 Coaches are also under the microscope with four weeks of games behind us. Are any seats warming around the league? And have any coordinators shown enough in the early going to put themselves on the radar for head coach interviews if they keep this up? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 5.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Key injuries | Teams needing a trade 
 Warming seats | Rising coordinators 
 Fantasy football advice 
 More notes, intel 

 
 

 Which player's Week 4 injury could be most detrimental to his team? 
 Graziano: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is the obvious answer if he has to miss time (which we don't know for sure yet). They're just so different without him. Having him on the field makes things easier for running back Derrick Henry , whereas defenses can lock in on Henry when they don't have to fear the QB run.

 Fowler: Can't understate that one. The Ravens are hopeful he won't miss time, but this week feels uncertain. I'll go with Broncos corner Pat Surtain II , who is set to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury . With Denver's offense struggling to consistently score points, it needs the defense to reestablish its dominant form. But after ripping through the league with 68 sacks last season, the Broncos have eight through four games ... which heightens the importance of having a former Defensive Player of the Year such as Surtain in the secondary. Normally I would go with the star quarterback who's hurt, but Surtain's absence could have a sizable ripple effect for a team on the ropes.

 Graziano: A Saquon Barkley absence could exacerbate the Eagles' problems. I know Barkley isn't having the best season, but the Philadelphia offense is getting really low on good players. It had to play Sunday without right tackle Lane Johnson (who has since retired ), top wide receiver  DeVonta Smith  and, other than the first four plays, Barkley. It's a thin group around Jalen Hurts right now, and even at full strength it was trying to figure out a new offense under a first-time playcaller. If the Eagles are going to pull out of this, they're going to need as many of their stars as close to full strength as possible.

 

 Fowler: Yeah, the Eagles are depleted in the short term, and their healthiest back right now is third-stringer Will Shipley . Hamstring injuries linger, and unfortunately for Philly, their top two playmakers are managing them . Plus, tight end Dallas Goedert has missed two weeks and guard Cam Jurgens is in concussion protocol  (Update: Jurgens was traded to Baltimore on Wednesday). The Eagles could use reinforcements, so it might be worth it for them to explore the trade or free agency market for depth.

 An underrated absence is that of Vikings guard Donovan Jackson , who is undergoing season-ending knee surgery . He's a good player, which Minnesota can't afford to lose, particularly on an offense that ranks 31st in total yards. Either Joe Huber , who went undrafted in 2025, assumes the starting job, or Minnesota adds to the roster in short order.

 

 
 Which team most needs to make a trade -- and at what position? 
 Fowler: The Lions should make a move for a cornerback. They were in on Joey Porter Jr . before Pittsburgh traded him to Dallas . Detroit's secondary is swimming right now, and though safety Brian Branch is close to a return and safety Kerby Joseph should eventually be back, the Lions don't have enough corner help to run the coverages they want. This team has elite players on both sides of the ball and must embrace its window of contention, whether it's slipping away or not.

 One potential option is Kansas City's Kristian Fulton , who is in and out of the Chiefs' lineup. He is owed real money -- $5 million of his $9.75 million base salary is guaranteed -- but perhaps the Chiefs and Lions could split the bill to facilitate a deal. Is it worth calling Pittsburgh for Jalen Ramsey ? Not sure he's available, but the Lions' defense seems far from settled.

 Graziano: Stop me if you've heard this before, but the Chiefs could use another wide receiver . I'm not buying that Tyreek Hill is much of an upgrade over what they have at this point in his career. If players such as Marvin Harrison Jr ., Brian Thomas Jr ., Jerry Jeudy or Calvin Ridley become available, the Chiefs should poke around. But the other team I think should be turning over whatever rock it can to find wide receiver help is the team Kansas City barely beat on Sunday -- the surprising 3-1 Raiders.

 

 Before the season, who would have thought that the Raiders could be adding at the deadline? Tight end Brock Bowers is their top receiver and likely would remain so even if they did get somebody, but Las Vegas would love to have a true X receiver so teams can't put a top corner such as Surtain on Bowers.

 Fowler: Receiver is a need for the Raiders, but they've been inclined to preserve draft capital and develop their young receivers, and I'm not sure the 3-1 start changes that. Las Vegas operates in that space between rebuilding and contention, and with only five selections in April's draft, Vegas could opt to lean on second-year players  Jack Bech  and  Dont'e Thornton Jr ., who returns soon from injured reserve, to play bigger roles. Also, Bowers basically is a wide receiver, so him as the No. 1 and Tre Tucker as the No. 2 isn't a bad setup.

 Another team to watch at receiver is the Colts, who are 2-2 with Pittsburgh and Tennessee coming up. They could easily be sitting at 4-2 after those two games despite a depleted receiving crew, and Indy is not hiding from being all-in to win now. Perhaps there's not a splash move that fits, but how about one that brings an upside receiver for a quality Day 3 pick? (The Sauce Gardner trade last year drained Indy's capital.)  Marvin Harrison Jr . would be an obvious fit -- and not just for sentimentality -- but Arizona won't just give him away. A midseason return from Alec Pierce could assuage the need to make a move.

 Graziano: It's tough to swing trades for offensive linemen, since the demand massively outweighs the supply. But teams that could/should be in the market include the Patriots, Ravens, Eagles and, of course, the Packers, who have been signing dudes out of retirement the past couple of weeks because their line has completely fallen apart.

 The Bengals could use help at linebacker. The Jaguars don't need much, but I could see them looking to add another edge rusher if the opportunity presents itself. And the Bills could need some help in the secondary as they continue to transition to Jim Leonhard's defense.

 

 
 Are any coaches' seats warming a little early? 
 Graziano: Before starting, I need to stress that I am not reporting that any coach is in imminent danger of losing his job. I don't have information to suggest that teams are considering big changes at this point in the season. That said, I can't imagine you're feeling too good if you're Todd Bowles right now. The Buccaneers have lost 11 of their past 13 games dating to their 2025 bye week, when they were 6-2 and eyeing a fifth straight division title.

 The extent to which things have fallen apart for Tampa Bay, which entered 2025 thinking it was primed for a Super Bowl run, is…

title: Fantasy football D/ST outlook for Weeks 5-8: Jaguars a solid option in October
summary: Looking for the right D/ST units to stream over the next four weeks? Here's what you need to know.
full_text:
I get it, no one likes homework.

 Streaming defenses might seem like an exhaustive amount of work for a fantasy football league, but those extra few bonus points that result from it pile up. And if you know anything about this wild, often unpredictable game, it's that an additional point here or there can prove the difference in a matchup.

 Again in 2026, picking defenses that face the league's weakest offenses has proven to be the optimal strategy. The top three team defense/special teams (D/ST) all rank outside the position's top 10 in fantasy points, and in only 50% of their games did they even score a point total greater than the league's average.

 D/STs that faced any of the preseason top 10 offenses for streaming purposes scored better than the league's average 55% of the time, and in 21% of their games they scored at least twice the league average.

 All that said, the NFL can change dramatically over the first month of a new season, and the list of optimal matchups often significantly shifts. Keeping up with these changes is the homework involved in maximizing your D/ST lineup slot output.

 But there's good news: I did your homework for you. What follows is my updated D/ST Road Map for Weeks 5-8, spanning the remainder of October (and first two days of November).

 Top 10 offenses to exploit 
 

 With four weeks in the books, here are the 10 offenses that have been the best so far for streaming opposing D/STs:

 1. Tampa Bay Buccaneers : added 6.5 fantasy points to a D/ST's score on average 
2. New York Giants : +3.9 
3 (tied). Atlanta Falcons : +3.5 
3 (tied). Los Angeles Chargers : +3.5 
5. Tennessee Titans : +2.9 
6. Pittsburgh Steelers : +2.7 
7. Philadelphia Eagles : +2.0 
8 (tied). Miami Dolphins : +1.7 
8 (tied). Indianapolis Colts : +1.7 
10. Houston Texans : +1.5

 What do the top four teams on the list have in common? Simple: They've all lost quarterbacks to injury at some point this season, and both the Buccaneers and Giants are starting lower-tier options at the position for the foreseeable future (the Giants for the duration). It's a reminder that the best offenses to exploit for D/ST streaming purposes are the ones with the shakiest quarterback situations.

 One caveat with the Falcons: Their Weeks 1 and 2 opponents totaled 44 fantasy points from their D/STs, but in Weeks 3 and 4, with QB Michael Penix Jr . back, their opponents scored minus-6 and minus-5 fantasy points from their D/STs, allowing 80 scoreboard points and 918 total yards. The full-season numbers might say that the Falcons are a plus matchup for D/STs, but they're at best a borderline top-10 target in my estimation.

 The New York Jets (+1.2) and Cleveland Browns (+0.2), preseason top-three teams on this list, lurk just beneath the cutoff, at 12th and 16th.

 Top 10 offenses to avoid 
 1. San Francisco 49ers : subtracted 6.0 points from a D/ST's score on average 
2. Kansas City Chiefs : minus-4.6 
3. Chicago Bears : minus-4.4 
4. Detroit Lions : minus-3.8 
5. Dallas Cowboys : minus-3.4 
6. Jacksonville Jaguars : minus-3.3 
7. Carolina Panthers : minus-3.1 
8. Buffalo Bills : minus-2.4

 Seven of these 10 were on the preseason list, but how about those Panthers? The Bryce Young -led offense -- one of the best to target with D/ST streaming during his first three NFL seasons -- has scored 32 or more points in three of its first four games, matching the number of times the Panthers did that from 2023-25 combined. Young has significantly cut his interception and sack rates and has his team looking like a legitimate candidate to stick on this side of the D/ST top-10 lists.

 The preseason No. 1 Los Angeles Rams (minus-0.4) narrowly missed the cut, but they've also faced one of the more challenging season-opening schedules (SF in Australia; NYG on MNF; @DEN; @PHI).

 The D/ST to lock in for October: Jacksonville Jaguars 
 

 There really isn't a defense you can lock in for every one of the next four weeks, being that the top teams available in more than half of ESPN leagues all have their byes between Weeks 5 and 8. But if you're hoping to find a multiple-week D/ST, the Jaguars' next two matchups (PHI, HOU), as well as their Week 8 exiting their bye (IND), fit the bill. Jacksonville is tied for fifth in D/ST scoring, behind 14- and 13-point performances in Weeks 1 and 3, and it will play the next two games in London, where D/STs have averaged three more fantasy points per game (7.95) than in all other locations (5.92) since the beginning of 2023.

title: Kyle Monangai, Chuba Hubbard starred in superb week for Africa's running backs in NFL
summary: The Chicago Bears' Kyle Monangai (ties to Cameroon) and the Carolina Panthers' Chuba Hubbard (ties to Nigeria) starred in an NFL week which saw running backs with links to Africa impress.
full_text:
The Chicago Bears ' Kyle Monangai (ties to Cameroon) and the Carolina Panthers ' Chuba Hubbard (ties to Nigeria) starred in an NFL week which saw running backs with links to Africa impress.

 Monangai, Hubbard and New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (ties to Liberia) each scored two touchdowns. The Bears beat the New York Jets 23-12 and the Panthers edged the Detroit Lions 32-26, but Kamara's Saints went down 45-24 to the Atlanta Falcons .

 That game saw Nigeria's Samson Ebukam pick up a sack for the winning side, while his compatriot Basil Chijioke 'CJ' Okoye became the first NFL Africa IPP graduate to pick up a sack in a regular season game as his New York Giants beat the Arizona Cardinals 36-24.

 

 African Player of the Week - Kyle Monangai (Chicago Bears) 
 Monangai, whose parents are from Cameroon, racked up 146 yards across 30 carries in the Bears' win over the Jets at Soldier field, scoring two touchdowns.

 He is increasingly becoming an important part of the Bears offense in his second season. Having scored five touchdowns in his first season last year, Monangai now already has three this season.

 He racked up 100 yards across 10 carries and scored a superb touchdown in the 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers in his first game of the season, in addition to 24 more yards gained across two receptions.

 This time, his four yards gained on a solitary reception took his total yards in the win over the Jets to 150.

 

 African Moment of the Week - Chuba Hubbard (Carolina Panthers) 
 Not only were Hubbard's two touchdowns in the win over the Lions vital in a game ultimately decided by a six-point margin, but both of them were easy on the eye and the second came off the back of a sensational marauding run through the Detroit defense.

 Hubbard shook off five tackles, weaving his way through the tightest of spaces in a 25-yard-run, before a sixth finally brought him down two yards from the goal line.

 To complete his Moment of the Week, Hubbard ran in for the touchdown off the very next play. It came at a crucial moment, as the extra point from Ryan Fitzgerald extended the Panthers' lead to 10 points in what proved to be the final notch on the scoreboard during the third quarter.

 The Lions did their best to claw their way back in the fourth, but largely due to the damage already done by Hubbard -- who was born in Canada to a Nigerian father and Canadian mother.

 

 Honorable mentions 
 There were several standout defensive performances by players with ties to Africa across the NFL in Week 4. However, the pick of the bunch was Foyesade Oluokun - a Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker with parental ties to Nigeria.

 Oluokun made seven tackles, one red zone interception, and one sack, as the Jags beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17.

 Another player of Nigerian heritage -- Seattle Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori -- had an equally impressive game in the 30-23 win over the LA Chargers.

 Africa-born Player Watch 
 Okoye's sack for the Giants was certainly the underdog story of the week. Having come through the 2022 NFL Africa Touchdown camp and then the IPP Program, he had already shown his potential with the LA Chargers and then Baltimore Ravens , but the 24-year-old rising Nigerian star's first regular season sack was a moment to remember.

 The Giants held a slender 19-14 lead when Okoye pinned Jacoby Brissett back eight yards with around two minutes left in the first half.

 For a defensive lineman who only played his first organized football three years ago in the 2023 pre-season, it was yet another major statement of his ability - and arguably the most convincing of them all to date. He joined the Falcons' Ebukam as yet another Nigerian born player to pick up a sack in a Week 4 win.

 Meanwhile, the LA Rams' 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles was a showcase of Zimbabwean brilliance.

 On the winning side, Nate Landman made 10 tackles for the Rams. However, the contribution of his Zimbabwean compatriot, Andrew Mukuba -- who also has family ties to DR Congo -- should not be overlooked. Mukuba picked up an interception for the Eagles.

 Perhaps the biggest compliment one could pay towards Africa's growing role in the NFL in recent years is that week on week, it is becoming increasingly difficult to fit the top highlights on both offense and defense into a single piece.

title: MVP?! 3 keys to watch if Panthers QB Bryce Young is on that path
summary: The 2023 first-round pick's start -- he leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards -- puts him in the MVP conversation.
full_text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- It was hard to ignore.

 As the Bank of America Stadium crowd basked in its first home win of the 2026 season, multiple "MVP" chants erupted during the Panthers' 32-26 win against the Detroit Lions on Sunday night. The three-lettered chorus was aimed at quarterback Bryce Young as he put together an epic aerial performance.

 And while it might be a bit premature for MVP consideration, especially for a signal-caller who has experienced highs and lows throughout his four-year career, Young's start to the season has undoubtedly made the conversation at least plausible as the Panthers enter their Week 5 bye and await the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6.

 Young, 25, leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards. He's tied for third in passing touchdowns -- with the likes of Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes , Detroit's Jared Goff and New Orleans' Tyler Shough -- with nine.

 

 "That's stats," Young said Sunday. "For us, the only stat we care about is the win column."

 It's worth noting the Panthers (2-2) have a .500 record through the first quarter of the season for the first time since 2021, and Carolina is also 10-8 with Young as a starter dating back to Week 3 of last season. Coming off their first playoff appearance since 2017 and first division title since 2015, the Panthers currently sit at the top of the NFC South division, ahead of the Falcons (2-2).

 Young is a large reason for Carolina's early success, as the Panthers have the top passing offense in the league entering Week 5. Carolina is averaging 301.3 passing yards per game, pushing the offense to rank fourth in the league with an average of 405.8 total yards per game.

 And while Young says he doesn't want to focus on stats (or a potential contract extension ), the weight of those aforementioned MVP chants are ultimately going to be impacted by numbers beyond the Panthers' win total.

 Let's look at three stats to monitor and ones that could further influence Young's path toward the league's top award:

 
 Bryce Young's touchdown-to-interception ratio 
 Young is protecting the ball quite well. Through four games, he has two interceptions and no fumbles lost. He's averaging 4.5 touchdowns for every one interception so far this season.

 Of the six QBs with nine or more passing touchdowns, only Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers (1) and Goff (0) have fewer than two interceptions entering Week 5.

 In his three previous seasons, Young has done a relatively good job of avoiding interceptions with the occasional multiple-pick downturn outing peppered into his annual performance. His career high for interceptions in a season is 11, which he produced while also throwing for a career-high 3,011 yards and 23 touchdowns in 2025.

 The 2023 first overall pick's scoring surge this season is impressive as he threw for 11 touchdowns during 16 games played as a rookie. In 2024, he threw for 15 touchdowns in 14 games (12 starts). He's currently on pace for 38 passing touchdowns and nine interceptions through four games this season.

 

 Young's passing yards per attempt 
 Young is pushing the ball downfield at a quality clip in 2026. In 2025, he averaged 6.3 yards per pass attempt, and that season was considered his breakout campaign. This season, he's up to 7.8 yards per pass attempt. He's also averaging 8.4 air yards per passing attempt, which is up from 6.2 last season.

 Young, with offensive coordinator Brad Idzik now in charge of playcalling , is letting it rip. He has thrown at targets 20 yards or more downfield on 11.1% of his passing attempts in 2026, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Last season, that average was 7.1%. He has also thrown intermediately -- passes between 10 and 19 yards -- at a 24.7% clip compared to 23% last season.

 

 

 Young's connection with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker 
 Young has undeniable chemistry with his top wide receivers McMillan and Coker. Through the first quarter of the season, Young has a 118.7 passer rating when targeting the duo.

 He has completed 44 of 61 passes to Coker and McMillan for 607 combined yards, four touchdowns and an interception. With a 72.1% completion percentage to McMillan and Coker, Young is gaining roughly 10 yards per completion.

 As Young continues to ascend, having two trusted playmakers in the lineup should only help him bolster his numbers and MVP case. Even with Coker (quad) sidelined this past Sunday, Young completed 14 passes to McMillan for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the win against Detroit.

full_text:
Week 4  of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. It was flag week in the NFL! I love a flag week. Who doesn't love a flag week? Referees threw 293 flags in Week 4, the most in a single week this season and in any season since 2019. My favorite flag thrower is Nathan Jones, the field judge for Carl Cheffers' crew -- I know, I know, normie pick -- but he kills it every time.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with the crowning of a new top team in the AFC, discuss why another top AFC team needs to ignore its quarterback and wonder where all the play-action went in the Rams' offense.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Jaguars are the class of the AFC 
 Bengals don't need to pass more 
 Rams need to rediscover play-action 
 Johnson is Coach of the Year 
 Stroud is finally back 
 Eagles' offense is unrecoverable 
 Lions' defense has no quick fix 
 Four extra inklings 

 

 
 

 I think ... the Jaguars are the class of the AFC 
 Here are the odds to represent the conference from DraftKings:

 

 The market has the Jaguars (3-1) in a weird spot right now. It doesn't like them enough to plant them atop the conference with the longstanding big three -- that's the Chiefs (4-0), Bills (3-1) and Ravens (3-1). But it thinks they're clearly better than the second tier of AFC contenders -- the Bengals (2-2), Patriots (2-2) and Broncos (2-2). It's not entirely sure what to do with the Jaguars.

 I know what to do. Stick 'em in the top tier.

 If I've said it once, I've said it a thousand times: Look at what the Jaguars have been since their Week 9 bye last season. They're 12-2 over 14 regular-season games, tied with the Seahawks for the best such record. Offensively, they are second in points per drive, and defensively they are third in points per drive.

 Fourteen games is a pretty big sample, but we can check for easy pitfalls just in case. The Jaguars are third in turnover margin over that time at plus-11 with only 14 giveaways in 14 games -- that feels suspicious. But we have a better metric for turnover impact than margin, and its turnover EPA -- it helps us put a weight on turnovers, as some interceptions (thrown in the red zone, for example) hurt more than others (thrown on third-and-long 40-plus yards downfield). The Jaguars are 16th in turnover EPA per game over this stretch of games, bang on league average.

 What about strength of schedule? Have they been treading over cupcakes? That was a legitimate concern throughout the 2025 season. They played a stretch of bad offenses, including the Daniel Jones -less Colts twice, the  Cam Ward  Titans twice and the  Brady Cook  Jets. To start 2026, the defense had faced Deshaun Watson 's Browns, the  Bo Nix  Broncos -- a worryingly good game for Nix, if you're a Jaguars believer -- and a disastrous game from the  Drake Maye  Patriots.

 Then they played the Bengals and Joe Burrow on Sunday ... a stiffer test.

 It was a solid team 22-17 win across the board. The Jaguars had a 34.5% pressure rate against Burrow. The pass rush, which I had lamented as a potential Achilles' heel for a contender not two weeks ago, showed up in a huge way. Arik Armstead had more pressures in this one game (six) than the entire Jacksonville defensive tackle room had produced through the first two weeks of the season. Burrow threw two picks on the day, and both were the result of pressure in the pocket.

 Defensively, the Jaguars accounted for the absence of outside corner Montaric Brown (hamstring) with a full menu of Travis Hunter coverage snaps. He played 71 defensive snaps, not sitting out a single play . He had seven targets in 48 coverage snaps and surrendered only four catches for 30 yards -- most of them underneath completions in zone coverage. He had two pass breakups on the day and another interception wiped out by a roughing the passer penalty.

 

 On offense, the Jaguars had one of the most impressive rushing days of coach Liam Coen's tenure. The Jaguars' running backs averaged 4.7 yards per carry (seventh-best game) with 2.4 of those yards coming before contact (second-best game). Second-year man Bhayshul Tuten had two big runs called back for penalties, and the Jaguars suffered a few stuffs at the hands of the Bengals' Dexter Lawrence II . But it was a balanced approach. Also, don't forget about Cam Little 's big leg -- he nailed two 50-plus-yard field goals. The Jaguars are a complete team.

 If you feel as if you've noticed a theme in the summary of Jacksonville's success against Cincinnati ... the Jaguars were swimming upstream against their own miscues. Jacksonville ate 125 yards worth of penalties in this game, its worst single-game number in the past six seasons. This scoreboard could have and should have been more lopsided with better discipline across the board.

 In the Coen tenure, the Jaguars have risen well against AFC contenders. They split with Cincinnati over the past two seasons and split the series with Houston last season in a weird loss to Davis Mills . They took Buffalo to the final bell in the postseason and beat Kansas City in the regular season at a final bell of their own.

 The only thing this team doesn't have is a recent, deep postseason run -- it hasn't made the divisional round since 2022 -- to give it a sense of tenure and legitimacy. The Ravens and Lamar Jackson were in the divisional round in 2024 and the conference championship in 2023. The Bills were in the divisional round last year and the conference championship in 2024. I don't need to explain the Chiefs' experience. We've seen all of them there, so it's easier to imagine seeing them again.

 We've also seen those quarterbacks win MVP trophies. Five of the past eight, to be exact.

 Continued doubt in the Jaguars is borne only by suspicion in Trevor Lawrence , who didn't immediately reach his billing as the next generational quarterback when he was selected with the No. 1 pick in 2021. Because he was shaky to start his career (under Urban Meyer and on a dreadful roster, mind you), his blossoming now must be fraudulent, right?

 

 If Lawrence is less trustworthy than Jackson, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes  as the difference-making passer on a top-tier contending team because of his lack of MVP trophies and deep postseason experience, then there's nothing I can say now to change your mind. You have to wait to see what awards he wins this season and how deep his team goes.

 

 But if I can convince you that sometimes, gifted quarterbacks don't land with the right playcaller at first -- that sometimes, Matthew Stafford has to sit and toil in Detroit for seasons before he can find his Sean McVay, and Matt Ryan must do the same -- then perhaps we can reframe this moment for Lawrence. I wrote it after Week 1 and still believe it after Week 4: The guy looks like an MVP. He doesn't play like a middling quarterback propped up by an elite playcaller -- nor does Coen coach him that way. Too much of this offense is built on his arm, his throws on the move, his pre-snap acumen. He is what we were promised. Not insufficient, just delayed.

 Don't buy the Jaguars yet if you don't want to. I understand your hesitancy. Just don't forget that you were offered a chance to buy in on the ground floor.

 

 

 I think ... the Bengals need to ignore Joe Burrow  about their pass-heavy approach 
 The Bengals threw the football on 81.7% of their offensive snaps against the Jaguars. Of course, they largely trailed in this game,…
